The passenger deployed the rip line, resulting in a rapid descent, ground impact, and serious injuries, with no mechanical failure reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain helicopter control and terrain clearance while in a hover after performing an evasive maneuver to avoid wildlife.
summary: The pilot of a helicopter hovering near a private heliport attempted an evasive maneuver to avoid a flock of Canada geese. The pilot lost control and terrain clearance, resulting in a crash that separated the main rotor blades and tail rotor gearbox.

synopsis: A loss of engine power shortly after takeoff due to fuel exhaustion, and the exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack when the flight instructor made an abrupt turn back toward the runway, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall/spin at an altitude too low for recovery. Contributing to the accident was an inadequate preflight inspection.
summary: A flight instructor and passenger experienced fuel exhaustion shortly after takeoff during a discovery flight, likely due to an unverified fuel quantity. The instructor attempted a return to the runway but stalled and entered a spin at low altitude, impacting a building.

synopsis: The failed retaining bolt and cracked backing plate, which resulted in a shift of the brake lining to contact the brake drum and a subsequent wheel lock when the brakes were applied.
summary: An airline transport pilot nosed over and inverted a tailwheel aircraft during a landing roll after experiencing excessive shimmy. A postaccident examination found a failed retaining bolt and cracked brake backing plate caused the left wheel to lock when brakes were applied.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during takeoff.
summary: During takeoff from an unimproved gravel airstrip, the pilot reported the tailwheel-equipped airplane veered right and struck a parked aircraft. The pilot stated there were no preaccident mechanical failures, resulting in substantial damage to the wings, fuselage, and elevator.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain proper pitch for a soft-field landing, which resulted in a loss of airplane control.
summary: The pilot ground looped a single-engine airplane while landing on a beach, causing both wings to strike the ground and sustain substantial damage. The pilot attributed the accident to failing to maintain back pressure on the yoke during the landing roll, noting no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: On August 24, 2018, a Cirrus SR22 (LZ-SEV) impacted terrain at Balchik Airfield (LBWB) while en route from Lesnovo Airport. The aircraft was destroyed and the pilot was fatally injured.
summary: On August 24, 2018, a Cirrus SR22 (LZ-SEV) impacted terrain at Balchik Airfield (LBWB) while en route from Lesnovo Airport. The aircraft was destroyed and the pilot was fatally injured.

synopsis: The Mexican government notified the NTSB of an accident involving a Cessna 310, XB-KQF, on August 28, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist Mexico's investigation, with all information to be released by the Mexican government.
summary: The Mexican government notified the NTSB of an accident involving a Cessna 310, XB-KQF, on August 28, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist Mexico's investigation, with all information to be released by the Mexican government.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain sufficient altitude after takeoff in dark night conditions which resulted in a collision with the water.
summary: An instrument-rated pilot departed at night over a lake, banked right, and crashed into the water without distress calls. Investigators found no mechanical failure but concluded the dark overwater departure lacked visual cues, likely causing spatial disorientation if instruments were not used.

synopsis: The flight instructor's delayed application of power during a power recovery following an autorotation, which resulted in an unrecoverable low rotor rpm during the landing flare and subsequent loss of control.
summary: A flight instructor and student attempted a power recovery from a practice autorotation at 150 ft, below the recommended 300 ft minimum. Insufficient engine power response led to low rotor rpm, loss of control, and substantial damage after the main rotor blades impacted the ground.

synopsis: The Mexican government notified the NTSB of an accident involving an Airbus A321-271N on August 20, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist Mexico's investigation, with all information to be released by the Mexican government.
summary: The Mexican government notified the NTSB of an accident involving an Airbus A321-271N on August 20, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist Mexico's investigation, with all information to be released by the Mexican government.

synopsis: The Mexican government notified the NTSB of an August 20, 2018, accident involving a Boeing 737. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist Mexico's investigation, with all information to be released by the Mexican government.
summary: The Mexican government notified the NTSB of an August 20, 2018, accident involving a Boeing 737. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist Mexico's investigation, with all information to be released by the Mexican government.

synopsis: The Mexican government notified the NTSB of an August 18, 2018, accident involving a Boeing 737. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist Mexico's investigation, with all information to be released by the Mexican government.
summary: The Mexican government notified the NTSB of an August 18, 2018, accident involving a Boeing 737. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist Mexico's investigation, with all information to be released by the Mexican government.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to see and avoid power wires while maneuvering at low altitude. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's inability to determine the airplane's altitude due to sun glare.
summary: The pilot struck power wires and impacted terrain while descending in a right turn about 200 feet above ground level. The accident was caused by the sun in his eyes and the aircraft being lower than anticipated, resulting in substantial damage to the wings and fuselage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain aircraft control during a go-around due to his premature flap retraction, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall and subsequent loss of control.
summary: The pilot of a single-engine aircraft carrying two passengers stalled during a go-around after an unstable approach. The accident resulted from speed mismanagement and premature flap retraction, which reduced the stall margin below the altitude required for recovery.

synopsis: A loss of directional control during a touch-and-go landing in gusting crosswind conditions.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot lost directional control during a touch-and-go landing in gusting crosswinds on runway 14. The aircraft struck the left wing and came to rest inverted 1,800 feet down the runway.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane reported a left ground loop during the landing roll, causing substantial damage to the right wing and elevator. The pilot stated no preaccident mechanical failures occurred that would have prevented normal operation.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during takeoff with a tailwind.
summary: During a touch-and-go landing on runway 24, the pilot reduced flaps and applied full throttle, but the airplane drifted left despite right rudder input. The aircraft exited the runway, crossed a ditch, and upon landing, the nose gear separated, causing substantial damage to the wing and fuselage with no reported mechanical failure.

synopsis: The fisherman's fishing rod striking the helicopter's rotating main rotor disk during loading.
summary: While hot loading fishermen, a fishing rod struck the helicopter's main rotor disc, causing damage beyond repair limits. The pilot reported no flight control anomalies or pre-existing mechanical failures during the hover.

synopsis: The Safety Investigation Board Pakistan notified the NTSB of an August 08, 2018 incident involving a Boeing 777. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the SIB.
summary: The Safety Investigation Board Pakistan notified the NTSB of an August 08, 2018 incident involving a Boeing 777. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the SIB.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain pitch control on uneven terrain during the landing roll, which resulted in a nose-over.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane nosed over while landing uphill at an off-airport unimproved site after hitting a bush or bump that raised the tail and caused the propeller to strike the ground. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the empennage, fuselage, and wing spars with no reported preaccident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's improper preflight fuel planning and in-flight fuel management, which resulted in fuel exhaustion and the total loss of engine power.
summary: The pilot reported that on final approach, the engine lost all power due to fuel exhaustion caused by a miscalculation of endurance. The aircraft struck a power line and impacted a field, sustaining substantial wing damage, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a bounced landing.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane reported flaring high during landing, causing a bounce and a crossways touchdown where both wings struck the runway. The aircraft came to rest nose-down with substantial left wing damage, and the pilot reported no preaccident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The delayed application of carburetor heat by the pilot which led to accumulation of carburetor ice, eventual loss of engine power, and the subsequent forced landing in high vegetation.
summary: The pilot experienced engine roughness and total power loss during descent due to carburetor ice, likely caused by delayed application of carburetor heat. This resulted in a forced landing in a farm field where the aircraft nosed over in high vegetation.

synopsis: The pilot receiving instruction's failure to extend the landing gear and the flight instructor's failure to verify that the landing gear was extended before landing. Contributing to the accident was the flight instructor's delayed remedial action and distraction.
summary: During a simulated single-engine approach in a twin-engine airplane, the flight instructor and student failed to extend the landing gear due to the instructor's distraction while correcting the student's flight path. The aircraft landed gear-up, sustaining substantial engine damage, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: a tailstrike caused by inappropriate recovery technique after a bounced landing. Contributing to the accident was the failure of the radio altimeter, caused by the approach being over calm/flat water, that was not recognized by the flight crew.
summary: Hawaiian Airlines Flight 56, an Airbus A321, struck its tail during landing at KLAX after the First Officer lost automated radio altimeter callouts over water due to a known system limitation. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the aft lower skin, though no injuries occurred among the 197 people onboard.

synopsis: The total loss of engine power due to oil starvation after an interruption of oil circulation for reasons that could not be determined based on the available evidence.
summary: The pilot experienced a catastrophic engine failure during cruise flight caused by a lack of lubrication, resulting in total power loss and an emergency landing that damaged the fuselage and left wing. Examination revealed fractured connecting rods and metal debris, though the specific source of the oil circulation interruption could not be determined.

synopsis: The UK government notified the NTSB of an August 1, 2018, accident involving a Robinson R22 helicopter. The NTSB appointed a representative to assist the UK investigation, with all information to be released by the UK government.
summary: The UK government notified the NTSB of an August 1, 2018, accident involving a Robinson R22 helicopter. The NTSB appointed a representative to assist the UK investigation, with all information to be released by the UK government.

synopsis: The pilot failed to maintain adequate speed while maneuvering at a low attitude during night and entered an aerodynamic stall and subsequent spin.
summary: A pilot flying a personal aircraft at night entered a steep spin while maneuvering to avoid a cloud during the base-to-final turn. The likely cause was failure to maintain proper airspeed, resulting in an accelerated stall, terrain impact, and a postimpact fire.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to properly adjust the fuel/air mixtures, which resulted in a partial loss of engine power to both engines due to fuel starvation and a subsequent forced landing to a field.
summary: The pilot of a multiengine airplane experienced engine vibration and loss of power during cruise after failing to enrich fuel mixtures while leaning. This distraction caused a forced gear-up landing in a field, resulting in substantial damage to the aircraft.

synopsis: The pilot's delayed decision to abort the takeoff, which resulted in the loss of lateral control of the airplane and collision with trees at the end of the runway. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's decision to depart with a center of gravity exceeding the aft limit and his inadequate preflight planning of the airplane's weight and balance calculations and runway length data.
summary: A private pilot attempted takeoff in a light aircraft on a grass runway but failed to gain altitude due to soft surface conditions, an aft center of gravity, and near-maximum weight. The pilot's delayed abort decision, based on incorrect runway length data, resulted in a collision with trees at the runway end.

synopsis: The pilot's improper fuel management, which resulted in a total loss of right engine power due to fuel starvation; the pilot's inadequate flight planning; the pilot's failure to secure the right engine following the loss of power; and his failure to properly configure the airplane for the go-around, which resulted in the airplane's failure to climb, an exceedance of the critical angle of attack, and an aerodynamic stall.
summary: A private pilot flying a multi-engine airplane at night lost right engine power due to fuel starvation while conducting an instrument approach. The pilot attempted a go-around without securing the engine or retracting landing gear and flaps, resulting in an aerodynamic stall and crash.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: The pilot practicing steep approaches flared the helicopter too hard and low, causing the tail skid to strike the runway and resulting in a hard landing. This impact sustained substantial damage to the vertical stabilizer, with no preaccident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's improper decision to initiate the flight in marginal visual flight rules over mountainous terrain, which resulted in an inadvertent encounter with instrument meteorological and downdraft conditions and the subsequent controlled flight into trees and terrain.
summary: The pilot departed in visual conditions but entered instrument meteorological conditions near a ridge, causing the lead aircraft to disappear. A sudden downdraft and terrain proximity led to a tree and terrain impact with substantial wing damage, attributed to unexpected weather changes in mountainous terrain.

synopsis: On September 1, 2018, a Cessna 182M (ZS-IAM) collided with trees during final approach to Leshiba Wilderness, South Africa. The pilot and passenger were seriously injured, and the aircraft sustained substantial damage.
summary: On September 1, 2018, a Cessna 182M (ZS-IAM) collided with trees during final approach to Leshiba Wilderness, South Africa. The pilot and passenger were seriously injured, and the aircraft sustained substantial damage.

synopsis: The flight crew's failure to adequately monitor the airplane's airspeed, which led to the captain's aggressive control inputs to increase airspeed; these aggressive inputs resulted in injuries to three cabin crewmembers.
summary: During descent, the captain's altimeter adjustment and mode selection caused autothrottles to hold, leading to a pitch-up and speed decay. The captain's aggressive recovery maneuvers injured three flight attendants, though the aircraft landed safely.

synopsis: On July 17, 2018, a Cessna 182 pilot experienced an engine failure during a local flight from Les Rabassières, France, and declared an emergency. The aircraft subsequently suffered a runway excursion upon landing, resulting in substantial damage but no injuries to the sole occupant.
summary: On July 17, 2018, a Cessna 182 pilot experienced an engine failure during a local flight from Les Rabassières, France, and declared an emergency. The aircraft subsequently suffered a runway excursion upon landing, resulting in substantial damage but no injuries to the sole occupant.

synopsis: The pilot's inadvertent activation of the fuel pump control rocker switch, which resulted in a loss of engine power shortly after takeoff. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's distraction with an entangled headset cord.
summary: During takeoff, a pilot distracted by a stuck headset module inadvertently moved the fuel pump switch to HIGH BOOST/PRIME, causing engine power loss at 200 feet. The pilot deployed the airframe parachute below minimum altitude, resulting in substantial fuselage damage upon impact.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to attempt to take off in an overweight airplane in high density altitude conditions, which resulted in the airplane's inability to climb, an aborted takeoff, and a subsequent runway excursion.
summary: The pilot attempted an intersection takeoff in high density altitude conditions with an airplane exceeding maximum gross weight by 300 lbs. The aircraft failed to climb properly, struck the runway hard, veered off, and sustained substantial wing damage due to the overweight and high density altitude conditions.

synopsis: The partial loss of engine power due to a fractured exhaust valve, which resulted in a forced landing on unsuitable terrain and a subsequent rollover.
summary: A private pilot conducting a cross-country flight experienced engine roughness and violent shaking 12 miles from departure, forcing a landing where the aircraft flipped. The accident was caused by a fractured No. 4 cylinder exhaust valve due to fatigue, as the engine had not been overhauled since 28 years prior despite a 12-year recommendation.

synopsis: A loss of directional control during takeoff and initial climb for reasons that could not be determined based on the available information.
summary: The pilot lost directional control immediately after liftoff, forcing an off-runway landing between trees. Post-accident examination found no mechanical anomalies but noted unshielded floor cutouts and a potential rudder pedal entrapment hazard, though the specific cause of the control loss remained undetermined.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain lateral control during a hover.
summary: A student pilot hovering a helicopter encountered a wind gust that pushed the aircraft left, causing a skid impact and a roll onto its left side. The helicopter sustained substantial damage to the windscreen and tailboom, with no preaccident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of control during approach for landing following a total loss of left engine power for undetermined reasons.
summary: The unlicensed pilot of a twin-engine airplane lost left engine power twice during the approach, then turned below minimum control speed and rolled inverted into the ground. The accident resulted from the pilot's lack of proficiency in one-engine-inoperative procedures, though the specific cause of the engine failure and potential drug effects could not be determined.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain lateral control during the aborted landing.
summary: A student pilot soloing in a traffic pattern drifted left during a fifth touch-and-go attempt. Insufficient right rudder while aborting caused a hard left bank and fence collision, resulting in substantial wing damage with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot receiving instruction's failure to maintain control during a night landing pattern crosswind turn due to spatial disorientation and the flight instructor's inadequate supervision and delayed remedial action, which resulted in impact with terrain.
summary: A flight instructor and a student pilot crashed a training aircraft into terrain during the student's first night flight in Alaska. The accident occurred when the student became disoriented and descended below pattern altitude due to a dark, moonless night with no visible horizon.

synopsis: The airplane's collision with a bird during straight-and-level flight.
summary: During straight-and-level flight, a large bird struck the airplane's right wing, degrading control and causing substantial damage. The pilot executed an off-airport landing without further incident, reporting no preaccident mechanical failures.

synopsis: On September 5, 2018, a Robinson R44 (I-CCNI) impacted terrain while maneuvering at low altitude near Plzen-Skvmany, Czech Republic. The pilot and three passengers sustained fatal injuries during this incident.
summary: On September 5, 2018, a Robinson R44 (I-CCNI) impacted terrain while maneuvering at low altitude near Plzen-Skvmany, Czech Republic. The pilot and three passengers sustained fatal injuries during this incident.

synopsis: The total loss of engine power for reasons that could not be determined based on the available evidence.
summary: A commercial pilot conducting a personal night cross-country flight experienced a total engine power loss shortly after takeoff, forcing a landing that caused substantial damage. Although a failed right magneto coil and severe spark plug wear were found, the investigation could not determine the cause of the total power loss.

synopsis: The pilot's improper hand propping procedure, which resulted in a runaway airplane and subsequent impact with a hangar.
summary: The pilot hand-propped the aircraft alone after FBO personnel refused to assist with a low battery. The airplane moved forward and struck a hangar, sustaining substantial left wing damage, likely because the pilot failed to secure the brakes or use a second person as required.

synopsis: The pilot's improper decision not to abort the takeoff after the airplane encountered standing water on the runway, which decreased its speed and led to its subsequent inability to climb and resulted in a runway overrun.
summary: The pilot attempted takeoff on a wet, 2,200-ft turf runway but lost airspeed due to standing water. Despite retracting flaps, the aircraft exited the runway end into a cornfield, sustaining substantial engine mount damage with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The accumulation of carburetor ice before takeoff, which resulted in a partial loss of engine power on initial climb and a forced landing on unsuitable terrain.
summary: A private pilot experienced partial engine power loss and vibration at 400 feet after takeoff, likely due to carburetor ice formed during low-power taxi and run-ups. The pilot executed a forced landing in a field, resulting in nose gear collapse, though no mechanical failures were found post-accident.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to verify that the emergency canopy release was in the correct position when opening the canopy during landing, which resulted in the canopy separating from the airplane and subsequently impacting the empennage.
summary: The pilot reported that after landing, the canopy separated from the airframe and struck the empennage, causing substantial damage. This occurred because the emergency canopy release, which anchors the canopy during motor operation, was inadvertently released during the flight.

synopsis: The pilot's exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack during takeoff, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall.
summary: A private pilot lost control of an airplane during takeoff, causing it to impact the ground and be destroyed. The investigation concluded the pilot likely overrotated, inducing an aerodynamic stall, as no mechanical failures or power loss were found.

synopsis: The Government of Turkey notified the NTSB of a Bell 430 accident on September 06, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist Turkey's investigation, with all information to be released by the Turkish government.
summary: The Government of Turkey notified the NTSB of a Bell 430 accident on September 06, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist Turkey's investigation, with all information to be released by the Turkish government.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll, which resulted in a ground-loop.
summary: Two pilots practicing landings in a tailwheel biplane experienced a left ground-loop during the landing roll, causing the right wing and aileron to strike the ground. The pilot reported substantial damage to the right wing and aileron but noted no mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: The Brazilian government notified the NTSB of a September 01, 2018, accident involving a Beech 33 airplane. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist Brazil's investigation, with all information to be released by Brazil.
summary: The Brazilian government notified the NTSB of a September 01, 2018, accident involving a Beech 33 airplane. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist Brazil's investigation, with all information to be released by Brazil.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a bounced landing.
summary: The pilot returned to the departure airport for a precautionary landing after the engine ran rough with high cylinder head temperature and decreasing power. The aircraft bounced on touchdown, sustaining substantial fuselage damage, though the FAA inspector found no mechanical failures.

synopsis: On September 7, 2018, the pilot in command of a Yakovlev YAK-9UM (VH-YIX) was fatally injured when the aircraft impacted terrain during a local flight from Latrobe Valley Airport. The airplane sustained substantial damage, and the Australian Transport Safety Bureau is investigating the accident.
summary: On September 7, 2018, the pilot in command of a Yakovlev YAK-9UM (VH-YIX) was fatally injured when the aircraft impacted terrain during a local flight from Latrobe Valley Airport. The airplane sustained substantial damage, and the Australian Transport Safety Bureau is investigating the accident.

synopsis: The pilot under instruction's failure to maintain the twin-engine airplane's minimum control airspeed with one engine inoperative and the flight instructor's distraction when reconfiguring the airplane following the simulated engine failure, which resulted in no power being available to the left engine and a loss of control during landing when the throttles were advanced to increase airspeed.
summary: A flight instructor in a multiengine airplane forgot to turn the left engine fuel selector back on after a simulated failure. The aircraft rolled left and settled in a lagoon beside the runway with substantial fuselage damage because the left engine produced no power when the pilot increased throttle.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a bounced landing, and his subsequent failure to maintain directional control in gusting, right quartering tailwind conditions.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane exited runway 09 during landing after a firm touchdown caused a bounce and a left-wing-low attitude. Despite corrective rudder and brake inputs, the aircraft veered right and sustained substantial fuselage damage with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The student pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a bounced landing.
summary: A solo student pilot landed on the left main gear and bounced during approach to runway 33 after struggling to maintain airspeed, causing substantial damage to the firewall and fuselage. The pilot executed a go-around and landed safely, reporting no mechanical failures with winds at 6 knots.

synopsis: A Piper PA32 300 operated by Wings of Hope experienced a hard landing at Sir Barry Bowen Municipal Airport in Belize City on August 29. The aircraft had originated from San Pedro Airport, and the incident is under investigation by the Belize Department of Civil Aviation.
summary: A Piper PA32 300 operated by Wings of Hope experienced a hard landing at Sir Barry Bowen Municipal Airport in Belize City on August 29. The aircraft had originated from San Pedro Airport, and the incident is under investigation by the Belize Department of Civil Aviation.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to secure his seat position prior to takeoff, which resulted in a loss of airplane control and subsequent hard landing.
summary: The pilot reported that his seat slid aft during the takeoff roll, preventing control of the throttle and rudder, which caused the aircraft to veer left, strike the ground, and rest on its nose. The investigation concluded the seat pin was likely not engaged in the rail hole despite the pilot's attempt to lock it.

synopsis: Impact with terrain for reasons that could not be determined based on the available information.
summary: An 85-year-old pilot flying an experimental amateur-built airplane entered a steep climb followed by a dive into terrain without attempting to recover. No mechanical failures or medical incapacitation were found, and the cause of the impact could not be determined.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance with a hangar while maneuvering to his hangar. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's limited experience in helicopters.
summary: An unlicensed pilot hover-taxied an experimental amateur-built helicopter into a hangar, likely ascending too high. The accident involved a fractured left anti-torque pedal caused by poor fabrication, though it remains unclear if the failure preceded the collision or resulted from it.

synopsis: The Government of Guyana notified the NTSB of a September 10, 2018, accident involving a BELL 206 helicopter. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by Guyana.
summary: The Government of Guyana notified the NTSB of a September 10, 2018, accident involving a BELL 206 helicopter. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by Guyana.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain the runway heading during takeoff and the flight instructor's decision to conduct primary flight instruction in an airplane without dual controls.
summary: During takeoff, a student pilot's improper rudder and brake inputs caused the aircraft to veer off the runway, resulting in a tail strike and subsequent excursion into a ditch. The flight instructor aborted the takeoff, but the airplane sustained substantial damage to the wings and fuselage with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: A right engine turbine uncontainment resulting from failure of the high pressure turbine (HPT) lenticular seal due to a fatigue crack originating from an overheated region at a knife edge tip. Contributing to the failure was Pratt & Whitney's decision to introduce the temperature-resistant knife-edge coating as a new-part number lenticular seal on an attrition basis without the option to recoat existing lenticular seals, which delayed implementation of the more durable seal material into the fleet.
summary: A PW2000 engine high-pressure turbine uncontained failure occurred due to a lenticular seal fracture caused by thermo-mechanical fatigue from a second-run seal with worn coating running against new honeycomb material. The failure destroyed turbine components, breached cases, and released fuel, though the specific crack initiation site was obliterated by secondary damage.

synopsis: The pilot's exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack during an attempted go-around after the airplane bounced, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall.
summary: During landing, a tailwheel-equipped airplane bounced and veered left, prompting the pilot to apply full throttle for a go-around while maintaining back pressure. This caused a high angle of attack, resulting in an aerodynamic stall, spin, and ground impact that sustained substantial fuselage damage.

synopsis: The student pilot's improper approach path after the airplane encountered turbulence, which resulted in the airplane landing hard short of the runway.
summary: A solo student pilot flying a light aircraft encountered turbulence and increased lift during approach to runway 9. After reducing power caused a rapid altitude loss, the pilot added power but landed hard short of the runway, collapsing the nose gear and damaging the left wing.

synopsis: The failure of the landing gear extension motor due to wear, which resulted in the right main landing gear not fully extending and locking into place during landing. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's failure to ensure that all three landing gear were down and locked before landing.
summary: A private pilot landed a cross-country flight with a collapsed right main gear, causing the aircraft to veer off and damage the right horizontal stabilizer. The accident resulted from internal wear in the 37-year-old original landing gear extension motor, which prevented full extension despite the pilot believing the gear was down.

synopsis: A fuel leak from the carburetor float bowl due to a missing plug, which resulted in excessive fuel consumption and a total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's decision to depart on the accident flight leg after noting the airplane's unexpectedly high fuel consumption during the previous leg.
summary: A commercial pilot flying a newly purchased airplane experienced engine power loss due to a missing carburetor float bowl plug causing excessive fuel consumption. The pilot's decision to depart again after noting high fuel burn led to fuel exhaustion and a forced landing that substantially damaged the airframe.

synopsis: The student pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: A solo student pilot in a weight-shift-control aircraft flared too late during a full-stop landing, causing the aircraft to strike the runway hard. This resulted in substantial damage to the center-frame bar and left wing tubes, with no mechanical malfunctions reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane reported that during the landing roll on grass, the aircraft veered left and ground looped despite recovery attempts. The right landing gear collapsed and the wing struck a ditch, causing substantial damage with no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from a tree while maneuvering at a low altitude.
summary: The pilot maneuvered the airplane at low altitude and struck a lone tree taller than surrounding vegetation, likely due to not seeing the obstacle. The aircraft continued into a forested area and came to rest nose-down, with no preimpact mechanical failures found.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate preflight planning before takeoff in the high density altitude conditions, which resulted in the airplane being unable to maintain sufficient airspeed to continue to climb.
summary: The pilot aborted an initial takeoff due to poor acceleration and attempted a second departure from a longer runway. At 100 feet, the aircraft failed to climb, stalled, and crashed into trees, likely caused by high density altitude reducing climb performance.

synopsis: The pilots' loss of control during an instrument approach in instrument meteorological conditions as a result of spatial disorientation.
summary: An instrument-rated pilot flying in instrument meteorological conditions descended below minimum altitude during an ILS approach, drifted off course, and lost control. The pilot likely became spatially disoriented due to reduced visibility and high workload, resulting in a high-velocity impact with terrain.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain lateral control of the airplane during landing, which resulted in a loss of directional control and subsequent runway excursion.
summary: During landing on runway 8, the pilot reported the right wing lifted and the airplane drifted left, causing it to veer off the left side and impact trees. The pilot attributed the accident to no mechanical failures, noting variable winds of 5 knots, resulting in substantial damage to the wings and fuselage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to yield to traffic established on the taxiway, which resulted in a ground collision. The failure of the other pilot to yield to traffic established on the taxiway, which resulted in a ground collision.
summary: Two pilots collided while taxiing on taxiway delta when one entered without yielding to the other. The aircraft already on the taxiway sustained substantial damage to its left wing and rudder, with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: A partial loss of engine power that was the result of a loss of compression in the No. 1 and 4 cylinders due to damage and material separation from the exhaust valve heads, which resulted in a subsequent forced, hard landing. Contributing to the accident was inadequate maintenance inspection.
summary: A flight instructor experienced partial engine power loss in a helicopter at 1,600 ft MSL due to damaged exhaust valves in cylinders 1 and 4. The pilot performed a hard emergency landing on a golf course, resulting in tail rotor separation and main rotor blade damage.

synopsis: The pilot's diverted attention during takeoff initial climb, which resulted in a collision with rising terrain.
summary: The pilot reported that during the initial climb, diverted attention while entering fuel data caused the airplane to bank left into rising terrain and powerlines. Despite corrective actions, the aircraft impacted the ground near a ravine, sustaining substantial damage to the wings and fuselage with no mechanical anomalies found.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to properly secure his seat before initiating the takeoff, which resulted in the seat sliding back as the airplane accelerated during takeoff, his inability to reach the pedals, and the subsequent loss of directional control and impact with trees and shrubs.
summary: A private pilot lost directional control during takeoff when his seat slid back, preventing pedal access and causing the aircraft to leave the runway and strike trees. The accident likely resulted from the pilot failing to fully engage the seat locking pins after applying a twisting force while adjusting the seat.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a hard, bounced landing and subsequent loss of directional control on an unimproved airstrip.
summary: During approach to an unimproved airstrip, a pilot executed a steep descent with full flaps, causing a tailwheel-equipped airplane to bounce and veer left on the uneven dirt surface. The aircraft struck trees, sustaining substantial damage to the left wing and fuselage, with no preaccident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: A Robin DR400-120 (F-GIKQ) carrying a pilot and flight instructor overran runway 28 at Saint Chamond - L'Horme airport during takeoff. The aircraft came to rest on a highway 150 meters from the runway end with no injuries reported.
summary: A Robin DR400-120 (F-GIKQ) carrying a pilot and flight instructor overran runway 28 at Saint Chamond - L'Horme airport during takeoff. The aircraft came to rest on a highway 150 meters from the runway end with no injuries reported.

synopsis: The Brazilian government notified the NTSB of a September 15, 2018, accident involving a Beech C90. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist Brazil's investigation, with all information to be released by Brazil.
summary: The Brazilian government notified the NTSB of a September 15, 2018, accident involving a Beech C90. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist Brazil's investigation, with all information to be released by Brazil.

synopsis: The pilot's exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack during the landing flare, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall.
summary: During landing, the pilot flared too high, causing an aerodynamic stall and a hard landing that collapsed the nose gear. The aircraft veered off the runway, nosed over, and sustained substantial damage to the wings, fuselage, and empennage with no preaccident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's mismanagement of the available fuel, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel starvation.
summary: The pilot crashed a single-engine airplane into a home during the landing phase of a return flight due to fuel starvation. The accident likely occurred because the pilot failed to switch the fuel selector from the left tank, which was empty, to the right tank, resulting in total engine power loss.

synopsis: The pilot of the race 13 airplane's failure to maintain clearance from the race 37 airplane during the closed course air race. The pilot of the race 13 airplane's failure to maintain clearance from the race 37 airplane during the closed course air race.
summary: During a closed course air race, the pilot of race 13 collided with race 37 while overtaking on the right near a pylon. The pilot of race 13 failed to maintain adequate separation, causing damage to both aircraft, though both landed uneventfully.

synopsis: Loss of engine power due to fuel contamination.
summary: The pilot experienced total engine power loss on final approach due to ingesting a fuel and water mixture from a contaminated aft boost pump. Unable to restore power, the pilot performed a forced landing in a field, where the aircraft struck rocks and sustained substantial damage.

aircraft: Calvin Nate H VELOCITY STD RG E
synopsis: The pilot's failure to use carburetor heat in conditions conducive to serious carburetor icing at glide power, which resulted in a partial loss of power and an aerodynamic stall.
summary: A private pilot flying an experimental amateur-built airplane stalled and impacted terrain short of the runway during a low-power visual approach. The accident likely resulted from carburetor icing due to the pilot failing to use carburetor heat in conducive weather conditions.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain a proper descent rate, which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: The pilot of an experimental, amateur-built airplane reported a hard landing with excessive airspeed during a touch-and-go, causing nose gear collapse and a runway excursion. The aircraft cartwheeled and sustained substantial right wing spar damage, though the pilot reported no mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: Loss of oil in flight as a result of a loose oil filter adapter which resulted in the pilot initiating an immediate landing to an open field. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's manipulation of the throttle that led to a reduction in rotor rpm, which resulted in his inability to perform a normal landing.
summary: The pilot of a helicopter in cruise flight landed immediately after an oil light illuminated, impacting terrain with forward speed. The accident was likely caused by a loose oil filter adapter that drained oil, though the engine retained power and a normal landing might have prevented damage.

synopsis: The student pilot's mismanagement of the fuel selector valve during the simulated forced landing demonstration and the flight instructor's inadequate supervision to ensure the fuel selector was properly set, which resulted in a loss of engine power and subsequent forced landing on unsuitable terrain.
summary: During a simulated engine failure training flight at 600 feet, a student pilot mismanaged the fuel selector valve while a flight instructor failed to adequately supervise. This caused fuel starvation, resulting in a forced landing where the aircraft impacted fencing and ditches.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in the airplane porpoising.
summary: The pilot reported that during landing after an instructional flight, the airplane porpoised and the nose landing gear collapsed, causing substantial damage to the lower fuselage. The pilot stated there were no mechanical malfunctions that would have precluded normal operation.

synopsis: Fatigue failure of the No. 1 cylinder intake valve, which resulted in the loss of engine power.
summary: An airline transport pilot and flight instructor lost engine power during an instrument approach due to a fatigued No. 1 cylinder intake valve failure. The aircraft struck power lines and vehicles before landing on a roadway, with the valve failure traced to potential maintenance issues with rocker arms and lifters.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion and the pilot's subsequent exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's decision to initiate and continue the flight into dark night conditions with a known electrical problem.
summary: The commercial pilot and his passenger continued a night flight with a known electrical failure and no fuel quantity indication, leading to fuel exhaustion. During a go-around, the engine lost power, causing an aerodynamic stall and terrain impact due to the pilot's failure to maintain airspeed.

synopsis: The pilot's improper fuel management during the landing approach, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel starvation. Contributing to the accident was his failure to follow the published emergency procedures after the loss of engine power.
summary: The pilot of a single-engine aircraft experienced total engine power loss during landing approach due to fuel starvation after failing to select the fullest tank or engage the auxiliary fuel pump as required. This resulted in a forced landing short of the runway where the airplane impacted trees and a fence.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from a power line pole during an agricultural application flight.
summary: During an agricultural application flight, the pilot reported the airplane's right wing struck a power line pole and impacted terrain. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the wings, fuselage, and empennage with no preaccident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The AAIA of Hong Kong notified the NTSB of an August 30, 2018 accident involving a Boeing 747. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the AAIA.
summary: The AAIA of Hong Kong notified the NTSB of an August 30, 2018 accident involving a Boeing 747. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the AAIA.

synopsis: The BFU of Germany notified the NTSB of a September 16, 2018, accident involving a Boeing 747. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the BFU investigation as the State of Manufacturer, with all information to be released by the BFU.
summary: The BFU of Germany notified the NTSB of a September 16, 2018, accident involving a Boeing 747. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the BFU investigation as the State of Manufacturer, with all information to be released by the BFU.

synopsis: an inadvertent encounter with wake turbulence.
summary: American Airlines flight 2197, a Boeing 737-800, encountered wake turbulence while descending through 3,100 feet on approach to Phoenix Sky Harbor, three miles behind an Airbus. A flight attendant securing galley items was seriously injured with a broken rib, though the aircraft and others remained unharmed.

synopsis: A loss of directional control during landing due to overstress failure of the left seat's left rudder pedal arm clevis, which occurred as a result of manufacturing defects.
summary: During an instructional landing approach, the aircraft experienced uncommanded yaw and roll due to a fractured left rudder pedal arm clevis caused by manufacturing defects. The instructor could not maintain runway alignment, resulting in a 90° veer off the runway and a collision with trees that caused substantial damage.

synopsis: The pilot's operation of the airplane with the alternator switch in the off position, which allowed the selected battery to discharge and resulted in an ignition system failure and a total loss of engine power.
summary: The private pilot of an experimental amateur-built airplane experienced total engine power loss due to a discharged battery caused by failing to activate the unlabeled alternator switch. This resulted in a forced landing where the aircraft nosed over and sustained substantial damage.

synopsis: The student pilot's improper pitch attitude control during the initial climb, which resulted in a loss of airspeed, and his subsequent decision to conduct a 180° turn following the perceived anomaly, which resulted in a runway overrun.
summary: A student pilot conducting a supervised solo flight experienced a rapid airspeed decrease during initial climb due to an excessively high pitch attitude. The student declared an emergency and turned 180° to land, but the aircraft overran the runway and struck a fence, causing substantial damage.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control during landing.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane experienced a bounce and left drift during a three-point landing on runway 34. While correcting with right rudder, the left wing lifted, causing the right main gear to collapse and the right wing to strike the ground, resulting in substantial damage.

synopsis: The pilot's selection of an empty fuel tank for takeoff, which resulted in fuel starvation and the subsequent total loss of engine power.
summary: The pilot of a float-equipped airplane reported an engine power loss at 200 feet during initial climb after selecting an empty center fuel tank. The aircraft struck trees and sustained substantial right wing damage, though passengers noted the engine regained power after switching tanks.

synopsis: An impact with terrain for reasons that could not be determined based on the available information.
summary: A pilot and passenger crashed a personal aircraft while hunting sheep in remote mountains after failing to file a flight plan. Post-accident examination found no mechanical failures, but the lack of a flight plan delayed the search and increased risk to SAR assets.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control during the landing roll and his subsequent attempted go-around.
summary: The pilot of an experimental tailwheel airplane veered off the runway during landing due to directional control issues. After striking a taxiway sign while attempting a climb, the aircraft landed on the grass safety area with substantial damage to the left main landing gear, though no mechanical failures were reported.

synopsis: The pilot's selection of an unsuitable off-airport landing area, which resulted in a ground loop.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane reported that during landing at an off-airport dirt and grass area, slippery ground and bumps caused the left wing to strike, leading to a ground loop and nose-down rest. The aircraft sustained substantial left wing damage with no preaccident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's improper decision to continue the flight in deteriorating weather conditions, which resulted in an inadvertent entry into a box canyon and subsequent controlled flight into mountainous terrain.
summary: An airline transport pilot flying cargo to a remote lodge entered a box canyon in low clouds and impacted terrain while attempting a steep right turn to exit. The accident likely resulted from deteriorating weather preventing terrain clearance, with no mechanical or confirmed medical impairment found.

synopsis: The pilot's descent below minimum descent altitude during the nonprecision instrument approach for reasons that could not be determined based on the available information.
summary: The airline transport pilot of a multiengine airplane descended below the 1,100-foot minimum descent altitude while on a VOR approach in 400-foot overcast conditions. The aircraft impacted terrain 3.5 miles from the runway threshold and was destroyed by fire, though the specific reason for the descent below MDA could not be determined.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power for reasons that could not be determined based on the available information.
summary: The pilot of a helicopter that had been stored for seven years experienced a total engine power loss between 500 and 1,000 feet agl during the accident flight. The subsequent autorotation resulted in a nose-over impact that severed the tailboom, but the cause of the power loss could not be determined.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain lateral control after landing on water in gusting wind conditions.
summary: The pilot of a float-equipped airplane nosed over during the water landing phase after a gust lifted the right wing and the left float struck the water. Both occupants were rescued, and the aircraft sustained substantial damage to the left wing lift strut with no preaccident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: A recent hard landing resulted in a fracture of a joint from a cylinder to a main landing gear.
summary: The pilot reported the aircraft veered left off the runway during landing roll, sustaining damage to the right wing and stabilizer. A failed weld on the main landing gear cylinder joint caused the collapse, likely from a recent hard landing, though the exact timing could not be determined.

synopsis: The ground crewmember's improper grabbing of the hovering helicopter's skid during an external load hook-up, which resulted in the helicopter descending and the main rotors striking ground equipment.
summary: A pilot in a skid-equipped helicopter descended while a ground crewmember grabbed the skid during bucket attachment, causing main rotor blades to strike ground equipment. The helicopter landed on a grass bale with substantial damage to the rotor drive systems, though the pilot reported no mechanical failures.

synopsis: On September 21, 2018, a Cessna T210L with three occupants impacted terrain on Mount Pico de Orizaba, Mexico, resulting in fatal injuries. The Dirección General de Aeronáutica Civil (DGAC) is investigating the accident, and this report provides only informational details released by the Mexican government.
summary: On September 21, 2018, a Cessna T210L with three occupants impacted terrain on Mount Pico de Orizaba, Mexico, resulting in fatal injuries. The Dirección General de Aeronáutica Civil (DGAC) is investigating the accident, and this report provides only informational details released by the Mexican government.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airplane control while maneuvering which resulted in the airplane exceeding its critical angle of attack and an accelerated stall.
summary: A student pilot with 10 hours of experience in the aircraft entered an accelerated stall while performing a low-altitude personal flight over his home. The airplane rolled inverted and impacted terrain after the pilot attempted a maneuver without sufficient training in performance characteristics.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll.
summary: The pilot landed a normally operating aircraft on runway 30, but it veered right and exited the runway, striking taxiway lights. The pilot attributed the loss of directional control to unseen dust devils despite reported calm winds and no mechanical failures.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to relinquish the flight controls during landing when the flight instructor told him to do so, and the instructor's subsequent inability to properly control the glider, which led to a hard landing.
summary: During a glider landing, a flight instructor and student pilot were involved when the student failed to relinquish controls after the instructor took command. This resulted in a hard landing and serious injuries to the student.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane veered left during landing on an unimproved canyon airstrip in moderate turbulence and a reported tailwind. The aircraft exited the runway, struck rocks, and sustained substantial damage after the left main gear separated, with no preaccident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: On September 25, 2018, a Robinson R44 II helicopter (C-GMCT) impacted terrain while diverting to Toronto/Buttonville due to deteriorating weather. The pilot was fatally injured during the flight from North Bay.
summary: On September 25, 2018, a Robinson R44 II helicopter (C-GMCT) impacted terrain while diverting to Toronto/Buttonville due to deteriorating weather. The pilot was fatally injured during the flight from North Bay.

synopsis: The operator's decision to allow a flight in an airplane with known, unresolved maintenance discrepancies, and the flight crew's failure to properly configure the airplane in a way that would have allowed the emergency or parking brake systems to stop the airplane during landing.
summary: The flight crew of a business jet overran the runway during landing after the normal braking system failed due to antiskid wiring discrepancies and an incorrectly positioned brake selector switch. Despite prior knowledge of the malfunction and an INOP placard, the crew failed to configure the emergency braking system or use the parking brake to stop the aircraft.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to identify that he was not utilizing the full runway for takeoff, and his delayed decision to abort the takeoff, which resulted in a runway overrun.
summary: The pilot entered the runway halfway down a 5,000-ft runway and attempted takeoff at 60 knots, but the aircraft failed to lift off and overran the end, striking a drainage ditch. The pilot reported no mechanical failures, attributing the excursion to insufficient runway remaining after a late decision to continue.

synopsis: The Brazilian government notified the NTSB of a September 24, 2018, accident involving a Honda HA-420. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist Brazil's investigation as the State of Manufacturer and Design.
summary: The Brazilian government notified the NTSB of a September 24, 2018, accident involving a Honda HA-420. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist Brazil's investigation as the State of Manufacturer and Design.

synopsis: The Government of the Federated States of Micronesia notified the NTSB of a Boeing 737 accident on September 28, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the FSM.
summary: The Government of the Federated States of Micronesia notified the NTSB of a Boeing 737 accident on September 28, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the FSM.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power after the separation of the No. 3 cylinder from the crankcase due to improper maintenance.
summary: A private pilot experienced a No. 3 cylinder separation and total power loss during cruise, forcing an instrument landing in a marsh where the right wing struck a tree. Postaccident examination found undertorqued cylinder nuts likely caused the separation, though the investigation could not determine if this resulted from improper overhaul or undocumented maintenance.

synopsis: The inability of the pilot of the Piper and the student pilot and flight instructor of the Diamond to see and avoid the other airplane. Contributing to the collision was the Piper pilot's failure to use the correct common traffic advisory frequency to announce his airplane's position. The inability of the pilot of the Piper and the student pilot and flight instructor of the Diamond to see and avoid the other airplane. Contributing to the collision was the Piper pilot's failure to use the correct common traffic advisory frequency to announce his airplane's position.
summary: A Piper landing on an intersecting runway collided with a Diamond taking off at an uncontrolled airport. The accident likely occurred because the Piper pilot used an incorrect CTAF frequency, preventing other pilots from hearing his position reports.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed and his exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's improper fuel management, which resulted in fuel starvation and the subsequent total loss of engine power.
summary: The pilot experienced an engine power loss during the landing phase at the departure airport after fueling issues at two other locations. The subsequent hard landing and substantial left wing damage resulted from an aerodynamic stall caused by the left fuel tank being completely empty.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain main rotor speed after setting the engine fuel control to idle, which resulted in a loss of helicopter control and impact with water.
summary: A private pilot flying a helicopter with a safety pilot and two passengers set the throttle to IDLE while en route over water, likely intending to practice an autorotation. The pilot failed to reduce collective pitch to maintain rotor speed, muted the low rotor RPM alert, and the helicopter impacted the water, destroying the aircraft and killing three occupants.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain lateral control of the airplane during a step-turn takeoff.
summary: During takeoff from an ocean bay, a pilot flying a float-equipped airplane turned left into the wind, causing the left wing to lift and the right wing to strike the water. The aircraft pivoted 90° clockwise and sustained substantial wing damage, with the pilot reporting no mechanical failures.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power during initial climb due to fuel starvation.
summary: The pilot selected the main fuel tank for takeoff, but the engine lost power at 50 feet, causing the aircraft to impact the runway and burn. The accident was likely caused by fuel starvation due to the tank being less than half full, contradicting later manufacturer guidance to use the front tank.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed and the exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack during a turn, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall and subsequent loss of control. Contributing to the accident was an undetermined engine anomaly.
summary: The pilot and passenger departed with an engine problem, prompting a return to the airport. The aircraft stalled and crashed in a nose-low attitude, likely due to the pilot failing to maintain proper airspeed, though the engine issue's cause remained undetermined.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed and his exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack while making a turn in gusting wind conditions while flying through hilly terrain, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall.
summary: The pilot and two passengers crashed a single-engine airplane in mountainous terrain during a local flight after likely stalling while turning left at low airspeed. The investigation found no mechanical failure, noting the aircraft was slightly overweight and the pilot had used buprenorphine, though its contribution to the accident could not be determined.

synopsis: On September 12, 2018, a Gulfstream GIV (5N-BOD) experienced a runway excursion at Nnamdi Akizkiwe International Airport (DNAA) in Abuja, Nigeria. The flight crew and passenger were uninjured, the aircraft was undamaged, and the Nigerian Accident Investigation Bureau is investigating the incident.
summary: On September 12, 2018, a Gulfstream GIV (5N-BOD) experienced a runway excursion at Nnamdi Akizkiwe International Airport (DNAA) in Abuja, Nigeria. The flight crew and passenger were uninjured, the aircraft was undamaged, and the Nigerian Accident Investigation Bureau is investigating the incident.

synopsis: The Mexican government notified the NTSB of an incident involving an Airbus A320 on September 26, 2018. The NTSB appointed a representative to assist Mexico's investigation, with all information to be released by the Mexican government.
summary: The Mexican government notified the NTSB of an incident involving an Airbus A320 on September 26, 2018. The NTSB appointed a representative to assist Mexico's investigation, with all information to be released by the Mexican government.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to avoid wake turbulence from a crossing heavy airplane.
summary: The pilot of an inbound aircraft encountered severe wake turbulence from a crossing Boeing C-17 after descending below its flightpath. This resulted in structural damage, including buckled wings, a shifted left wing, and a cracked spar, contrary to FAA guidance to stay above the preceding aircraft.

synopsis: The Air Accident Investigation Unit of Ireland notified the NTSB of an incident involving an Embraer 190-200 LR on October 16, 2017. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation as the State of Manufacturer and Design, with all information to be released by the AAIU.
summary: The Air Accident Investigation Unit of Ireland notified the NTSB of an incident involving an Embraer 190-200 LR on October 16, 2017. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation as the State of Manufacturer and Design, with all information to be released by the AAIU.

synopsis: The total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion.
summary: The pilot of a seaplane with long-range tanks experienced total engine power loss at 1,000 feet agl during a return flight, likely due to fuel exhaustion. The subsequent emergency landing resulted in tree impact, float separation, and substantial damage to the wings and fuselage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain the proper descent rate during landing. Contributing to the accident were the pilot's failure to conduct preflight performance calculations, which resulted in his operating the helicopter in high-density altitude conditions, and his lack of experience in high-altitude, mountainous flying.
summary: A helicopter pilot conducting an EMS flight in high-density altitude conditions attempted a landing at a ski resort without calculating performance limits. The pilot lost rotor speed during a go-around and subsequent approach, resulting in a hard landing, rotation over a barrier cable, and substantial damage to the fuselage and vertical stabilizer.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from trees during a visual approach for landing. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's distraction during the approach.
summary: A pilot approaching for a straight-in landing on runway 8R became distracted by runway assignment confusion with another aircraft. This distraction caused the pilot to lose situational awareness, descend below the proper approach path, and crash into trees while in a nose-low attitude.

synopsis: The Government of Mexico notified the NTSB of an incident involving an Airbus A330 on July 23, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by Mexico.
summary: The Government of Mexico notified the NTSB of an incident involving an Airbus A330 on July 23, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by Mexico.

synopsis: a passenger leaving a bag in the aisle that the flight attendant tripped over.
summary: A flight attendant on American Airlines flight 2308, an Airbus A321 at DFW, tripped over a bag and broke her ankle while the aircraft was at the gate with the main cabin door closed but before pushback. The injured crew member was unable to walk and was transported to an urgent care facility.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to land with insufficient runway remaining to stop, which resulted in a runway overrun.
summary: A commercial pilot flying a single-engine airplane after an annual inspection overran the runway during a full-stop landing. The pilot attributed the accident to landing too far down the runway, resulting in excessive speed that prevented stopping before the end.

synopsis: The pilot's attempt to move the helicopter from a sloped surface after an overspeed event, which resulted in a loss of helicopter control and impact with a car. The overspeed event resulted from misrouted and damaged wiring in the magneto, which subsequently resulted in errant and random signals to the governor.
summary: A commercial pilot experienced an engine and main-rotor overspeed during helicopter takeoff, causing a precautionary landing and subsequent uncontrollable rotation while attempting to reposition the aircraft. The incident, which damaged the tail rotor and vertical stabilizer, was caused by misrouted and damaged magneto wiring sending errant signals to the governor controller.

synopsis: Maintenance personnel's improper installation of the muffler attachment hardware, which resulted in the muffler separating in flight, thermal damage that interrupted the magnetos' function, and the subsequent total loss of engine power.
summary: A private pilot and flight instructor experienced engine power loss and fire indications during climb at 2,800 ft due to an improperly secured exhaust muffler. The crew deployed the parachute system to land in a parking lot, sustaining substantial wing spar damage from thermal damage that shorted the magnetos.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from a vehicle while taxiing for departure.
summary: The pilot reported that while taxiing for departure, the airplane's left wing struck a parked fuel truck on the ramp edge. The aircraft sustained substantial left wing damage, with no preaccident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to correctly identify the runway environment during an instrument approach at night in instrument meteorological conditions because he mistook building lights for runway lights, which resulted in landing short of the runway.
summary: During a night instrument approach in IMC, the pilot mistook building lights for runway lights and landed short in a soybean field, sustaining substantial left wing damage. After climbing briefly, he established visual contact and landed safely on the runway with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The total loss of engine power due to carburetor icing, which resulted from the pilot's failure to use carburetor heat while operating at low power settings in conditions conducive to the formation of carburetor ice.
summary: The pilot experienced engine power loss due to likely carburetor icing while descending in mountainous terrain. He executed an emergency landing on a ridge, resulting in substantial left wing damage after the left main gear separated.

aircraft: Airborne Windsports Pty Ltd Edge XT 912
synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in the weight-shift-controlled aircraft landing crooked on a turf runway.
summary: During landing on a turf runway, a weight-shift-controlled aircraft landed crookedly, causing the front wheel to dig in and the aircraft to roll onto its right side. The pilot reported no preaccident mechanical failures, resulting in substantial wing damage.

synopsis: Loss of engine power due to water in the fuel lines.
summary: A certified flight instructor and student experienced an engine power loss at 300 feet during a touch-and-go maneuver, likely caused by water in the left fuel tank. The instructor executed a gear-up forced landing to the runway after troubleshooting failed, with post-accident inspection confirming water in the fuel system and no mechanical engine issues.

synopsis: A Piper PA-28-181 (F-GKEC) lost engine power on approach to Lyon-Bron Airport, forcing a landing that caused substantial damage to the aircraft. The two occupants sustained no injuries, and the French BEA is investigating the accident.
summary: A Piper PA-28-181 (F-GKEC) lost engine power on approach to Lyon-Bron Airport, forcing a landing that caused substantial damage to the aircraft. The two occupants sustained no injuries, and the French BEA is investigating the accident.

synopsis: On August 12, 2018, a Cessna 172 (C-FJCP) impacted terrain near Edson, Alberta, under unknown circumstances, resulting in fatal injuries to the pilot. The Transportation Safety Board of Canada is investigating the accident with assistance from a U.S. accredited representative.
summary: On August 12, 2018, a Cessna 172 (C-FJCP) impacted terrain near Edson, Alberta, under unknown circumstances, resulting in fatal injuries to the pilot. The Transportation Safety Board of Canada is investigating the accident with assistance from a U.S. accredited representative.

synopsis: A Piper PA-28-161 departed a cut hay field near Black Diamond, Alberta, and collided with hay bales under unknown circumstances. One occupant sustained fatal injuries and the other serious injuries, prompting an investigation by the Transportation Safety Board of Canada.
summary: A Piper PA-28-161 departed a cut hay field near Black Diamond, Alberta, and collided with hay bales under unknown circumstances. One occupant sustained fatal injuries and the other serious injuries, prompting an investigation by the Transportation Safety Board of Canada.

synopsis: A Piper PA-34-200T departed controlled flight and impacted terrain shortly after takeoff from Calgary Springbank Airport, killing the flight instructor and student pilot. The Transportation Safety Board of Canada is investigating the accident with assistance from the NTSB.
summary: A Piper PA-34-200T departed controlled flight and impacted terrain shortly after takeoff from Calgary Springbank Airport, killing the flight instructor and student pilot. The Transportation Safety Board of Canada is investigating the accident with assistance from the NTSB.

synopsis: A Cessna U206G amphibious float-equipped airplane nosed over while landing at Little Doctor Lake, resulting in three fatal and two minor injuries. The Transportation Safety Board of Canada is investigating the accident with assistance from a U.S. accredited representative.
summary: A Cessna U206G amphibious float-equipped airplane nosed over while landing at Little Doctor Lake, resulting in three fatal and two minor injuries. The Transportation Safety Board of Canada is investigating the accident with assistance from a U.S. accredited representative.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll in tailwind and crosswind conditions. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's fatigue.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane lost directional control and ground looped right during landing on runway 35, causing left wing impact and substantial damage. The pilot attributed the accident to fatigue and accepting a crosswind runway instead of requesting runway 13, reporting no mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's improper retraction of the flaps during a go-around, which resulted in the airplane's failure to climb and its subsequent collision with trees.
summary: A noninstructor-rated pilot acting as PIC in the right seat of a student's airplane impacted trees during a go-around after retracting flaps fully in one motion. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the wings, fuselage, and empennage, with the pilot attributing the accident to improper flap retraction rather than mechanical failure.

aircraft: Raymon A. King SUPER CUB REPLICA
synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the takeoff roll with crosswind conditions.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane reported that during a lake takeoff roll at 25 knots, a right crosswind gust pushed the aircraft into the water, causing it to spin and nose over. The pilot attributed the substantial damage to the right wing and rudder to the gusts, noting no mechanical failures.

synopsis: A Robinson R-44-II helicopter, RA-05758, impacted water and sank near Bodaybo, Russia, before colliding with a power transmission line. The pilot and passenger sustained fatal injuries, and the Interstate Aviation Committee of Russia is investigating the accident.
summary: A Robinson R-44-II helicopter, RA-05758, impacted water and sank near Bodaybo, Russia, before colliding with a power transmission line. The pilot and passenger sustained fatal injuries, and the Interstate Aviation Committee of Russia is investigating the accident.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during takeoff in gusting crosswind conditions.
summary: During takeoff in a crosswind on runway 31, the pilot lost directional control as the tailwheel lifted, causing the aircraft to veer left and depart the runway despite rudder and brake inputs. The airplane skidded on gravel and sustained substantial damage to the fuselage and horizontal stabilizer with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: A Cessna 208B, VH-FAY, disappeared from radar during cruise flight over international waters while en route from Saipan to Sapporo. The pilot was fatally injured, and wreckage was recovered from the ocean, with the investigation conducted by the Australian Transport Safety Bureau.
summary: A Cessna 208B, VH-FAY, disappeared from radar during cruise flight over international waters while en route from Saipan to Sapporo. The pilot was fatally injured, and wreckage was recovered from the ocean, with the investigation conducted by the Australian Transport Safety Bureau.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from an obstacle during takeoff.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane struck a concrete column during takeoff from an off-airport site while turning to avoid trees. The pilot attributed the accident to insufficient room for obstacle clearance, noting no mechanical failures and substantial damage to the right wing and fuselage.

synopsis: The pilot's improper decision to attempt a gear-up glide to the runway and his subsequent failure to extend the landing gear before landing. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's failure to use a checklist before landing.
