synopsis: Pilot incapacitation due to carbon monoxide poisoning as a result of an undetected crack in an engine exhaust muffler, which permitted entry of exhaust gasses into the cabin via the cabin heat system.
summary: A student pilot and three others died when their aircraft collided with terrain after the crew suffered carbon monoxide poisoning from a cracked exhaust muffler. The corrosion-induced crack allowed exhaust gases into the cabin heating system, causing confusion and loss of control despite the pilot's reported heart attack.

synopsis: The pilot's improper fuel management, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel starvation during the initial climb. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's decision to initiate a 180° turn following the loss of power.
summary: The pilot experienced total engine power loss during initial climb due to fuel starvation after operating on an empty right tank. The aircraft impacted the ground left of the runway with substantial damage after the pilot attempted a turn instead of landing straight ahead.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to attain adequate airspeed before attempting the takeoff with a tailwind, which resulted in the airplane being unable to sustain flight.
summary: A private pilot with three passengers attempted a takeoff from a 2,600-ft turf runway with an 8-knot tailwind. The aircraft failed to sustain flight due to inadequate airspeed, entered pitch oscillations, and crashed into treetops before cartwheeling.

synopsis: The GPIA of Portugal notified the NTSB of an incident involving an Embraer 190 on November 11, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the GPIA.
summary: The GPIA of Portugal notified the NTSB of an incident involving an Embraer 190 on November 11, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the GPIA.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control during landing, which resulted in impact with a snow pile and necessitated a go-around, during which the airplane impacted trees.
summary: During landing on a snow-plowed runway, the pilot reported the airplane slipped sideways, struck a snow pile, and turned left. After initiating a go-around, the aircraft impacted trees, sustaining substantial left wing damage with no preaccident mechanical failures.

synopsis: An encounter with low-level windshear and turbulence during the landing approach, which resulted in a loss of airplane control.
summary: The pilot encountered heavy turbulence and low-level wind shear while approaching an airport in instrument meteorological conditions. Despite adding full power, the aircraft descended rapidly and collided with the Atlantic Ocean, resulting in a loss of control and fuselage separation.

synopsis: The Government of Bahamas notified the NTSB of a November 08, 2018, accident involving a Piper PA23. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the Bahamas.
summary: The Government of Bahamas notified the NTSB of a November 08, 2018, accident involving a Piper PA23. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the Bahamas.

synopsis: The pilot receiving instruction's failure to maintain directional control during landing.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot experienced a runway excursion during landing on Runway 19 when the aircraft veered left despite corrective inputs. The plane exited the runway, impacted a ditch, and inverted with substantial left wing damage, though no mechanical failures were reported.

synopsis: The Guyana Civil Aviation Authority notified the NTSB of a Boeing 757 accident on November 9, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the GCAA investigation, with all information to be released by the GCAA.
summary: The Guyana Civil Aviation Authority notified the NTSB of a Boeing 757 accident on November 9, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the GCAA investigation, with all information to be released by the GCAA.

synopsis: The partial loss of engine power for reasons that could not be determined based on the available information.
summary: During the maiden flight takeoff, the pilot and passenger experienced partial engine power loss and landed in a rock-covered field. A postimpact fire consumed the aircraft, but the cause of the power loss remained undetermined due to fire damage preventing propeller control unit testing.

synopsis: The passenger's improper decision to hold her cell phone outside the helicopter, which resulted in it departing the helicopter and striking the tail rotor.
summary: During a helicopter tour flight at 100 knots, a passenger held a cell phone outside the cabin, causing it to strike the tail rotor. The incident resulted in substantial damage to the tail rotor, with the pilot reporting no pre-existing mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot under instruction's failure to maintain directional control and the flight instructor's delayed remedial action.
summary: A flight instructor and student in a skid-equipped helicopter conducted a transition flight when the student performed a touchdown autorotation. The helicopter slid off the runway, rolled onto its left side, and sustained substantial damage to the rotor drive systems, with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing in a crosswind. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's lack of experience in tailwheel airplanes for which he did not have an endorsement.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane exited the left side of runway 17 during a crosswind approach, sustaining substantial left wing damage after the aircraft fishtailed and impacted a lava field. The pilot attributed the accident to his lack of tailwheel endorsement and only three hours of experience in such aircraft.

synopsis: The student pilot's loss of control at low altitude during a forced landing, which resulted in impact with terrain and substantial damage to the right wing. A contributing factor in the accident was the loss of engine power for undetermined reasons.
summary: A student pilot experienced two engine power losses due to fuel exhaustion while flying a single-engine airplane. The first forced landing was successful, but a subsequent takeoff resulted in a stall and wing damage after the engine lost total power, though the investigation could not determine the cause due to conflicting fuel reports.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to attain a sufficient climb rate during initial climb in high-density altitude conditions with the airplane near its forward center of gravity and maximum gross weight limits, which resulted in an impact with trees.
summary: During an uphill takeoff from a high-density altitude airport, the pilot rotated early and repeatedly pitched up until the stall warning sounded, resulting in a tree strike and terrain impact. The pilot reported no mechanical failures, noting the aircraft was near its forward center of gravity limit with substantial right wing damage.

synopsis: The pilot's spatial disorientation and subsequent loss of control after takeoff in dark night instrument meteorological conditions.
summary: The pilot, lacking a current instrument proficiency check, departed at night under IFR and drifted left before turning right and descending from 500 feet. Spatial disorientation in dark, hazy conditions likely caused a loss of control and terrain impact.

synopsis: The Dominican Republic notified the NTSB of a November 14, 2018, accident involving a Piper PA25. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the Dominican Republic's investigation, with all information to be released by the Dominican government.
summary: The Dominican Republic notified the NTSB of a November 14, 2018, accident involving a Piper PA25. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the Dominican Republic's investigation, with all information to be released by the Dominican government.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to monitor the airport's visual approach path indicator during the final approach to the upsloping runway, which resulted in a low approach path and impact with terrain.
summary: The pilot and a pilot-rated passenger crashed a multileg flight aircraft into trees and a house during final approach due to flying below the glideslope and exceeding stall speed. The accident likely resulted from a visual illusion caused by the upsloping runway and failure to monitor the visual approach path indicator, with no mechanical failures found.

synopsis: The Chilean government notified the NTSB of an October 24, 2018, accident involving a GARLICK UH1D helicopter. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist Chile's investigation, with all information to be released by Chile.
summary: The Chilean government notified the NTSB of an October 24, 2018, accident involving a GARLICK UH1D helicopter. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist Chile's investigation, with all information to be released by Chile.

synopsis: The pilot's improper decision to conduct a low-level flight over a river, and his failure to see and avoid power lines, which resulted in the helicopter's impact with power lines and the water.
summary: A pilot repositioning a helicopter with a passenger for maintenance struck power lines while flying low over a river, causing the aircraft to descend into the water. Post-accident examination found no mechanical failures, suggesting the pilot failed to see the lines.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to perform a low-level maneuver at an altitude where he was unable to recover the airplane before impacting terrain.
summary: A commercial pilot flying a warbird with a passenger during a WWII reenactment performed a low pass and steep descent below the briefed 1,000 ft minimum. The pilot failed to recover from the maneuver, resulting in a near-vertical impact with terrain.

synopsis: The pilots' failure to execute a go-around when the nighttime autopilot-coupled approach became unstable, which resulted in a loss of control and subsequent impact with terrain. Also causal was the flight instructor's inadequate supervision of the pilot and his failure to perform remedial action. Contributing to the accident was the inadvertent application of pressure to the pitch control while the autopilot was engaged, which caused an out-of-trim condition that was not identified by either pilot and resulted in control difficulty when the autopilot was disengaged.
summary: A pilot/owner and flight instructor crashed a single-engine airplane short of the runway during a night GPS approach after the autopilot trimmed full nose-down to counteract pilot control pressure. The resulting nose-down tendency and subsequent flap retraction caused an excessive descent rate, leading to impact with trees and a localizer antenna.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: The pilot reported a hard landing on runway 36R after feeling an issue with the nosewheel tire upon initial touchdown, causing the aircraft to briefly lift off before impacting again. This sequence resulted in substantial fuselage damage, though the pilot taxied to the ramp without further incident.

synopsis: A partial loss of engine power during initial climb for undetermined reasons, and pilot's failure to maintain airspeed during a turn back to the runway, which resulted in an exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack, and subsequent aerodynamic stall.
summary: A flight instructor and student departed in a light sport airplane after a prior vapor lock incident. The aircraft entered a stall during a left turn back to the airport following an unexplained engine power loss, resulting in a ground impact.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed with a tailwind, which resulted in the helicopter settling with power, and his subsequent incorrect collective application while attempting to recover, which resulted in a loss of helicopter control due to a loss of tail rotor effectiveness.
summary: A helicopter pilot conducting a photography flight at 70 feet experienced a settling with power condition in a 10-knot tailwind. Despite increasing collective and applying forward cyclic, the helicopter impacted the ground hard, sustaining substantial damage to the main rotor and fuselage with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's improper preflight fuel planning, which resulted in fuel exhaustion and a total loss of engine power.
summary: The pilot departed despite a NOTAM indicating no fuel availability, resulting in engine power loss and an off-airport field landing. The aircraft overran the landing area, struck a drainage culvert, and nosed over, sustaining substantial damage to the fuselage and windscreen.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in landing on the landing gear first and a subsequent loss of directional control, a runway excursion, and impact with a tree and a fence during an attempted go-around.
summary: During initial approach in haze, the pilot executed a go-around and landed on the opposite runway, touching down on the nose gear first. The aircraft veered off the runway, struck a tree and fence during a second go-around attempt, sustaining substantial left wing damage with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's improper decision to fly in an area where moderate icing conditions were forecasted in an airplane that was not certified for such conditions, and in the effort to get out of the icing conditions, his decision to fly below the minimum descent altitude for the localizer approach to the diversion airport resulting in the airplane impacting a power line and terrain. Contributing was the pilot's inadequate preflight planning.
summary: The pilot of a non-ice-certified aircraft encountered moderate rime ice, causing an uncontrolled descent due to an inoperable deice system. While attempting to avoid re-entering icing conditions, the pilot descended below minimums and impacted a power line near the diversion airport.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain airplane control during takeoff and the flight instructor's delayed remedial action, which resulted in an off-runway landing and subsequent collision with trees.
summary: A student pilot and flight instructor experienced an uncommanded left bank and control unresponsiveness during takeoff from a turf runway. The instructor landed straight ahead to avoid trees but struck them, causing substantial damage, likely due to the student's loss of control and delayed remedial action.

synopsis: An inflight failure of the airplane's horizontal stabilizer.
summary: During cruise, a pilot responded to a traffic alert with control inputs that caused a spin and subsequent high-speed descent. The horizontal stabilizer separated, likely due to structural failure from improper material layup or excessive forces, before the pilot deployed the ballistic parachute for a safe landing.

synopsis: The seizure of two bearings in the reduction gearbox, resulting in the total loss of engine power. Contributing to the accident was a high descent rate which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: A commercial pilot testing an experimental diesel engine reduction gearbox experienced total power loss above 500 feet due to seized propeller shaft bearings. The subsequent hard landing caused the left main landing gear axle to separate and damaged the left wing lift strut.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane in dark night conditions that resulted in an in-flight positive overload failure of the wings and the subsequent in-flight breakup of the airplane.
summary: The pilot and two medical crewmembers were repositioning an aeromedical aircraft in dark night IMC when it entered an unintended descending turn. The pilot likely initiated a pull-up maneuver to recover from a spiral dive, causing positive overload that fractured the wing spars and led to in-flight breakup.

synopsis: The pilot's delay in applying carburetor heat, which resulted in a total loss of engine power during descent due to carburetor icing.
summary: A sport pilot flying a personal cross-country flight experienced total engine power loss during descent due to carburetor icing. The pilot applied carburetor heat too late, resulting in a forced landing where the aircraft struck a fence and came to rest inverted.

synopsis: A loss of control during the landing roll and subsequent runway excursion for reasons that could not be determined based on the available evidence.
summary: A private pilot lost directional control during landing, causing the aircraft to veer left, depart the runway, and collapse the nose gear after impacting a berm. The pilot applied rudder, brakes, and beta power but could not maintain the runway, and the investigation could not determine the cause of the excursion.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to see and avoid the airplane on the runway while landing and the pilot receiving instruction's and flight instructor's failure to properly scan the approach before pulling onto the runway during takeoff. The pilot's failure to see and avoid the airplane on the runway while landing and the pilot receiving instruction's and flight instructor's failure to properly scan the approach before pulling onto the runway during the takeoff.
summary: A low-wing airplane on final approach collided with a high-wing airplane beginning a takeoff roll at a nontowered airport. The accident resulted from a failure to see or hear each other on the CTAF despite both crews reporting their positions, causing substantial damage to both aircraft.

synopsis: The CAA of Colombia notified the NTSB of an incident involving a HAIC Harbin Y12E on August 26, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the CAA investigation, with all information to be released by the CAA.
summary: The CAA of Colombia notified the NTSB of an incident involving a HAIC Harbin Y12E on August 26, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the CAA investigation, with all information to be released by the CAA.

synopsis: Impact with a lake for undetermined reasons.
summary: During a pleasure flight at 700 feet, the pilot experienced engine shaking and total power loss, forcing a lake landing after a failed restart attempt. The submerged aircraft was recovered three weeks later, but an initial engine examination could not determine the cause of the power loss.

synopsis: The mechanic's failure to properly secure the air reference line, which resulted in a loss of engine power.
summary: During a ferry flight climb, a pilot experienced an engine surge and deployed the ballistic parachute at 3,500 feet, resulting in an off-airport landing with substantial fuselage damage. An FAA inspector determined the cause was likely a mechanic's failure to properly secure air reference lines during recent cylinder replacement, leading to engine power loss.

synopsis: The student pilot's improper decision to taxi past another airplane occupying the taxiway and her subsequent failure to maintain clearance from the airplane. The other pilot's improper decision to taxi past another airplane occupying a taxiway and her subsequent failure to maintain clearance from the airplane.
summary: A student pilot in a low-wing airplane collided with a flight instructor's high-wing airplane on a taxiway after landing. While attempting to pass on the left, the student's right wing struck the other aircraft's lift strut, causing a 180° turn and substantial damage to both wings.

synopsis: The pilot's overcorrection during the landing, which resulted in a loss of directional control.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane overcorrected during landing when the right wing lifted, causing the aircraft to veer off the runway. The left main gear collapsed in the dirt, resulting in substantial damage to the left wing with no preaccident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of consciousness while taxiing due to an accumulation of toxic levels of carbon dioxide gas inside the airplane as a result of dry ice sublimation. Also causal was the pilot's decision to fly the airplane in an unventilated configuration, the operator's policy that allowed this configuration, and the shipping company's inadvertent loading of excess dry ice, which exacerbated the concentration of carbon dioxide.
summary: A pilot became unconscious while taxiing a cargo aircraft due to carbon dioxide poisoning from sublimating dry ice in an unventilated cabin. The incident resulted from the shipper underreporting dry ice quantities and the pilot operating with closed vents despite available safety advisories.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in an abnormal landing and subsequent porpoise.
summary: During the landing flare, the pilot reported the aircraft ballooned and porpoised, causing the nosewheel to collapse and the airplane to rest nose down with substantial engine mount damage. The pilot stated no preimpact mechanical failures occurred.

synopsis: The student pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a bounced landing.
summary: During a night landing, a student pilot relaxed back pressure, causing the nose gear to strike the runway and the aircraft to bounce. Although the instructor recovered the flight and completed two more landings, a subsequent inspection revealed substantial fuselage damage with no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The French government notified the NTSB of an April 5, 2018, accident involving an amateur-built ROTORWAY EXEC helicopter. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist France's investigation, with all information to be released by the French government.
summary: The French government notified the NTSB of an April 5, 2018, accident involving an amateur-built ROTORWAY EXEC helicopter. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist France's investigation, with all information to be released by the French government.

synopsis: Collision with terrain for reasons that could not be determined based on the available information. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's poor preflight planning and poor decision to depart on the accident flight.
summary: A private pilot flying a cross-country night VFR flight became lost and impacted terrain near an airport while circling with gear and flaps retracted. The aircraft was destroyed by impact and fire, likely due to spatial disorientation and fuel exhaustion, though the exact cause of the impact could not be determined.

synopsis: The AAIC of Thailand notified the NTSB of an incident involving a Boeing 737 on October 19, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the AAIC.
summary: The AAIC of Thailand notified the NTSB of an incident involving a Boeing 737 on October 19, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the AAIC.

synopsis: The failure of the right brake while taxiing after landing, which resulted in a loss of directional control and collision with a parked airplane.
summary: The pilot lost directional control while taxiing after landing due to a wind gust and a failed right brake caused by a leaking O-ring. The aircraft subsequently struck a parked airplane on the ramp after the pilot cut the engine to stop the exaggerated turn.

synopsis: The pilot's inadvertent retraction of the landing gear during landing rollout, resulting in a landing gear collapse.
summary: The pilot inadvertently retracted the landing gear instead of flaps during a high-speed rollout after bouncing on landing, causing the nose and right main gear to collapse. The accident occurred because the squat switch failed to prevent retraction due to insufficient weight on the right main gear.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare with a gusting, right quartering headwind, which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: During a night landing, the pilot flared too high, causing a hard landing and runway excursion. The pilot maneuvered the aircraft back onto the runway, but the left-wing rib sustained substantial damage with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The Dominican Republic notified the NTSB of a November 22, 2018, accident involving a Eurocopter EC120 helicopter. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the Dominican Republic.
summary: The Dominican Republic notified the NTSB of a November 22, 2018, accident involving a Eurocopter EC120 helicopter. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the Dominican Republic.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll in gusting tailwind conditions.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane encountered variable crosswind gusts during landing on runway 25, causing the aircraft to weather-vane left, exit the runway into mud, and nose over. The pilot reported no mechanical failures, attributing the substantial rudder damage to the gusts despite reported winds of 5 to 8 knots.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during takeoff from an unimproved dirt road.
summary: During takeoff from an unimproved dirt road, the pilot reported the gyroplane's tires dug in, causing a left veer that led to an overcorrection and a left-side rollover. The incident resulted in substantial damage to the tailboom and mast, with no preaccident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The AIG of Bolivia notified the NTSB of a Boeing 737 accident on November 22, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the AIG of Bolivia.
summary: The AIG of Bolivia notified the NTSB of a Boeing 737 accident on November 22, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the AIG of Bolivia.

synopsis: On November 24, 2018, a Robinson R22 BETA helicopter collided with terrain near Alice Springs, Australia, sustaining substantial damage. The pilot suffered serious injuries while the passenger was fatally injured.
summary: On November 24, 2018, a Robinson R22 BETA helicopter collided with terrain near Alice Springs, Australia, sustaining substantial damage. The pilot suffered serious injuries while the passenger was fatally injured.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing with a crosswind, which resulted in a runway excursion and subsequent ground-loop.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane ground looped and exited runway 27 after the left wing abruptly rose during a three-point landing. The pilot reported no mechanical failures, attributing the substantial damage to the right wing and tail cone to the loss of directional control despite corrective inputs.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to see and avoid a power line during an agricultural application flight.
summary: During an agricultural spray flight, the pilot struck a power line at 20 feet, causing engine failure and a forced landing. The aircraft hit a tree and rotated 180 degrees, sustaining substantial damage to the left wing and fuselage with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to remove the gust lock before flight, which resulted in the airplane's inability to rotate and a subsequent runway overrun. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's failure to follow the preflight checklist.
summary: The pilot, rushing before takeoff at near maximum gross weight, failed to remove the control lock from the yoke. This prevented rotation, causing the airplane to overrun the runway, impact water, invert, and sustain substantial damage to the fuselage and empennage.

synopsis: The student pilot's exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack during a go-around, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall, and the flight instructor's delayed remedial action.
summary: During a student's touch-and-go training on Runway 34, the flight instructor reported the student aggressively pitched up after a go-around instruction, causing a stall and left drift that resulted in a crash with substantial damage to the fuselage and left wing. The instructor attributed the accident to the student's actions, noting no mechanical failures and gusty winds from 290° at 9 to 15 knots.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to follow the air traffic controller's instructions and his subsequent failure to maintain adequate lookout to see and avoid the other airplane on the taxiway. The other pilot's failure to follow the air traffic controller's instructions and his subsequent failure to maintain adequate lookout to see and avoid the other airplane on the taxiway.
summary: The Pilatus pilot, while taxiing onto a runway after an IFR clearance, struck a Cessna's left wing with his propeller despite ATC instructions to yield. The collision caused substantial damage to both aircraft, with video evidence showing the Pilatus failed to stop before entering the taxiway.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain a proper glidepath during the approach, which resulted in impact with a fence and terrain.
summary: A solo student pilot on a night final approach initiated a go-around after realizing the aircraft was low at 87 knots with 20º flaps. The right main gear struck a fence and the airplane impacted terrain, sustaining substantial left wing damage with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The total loss of engine power due to the interruption of oil circulation for reasons that could not be determined based on the available evidence.
summary: During descent, the pilot experienced engine jolts, sparks, and total power loss due to a seized turbocharger and connecting rod failure causing oil circulation interruption. The pilot deployed the whole-airframe parachute, but the aircraft impacted trees and terrain with substantial damage.

synopsis: The pilot's improper decision to fly with an air cast boot on his foot, which led him to rely on the passenger to apply brakes and rudder, which was performed improperly and led to a loss of directional control.
summary: A pilot wearing an air cast boot requested a passenger to apply brakes during landing, but insufficient differential braking caused the aircraft to veer and exit the runway into a ditch. The pilot attributed the accident to his inability to fully apply brake pressure due to the boot, resulting in substantial right wing damage with no mechanical failures.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power for reasons that could not be determined based on the available evidence.
summary: A student pilot flying a single-engine aircraft lost engine power at 30 feet after departure, impacting trees and destroying the airplane in a post-crash fire. Although water was found in the fuel system earlier that day, the specific cause of the power loss could not be determined because the wreckage was not recovered.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control while landing in crosswind conditions.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane drifted left after landing on runway 29 in 8-knot crosswinds, exiting the runway and striking a sign. The aircraft sustained substantial fuselage and empennage damage, with the pilot reporting no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack following a loss of the left engine power shortly after takeoff, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall at an altitude too low for recovery. Contributing to the accident was the loss of left engine power due most likely to a fuel system issue that could not be determined based on the available evidence.
summary: An airline transport pilot conducting a personal test flight in a twin-engine airplane lost control after likely suffering left engine power loss due to a degraded fuel system. The aircraft entered a downward spiral and impacted terrain after the pilot exceeded the critical angle of attack during single-engine operation.

synopsis: The student pilot's improper decision to maneuver the airplane through an area of construction and his subsequent failure to maintain clearance from a concrete pole barrier while taxiing.
summary: A solo student pilot taxiing toward the fuel farm struck a concrete pole barrier with the right wing while maneuvering through a construction zone. The incident caused substantial damage to the wing and baggage door floorboards, with no preaccident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The Brazilian government notified the NTSB of a Boeing 737 accident on November 28, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist Brazil's investigation, with all information to be released by Brazil.
summary: The Brazilian government notified the NTSB of a Boeing 737 accident on November 28, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist Brazil's investigation, with all information to be released by Brazil.

synopsis: The pilot's controlled flight into terrain as a result of his spatial disorientation during departure in dark nighttime conditions.
summary: A private pilot departed a cross-country flight at civil twilight and crashed into a marsh two miles north of the airport. The investigation attributed the controlled flight into terrain to spatial disorientation caused by a lack of visual cues, with potential cognitive impairment from antidepressant use remaining undetermined.

synopsis: A Cessna U206D operated by Bushflying Air Safaris impacted terrain near Machadodorp, South Africa, seriously injuring the pilot and four passengers while substantially damaging the aircraft. The South African Civil Aviation Authority is investigating the accident with assistance from an NTSB representative.
summary: A Cessna U206D operated by Bushflying Air Safaris impacted terrain near Machadodorp, South Africa, seriously injuring the pilot and four passengers while substantially damaging the aircraft. The South African Civil Aviation Authority is investigating the accident with assistance from an NTSB representative.

synopsis: The pilot's inability to regain airplane control after a left roll that began for reasons that could not be determined based on the available evidence.
summary: A pilot flying a Tamarack ATLAS-equipped aircraft in IMC experienced an uncommanded left roll and autopilot disconnect at 3,000 feet, leading to an emergency descent and crash. The probable cause involved asymmetric deflection of the Active Camber Surfaces, which lacked centering strips to return to a neutral position during system faults.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to lower the flaps during the approach and maintain sufficient airspeed while flying in instrument meteorological and icing conditions and the accumulation of ice on the wings' leading edges, which resulted in the exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack and subsequent aerodynamic stall. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's lack of proper qualification to operate the airplane under a single-pilot exemption due to his lack of total turbine time, which led to task saturation and his failure to properly configure the flaps for landing.
summary: A single-pilot commercial flight carrying 10 passengers in an 8-passenger aircraft stalled during an ILS approach in icing conditions. The accident resulted from the pilot's lack of required turbine experience, failure to lower flaps, and ice accumulation causing an aerodynamic stall and runway excursion.

synopsis: The Brazilian government notified the NTSB of a Cessna 525 accident on November 26, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist Brazil's investigation, with all information to be released by Brazil.
summary: The Brazilian government notified the NTSB of a Cessna 525 accident on November 26, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist Brazil's investigation, with all information to be released by Brazil.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to perform a touch-and-go landing at a high-density altitude airport, with a tailwind, and on an upsloping runway, which resulted in decreased airplane performance and the airplane's inability to become airborne within the available runway.
summary: During a touch-and-go landing in high density altitude with a tailwind and upslope, the pilot attempted takeoff but the aircraft failed to accelerate and stalled. The airplane settled off the runway, nosed over, and came to rest inverted with substantial damage due to insufficient remaining runway distance.

synopsis: The pilot's improper decision to fly the unairworthy airplane and his failure to feather the left propeller following a partial loss of power from the left engine after takeoff. Also causal was the partial loss of power to the left engine due to detonation.
summary: The pilot and passenger attempted to reposition an unairworthy aircraft that suffered left engine failure and smoke shortly after takeoff. The pilot's failure to feather the left propeller caused a loss of climb performance, resulting in a collision with buildings and a post-impact fire.

synopsis: Ethiopian Airlines Boeing 767-300 experienced a right engine fan blade failure during takeoff from Addis Ababa. The aircraft returned for an uneventful landing with no injuries, revealing two fractured blades and minor fuselage damage.
summary: Ethiopian Airlines Boeing 767-300 experienced a right engine fan blade failure during takeoff from Addis Ababa. The aircraft returned for an uneventful landing with no injuries, revealing two fractured blades and minor fuselage damage.

synopsis: The airplane's collision with a bird during a practice instrument approach.
summary: A student pilot reported a bird strike on the left wing while inbound on a practice ILS approach one mile from the runway. The aircraft sustained substantial damage but landed safely with no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power for undetermined reasons.
summary: The pilot reported an abrupt engine power loss at 2,500 feet MSL, forcing a landing on an abandoned runway where the aircraft exited and impacted vegetation. Post-accident examination found no mechanical anomalies, and the cause of the power loss remained undetermined.

synopsis: On October 4, 2018, the pilot of an Air Tractor AT-401B (5N-BTV) executed a forced landing near Rukubi, Nigeria, following a loss of engine power. The pilot sustained minor injuries and the airplane was substantially damaged.
summary: On October 4, 2018, the pilot of an Air Tractor AT-401B (5N-BTV) executed a forced landing near Rukubi, Nigeria, following a loss of engine power. The pilot sustained minor injuries and the airplane was substantially damaged.

synopsis: The Government of Mexico notified the NTSB of a November 08, 2018, accident involving a Piper PA25. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist Mexico's investigation, with all information to be released by the Mexican government.
summary: The Government of Mexico notified the NTSB of a November 08, 2018, accident involving a Piper PA25. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist Mexico's investigation, with all information to be released by the Mexican government.

synopsis: The student pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a hard, bounced landing and nose landing gear collapse.
summary: A solo student pilot reported that after a hard bounce following touchdown, the nose landing gear collapsed and the left wing struck the grass, causing substantial damage. The pilot stated there were no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: the captain initiating a cross bleed start while under tow.
summary: PSA Airlines flight 5544, a CRJ200, struck a tug during engine start at LaGuardia while under tow. The captain initiated a cross-bleed start with the parking brake released, causing lateral thrust that jackknifed the tug and damaged the aircraft's right side.

synopsis: A partial loss of engine power for reasons that could not be determined based on the available information.
summary: During a practice landing pattern, the pilot experienced engine sputtering and struck an airport fence with the propeller and landing gear, causing substantial damage. The investigation found the fuel selector ring between detents, but the exact fuel distribution and cause of power loss could not be determined.

synopsis: On November 28, 2018, a Bell 407 GX helicopter executed a precautionary landing near West Bangkala, Indonesia, after an engine chip detector caution light illuminated. The pilot and passenger were uninjured, but the helicopter sustained substantial damage, prompting an investigation by the National Transportation Safety Committee.
summary: On November 28, 2018, a Bell 407 GX helicopter executed a precautionary landing near West Bangkala, Indonesia, after an engine chip detector caution light illuminated. The pilot and passenger were uninjured, but the helicopter sustained substantial damage, prompting an investigation by the National Transportation Safety Committee.

synopsis: The flight instructor's failure to maintain the runway heading during an attempted takeoff in gusting crosswind conditions, which resulted in a collision with trees.
summary: During a student touch-and-go in crosswinds, the flight instructor took control after the aircraft veered left but failed to retract partial flaps. The airplane exited the runway left, struck trees, and crashed into a ravine with substantial right wing damage, with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: (1) The flight crewmembers' decision, due to plan continuation bias, to continue the approach despite indications of windshear and a higher-than-expected tailwind and (2) the flight crew's misperception of the airplane's touchdown point, which was farther down the runway than the crew assumed because of the faster-than-expected groundspeed. Contributing to the accident was Southwest Airlines' lack of guidance to prompt flight crews to reassess operator-provided landing data when arrival weather conditions differ from those used in the original landing data calculation.
summary: Southwest Airlines flight 278 overran runway 8 at Burbank due to a late touchdown, excessive tailwind, and high approach speed that invalidated the calculated stopping margin. The crew failed to go around despite adverse weather reports and manual braking issues, resulting in the aircraft stopping in an arresting system.

synopsis: The airplane's encounter with severe turbulence.
summary: Spirit Airlines flight 1069, an Airbus A320, encountered moderate turbulence at FL230 during descent into Las Vegas. A flight attendant preparing the cabin was thrown to the floor and sustained a fractured left fibula, while the aircraft remained undamaged.

synopsis: an object which fell from an overhead bin struck a flight attendant resulting in a serious injury.
summary: During taxi at Chicago O'Hare, a flight attendant on American Airlines flight 114 was injured when a laptop fell from an overhead bin after she opened it. The object struck her eye, displacing it, causing the flight to return to the gate and the attendant to be hospitalized.

synopsis: The airplane's encounter with severe turbulence.
summary: Delta Air Lines flight 278, a Boeing 767-300ER, encountered severe turbulence at FL350 while avoiding weather near SUNNS intersection. Three flight attendants were injured during meal service after the aircraft suddenly hit turbulence despite radar showing only green returns, causing a momentary EICAS overspeed message.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in hard, bounced landing, runway excursion, and impact with a hangar.
summary: The pilot reported an unexpected descent at 15 feet during landing, causing a hard nosewheel touchdown and porpoising. Despite applying full power, the aircraft veered left, exited the runway, and struck a hangar, sustaining substantial right wing damage with no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The New Zealand government notified the NTSB of an accident involving an Aerospatiale AS350 helicopter on November 06, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by New Zealand.
summary: The New Zealand government notified the NTSB of an accident involving an Aerospatiale AS350 helicopter on November 06, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by New Zealand.

synopsis: The student pilot's improper landing flare and subsequent failure to maintain directional control during landing.
summary: A solo student pilot flying a tailwheel airplane ground looped right and exited the runway during final approach after a forward slip caused a bounce. The right main gear struck a guard rail, damaging the right wing lift strut, with no preaccident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: Maintenance personnel's improper assembly of the engine during overhaul, which resulted in lubrication restriction due to a bearing shift and the subsequent engine failure.
summary: During cruise, a pilot experienced engine failure after an explosion and performed a forced landing that collapsed the landing gear. Post-accident investigation attributed the failure to silk thread applied during a prior overhaul, which caused bolt torque loss, bearing shift, and oil starvation.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power due to fuel starvation.
summary: The pilot flew a low-fuel aircraft to a nearby airport, where abrupt turns during the landing approach uncovered fuel tank outlets. This caused fuel starvation, total engine power loss, and a terrain impact short of the runway.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of airplane control during the engine start.
summary: During initial engine start, the pilot reported the engine surged to full RPM after throttle pumping, causing the airplane to overrun the runway despite full brake application. The aircraft struck two lamp posts and sustained substantial damage to the wings, fuselage, and empennage, with no preaccident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: A Mexican-registered Cessna T206H suffered engine power loss near Tampico, forcing a landing on a highway where it struck a motorcycle. The pilot and passenger were uninjured, but the collision caused fatal injuries to the two motorcycle occupants.
summary: A Mexican-registered Cessna T206H suffered engine power loss near Tampico, forcing a landing on a highway where it struck a motorcycle. The pilot and passenger were uninjured, but the collision caused fatal injuries to the two motorcycle occupants.

synopsis: On December 7, 2018, the sole pilot of a Pilatus Britten-Norman BN2A-20, VH-OBL, was fatally injured when the aircraft collided with terrain near Hobart Aerodrome. The aircraft was destroyed, and the investigation remains under the jurisdiction of the Australian Transport Safety Bureau.
summary: On December 7, 2018, the sole pilot of a Pilatus Britten-Norman BN2A-20, VH-OBL, was fatally injured when the aircraft collided with terrain near Hobart Aerodrome. The aircraft was destroyed, and the investigation remains under the jurisdiction of the Australian Transport Safety Bureau.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power and catastrophic engine failure due to the failure of the left turbocharger, which resulted in oil loss and oil starvation. Contributing to the accident was the failure of maintenance personnel to overhaul the turbocharger in accordance with manufacturer guidance.
summary: The pilot reported an engine failure 20 minutes after departure caused by a fractured left turbocharger turbine wheel, which led to oil starvation and catastrophic engine failure. The pilot executed a forced landing on a road, resulting in substantial damage to the aircraft.

synopsis: The flight instructor's failure to maintain directional control during landing.
summary: During landing, a student pilot and flight instructor were involved when the student's braking or rudder input caused a skid, leading the aircraft to exit the runway, strike a sign, and invert. The instructor reported no mechanical failures, resulting in substantial damage to the fuselage and empennage.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power for undetermined reasons.
summary: The pilot ejected after experiencing unexplained engine power loss below 500 feet during departure, causing the aircraft to impact and submerge in the ocean. Post-accident examination found recovered components functional, but the cause of the power loss remained undetermined due to unrecovered wreckage.

synopsis: The Hong Kong Air Accident Investigation Authority notified the NTSB of a December 11, 2018, accident involving a Boeing 777-300ER. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the Hong Kong authority.
summary: The Hong Kong Air Accident Investigation Authority notified the NTSB of a December 11, 2018, accident involving a Boeing 777-300ER. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the Hong Kong authority.

synopsis: The UK government notified the NTSB of a November 2, 2018, accident involving a Piper PA34. The NTSB appointed a representative to assist the UK investigation, with all information to be released by the UK government.
summary: The UK government notified the NTSB of a November 2, 2018, accident involving a Piper PA34. The NTSB appointed a representative to assist the UK investigation, with all information to be released by the UK government.

synopsis: The Spanish government notified the NTSB of a Cessna 177 accident on December 07, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist Spain's investigation, with all information to be released by Spain.
summary: The Spanish government notified the NTSB of a Cessna 177 accident on December 07, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist Spain's investigation, with all information to be released by Spain.

synopsis: The Air Accident Investigation Unit of Belgium notified the NTSB of a serious incident involving an Airbus A330-223 on December 11, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation as the State of Manufacturer and Design of the engine.
summary: The Air Accident Investigation Unit of Belgium notified the NTSB of a serious incident involving an Airbus A330-223 on December 11, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation as the State of Manufacturer and Design of the engine.

aircraft: Czech Sport Aircraft As Piper Sport
synopsis: A total loss of engine power due to an interruption of fuel flow.
summary: The pilot experienced a total engine power loss while on an extended base leg, forcing a landing that resulted in substantial wing damage after striking a fence and utility pole. Data indicated a temporary fuel pressure drop and zero flow, but the investigation could not determine the specific cause of the fuel flow interruption.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed during the initial climb after takeoff, which resulted in an exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack and a subsequent aerodynamic stall and spin.
summary: During the initial climb of a personal flight, the pilot's aircraft entered a right spin and impacted the ground vertically. The accident resulted from the pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed, causing an aerodynamic stall and spin with no pre-impact mechanical anomalies found.

synopsis: The pilot's exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack, which led to an aerodynamic stall while turning in the traffic pattern at low altitude.
summary: A commercial pilot flying an experimental amateur-built airplane stalled during a tight left turn at 300 feet in the traffic pattern. The accident resulted from operating near stall speed with idle power, possibly influenced by unverified cockpit modifications, before the ballistic recovery system activated.

synopsis: The DGAC of Mexico notified the NTSB of an incident involving a Boeing 737 on December 12, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the DGAC.
summary: The DGAC of Mexico notified the NTSB of an incident involving a Boeing 737 on December 12, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the DGAC.

synopsis: The pilot's exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall and impact with terrain during landing in icing conditions.
summary: The pilot of a retractable-gear aircraft stalled during an IFR night approach in icing conditions while leveling off at 1,620 feet. The aircraft impacted a field 2.4 nautical miles short of the runway with substantial damage, though the pilot reported no mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's improper preflight performance planning and his subsequent failure to attain sufficient speed for the airplane to climb with a tailwind.
summary: The pilot of a ski-equipped airplane aborted a first takeoff and, during a second attempt with a tailwind, settled back onto the runway before overrunning and striking a tree. The pilot attributed the accident to unknown wind conditions, high density altitude, and insufficient runway length compared to the aircraft's required takeoff distance.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control during the landing roll and his subsequent overapplication of left rudder, which resulted in the right wing impacting the runway.
summary: During the landing roll, the pilot reported the airplane veered right twice. After overcorrecting with excessive left rudder, the right wingtip struck the runway, substantially damaging the trailing edge spar, with no preimpact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's diverted attention during the takeoff climb due to a loss of engine power, which resulted in the airplane's exceedance of the critical angle of attack and subsequent stall/spin.
summary: The pilot experienced engine power loss during initial climb due to fuel starvation from improper valve settings and an inoperative left magneto. This likely caused a stall and spin at low altitude, resulting in a crash into open terrain.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to see and avoid a parked glider while taxiing from the runway.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane struck a parked glider while cutting a corner on the taxiway after landing. The collision occurred because the pilot failed to see the glider, causing the elevator to hit the glider's stabilizers and sustain substantial damage.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare in gusting crosswind conditions.
summary: The gyroplane pilot reported a hard landing during a simulated engine-out flare caused by suspected wind shear, resulting in substantial damage to the main rotor and mast. The pilot stated no mechanical failures existed, noting winds from 300° at 12 knots gusting to 15 knots on runway 35.

synopsis: A partial loss of engine power due to the No. 1 cylinder's valve keeper becoming dislodged, which ultimately resulted in the intake valve becoming stuck in the valve guide and in the loss of compression to the cylinder.
summary: A private pilot executing a forced landing after engine power loss during descent nosed over the aircraft. The accident resulted from a stuck intake valve caused by a dislodged keeper and broken spring seat, likely undetected due to missing periodic maintenance inspections.

synopsis: The right brake being locked during the landing roll on the turf runway for reasons that could not be determined during postaccident examinations, which resulted in a noseover.
summary: A private pilot landing a personal aircraft on a turf runway experienced a locked right brake, causing the airplane to pull right. Despite corrective inputs, the airplane nosed over and sustained substantial damage, though the cause of the brake lock remained undetermined.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain proper alignment with the runway during final approach, which resulted in impact with a tree.
summary: A sport pilot flying a personal local flight impacted a tree with the left wingtip on final approach due to fixating on airspeed and drifting north of the course. The aircraft spun around the tree and descended nose down to the ground, with no preaccident mechanical malfunctions reported.

synopsis: The cold seizure of the cylinder/piston due to the pilot's failure to adequately warm the engine before takeoff, which resulted in a loss of engine power during a departure climb.
summary: During the climb of a personal flight, the pilot experienced partial engine power loss and performed an off-airport landing that resulted in a collision with a power pole. The pilot attributed the failure to a cold seizure caused by operating the engine below the required 150°F coolant temperature.

synopsis: The in-flight failure of the fuselage, as a result of the pilot conducting maneuvers that exceeded the structural capabilities of the airplane.
summary: The pilot likely performed an aggressive high-speed pull-up, possibly during aerobatics, causing the airplane to break up in-flight. This maneuver generated excessive structural loads that failed the fuselage longerons and wing spars, resulting in the aircraft's disintegration over a swamp area.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from trees during a visual approach for landing in night visual meteorological conditions. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's lack of recent experience flying at night.
summary: A private pilot flying a personal night flight impacted trees short of the runway due to a likely visual illusion caused by sparsely lit terrain and the absence of PAPI or VASI lights. The pilot had not flown at night in over four months, and no mechanical discrepancies were found.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain the proper airspeed during landing, which resulted in the airplane landing too fast and too far down the runway to safely stop it.
summary: The pilot of a recently purchased airplane aborted a landing after the front right cockpit door opened during initial climb. The aircraft overran the runway and struck a fence due to being too high and fast, sustaining substantial damage to the left wing and elevator.

synopsis: An in-flight loss of control following an encounter with supercooled large droplet icing conditions, which ultimately resulted in an uncontrolled descent and subsequent inflight breakup. Also causal was the pilot's failure to maintain an appropriate airspeed for flight in icing conditions.
summary: The pilot and passenger encountered supercooled large droplet icing while operating below the minimum recommended airspeed, causing ice accumulation that exceeded the protection system's capability. This led to an aerodynamic stall, loss of control, right wing separation, and the aircraft impacting water.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of airplane control due to spatial disorientation during initial climb in instrument meteorological conditions.
summary: The pilot departed in IMC and entered a left turn per clearance. At 2,410 feet, the stick shaker activated, airspeed dropped to 75 knots, and the aircraft stalled, rolled inverted, and impacted terrain likely due to spatial disorientation.

synopsis: The flight crew's encounter with windshear during the landing flare, which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: The flight crew encountered low-level windshear during the landing flare of a second approach after a cold front shifted the wind. This resulted in a hard touchdown that substantially damaged the aircraft.

synopsis: A partial loss of engine power due to debris obstructing the metering plug orifice in the throttle and metering unit.
summary: The pilot/mechanic performed maintenance on an airplane with a history of fuel issues, replacing fuel system components before departing. During climb, the engine lost power due to debris obstructing the metering plug, forcing a landing that resulted in substantial damage to the fuselage and left wing.

synopsis: The ASC of Taiwan notified the NTSB of an incident involving a Boeing 747 on December 13, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the ASC of Taiwan.
summary: The ASC of Taiwan notified the NTSB of an incident involving a Boeing 747 on December 13, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the ASC of Taiwan.

synopsis: The structural failure of the home-built landing platform during landing, which resulted in the helicopter rolling over.
summary: The pilot reported that while cooling down the engine after a normal landing on a home-built platform, the structure failed and collapsed. The helicopter rolled onto its right side, sustaining substantial tailboom damage, with no preaccident mechanical malfunctions identified.

synopsis: CENIPA notified the NTSB of a December 20, 2018 incident involving a Boeing 777. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist CENIPA's investigation as the State of Manufacturer, with all information to be released by CENIPA.
summary: CENIPA notified the NTSB of a December 20, 2018 incident involving a Boeing 777. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist CENIPA's investigation as the State of Manufacturer, with all information to be released by CENIPA.

synopsis: The pilot's exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack during landing in gusting crosswind conditions, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall.
summary: During landing flare on runway 35, a pilot encountered a 23-knot gust that lifted a wing 90 degrees. To prevent flipping while over a drainage ditch, she intentionally stalled the aircraft, causing it to impact the ditch with substantial wing damage despite no mechanical failures.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power due to a loose carburetor bowl.
summary: During an instructional flight shortly after takeoff, the engine lost total power due to a loose carburetor bowl causing a fuel leak. The instructor executed a forced landing on a taxiway, resulting in substantial damage, as the aircraft had not received required service bulletin inspections.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to retract the amphibious float's landing gear wheels before landing on the water. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's failure to use the after takeoff and before landing checklists.
summary: The pilot of an amphibious float-equipped airplane nosed over during a water landing with landing gear extended after failing to verify blue gear-up lights. The pilot attributed the substantial damage to relying on memory instead of using the required before-landing checklist.

synopsis: Collision with a bird in flight, which resulted in damage to the engine, a fuel leak, and a subsequent total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion.
summary: The pilot reported that a bird strike at 2,500 feet likely damaged the fuel system, causing fuel leakage and subsequent engine power loss. This forced an emergency landing on a road where the aircraft struck trees and a sign, resulting in substantial damage to the fuselage and wings.

synopsis: The student pilot's exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack during the initial climb, resulting in an aerodynamic stall from which the pilot did not recover.
summary: A solo student pilot crashed a light aircraft shortly after takeoff during a third touch-and-go landing while flying a non-standard right traffic pattern. The accident resulted from an aerodynamic stall caused by excessive climb rate and angle of attack, with no evidence of mechanical failure or medical incapacitation.

synopsis: The pilot's improper decision to land on a roadway during dark night conditions with inoperable landing and taxi lights, which resulted in an impact with a snow berm.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane nosed over after striking a snow berm on a roadway during a night landing caused by inoperable lights. A postaccident examination revealed the lights failed due to a broken factory connection at the 4-pin connector, resulting in substantial damage to the wings, stabilizer, and rudder.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to see and avoid a cell tower wire during a pipeline patrol flight. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's distraction due to writing down observations about the pipeline while flying.
summary: A commercial pilot conducting a pipeline patrol flight struck a cell tower wire while looking down to write observations, tearing off a 4-foot section of the left wing. The pilot declared an emergency and landed safely, noting that an observer or delaying note-taking could have prevented the incident.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing.
summary: A solo student pilot landing on runway 33 veered left off the centerline, exited the runway, and nosed over, sustaining substantial damage to the lower left-wing lift strut. The pilot reported no mechanical failures, and wind conditions were light and variable from the northwest.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to apply adequate torque to a fuel line during recent maintenance, which allowed the line to loosen in flight and fuel to enter the hot engine compartment and resulted in an in-flight fire that consumed the airplane.
summary: During a touch-and-go climb, a pilot smelled an odor and saw flames from a fuel leak caused by a loose line installed with inadequate torque. The pilot rejected the takeoff and landed, but a post-crash fire consumed the aircraft.

synopsis: The Government of Turkey notified the NTSB of a Cessna 172 accident on November 19, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the Turkish investigation, with all information to be released by Turkey.
summary: The Government of Turkey notified the NTSB of a Cessna 172 accident on November 19, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the Turkish investigation, with all information to be released by Turkey.

synopsis: The Government of Turkey notified the NTSB of a Cessna 150 accident on October 30, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the Turkish investigation, with all information to be released by Turkey.
summary: The Government of Turkey notified the NTSB of a Cessna 150 accident on October 30, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the Turkish investigation, with all information to be released by Turkey.

synopsis: The Government of Turkey notified the NTSB of a Cessna 172 accident on June 27, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the Turkish investigation, with all information to be released by Turkey.
summary: The Government of Turkey notified the NTSB of a Cessna 172 accident on June 27, 2018. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the Turkish investigation, with all information to be released by Turkey.

synopsis: The Mexican government notified the NTSB of an accident involving an Agusta A109S helicopter on December 24, 2018. The investigation remains under Mexican jurisdiction, with the NTSB appointing a representative to assist.
summary: The Mexican government notified the NTSB of an accident involving an Agusta A109S helicopter on December 24, 2018. The investigation remains under Mexican jurisdiction, with the NTSB appointing a representative to assist.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed during the instrument approach which led to an aerodynamic stall.
summary: During an RNAV approach in instrument meteorological conditions, the pilot hand-flew the aircraft, performing S-turns before losing airspeed and stalling. The airplane descended steeply and impacted the ground, likely because the pilot failed to maintain adequate airspeed and could not recover from the stall in time.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power due to the fatigue fracture of the No. 2 exhaust rocker arm stud.
summary: A flight instructor and student experienced a partial engine power loss during a local instructional flight due to a fatigued No. 2 exhaust rocker arm stud. The instructor attempted a water landing, but the aircraft flipped upon touchdown, causing substantial damage to the vertical stabilizer and rudder.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from the fire truck.
summary: During a night air medical approach, a pilot slowed the helicopter near obstructions, causing the tail rotor to strike a fire truck's hose rack. This impact resulted in a loss of control, ground impact, and substantial tail rotor damage, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The partial loss of engine power for undetermined reasons.
summary: During a personal flight landing at a high-elevation dirt airport, the pilot experienced a total loss of engine power after turning off carburetor heat. Although the pilot suspected carburetor icing, weather conditions made this unlikely, leaving the cause of the power loss undetermined as the aircraft pancaked with substantial damage.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain directional control during takeoff, which resulted in a runway excursion and impact with a sign.
summary: A solo student pilot lost directional control during takeoff for a stop-and-go landing, causing the aircraft to exit the runway left and strike a sign. The left main gear separated and the wing lift strut sustained substantial damage, with the pilot reporting no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: An in-flight collision with a bird during low-altitude maneuvering, which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: A student pilot and flight instructor practicing takeoffs and landings in a helicopter struck a turkey vulture at 300 ft AGL, causing tail rotor damage and yaw. The instructor executed an autorotation to a golf course, resulting in a hard landing with substantial damage to the tailboom and fuselage.

synopsis: The manufacturer's inadequate cleaning of the crucible before melting the nickel alloy used in casting the low pressure turbine stage 3 blades that resulted in a casting anomaly from where an intergranular crack occurred became the origin of a fatigue crack that led to the fracture of a low pressure turbine stage 3 blade.
summary: Korean Air flight 0753, an Airbus A220-300, experienced a left engine shutdown at 29,000 feet due to a fractured low pressure turbine blade. The failure originated from a subsurface intergranular crack caused by hafnium contamination from an inadequately cleaned crucible, which was undetectable by standard inspections.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control in gusting crosswind conditions.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane sustained substantial fuselage and wing damage after a crosswind gust caused a balloon and drift during landing on runway 16. The pilot reported no mechanical failures and recommended using less flaps and more airspeed for future crosswind landings.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate preflight and in-flight fuel planning, which resulted in the total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion.
summary: A commercial pilot conducting a personal cross-country flight with one passenger experienced total engine power loss due to fuel exhaustion. The pilot attempted an off-airport forced landing, impacting trees and terrain with substantial damage, attributing the accident to poor fuel and distance calculations.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of airplane control for reasons that could not be determined based on the available information.
summary: The pilot of a personal aircraft lost control during touch-and-go landings, resulting in a fatal crash into a building. No mechanical failures were found, and while the pilot tested positive for seizure medications, the investigation could not determine if a medical event caused the loss of control.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain a positive rate of climb after takeoff which resulted in an impact with trees and terrain. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's inability to see a visible horizon due to the dark night lighting conditions and limited ground lights in the vicinity of the airport.
summary: A private pilot departed a dark, unlit airport at night and impacted terrain 1/3 mile away shortly after takeoff. The investigation suggests spatial disorientation or distraction during climb configuration caused the loss of control, with no mechanical failures found.

synopsis: an inadvertent loss of airspeed and increased pitch attitude prior to touchdown.
summary: American Airlines flight 567, a Boeing 757, sustained substantial tail strike damage upon landing at Charlotte Douglas International Airport in fog. The First Officer advanced throttles due to a perceived fast radar altitude countdown, resulting in a hard landing with 107 knots airspeed and a 9-degree nose-up pitch that crushed the rear fuselage and seized the APU.

synopsis: A partial loss of engine power during a go-around for reasons that could not be determined based on the available information, which resulted in a forced landing.
summary: The pilot executed a go-around due to animals on the runway but experienced unexplained engine power loss, forcing a landing short of the runway where the aircraft struck trees. Post-accident examinations found no mechanical failure or fuel issues, and the cause of the power loss remains undetermined.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the takeoff roll.
summary: A student pilot soloing a flight school aircraft veered left during takeoff, exited the runway, struck a berm, and collapsed the nose gear. The chief pilot reported no pre-accident mechanical failures, resulting in substantial fuselage damage.

synopsis: The AAIB of India notified the NTSB of a December 21, 2018, incident involving a Boeing 747. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the AAIB.
summary: The AAIB of India notified the NTSB of a December 21, 2018, incident involving a Boeing 747. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the AAIB.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of helicopter control while maneuvering at a low altitude after being struck in the head by a bird.
summary: A pilot flying a doorless helicopter 20 feet above water struck a seabird in the head while turning, causing him to flare and settle into the water. The helicopter subsequently inverted and sustained substantial damage to the fuselage and main rotor blades with no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The student pilot's loss of directional control while landing on an ice-covered runway, which resulted in a loss of directional control, and his failure to attain sufficient airspeed during a subsequent aborted landing, which resulted in a nose-over.
summary: A student pilot soloing a cross-country flight landed on Runway 13 in 10-knot winds but encountered ice, causing the aircraft to drift left and exit the runway. After aborting the landing and colliding with lighting, the aircraft nosed over due to insufficient airspeed, sustaining substantial damage to the right wing strut.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to properly configure the landing gear before performing a water landing.
summary: The pilot of an experimental amphibious airplane forgot to retract the landing gear after takeoff due to distraction. The aircraft landed in a river with gear extended, nosed down immediately upon touchdown, and partially sank.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing.
summary: The pilot-in-command ground looped a tailwheel-equipped airplane to the right during a three-point landing, causing the left wing to strike the ground and sustain substantial damage. The owner reported no preaccident mechanical failures, attributing the incident to the pilot's first flight in command.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in hard, bounced landing, loss of directional control, runway excursion, and impact with a fence and terrain during an attempted go-around.
summary: The pilot reported that during a precautionary short final approach with extra speed, the aircraft descended hard, bounced, and veered off the runway into snow. A subsequent go-around attempt resulted in a fence and terrain impact, causing substantial left wing damage with no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot/mechanic's improper installation and securing of the mixture control cable, which led to a simultaneous loss of total engine power and failure of the nose landing gear to fully extend when the cable caught on the nose landing gear assembly.
summary: The pilot and flight instructor experienced an engine power loss and partial gear extension during the base leg of an instructional flight, forcing a landing that damaged the airframe. The accident occurred because the mixture control cable was improperly secured, caught on the nose gear during extension, and pulled the mixture to the lean position, cutting off fuel.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain yaw control and his exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack during an aborted landing, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane reported that the aircraft yawed left upon landing and during the subsequent go-around attempt. Despite applying full right rudder and power, the airplane stalled and collided with the ground, sustaining substantial damage, with no preimpact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The failure of the nose landing gear actuator hydraulic hose, which resulted in the loss of hydraulic fluid and hydraulic system pressure and a subsequent gear-up landing.
summary: A private pilot experienced a landing gear malfunction on a personal flight after a hydraulic hose failed during retraction. The hose, which had not been updated per a service bulletin, ruptured and caused hydraulic fluid loss, preventing main gear extension and resulting in a damaged emergency landing.

synopsis: The pilot's improper preflight planning, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion.
summary: The pilot of a newly purchased airplane experienced fuel exhaustion and engine power loss 15 minutes from destination due to relying on incorrect fuel capacity and consumption data from the previous owner.
