Nonstandard crossing phraseology and ineffective coordination between local controller 1 (LC1) and local controller 2 (LC2) which resulted in degraded shared situation awareness, and a runway incursion. Nonstandard crossing phraseology and ineffective coordination between local controller 1 (LC1) and local controller 2 (LC2) which resulted in degraded shared situation awareness, and a runway incursion. Nonstandard crossing phraseology and ineffective coordination between local controller 1 (LC1) and local controller 2 (LC2) which resulted in degraded shared situation awareness, and a runway incursion. Nonstandard crossing phraseology and ineffective coordination between local controller 1 (LC1) and local controller 2 (LC2) which resulted in degraded shared situation awareness, and a runway incursion.
summary: Local controllers LC1 and LC2 cleared four aircraft to cross runway 4L at JFK while Swiss flight SWR17K was on takeoff roll. The pilot rejected the takeoff at 50 knots due to the incursion caused by non-standard phraseology that led LC1 to misinterpret the crossing sequence.

synopsis: The pilot's improper installation and inspection of the right lower wing strut attachment bolt, which resulted in the inflight failure of the right wing.
summary: The pilot flew an unregistered, self-assembled aircraft that crashed after the right wing failed during initial climb. The accident resulted from an improperly installed wing strut bolt that provided no structural support, causing the wing to fold under aerodynamic loads.

synopsis: Failure of a landing gear extension system hydraulic hose, which resulted in a landing with the landing gear retracted.
summary: During approach, the pilot could not extend landing gear due to a deteriorated hydraulic hose that leaked all fluid, forcing a gear-up landing at a diverted airport. The aircraft skidded right, ending upright off the runway with substantial damage to the right horizontal stabilizer and elevator.

synopsis: A degraded ignition system, which resulted in a total loss of engine power. Contributing to the accident was maintenance personnel's inadequate inspection of the ignition system.
summary: The pilot experienced engine power loss shortly after takeoff due to a degraded ignition system with loose P-lead connections and worn spark plugs. This caused a forced landing in snow where the aircraft nosed over and came to rest inverted.

synopsis: The student pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a bounced, hard landing.
summary: A student pilot and flight instructor were involved in an accident during the student's second solo landing in a light aircraft. The student reported being too high and fast due to poor depth perception and radio distractions, causing the airplane to porpoise four times, sustain substantial fuselage damage, and become uncontrollable.

aircraft: Schleicher Alexander Gmbh & Co ASH 26 E
synopsis: Reduced takeoff performance for reasons that could not be determined, which resulted in a forced landing.
summary: The pilot of a self-launching motorglider experienced poor climb performance during a second practice takeoff, leading to a ground impact after a turn. Investigators suspected a flap misconfiguration caused the reduced climb, though the pre-accident flap position could not be determined.

synopsis: The flight instructor's failure to maintain adequate airspeed during landing which resulted in a loss of directional control and runway excursion. Contributing to the accident was the pilot receiving instructions failure to maintain runway alignment.
summary: A student pilot and flight instructor on short final approach aligned with the wrong runway. The instructor's corrective maneuver caused a stall, resulting in an inverted landing in a field that seriously injured the student and substantially damaged the fuselage.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power due to a failure of the No. 4 cylinder piston boss.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot experienced a total engine failure during a cross-country flight due to catastrophic No. 4 piston assembly failure and camshaft wear. The instructor performed a forced landing that caused substantial wing damage, occurring 21 years and 2,190 hours after the engine's last overhaul, exceeding the 12-year TBO limit.

synopsis: The pilot's inflight loss of control during landing following an encounter with a wind gust which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: During a second landing approach, a pilot encountered a sudden strong wind gust at 10 feet, causing the nose to rise abruptly. Despite attempting a go-around, the aircraft landed hard, collapsing the landing gear and sustaining substantial fuselage damage with no pre-accident mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to properly configure the airplane during a go-around in gusting wind conditions, and his subsequent exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall at an altitude too low for recovery.
summary: The pilot of an experimental airplane stalled and crashed into terrain during a go-around after failing to retract flaps as required. This procedural error reduced climb performance, causing an aerodynamic stall at an altitude too low for recovery, resulting in a postimpact fire.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to attain a proper touchdown point while landing, which resulted in a runway overrun.
summary: The pilot landed long on a 3,000-ft turf runway during the landing phase, causing the airplane to overrun the departure end. This resulted in substantial damage to the wings, fuselage, and empennage, with no preimpact mechanical malfunctions reported.

aircraft: James E Davidson Jr RANS S-7S COURIER
synopsis: The pilot's unintentional use of a winter-blend fuel that was susceptible to vaporization, which resulted in fuel starvation and a loss of engine power due to vapor lock. Contributing to the accident was the airplane's undersized fuel lines, which limited the available fuel flow and volume.
summary: The pilot experienced total engine power loss shortly after takeoff while testing a winter-blend auto fuel mixture in an aircraft with undersized fuel lines and a blocked vent. Investigators determined that exhaust heat caused the fuel to vaporize, creating a vapor lock that starved the engine and led to a gear-collapse landing.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control while landing in gusting crosswind conditions.
summary: During a landing in left crosswind, the pilot aborted a bounced approach after a gust rolled the aircraft, causing a right wing strike. A subsequent loss of directional control on the second touchdown led to an excursion, bending the right gear and damaging the wings and engine mount.

synopsis: The pilot/owner's failure to ensure adequate maintenance of the airplane, which resulted in a partial loss of engine power during takeoff.
summary: The pilot/owner experienced a partial engine power loss and stall during takeoff due to a cracked, non-sealing intake valve in cylinder No. 2. The aircraft impacted a field with substantial fuselage damage, an accident likely preventable had the required annual inspection been performed.

synopsis: A loss of power of the No. 1 engine for reasons that could not be determined, and the incorrect installation of a B-nut fitting in the propeller feathering system, which allowed engine oil to spray onto the exhaust system when the propeller was feathered following the loss of engine power. Contributing to the accident was an incorrectly repaired fuel leak, which resulted in an explosion that separated the aileron bell housing that resulted in a loss of control and subsequent impact with terrain.
summary: Pilots of a four-engine aircraft transporting fuel and propane tanks encountered a No. 1 engine fire and explosion shortly after takeoff. The accident resulted from a leaking fuel tank and an incorrectly installed feathering system fitting that sprayed oil onto the hot exhaust, causing an uncontrolled descent into terrain.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to continue an unstabilized approach, which resulted in a bounced landing, and his failure to maintain proper airspeed and climb attitude after aborting the landing, which led to the airplane exceeding its critical angle of attack and resulting in an aerodynamic stall.
summary: The pilot aborted a landing after propeller contact and gear scraping, then stalled during a tight low-altitude turn to avoid traffic. The aircraft impacted the ground with no pre-impact mechanical deficiencies found, though video showed all gear extended during the takeoff.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to attain a proper touchdown point during landing which resulted in a runway excursion and subsequent nose over.
summary: The pilot reported that while landing on a dirt runway, the aircraft touched down high and overshot the runway end while avoiding a mudhole. The airplane struck rock boundary markers and came to rest inverted, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate compensation for the gusting crosswind condition during landing.
summary: During final approach to runway 35 in gusty crosswinds, the pilot encountered suspected wind shear causing a right roll and wingtip contact at 20 feet. The pilot aborted the landing, but the aircraft impacted the runway and sustained substantial damage to the fuselage and right wing with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to extend the landing gear before landing.
summary: The pilot, during a visual approach after an IFR flight, neglected to lower the landing gear while distracted by departing traffic and sun glare. The aircraft settled on the runway with gear up, skidded, and sustained substantial fuselage damage, with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control of the airplane during landing in gusty wind conditions.
summary: A pilot with 3 hours of experience lost control during short final on runway 17 when a gust lifted the right wing, causing a hard landing in a field. The aircraft sustained substantial wing damage, with no preimpact mechanical failures reported despite recorded gusts to 15 knots.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control during the landing flare.
summary: The pilot reported the airplane stalled during the landing flare. Adding power for a go-around caused a left yaw and wing drop, resulting in a nose-over into grass with substantial wing damage, though no mechanical failures were identified.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power due to a loss of cooling oil to the turbine-to-compressor coupling shaft and subsequent fracture of the shaft at an altitude too low for the pilot to complete a successful autorotation. Contributing to the accident was carbon buildup in the piccolo tube screen and nozzles and the disintegration of the spur adapter gearshaft O-rings for reasons that could not be determined.
summary: A helicopter pilot conducting aerial application operations experienced a total engine power loss at 150 ft agl due to a fractured turbine-to-compressor coupling shaft caused by oil coking from missing O-rings. The pilot attempted an emergency autorotation but impacted flat terrain, likely due to insufficient altitude to complete a successful landing.

synopsis: A cabin fire as a result of a damaged lithium-ion battery pack.
summary: The pilot dropped a portable ADS-B receiver and lithium-ion battery from the aircraft top onto the ramp, damaging the battery. During the subsequent engine runup, the damaged battery likely entered thermal runaway, causing a fire that consumed the cockpit and substantially damaged both wings.

synopsis: An encounter with convectively induced turbulence during descent.
summary: During Delta flight 1044's descent through 10,000 ft into Atlanta, a flight attendant sustained a fractured foot after being thrown by moderate turbulence while performing cabin checks. The crew attributed the event to entering a small cumulus cloud, with no prior turbulence warnings issued.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control during the landing roll.
summary: The pilot reported the aircraft veered right after touchdown despite rudder and brake inputs, exiting the runway and striking an unoccupied airplane and hangar door. Although the pilot suspected a seized right brake, post-accident inspections found no mechanical anomalies and confirmed both brakes functioned normally.

synopsis: A loss of collective control authority due to fatigue failure of the collective servo cylinder extension arms from corrosion pitting.
summary: During a pipeline inspection flight, a helicopter pilot and passenger experienced an uncontrolled descent caused by fatigue fractures in the collective control servo arms initiated by corrosion pits. The pilot performed a forced landing into an orchard, resulting in substantial tailboom damage, though the investigation could not link the failure to recent blade installation.

synopsis: Maintenance personnel's improper installation of an engine-driven vacuum pump, which resulted in oil starvation to the engine and a subsequent total loss of engine power. Contributing to the accident was the A&P IA's lack of supervision.
summary: A pilot conducting a post-inspection test flight experienced engine failure due to oil loss caused by a mechanic trainee's improper vacuum pump installation. The unsecured pump blocked the oil passage, depleting the sump and forcing an off-airport landing where the aircraft struck a power line.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power as a result of an improperly fabricated fuel-air mixture cable bracket. Contributing was the pilot's decision to fly the airplane with a known mechanical engine issue, and the presence of another airplane that was back taxiing on the runway while the pilot was attempting to maneuver the airplane for landing.
summary: The pilot of an experimental amateur-built airplane experienced a complete engine power loss during a test flight due to an improperly fabricated fuel/air mixture cable bracket. This caused an excessively lean mixture, forcing a perpendicular landing off the runway that resulted in substantial damage to the right wing and fuselage.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power for undetermined reasons, which resulted in a forced landing and a subsequent impact with terrain.
summary: The pilot of an experimental helicopter crashed into a residential area during a charity golf ball drop, likely due to total engine power loss. Potential causes included fuel system deterioration from ethanol, pilot cardiac issues, or impairment from gabapentin use, though fire damage prevented definitive confirmation.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane during an aborted landing, which resulted in a runway excursion, and subsequent collision with trees.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane bounced during landing after pulling back to bleed airspeed while high on the base leg. Loss of directional control led to a runway excursion and a forced landing in trees, causing substantial wing damage with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain aircraft control during the landing roll in gusting wind conditions.
summary: The pilot reported that during landing on runway 33, a strong wind gust lifted the left wing and tail, causing the right wing to strike the ground and the airplane to nose over. This resulted in substantial damage to the right-wing lift strut with no preimpact mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate preflight planning and failure to abort the takeoff at the predetermined decision point.
summary: The pilot and passenger attempted a takeoff from a wet turf runway, but the aircraft failed to become airborne and overran the end, colliding with a berm. The pilot attributed the accident to not executing a go/no-go decision at a runway hump, resulting in a post-accident fire that destroyed the aircraft.

synopsis: The pilot's delayed use of carburetor heat which resulted in the loss of engine power due to carburetor icing.
summary: The pilot experienced engine power loss during a night GPS approach in IMC, likely due to carburetor icing that carburetor heat could not clear. The aircraft subsequently impacted a building and retaining wall, sustaining substantial damage to the engine mounts and forward fuselage.

synopsis: The failure of the right main landing gear axle due to multiple fatigue crack initiation points joining into a single larger crack.
summary: The pilot landed on a grass runway when the right main landing gear axle fractured due to fatigue, puncturing the fuel tank and causing a postimpact fire that destroyed the aircraft. The pilot sustained thermal injuries and was hospitalized.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of control during the descent for reasons that could not be determined, which resulted in a steep descent into terrain.
summary: A private pilot and pilot-rated passenger crashed a personal aircraft into a wooded area during the final approach phase after an uncommanded steep descent. The investigation could not determine if a sudden incapacitating medical event involving either occupant caused the accident, as no mechanical failures were found.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed during the final approach, which resulted in an inadvertent aerodynamic stall. Contributing to the accident the flight instructor's delayed remedial action.
summary: A student pilot stalled a training aircraft 5 to 10 feet above the runway during the eleventh landing by failing to correct decreasing airspeed. The hard impact caused the right wing to strike the ground, damaging the wing spar, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of control during takeoff that resulted in a hard landing.
summary: The pilot experienced an uncorrectable right yaw during takeoff from a trailer, resulting in a hard landing that caused substantial tailboom damage. Despite the pilot reporting no mechanical failures, a supervisor confirmed normal control function and gauges before repositioning the helicopter.

synopsis: The failure of the nose oil seal to remain secure in the engine crankcase, which resulted in a loss of engine oil and partial loss of engine power.
summary: The pilot experienced engine roughness and low oil pressure while climbing for a practice approach, forcing a field landing with substantial fuselage damage. The accident resulted from a protruding nose oil seal causing oil loss and bearing failure, likely due to the engine exceeding manufacturer overhaul limits.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power due to the due to the pilot's delayed application of carburetor heat.
summary: The pilot experienced a total loss of engine power likely due to carburetor icing, despite applying carburetor heat. This resulted in a forced landing into rough terrain where the aircraft struck a ditch, substantially damaging the fuselage.

synopsis: A loss of directional control during the landing roll.
summary: During landing approach in 9-knot gusting winds, the pilot touched down straight but the airplane veered left and ground looped right. The left main landing gear collapsed, causing the aircraft to depart the runway and sustain substantial left wing damage.

synopsis: The pilot under instruction's inadvertent use of the mixture control, which resulted in a total loss of engine power.
summary: A student pilot inadvertently pulled the mixture control while practicing takeoffs and landings in a helicopter, causing total engine power loss. The flight instructor executed an autorotation, but the main rotor blade struck and severed the tailboom during the forced landing in an open field.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to attain a proper touchdown point during a simulated loss of engine power approach, which resulted in a hard landing short of the runway. Also causal was the flight instructor's delayed remedial action during the approach and subsequent aborted landing.
summary: During a simulated engine failure in the traffic pattern, a flight instructor and private pilot landed short of the runway after the student extended flaps prematurely. The aircraft bounced, entered an uncontrolled nose-high left-wing-low attitude during a go-around attempt, and nosed over, causing substantial damage with no mechanical failure reported.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate yaw control of the helicopter while maneuvering at a low altitude and airspeed, which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: During an enroute proficiency flight, a helicopter entered an uncommanded left turn at 50 feet AGL and impacted the ground after the pilot failed to apply sufficient right pedal input. The accident resulted from loss of tail rotor effectiveness at low speed, not mechanical failure, though a cockpit recorder malfunction was also noted.

synopsis: The pilot's excessive turn rate and bank angle while at low airspeed and altitude, resulting in an accelerated aerodynamic stall, loss of airplane control, and collision with terrain.
summary: Shortly after takeoff, a pilot executed a sharp left turn with gear extended and flaps retracted, reaching 300 feet and 90 knots before entering an accelerated stall. The aircraft impacted the ground and was destroyed by fire, with no preexisting mechanical failure found and the reason for the maneuver undetermined.

synopsis: The uncommanded movement of the left propeller into reverse during approach for undetermined reasons, resulting in an in-flight loss of control of the airplane at low altitude during approach.
summary: The pilot of an experimental twin-engine airplane entered an uncontrollable spin and impacted the ground during the base leg after the left propeller uncommanded moved to reverse pitch upon power reduction. The cause of the uncommanded pitch change was undetermined, and the pilot's mistaken response to the right engine likely exacerbated the situation.

synopsis: The captain's unintentional use of the nose down pitch trim during final approach which limited the elevator control authority resulting in a hard landing that collapsed the left main landing gear.
summary: During an Embraer EMB-145LR approach to HOU, the captain initiated a go-around too late after excessive nose-down pitch trim limited control authority, causing a hard landing. The left main landing gear separated due to vertical acceleration exceeding design limits, resulting in substantial left wing damage.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of control following an encounter with structural icing, which resulted in an inflight breakup of the airplane.
summary: The pilot reported losing autopilot during cruise at 20,000 ft in icing conditions before the aircraft broke up in flight. The probable cause was structural ice accumulation altering handling characteristics, leading to loss of control and subsequent breakup.

synopsis: The flight instructor's failure to maintain control of the airplane during an encounter with wind while holding short of the runway.
summary: A flight instructor holding short of the runway during a storm reported that a wind gust lifted the right wing, pushing the aircraft sideways and causing it to overturn. The accident resulted in substantial damage to the wing, vertical stabilizer, and rudder, with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from tower guy wires while maneuvering during a low-level aerial application flight.
summary: A pilot performing low-altitude aerial application work struck tower guy wires and impacted terrain after becoming distracted by a map. The aircraft sustained substantial damage, and the pilot attributed the accident to a lack of focus and an inadequate pre-application briefing.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control during the landing roll on a soft turf runway.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane nosed over and inverted while landing on a soft turf runway. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the vertical stabilizer, rudder, and right wing strut, with no preimpact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from power lines during a low level aerial application.
summary: During aerial application, a helicopter pilot struck known power lines and executed a forced landing. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the main rotor, transmission, tail rotor drive shaft, and tail boom, with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The flight instructor's delayed action to arrest the descending, left pedal turn while maneuvering for a low-altitude hover with the helicopter near the maximum gross weight limitation, which resulted in an impact with the ground and a dynamic rollover.
summary: A flight instructor and student in an overloaded helicopter experienced a dynamic rollover during a descending left turn at 10 feet AGL. The accident likely resulted from delayed collective input due to high gross weight and turn demands, leaving insufficient altitude to arrest the descent.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain aircraft control during landing roll.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane nosed over and inverted while braking on a grass airstrip after a normal three-point landing. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the right wing, fuselage, and vertical stabilizer, with no preaccident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The flight instructor's failure to maintain clearance from a fence during a takeoff attempt.
summary: A flight instructor practicing short-field takeoffs with a pilot-rated owner clipped a fence with the right wing after turning prematurely. The aircraft flipped, impacted terrain, and sustained substantial damage to the forward fuselage and wings, with no preimpact malfunctions reported.

synopsis: The airplane's collision with a tree during an aborted landing. Contributing to the accident was the airplane's reported brake malfunction for undetermined reasons.
summary: The pilot reported brake failure during the landing roll on a dirt airstrip, prompting a go-around that resulted in a collision with a tree and terrain impact. Post-accident examination found no preexisting mechanical malfunction, leaving the cause of the brake failure undetermined due to extensive impact damage.

synopsis: The passenger's intentional departure from the balloon in flight as an act of suicide.
summary: During a sunset balloon flight at 1,300 ft, a passenger jumped from the basket after the pilot turned away to grant privacy. The passenger died from multiple blunt force injuries, with the medical examiner listing the manner of death as suspected suicide.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the takeoff roll.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane veered right during takeoff from a narrow road after a precautionary landing for engine power loss. The aircraft struck vegetation and inverted, sustaining substantial damage to the wings and stabilizer, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing with a crosswind.
summary: The pilot reported that during the flare for landing on runway 22, a left gust caused the aircraft to veer left and exit the runway, collapsing the right main gear and damaging the fuselage. The pilot stated no mechanical failures existed, attributing the accident to the crosswind conditions.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control while landing in variable wind conditions, which resulted in runway excursion and collision with an approach light.
summary: During a landing roll while warming up the engine for an oil filter change, the pilot lost directional control due to an abrupt wind shift. The airplane veered off the runway left side and struck a precision approach path indicator light, causing substantial damage to the right wing with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control of the airplane during takeoff in gusting wind conditions, which resulted in collision with an object.
summary: During takeoff in a right crosswind, a gust pushed the aircraft into a runway wall, shearing off the left main landing gear. The pilot continued to his home airport for an emergency landing where the left wing struck the runway, causing substantial damage to the main wing spar.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing.
summary: A student pilot practicing stop-and-go landings experienced a nose-down pitch before touchdown, causing the propeller to strike the runway. The aircraft subsequently ground looped, struck the right wingtip, and nosed over inverted, resulting in substantial damage to the rudder and wings with no reported mechanical failure.

synopsis: A partial loss of engine power due to sticking exhaust valves. Contributing to the accident was maintenance personnel's failure to use available engine data while troubleshooting a known engine issue and maintenance personnel's failure to comply with inspections called out in a relevant service bulletin.
summary: Pilots experienced multiple cylinder power losses and a forced landing with substantial damage after a thermostatic oil cooler bypass valve failure caused high oil temperatures and carbon buildup. This led to sticking exhaust valves, a condition likely undetected because maintenance ignored historical data trends and the engine was overdue for overhaul.

synopsis: An inadvertent encounter with the rotor wash of a nearby hovering helicopter during landing, which resulted in a loss of control and a runway excursion.
summary: The pilot reported that while landing, the airplane encountered rotor wash from a hovering military helicopter on the adjacent ramp, causing it to levitate and turn right. The aircraft subsequently departed the runway and sustained substantial fuselage damage, with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The loss of directional control during the landing roll for reasons that could not be determined, due to impact damage sustained to the brake system.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot landed a training aircraft on a grass runway, but ineffective brakes caused the plane to veer left and strike a parked utility trailer. Post-accident inspection found the right brake pedal bound by impact damage, preventing a determination of the system's pre-crash effectiveness.

synopsis: The incomplete extension of the landing gear into the down-and-locked position for reasons that could not be determined. .
summary: During a post-maintenance flight test, the pilot and pilot-rated passenger mechanic lost all electrical power shortly after takeoff. The aircraft sustained substantial damage when the right main landing gear collapsed on landing, likely due to incomplete manual extension, though the cause of the power loss remained undetermined.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airplane control during a go-around in a gusting crosswind, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall and collision with terrain. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's lack of system knowledge regarding the operation of the flaps.
summary: During landing, a pilot encountered a gust, initiated a go-around, and stalled due to full flap retraction caused by incorrect switch usage. The aircraft impacted the ground with substantial damage, as the pilot likely misunderstood the flap switch operation despite the equipment functioning normally.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during takeoff with a gusty crosswind.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane departing Runway 8 encountered a sudden strong crosswind gust during the takeoff roll, causing the aircraft to weather-vane left and exit the runway. The airplane collided with precision approach position indicator lights and sustained substantial damage to the wings and fuselage before resting in a ditch, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: A loss of engine power during initial climb due to fuel vapor lock. Contributing to the accident was the incorrect installation of the ancillary fuel supply system components.
summary: The pilot of an experimental float-equipped Piper PA-22 experienced engine power loss shortly after takeoff due to fuel vapor lock. The accident resulted from a fuel strainer installed near a hot exhaust pipe and a purge valve routed through the engine compartment, causing fuel starvation and a hard landing.

synopsis: The pilot's improper flare, which resulted in a hard landing and the main rotor blades contacting the tail boom.
summary: During a power-off autorotation practice, a pilot flying a heavy helicopter flared too late at 40 ft AGL due to insufficient aggression for the weight. The tail skid struck the ground hard, causing main rotor blades to contact the tail boom and fuselage, resulting in substantial damage.

synopsis: The pilot's exceedance of the airplane's design limitations, which resulted in an in-flight breakup.
summary: An experienced pilot flying a single-engine aircraft with one passenger and two dogs encountered turbulence and exceeded maximum airspeed limits during a descent from FL 240 to 6,000 ft. The aircraft likely sustained structural damage from the airspeed exceedances and turbulence, leading to an in-flight breakup and loss of control.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain proper airspeed on approach which resulted in an extended touchdown, bounced landing, and runway overrun.
summary: The pilot reported a high-speed approach to a private grass airstrip resulted in a long landing and bounce. An attempted go-around failed to generate sufficient airspeed, causing the aircraft to strike a ditch and road sign, sustaining substantial damage with no preimpact mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control during landing roll due to a loose tailwheel leaf spring assembly.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot experienced a tailwheel shimmy during a 3-point landing in a tailwheel-equipped airplane. The loose tailwheel leaf spring assembly caused loss of directional control, leading to left main gear collapse and substantial left wing damage.

synopsis: The pilot's adjustment of the carburetor to an incorrect setting, which resulted in partial loss of engine power during takeoff.
summary: The pilot of an experimental amateur-built airplane experienced partial engine power loss during takeoff from a private dirt strip due to an overly lean carburetor setting. The aircraft failed to gain altitude, struck fences, and nosed over after the pilot elected to continue the takeoff to avoid an irrigation canal.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control while landing on a wet turf runway, which resulted in a runway excursion and impact with trees. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's failure to ensure the passenger's proper use of seatbelts before the landing.
summary: The pilot landed on a wet turf runway, aborted a go-around due to trees, and overshot into a grove, causing substantial fuselage damage and a serious injury to an unrestrained passenger. The pilot reported no mechanical failures but admitted failing to confirm the passenger was wearing a seatbelt before landing.

synopsis: A failure of the sUAS's magnetometer while operating in close proximity to commercial air conditioning equipment, which resulted in the sUAS's erratic maneuvering. Contributing to the accident was the RPIC's failure to input the appropriate command to disarm the sUAS and the manufacturer's failure to include detailed information on how to disarm the sUAS in an emergency situation in their user/operator guidance documents.
summary: A remote pilot in command sustained serious injuries while manually disarming a small unmanned aircraft system that moved erratically shortly after takeoff from a hospital roof. The incident was likely caused by magnetometer failure due to magnetic interference from nearby air conditioning units, compounded by a lack of emergency disarm instructions in the manual.

synopsis: The pilot's mismanagement of the airplane's approach resulting in a collision with terrain.
summary: The pilot landed short in a field while approaching a private grass strip after the aircraft developed an uncontrollable sink rate. The accident occurred despite adding power, with the aircraft having been grounded for two years and lacking current inspections or a pilot flight review.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to properly inspect and sump the fuel system before the flight and the maintenance personnel's inadequate maintenance of the fuel system which resulted in fuel starvation and the subsequent loss of engine power due to the contamination of the right tank fuel gascolator and fuel lines.
summary: The pilot experienced engine power loss shortly after takeoff due to fuel starvation caused by sediment clogging the right tank's gascolator, which the owner had never drained. This resulted in an off-airport landing where the aircraft flipped inverted, sustaining substantial damage to the wing, rudder, and engine mount.

synopsis: A failure of the electrical system, resulting in a loss of fuel injection and subsequent loss of engine power.
summary: The pilot reported low voltage and subsequent engine power loss during flight, leading to a forced landing with substantial damage. A loose connector on the electronic fuel injection system was found, which may have caused the failure, though impact damage could not be ruled out.

synopsis: The inadequate landing flare by the flight instructor that resulted in a loss of directional control and impact with terrain.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot in a single-engine seaplane struck a sand bank and nosed over during landing after the instructor corrected a high glide path. The instructor attributed the accident to a flat touchdown attitude causing an inadvertent water loop, resulting in substantial damage to the left wing spar.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane during landing in gusting wind conditions.
summary: A student pilot flying an airplane encountered a wind gust during the landing flare on runway 20, causing a hard landing and right wing impact. The aircraft exited the runway and came to rest upright on adjacent grass with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack while maneuvering at low altitude, resulting in an aerodynamic stall and subsequent impact with terrain. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's distraction by his cell phone use while maneuvering.
summary: The pilot of a non-registered tandem airplane stalled and spun into terrain while conducting low-altitude predator control. The accident likely resulted from exceeding the critical angle of attack at 113 feet AGL and 25 knots, compounded by cell phone distraction and potential medication effects.

synopsis: The uncontained left engine failure was caused by the failure and liberation of the HPT stage 1 aft blade retainer as a result of a fatigue crack in the upper collet radius that originated from a surface connected cluster of Oxide/Carbonitride/Nitride/Carbide (OCNC) particles. Contributing to the failure of the HPT stage 1 aft blade retainer was an unknown material behavior unique to OCNC clusters in Rene 65 material that are surface connected in highly stressed material that may result in a localized reduction of material fatigue life capability.
summary: A fatigue crack initiated in the No. 1 engine HPT stage 1 aft blade retainer due to surface-connected OCNC particles under high stress from assembly interference fits. The crack propagated to final overload failure, which was not contained by the turbine case.

synopsis: The non-certificated pilot's failure to configure the airplane for takeoff, which resulted in a runway excursion.
summary: A non-certificated pilot forgot to adjust the propeller control before takeoff from a private airstrip, causing the airplane to overrun the runway and impact parked machinery. The fuselage sustained substantial damage, and the pilot refused to cooperate with investigators or make the aircraft available for examination.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to ascertain a proper touchdown point and late decision to initiate a go-around, which resulted in a subsequent collision with vegetation.
summary: The pilot landed long on a dirt runway and aborted due to insufficient remaining distance. The aircraft failed to accelerate on the soft surface, struck a tree limb while in ground effect, cartwheeled, and was destroyed by a post-impact fire with no pre-impact mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's flight into convective weather, which resulted in a loss of control due to spatial disorientation and a subsequent inflight breakup of the airplane. Contributing to the accident was the lack of accurate weather intensity depiction on the controller's display, which limited the controller's ability to warn the pilot of hazardous weather along the route of flight.
summary: The pilot of a single-engine aircraft encountered strong updrafts in developing convective weather while flying IFR, leading to spatial disorientation and loss of control. The accident resulted in an in-flight breakup, contributed to by the controller's inability to warn the pilot due to radar system underreporting of the storm's intensity.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain airplane control while practicing a power-on stall, which resulted in an inadvertent spin at an altitude from which he was unable to recover.
summary: A student pilot conducting a solo flight intentionally entered a power-on stall at low altitude but failed to maintain control, resulting in an inadvertent spin. The aircraft descended in a spiral and crashed with extensive fire damage, as no mechanical failure or medical impairment was found.

synopsis: The student pilot's selection of an improper fuel tank selector position, which resulted in fuel starvation and a total loss of engine power. Contributing to the accident was the instructor's inadequate oversight.
summary: During an instructional approach, a student pilot's fuel selector valve failed to align with port positions, causing total engine power loss. The instructor took control but the aircraft impacted a residential area and was destroyed by impact and fire.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to extend the landing gear before landing.
summary: The pilot landed a post-maintenance test aircraft with flaps extended but likely with the landing gear retracted, causing substantial lower fuselage damage. Post-accident examination found no mechanical failures, indicating the gear was not deployed for the landing.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate preflight inspection, which resulted in an attempted departure with the flight control lock device installed, and subsequent nose landing gear collapse.
summary: The pilot reported that shortly after liftoff, the aircraft pitched down and bounced because a modified flight control lock was not removed during preflight. This resulted in a firm runway impact that collapsed the nose gear and caused substantial damage to the forward fuselage and left wing.

synopsis: The pilot's unstabilized approach, which resulted in a runway excursion and impact with terrain.
summary: The powered glider pilot, distracted by a helicopter and another glider while maneuvering for Runway 26, elected to land on Runway 17. The aircraft landed over 1000 feet down the runway, overran the departure end, and impacted terrain, causing substantial damage to the aft fuselage and empennage with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate use of carburetor heat, which resulted in a total loss of engine power shortly after takeoff due to fuel starvation as a result of carburetor ice.
summary: The pilot experienced a total engine power loss during takeoff after pattern work, likely caused by carburetor ice formed during extended taxiing. This forced a landing in a field where the empennage was damaged upon striking a barbed wire fence, with no mechanical failures found.

synopsis: A commercial pilot was fatally injured when his Breese 2, N99VY, crashed shortly after takeoff during a solo test flight near Culpeper Regional Airport. The aircraft entered a steep vertical descent with the whole airframe parachute deploying only after impact, though the engine and flight controls showed no pre-crash mechanical failure.
summary: A commercial pilot was fatally injured when his Breese 2, N99VY, crashed shortly after takeoff during a solo test flight near Culpeper Regional Airport. The aircraft entered a steep vertical descent with the whole airframe parachute deploying only after impact, though the engine and flight controls showed no pre-crash mechanical failure.

synopsis: The non-certificated pilot's continued visual flight rules flight into instrument meteorological conditions, which resulted in controlled flight into the water.
summary: A non-certificated pilot and passenger crashed a personal aircraft into a lake after departing in fog and continuing visual flight rules into instrument meteorological conditions. The pilot tested positive for THC, but the investigation concluded his lack of skill and experience likely caused the controlled flight into terrain.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from powerlines during an aerial application flight.
summary: The pilot of an aerial application airplane contacted a powerline with the rudder during the second spraying pass while flying below high-tension lines. The rudder separated, causing the aircraft to land sideways with substantial damage to the wings and fuselage, though no preimpact mechanical failures were reported.

synopsis: The airplane's collision with a deer on the runway during landing.
summary: During a night landing, the pilot attempted to avoid a deer on the runway by adding power but struck the animal. The impact damaged the left-wing lateral rib and landing gear, rendering the wing unrepairable and the aircraft unairworthy.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to switch fuel tanks while en route which resulted in the loss of engine power due to fuel starvation.
summary: During a cross-country flight, the pilot experienced engine power loss due to fuel starvation after becoming distracted and failing to switch fuel tanks. He executed a forced landing in a field, resulting in substantial left wing damage when the landing gear separated and the wing dragged on the ground.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the takeoff, that resulted in an impact with a tree and the ground.
summary: During takeoff from a turf runway with a crosswind, the pilot advanced the throttle too fast and failed to apply consistent right rudder. The left wing struck a tree, causing the aircraft to spin and sustain substantial damage, though all three occupants escaped without injury.

synopsis: The improper maintenance of the fuel control unit, which resulted in air leakage and a loss of control of fuel flow to the engine.
summary: During an agricultural flight, a pilot experienced unresponsive engine power and altitude loss due to an improperly torqued P3 adapter on the fuel control unit. This caused air leakage and erratic fuel metering, forcing a crash landing that resulted in substantial wing damage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane during the takeoff and his exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall and spin at low altitude. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's lack of experience in the accident airplane make and model.
summary: A sport pilot/repairman crashed an experimental amateur-built airplane during a post-maintenance flight at a grass airstrip. The owner attributed the loss of control and subsequent stall-spin to the pilot's early over-rotation, exacerbated by the aircraft's known left-turning tendencies and poor rudder effectiveness at slow speeds.

synopsis: The pilot receiving instruction's excessive use of brakes during landing, and the pilot providing instruction's inadequate supervision, resulting in a nose-over.
summary: During off-airport training in a tailwheel airplane, the student pilot bounced on landing and applied excessive braking, causing the tail to rise. The instructor's attempt to lower the tail with full aft elevator resulted in a nose-over, sustaining substantial damage to the rudder and wing struts.

synopsis: Insufficient lubrication of the engine's internal components, which resulted in a total loss of engine power.
summary: During a night cross-country cruise at 3,500 ft, the pilot declared an emergency after sudden oil pressure loss and engine roughness. The aircraft impacted terrain following total power loss caused by a seized piston and oil starvation, though the specific reason for the lubrication failure could not be determined.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to depart with the airplane over maximum gross weight, which reduced the climb performance and resulted in a collision with a tree.
summary: The pilot and passenger departed a private grass strip in an aircraft likely over maximum gross weight. After flying under power lines, the right wing struck a tree due to degraded climb performance, causing the airplane to impact the ground with substantial damage.

synopsis: The asymmetric reverse thrust during the landing roll for reasons that could not be determined, resulting in the flightcrew's inability to maintain directional control and a subsequent runway excursion.
summary: Pilots of a multi-engine turbo-propeller aircraft lost directional control during landing rollout due to asymmetric reverse thrust, causing a runway excursion and gear collapse. Although systems appeared functional, the specific cause of the asymmetric thrust could not be determined.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane during the landing and subsequent go-around attempt. Also causal was the flight instructor's delayed remedial action.
summary: During a training flight, the pilot inadvertently fully retracted flaps during a go-around, causing a high-speed runway contact and subsequent stall. The aircraft drifted off the runway, impacted the ground with its right wing, and sustained substantial structural damage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing. Contributing to the accident was the flight instructor's failure to take remedial action.
summary: A pilot and flight instructor ground looped a tailwheel airplane during the landing roll in a slight right crosswind. The pilot lost directional control despite rudder input, causing the aircraft to exit the runway and sustain substantial damage to the left gear, wing, and stabilizer with no reported mechanical failure.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to continue flight into icing conditions and inclement weather, which likely led to spatial disorientation when he attempted to divert from the planned course to the destination airport.
summary: A non-instrument-rated pilot flying an aerobatic aircraft departed for camp and entered instrument meteorological conditions with icing above 5,400 ft msl. The pilot likely became spatially disoriented and stalled while attempting to avoid clouds and terrain, resulting in a fatal impact with no mechanical failure found.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare and subsequent improper recovery from a bounced landing, which resulted in a nose over.
summary: The pilot reported that while landing on a grass site, the airplane bounced and he inadvertently pushed the stick forward, causing the nose to lower. On the second touchdown, the propeller struck the ground, the airplane nosed over, and sustained substantial damage to the wing struts, vertical stabilizer, and rudder.

synopsis: The inability of the Boeing 75 pilot to anticipate that the Piper would stop earlier on the taxiway which resulted in the on-ground collision. The inability of the Boeing 75 pilot to anticipate that the Piper would stop earlier on the taxiway which resulted in the on-ground collision.
summary: A Boeing 75 pilot following a Piper on the taxiway collided with the Piper's right wing after the Piper turned 180 degrees to conduct an engine run-up near the runway approach end. The collision caused substantial damage to both wings, likely because the Boeing pilot did not anticipate the Piper's unexpected turn and stop.

synopsis: The commercial pilot's failure to maintain directional control of the airplane during takeoff. Contributing was the student pilot's application of brakes during the takeoff roll and the failure of both pilots to maintain a positive transfer of controls.
summary: A commercial pilot and student pilot experienced a takeoff accident in a student-owned airplane when the student held full power and brakes, causing a loss of directional control. The aircraft departed the runway, struck fences, and nosed over, with the student later discovering the elevator trim was set to full nose-up.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll, which resulted in a failure of the right main landing gear and subsequent ground loop.
summary: During the landing roll, the pilot lost directional control when the right main gear attachment bolts failed due to overstress and bending. This caused the aircraft to ground-loop, substantially damaging the right wing.

synopsis: The pilot's lack of familiarity with the airplane's fuel system, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion.
summary: The pilot of an experimental amateur-built biplane experienced an engine power loss due to fuel exhaustion during the cruise phase. While executing a forced landing in a field, tall grass wrapped around the landing gear, causing the aircraft to nose over and sustain substantial damage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to detect the tripped alternator circuit breaker in flight, which resulted in a drained battery that prevented the landing gear from fully extending to the down-and-locked position. Contributing to the accident was the improperly installed hardware on the landing gear extension handle, which prevented the extension of the handle and operation of the system.
summary: The pilot experienced electrical failure and landing gear malfunction during flight, likely caused by an open alternator breaker and incorrect maintenance hardware. The aircraft landed with the main gear in a transient position, resulting in substantial damage to the left horizontal stabilizer and elevator.

synopsis: The non-certificated pilot's unstable approach to landing, which resulted in a collision with approach lighting, hard landing, and postimpact fire.
summary: A non-certificated pilot on his first flight in a newly purchased airplane executed a steep, unstable approach and struck approach lights before landing hard and catching fire. The pilot admitted to misjudging the landing, while the investigation could not determine if mechanical issues contributed or assess the pilot's prior experience.

synopsis: The partial loss of engine power during cruise flight due to the improper installation of the master connecting rod main bushing set screws, which backed off and allowed the main bushing to shift, resulting in scoring damage on the crankshaft that led to the initiation of a fatigue crack and separation of the forward crankshaft.
summary: The pilot of a formation flight aircraft experienced engine power loss due to a fractured crankshaft caused by loose master rod set screws. This mechanical failure forced a landing at a closed gliderport where the airplane overran the runway, struck a camper, and sustained substantial damage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to extend the airplane's landing gear before landing.
summary: The pilot landed an aircraft with the gear retracted after failing to confirm gear extension due to sun glare on the position indicator lights. This resulted in substantial fuselage damage, though the pilot reported no preimpact mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: The non-instrument-rated pilot's loss of airplane control due to spatial disorientation while flying over water in dark night conditions. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's decision to conduct the overwater flight in conditions conducive to the development of spatial disorientation.
summary: A non-instrument rated pilot flying at night over the Gulf of Mexico lost control and impacted the water after diverting attention to change frequencies. The accident resulted from spatial disorientation, likely the Coriolis illusion, caused by dark conditions and the pilot's lack of instrument rating.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to ensure that a suitable landing area was available in case the restart of the motor glider's engine was unsuccessful. Contributing, was insufficient battery charge to extend the motor glider's pylon assembly.
summary: The pilot of a motor glider forgot to turn off a fuel pump during climb, likely depleting the battery. When attempting to restart the engine at 2,500 ft due to insufficient altitude, the propeller pylon failed to extend, resulting in an off-airport crash into trees.

synopsis: The pilot's exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack, resulting in an aerodynamic stall and loss of control.
summary: The pilot and passenger in a vintage biplane stalled during a local flight after the pilot likely exceeded the critical angle of attack while maneuvering. This caused a loss of control and a low-energy impact with terrain, as no mechanical failures were found.

synopsis: A loss of engine performance due to carbon fouling of three spark plugs that, when combined with the airplane's high gross weight condition, resulted in a collision with trees and terrain.
summary: A private pilot and two passengers crashed a fully fueled airplane shortly after takeoff in warm, humid conditions due to reduced engine performance from carbon-fouled spark plugs. Combined with high gross weight and density altitude, the power loss prevented the aircraft from climbing, causing it to impact trees and terrain with a postcrash fire.

synopsis: The flight instructor's failure to attain a proper touchdown point during a precautionary landing, which resulted in a runway excursion during landing.
summary: A private pilot and flight instructor practicing engine-out simulations in a single-engine airplane experienced a false high oil temperature warning caused by insufficient cooling between maneuvers. The instructor declared an emergency, executed a slip to lose altitude, and the aircraft nosed over after overrunning the runway, sustaining substantial damage.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power during approach for reasons that could not be determined.
summary: The pilot of a newly purchased aircraft experienced an engine power loss during the approach phase, leading to an emergency landing where the tailwheel struck power lines and the airplane inverted. While no mechanical failure was found, the investigation could not substantiate whether the power loss was fuel-related, though calculations suggested usable fuel likely remained.

synopsis: Maintenance personnel's failure to properly secure the EGT thermocouples, which resulted in catastrophic overtemperature of the engine and a total loss of engine power.
summary: A pilot conducting a local helicopter flight experienced total engine power loss shortly after takeoff, forcing a hard autorotation landing. The accident likely resulted from improperly secured thermocouples after maintenance, which displayed falsely low exhaust gas temperatures and allowed the pilot to unknowingly exceed operating limits.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate fuel management which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel starvation.
summary: The pilot diverted attention during preflight runup and failed to select a fuel tank with adequate fuel. This caused complete engine power loss during initial climb, resulting in a forced landing in a field that sustained substantial damage to the wings and fuselage.

synopsis: The pilot's improper fuel management resulting in a loss of engine power due to fuel starvation.
summary: During a post-maintenance check flight shortly after takeoff, the pilot experienced fluctuating fuel pressure followed by total engine power loss due to selecting a fuel tank with inadequate fuel. The pilot performed a forced landing that caused substantial damage to the right wing and elevator, with no pre-accident mechanical failures found.

synopsis: The flight instructor's delayed remedial action, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall and abnormal contact with the runway. Contributing to the accident was the student pilot's improper landing flare and go-around.
summary: During landing flare, a student pilot flared too high and failed to advance throttle during a go-around. The flight instructor took control, but the airplane stalled and impacted the runway, causing substantial damage to the right wing and empennage with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll.
summary: A pilot and flight instructor in a tailwheel airplane ground looped left shortly after touchdown on runway 22, exiting the runway despite corrective inputs. The right wing struck the ground causing substantial damage, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The jumper's unintentional deployment of his emergency parachute and subsequent impact with the airplane's horizontal stabilizer.
summary: During a skydiving flight, a jumper's emergency parachute deployed prematurely after his handle snagged, pulling him into the horizontal stabilizer. The aircraft subsequently spiraled and crashed, destroying the airplane and seriously injuring the jumper, while the pilot and other jumpers escaped safely.

aircraft: Brant T Phillips Super Cub EXP
synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain aircraft control during final approach and attempted go-around after encountering a sudden windshear.
summary: The pilot encountered unexpected windshear and excessive descent rate while landing at a private airstrip. Despite attempting a go-around, the aircraft struck a fence pole due to insufficient climb performance, sustaining substantial damage to the fuselage and left elevator.

synopsis: A partial loss of engine power due to an incorrect carburetor air inlet hose, which led to a reduction in air flow to the engine.
summary: The pilot experienced a partial loss of engine power during initial climb due to a non-compliant carburetor air inlet hose likely collapsing. This forced a landing where the aircraft struck a berm, causing substantial fuselage damage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from a trailer located on the edge of the runway during takeoff. Contributing to the accident was the location of the trailer on the side of the runway.
summary: The pilot of an agricultural airplane struck a parked hopper trailer with the right wing during takeoff while turning left. The aircraft then impacted terrain beyond the runway, though postaccident examination found no preimpact mechanical anomalies and confirmed the engine was developing power.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing rollout with a gusting crosswind that resulted in the airplane nosing over and impacting on the runway.
summary: The pilot of a personal flight nosed over on runway 07 during a landing rollout due to gusting crosswinds exceeding 20 knots. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the fuselage, wings, and empennage, with the pilot reporting no mechanical failures.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power due to fuel starvation as a result of a fuel vent line that was clogged by an insect nest.
summary: The pilot experienced engine surge and total power loss during cruise due to a fuel tank vent tube obstructed by mud dauber nesting. This caused fuel starvation, forcing a hard landing with substantial damage to the aircraft.

synopsis: A partial loss of engine power for undetermined reasons.
summary: During initial climb, the pilot reported partial engine power loss and executed a forced landing short and left of the runway, causing nose gear separation and substantial fuselage damage. Post-accident examination and ECU data showed no preimpact failures, and the cause of the power loss and RPM fluctuations remained undetermined.

synopsis: The student pilot's inadequate landing flare that led to a bounced landing, and his improper pitch control while he attempted a recovery from the bounced landing which resulted in a significant nose-down pitch attitude upon the second touchdown.
summary: A student pilot conducting a solo flight experienced a hard landing and bounce, resulting in nose gear separation and a runway excursion. The accident was caused by the pilot's failure to maintain adequate pitch control during the recovery, leading to substantial damage to the forward fuselage and engine mounts.

synopsis: The flight instructor's failure to implement the correct action for low rotor RPM recovery.
summary: A flight instructor and student practicing high-density altitude training in a helicopter attempted a go-around at an unapproved 6,500 ft site. The instructor's control inputs caused rotor RPM to decay, resulting in a ground impact with substantial damage to the fuselage and tail boom.

synopsis: The pilot's improper decision to re-attempt a takeoff with little runway remaining, after rejecting a takeoff in gusting wind conditions, which resulted in a runway overrun at a higher speed and collision with terrain.
summary: The pilot attempted takeoff on a 3,120 ft turf runway when a gust lifted the aircraft, prompting a rejected takeoff. He then re-applied power with only 800 ft remaining, causing the airplane to overrun into a watermelon field with substantial damage.

synopsis: A collision with a deer during the takeoff roll.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot aborted a night takeoff roll after three deer entered the runway. The instructor took control and applied maximum braking, but the aircraft struck a deer, causing substantial damage to the horizontal stabilizer.

synopsis: The pilot's delay in turning on the fuel tip tank transfer pumps after departure, resulting in fuel starvation to the engine, engine flameout, and a subsequent forced landing.
summary: The pilot of a vintage jet trainer experienced an engine flameout during descent due to inadequate fuel supply in the main tanks. This occurred because the pilot likely delayed activating fuel transfer switches, causing main tank fuel to deplete faster than it could be replenished from the tip tanks, resulting in a forced landing with substantial damage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the helicopter while attempting to take off from sloping terrain.
summary: The helicopter pilot attempted to relocate to flatter terrain on private property but lost control when raising the collective, causing the aircraft to move back. Main rotor blades struck upsloping terrain, resulting in a rollover and substantial fuselage damage with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: American Airlines A319 and a Hawker B300C experienced a runway incursion at DCA when the A319 was cleared for takeoff on Runway 1 while the B300C was landing on Runway 33. An ASDE-X alarm prompted the controller to cancel the takeoff and order a go-around, but the B300C had already landed, resulting in a loss of separation with no injuries.
summary: American Airlines A319 and a Hawker B300C experienced a runway incursion at DCA when the A319 was cleared for takeoff on Runway 1 while the B300C was landing on Runway 33. An ASDE-X alarm prompted the controller to cancel the takeoff and order a go-around, but the B300C had already landed, resulting in a loss of separation with no injuries.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the takeoff roll resulting in a runway excursion, and subsequent nose over.
summary: The pilot lost directional control during a takeoff roll, veering into tall vegetation where the aircraft nosed over and damaged right wing lift struts. The pilot and postaccident examination confirmed no preimpact mechanical malfunctions caused the incident.

synopsis: A partial loss of engine power due to the failure of the No. 2 cylinder rocker shaft bosses from fatigue cracking.
summary: A student pilot and flight instructor experienced an engine power loss shortly after takeoff, resulting in a crash before reaching airport property. The accident was caused by fatigue cracking and wear in the No. 2 cylinder's rocker shaft bosses, which prevented valve operation, with maintenance records failing to confirm required airworthiness directive inspections.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from power lines during approach.
summary: During an approach to an off-airport confined area, a helicopter pilot struck an unseen power line with the skid, causing the aircraft to nose over and spin. The helicopter impacted an adjacent road, resulting in substantial damage to the airframe and main rotor system, with no preimpact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to use the carburetor heat during a descent that resulted in the loss of engine power due to carburetor icing.
summary: The pilot experienced a total engine power loss during the downwind leg at 7,500 ft MSL, forcing a landing with substantial damage. The likely cause was carburetor icing, as the pilot failed to apply carburetor heat despite conducive weather conditions and POH emergency procedures.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power while maneuvering due to fuel starvation.
summary: During a glider tow, the pilot experienced an engine shutdown at 2,800 feet due to fuel starvation in a steep left bank. The aircraft subsequently crashed with substantial damage to the fuselage and wings because it lacked the glide performance to reach a safe landing site.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed, which resulted in a loss of airplane control during the go-around. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's failure to properly configure the airplane's flaps during the go-around.
summary: During a local flight go-around, the pilot reported engine power loss and deployed the parachute, causing substantial damage. The investigation found no mechanical failure, attributing the loss of control to inadequate airspeed, failure to retract flaps, and a forward center of gravity.

synopsis: The pilot's improper decision to take off with the airplane over its maximum allowable gross weight at a high density altitude, which degraded its climb performance and led an off airport landing.
summary: The pilot reported that during initial climb, the aircraft began sinking at 300 feet AGL, forcing a field landing where the gear collapsed and caused substantial damage. The pilot attributed the incident to the aircraft being 100 lbs overweight and operating at a high density altitude, which likely degraded climb performance.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power for undetermined reasons.
summary: A student pilot soloing a cross-country flight experienced total engine power loss at 5,500 feet, likely due to carburetor icing despite cruise power settings. The aircraft impacted wooded terrain one mile from the airport and came to rest inverted, though post-accident testing confirmed the engine ran normally at idle.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from powerlines while landing in a field.
summary: The pilot and two passengers in a hot air balloon struck powerlines during a landing descent, causing electrical arcing and substantial damage. The pilot attributed the incident to a downdraft from thermal activity, resulting in minor injuries to himself and serious injuries to the passengers.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate compensation for the prevailing wind conditions, which resulted in a loss of control during landing.
summary: A student pilot soloing a helicopter for landing practice lost control during a hover when a wind gust exceeded his 13-knot endorsement limit. Despite applying full left anti-torque pedal, the helicopter turned right, struck trees, and burned, with no mechanical failure found.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of control during climb out, which resulted in a collision with a tree.
summary: The pilot departed in gusty winds and lost control when the aircraft was pushed off the centerline to the left. This resulted in a collision with a tree, though the pilot reported no pre-existing aircraft anomalies.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to recognize and avoid an obstacle on the runway environment during takeoff roll. Contributing was flat light conditions.
summary: The pilot reported that during takeoff roll from a gravel airstrip, the left main wheel struck a gravel pile, causing the airplane to nose over and sustain substantial damage. Flat light conditions and gray silt-laden gravel prevented the pilot from seeing the obstacle.

synopsis: The pilot's excessive braking during the landing roll, resulting in a nose over.
summary: The pilot nose-overed an aircraft during the landing roll on a gravel airstrip by applying brakes too aggressively. This caused substantial damage to the vertical stabilizer, rudder, and both wing spars, with no preaccident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airplane control during landing.
summary: The pilot reported that while landing on a gravel road, the right main tire sank into soft terrain, causing the airplane to nose over and come to rest inverted. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the upper wings and vertical stabilizer, with no preaccident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to attain a proper touchdown point during landing with a tailwind which resulted in a runway overrun.
summary: The pilot of an airplane on final approach landed with a tailwind due to a wind shift and overran the runway, striking a fence and an occupied vehicle. The pilot cited the fence as preventing a go-around, resulting in substantial damage to the wings and empennage with no reported mechanical failures.

aircraft: Canadian Car & Foundry HARVARD MK IV
synopsis: The pilot's improper fuel tank selection, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel starvation. Contributing to the accident was a malfunctioning fuel selector at low fuel levels.
summary: The pilot experienced engine power loss during cruise due to fuel starvation after selecting the "LEFT" tank position instead of "RESERVE," causing a forced landing that damaged the fuselage and wing. Post-accident testing indicated the fuel selector lever likely failed to engage the reserve detent, drawing fuel only from the upper tank section.

synopsis: An intermittent electrical failure that switched two motor controllers off, resulting in a loss of hover capability and impact with the ground.
summary: During a hover test of an Aergility ATLIS 1 UAV, two motor controllers simultaneously switched off, causing an unarrested descent and hard landing. The autopilot failed to compensate for the loss of thrust, resulting in substantial damage to the wings and rotors due to a transient electrical event.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the helicopter while hovering.
summary: During an evening test flight, a pilot lost control of an experimental amateur-built helicopter while hovering to track rotor blades with LEDs, causing the aircraft to crash on its side. While the pilot attributed the accident to distraction, investigators found nonstandard flight control modifications that may have adversely affected handling.

synopsis: The inadvertent application of brakes during landing that resulted in a nose over.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane reported that the aircraft nosed over immediately upon touchdown on a dirt runway, likely due to the passenger applying the brakes. The incident caused substantial damage to the wings and vertical stabilizer, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain direction control during the landing roll with a left crosswind.
summary: The pilot lost directional control during landing on runway 31L in gusty crosswinds, causing the aircraft to ground loop left. This resulted in the collapse of the right main landing gear and substantial damage to the right wing, with no pre-impact mechanical malfunctions reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll with a gusty right crosswind.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane ground looped to the right while landing on runway 16 in gusty winds. The left main landing gear collapsed, causing substantial damage to the left wing, with no preimpact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from power lines during a low altitude operation.
summary: While hovering 30 feet AGL at 20 mph to dry an orchard, the pilot turned parallel to power lines, causing the tail rotor to sever them. The pilot landed immediately due to a felt imbalance, resulting in substantial tail rotor damage with no pre-impact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing roll, resulting in a ground loop and substantial damage to the airplane.
summary: The pilot ground-looped a tailwheel aircraft while braking after a fast taxi, causing substantial damage to the left wing and elevator. Post-accident examination found bent steering arms and taut rigging, which can contribute to tailwheel shimmy, though no other mechanical failures were identified.

synopsis: The pilot's improper short-field takeoff procedure, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall and subsequent hard landing.
summary: During a short-field takeoff near maximum gross weight, the pilot reported the airplane sinking and flaps retracting, leading to a stall and hard landing with substantial damage. Investigators concluded the pilot likely retracted flaps too early or took off with them improperly configured, causing an aerodynamic stall.

synopsis: A partial loss of engine power due to water contamination of the fuel system.
summary: The pilot experienced partial engine power loss while approaching the destination airport, forcing a hard landing short of the runway with substantial damage. Post-accident investigation attributed the power loss to water contamination in the fuel system, evidenced by rust and corrosion on the fuel strainer and manifold.

aircraft: Dennis T Kirby/Michael B Kirby MURPHY REBEL
synopsis: The pilot's improper installation of the aileron and flap control systems, which resulted in a loss of directional control during the takeoff roll and subsequent runway excursion.
summary: The pilot lost directional control during takeoff due to improperly reconnected aileron and flap controls, causing the aircraft to veer off the runway and impact a berm. The resulting post-crash fire destroyed the airplane.

aircraft: Oklahoma Fat Tire Flyers Llc CCX-2000
synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll, which resulted in aground loop.
