summary: The pilot reported encountering unexpected windshear at 150 ft, causing a significant sink rate and 10-knot airspeed loss that power could not arrest. The aircraft landed hard, bounced, and settled with substantial firewall damage, though no pre-accident mechanical failures were reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll.
summary: The pilot ground looped to the right and exited runway 02 while landing in 5-knot winds, causing the left wing to strike the ground and sustain substantial damage. The pilot reported no pre-accident mechanical failures and attributed the incident to the aircraft veering despite brake corrections.

synopsis: During a Part 91 instructional flight near Prescott, Arizona, a Cessna P210N sustained substantial damage after the student pilot experienced a lack of engine response at 200 feet AGL. The flight instructor executed a forced landing, resulting in a hard touchdown, multiple bounces, and an excursion off an embankment that damaged the right wing.
summary: During a Part 91 instructional flight near Prescott, Arizona, a Cessna P210N sustained substantial damage after the student pilot experienced a lack of engine response at 200 feet AGL. The flight instructor executed a forced landing, resulting in a hard touchdown, multiple bounces, and an excursion off an embankment that damaged the right wing.

synopsis: The Federal Aviation Administration’s (FAA) placement of a helicopter route in close proximity to a runway approach path; their failure to regularly review and evaluate helicopter routes and available data, and their failure to act on recommendations to mitigate the risk of a midair collision near Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (DCA); as well as the air traffic system’s overreliance on visual separation in order to promote efficient traffic flow without consideration for the limitations of the see-and-avoid concept. Also causal was the lack of effective pilot-applied visual separation by the helicopter crew, which resulted in a midair collision. Additional causal factors were the tower team’s loss of situation awareness and degraded performance due to the high workload of the combined helicopter and local control positions and the absence of a risk assessment process to identify and mitigate real-time operational risk factors, which resulted in misprioritization of duties, inadequate traffic advisories, and the lack of safety alerts to both flight crews. Also causal was the Army’s failure to ensure pilots were aware of the effects of error tolerances on barometric altimeters in their helicopters, which resulted in the crew flying above the maximum published helicopter route altitude. Contributing factors include: · the limitations of the traffic awareness and collision alerting systems on both aircraft, which precluded effective alerting of the impending collision to the flight crews; · an unsustainable airport arrival rate, increasing traffic volume with a changing fleet mix, and airline scheduling practices at DCA, which regularly strained the DCA air traffic control tower workforce and degraded safety over time; · the Army’s lack of a fully implemented safety management system, which should have identified and addressed hazards associated with altitude exceedances on the Washington, DC, helicopter routes; · the FAA’s failure across multiple organizations to implement previous NTSB recommendations, including Automatic Dependent Surveillance–Broadcast In, and to follow and fully integrate its established safety management system, which should have led to several organizational and operational changes based on previously identified risks that were known to management; and · the absence of effective data sharing and analysis among the FAA, aircraft operators, and other relevant organizations. summary: A US Army UH-60L helicopter conducting a night vision goggle evaluation collided with a PSA Airlines CRJ700 passenger flight near DCA. The mid-air collision destroyed both aircraft and killed all 67 people on board as they impacted the Potomac River.

synopsis: A Cirrus SR22T with two pilots crashed near Santa Barbara during a base turn to final while operating under Part 91. The aircraft impacted a field at 375 feet and 120 knots, resulting in a postimpact fire that destroyed the airframe after the parachute system activated.
summary: A Cirrus SR22T with two pilots crashed near Santa Barbara during a base turn to final while operating under Part 91. The aircraft impacted a field at 375 feet and 120 knots, resulting in a postimpact fire that destroyed the airframe after the parachute system activated.

synopsis: The failure of the left main landing gear forward strut.
summary: The pilot reported that the left main landing gear collapsed during the landing roll at 30 to 35 mph, causing the aircraft to rest on its nose and left wing with substantial damage. Postaccident examination revealed the left main gear strut was fractured and the rear strut was bent aft.

synopsis: A Learjet 55 air ambulance carrying four crew and two passengers crashed in Philadelphia shortly after takeoff in night IMC, killing all on board and one person on the ground. The aircraft entered a left turn, descended to 1,275 feet, and impacted a residential area with no distress calls received.
summary: A Learjet 55 air ambulance carrying four crew and two passengers crashed in Philadelphia shortly after takeoff in night IMC, killing all on board and one person on the ground. The aircraft entered a left turn, descended to 1,275 feet, and impacted a residential area with no distress calls received.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate fuel planning, which resulted in fuel starvation and a total loss of engine power.
summary: The pilot of a single-engine airplane experienced total engine power loss during final approach due to fuel starvation after failing to verify fuel quantity. The subsequent forced landing resulted in substantial damage when the nose gear separated upon contacting a curb.

synopsis: A private pilot flying an Aviat Pitts S-2B near Fellsmere, Florida, suffered serious injuries when the aircraft impacted the ground after an engine stoppage. The accident was caused by fuel exhaustion, as the pilot departed without refueling despite having flown multiple times since his last purchase.
summary: A private pilot flying an Aviat Pitts S-2B near Fellsmere, Florida, suffered serious injuries when the aircraft impacted the ground after an engine stoppage. The accident was caused by fuel exhaustion, as the pilot departed without refueling despite having flown multiple times since his last purchase.

synopsis: An onboard fire for unknown reasons.
summary: The pilot experienced a magneto failure during a pre-takeoff engine runup, followed by a burning wire smell and engine stoppage while taxiing back. Flames erupted from the right wing near the fuel cap during restart attempts, destroying the aircraft and preventing a determination of the fire's source.

synopsis: The pilot's improper fuel planning which resulted in the total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion.
summary: The pilot of a cross-country aircraft ran out of fuel while approaching the destination, forcing a landing in a grassy field that caused substantial fuselage damage. The pilot attributed the accident to failing to refuel earlier, confirming no mechanical malfunctions occurred.

synopsis: An in-flight collision with a bird in the airport traffic pattern.
summary: The pilot reported a bird strike at 2,000 ft MSL during a crosswind turn in the traffic pattern. Postaccident examination revealed substantial damage to the left wing, with no preaccident mechanical malfunctions reported.

synopsis: The pilot's distraction during taxi, which resulted in a taxiway excursion.
summary: The pilot reported that while taxiing for takeoff, distraction by a GPS fault message caused the airplane to depart the taxiway, roll down a hill, and strike trees. Both wings were substantially damaged, though the pilot noted no preimpact mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate separation during landing, which resulted in a runway collision with another airplane. The pilot's failure to maintain adequate separation during landing, which resulted in a runway collision with another airplane.
summary: The Ercoupe pilot landed at a non-towered airport, assuming the Legend Cub was clear, but struck the Cub's empennage with his left wing tip during the landing roll. Both aircraft sustained substantial damage after the Ercoupe pilot applied brakes upon seeing the Cub taxiing on the runway.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a hard, bounced landing and subsequent nose over.
summary: The pilot of an experimental amateur-built airplane nosed over while landing on a turf runway after the aircraft lost energy, bounced over a hill, and struck the ground hard on its nose gear. The pilot was seriously injured and the airplane sustained substantial damage, with no preaccident mechanical malfunctions found.

synopsis: The Japan Airlines flight crew's failure to maintain adequate clearance from the parked Delta Air Lines aircraft while taxiing in congested ramp conditions. The Japan Airlines flight crew's failure to maintain adequate clearance from the parked Delta Air Lines aircraft while taxiing in congested ramp conditions.
summary: Japan Airlines flight 68 (Boeing 787-9) struck the vertical stabilizer of parked Delta flight 1921 (Boeing 737-832) while taxiing at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport. The collision resulted from a misjudgment of clearance by the JAL crew in a congested, uncontrolled deice ramp, causing substantial damage to the Delta aircraft with no injuries.

synopsis: The pilot's flight into previously forecasted freezing rain, which resulted in ice accretion, reduced forward visibility, and a subsequent landing undershoot.
summary: The pilot departed a VFR return leg despite updated freezing rain forecasts, encountering icing that obscured the windshield despite using the defroster and ice protection system. Reduced visibility caused the aircraft to land short of the runway, resulting in serious pilot injury and substantial wing damage.

synopsis: The flight instructor's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll, that resulted in a ground loop, and a susbquent runway excursion.
summary: A flight instructor and student lost directional control during a landing roll in variable, gusty winds, causing a ground loop that inverted the aircraft off the runway. The instructor attributed the accident to insufficient tailwheel experience for those conditions, noting no mechanical failures occurred.

synopsis: The National Transportation Safety Board determines that the probable cause of this accident was the pilot's inadequate airspeed management due to workload and degraded situation awareness and his improper inputs leading up to and during the aerodynamic stall, which increased the airplane's angle of attack. Also causal was operation of the airplane above maximum gross weight, which reduced the airplane's stall margin. Contributing to the accident were the operator's inadequate safety management, which allowed the routine operation of flights that exceeded weight limitations, and the Federal Aviation Administration's inadequate oversight of the operator, which failed to identify and address the routine operation of overweight flights.
summary: On February 6, 2025, the pilot and nine passengers aboard Textron Aviation 208B N321BA, operating as Bering Air flight 445 under Part 135, were fatally injured when the aircraft was destroyed in an accident near Nome, Alaska.

synopsis: The tug driver's failure to ensure the taxiway was clear of aircraft prior to crossing, resulting in a collision with the left wing of the taxiing aircraft. Contributing to the accident was the limited visibility of the aircraft due to ambient lighting conditions and the absence of the aircraft's nose-gear light, which reduced the tug driver's ability to detect the aircraft's presence in time to avoid the collision.
summary: A tug driver sustained serious injuries after colliding with the left wing of an Air Wisconsin CRJ-200 during night taxi operations at Chicago O'Hare. The driver attributed the accident to the aircraft's lack of nose-gear lights and limited visibility, while the captain reported braking immediately upon recognizing the imminent impact.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane during an aborded crosswind landing.
summary: A student pilot soloing in the traffic pattern aborted a landing due to a left crosswind, causing the aircraft to roll and strike the ground with its left wing. The plane came to rest in the grass with substantial damage to the fuselage, engine mount, and wings, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

aircraft: Vulcanair S P A VULCANAIR V1.0
synopsis: A private pilot flying a Vulcanair V1.0 instructional flight lost engine power on short final approach to Delaware Airpark after adding power to correct a low glidepath. The pilot executed a forced landing in grass, causing the aircraft to nose over and sustain substantial damage to the vertical stabilizer, rudder, and left wing.
summary: A private pilot flying a Vulcanair V1.0 instructional flight lost engine power on short final approach to Delaware Airpark after adding power to correct a low glidepath. The pilot executed a forced landing in grass, causing the aircraft to nose over and sustain substantial damage to the vertical stabilizer, rudder, and left wing.

synopsis: Improperly torqued intake manifold bolts that allowed unmetered air to enter the engine, resulting in an overly lean fuel-air mixture, eventual failure of the No. 3 cylinder intake valve, and a total loss of engine power.
summary: During an aerial fence inspection, a helicopter pilot experienced engine power loss and performed a forced landing that resulted in substantial damage. The accident was likely caused by loose intake manifold bolts from a prior overhaul, which allowed unmetered air to create a lean mixture and burn cylinder intake valves.

synopsis: The flight instructor's inadequate preflight inspection of the airplane, which allowed the partially secured engine cowl to separate in flight.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot experienced partial engine cowling detachment at 3,000 ft MSL due to worn fasteners, causing an emergency landing that resulted in a runway excursion and left wing damage. The accident occurred because the instructor's brief preflight inspection failed to identify the unserviceable fasteners despite the aircraft being out of service for maintenance.

synopsis: A Gates Learjet 35A crashed near Scottsdale after the left main landing gear detached during landing due to improper maintenance following a prior hard landing. The captain was killed, and the aircraft struck a parked Gulfstream G200 after the gear failed to lock because the aft trunnion pin was not fully engaged.
summary: A Gates Learjet 35A crashed near Scottsdale after the left main landing gear detached during landing due to improper maintenance following a prior hard landing. The captain was killed, and the aircraft struck a parked Gulfstream G200 after the gear failed to lock because the aft trunnion pin was not fully engaged.

synopsis: An inflight upset due to an improperly secured load that resulted in serious injuries.
summary: During a high-altitude airdrop test, a 25,000lb package released prematurely due to improperly set cargo locks, causing violent pitch and yaw that injured two cargo crew members. The aircraft returned safely with no structural damage or pre-existing mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot of a Beech 58P operating a Part 91 business flight reported partial power loss on both engines during an instrument approach. Unable to reach the runway, he performed an off-field landing into wooded terrain, causing substantial damage to the aircraft and sustaining minor injuries.
summary: The pilot of a Beech 58P operating a Part 91 business flight reported partial power loss on both engines during an instrument approach. Unable to reach the runway, he performed an off-field landing into wooded terrain, causing substantial damage to the aircraft and sustaining minor injuries.

synopsis: The flight instructor's improper fuel management, which resulted in fuel starvation and a total loss of engine power. Contributing to the accident were multiple distractions that diverted the flight instructor's attention from the proper monitoring and management of the fuel load.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot experienced total engine power loss in a new aircraft type due to fuel exhaustion from the right tank. The instructor likely failed to monitor fuel levels while distracted by communications issues and student motion sickness, resulting in a forced landing with substantial damage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed while maneuvering to land, which resulted in an exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack and subsequent aerodynamic stall.
summary: The pilot aborted a landing attempt and executed a go-around at low speed and high angle of attack. The aircraft subsequently stalled, dropped a wing, and impacted the ground short of the runway due to aerodynamic stall rather than mechanical failure.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental Sparker, N769DM, experienced partial engine power loss and severe bucking shortly after departure. Upon attempting a return landing, the landing gear failed to fully extend and collapsed on touchdown, causing the aircraft to slide off the runway and separate its horizontal stabilizer.
summary: The pilot of an experimental Sparker, N769DM, experienced partial engine power loss and severe bucking shortly after departure. Upon attempting a return landing, the landing gear failed to fully extend and collapsed on touchdown, causing the aircraft to slide off the runway and separate its horizontal stabilizer.

synopsis: The pilot's improper use of throttle and brakes during engine start that resulted in a loss of control and impact with a hangar.
summary: The pilot advanced the throttle to full during preflight priming and failed to retard it before engine start. The aircraft taxied forward, veered left, and struck a hangar, sustaining substantial right wing damage with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power due to carburetor ice. Contributing was the student pilot and flight instructors' failure to utilize carburetor heat.
summary: During a student training flight, the engine lost power at 400 feet while turning base to final, forcing a field landing that nosed over and caused substantial damage. Post-accident testing ruled out mechanical failure, suggesting carburetor ice accumulation caused the power loss.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain clearance from a truck while taxiing.
summary: A student pilot taxiing to the ramp after a solo flight misjudged wingtip clearance from a parked work truck, causing the right wing and propeller to strike the vehicle. The incident resulted in substantial damage to the right wing, with no pre-accident mechanical malfunctions reported.

synopsis: The student pilot's inadequate landing flare that led to a bounced landing, and her improper pitch control during the attempted recovery that resulted in a nose down pitch attitude upon the second touchdown.
summary: A student pilot soloing a flight school aircraft flared too high, then landed flat and bounced, causing the nose gear to strike the runway and the propeller to contact the ground. The incident resulted in lower fuselage buckling, with the chief pilot confirming no preimpact mechanical failures.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain an appropriate glide path and the flight instructor's inadequate monitoring of the landing approach, which resulted in the airplane contacting the ground short of the runway.
summary: During a night dual instruction flight, a student pilot landed short of the runway while the instructor simulated an engine failure. The instructor attributed the accident to the student's misjudgment of depth perception caused by a belief that runway lights were inoperative, though the airport manager confirmed all lights were functional.

synopsis: The airplane's encounter with moderate turbulence during descent, which resulted in serious injury to a flight attendant.
summary: During Southwest flight 3338's descent from FL300 to FL250, moderate turbulence injured one flight attendant. The crew had reactivated the seatbelt sign but reportedly failed to provide a separate advisory to cabin crew before the event.

synopsis: The non-instrument-rated pilot's continued visual flight into instrument meteorological conditions, which resulted in spatial disorientation and a subsequent loss of control.
summary: An experienced VFR pilot without an instrument rating lost control of his airplane while flying at dusk in instrument meteorological conditions. The accident was likely caused by spatial disorientation after the pilot entered clouds and lost visual references, resulting in a high-energy impact with no preimpact mechanical failure.

synopsis: A private pilot and passenger were fatally injured when their Rockwell 112 crashed shortly after takeoff from runway 10 at Covington Municipal Airport. The aircraft departed at 2259, impacted terrain and trees 4,230 feet downrange, and was destroyed by a postimpact fire.
summary: A private pilot and passenger were fatally injured when their Rockwell 112 crashed shortly after takeoff from runway 10 at Covington Municipal Airport. The aircraft departed at 2259, impacted terrain and trees 4,230 feet downrange, and was destroyed by a postimpact fire.

synopsis: The truck driver's to see and avoid the airplane, which resulted in a collision.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot taxiing from the ramp were struck by an airport operations truck, damaging an engine mount. The truck driver, who was clear of the active movement area and not in contact with ATC, attributed the collision to a snowbank obscuring his vision.

synopsis: The pilot of a Grumman AA-5A experienced partial engine power loss during initial climb due to a puckered carburetor inlet duct partially blocking the venturi. He executed a forced landing in grass near the runway, sustaining minor injuries and causing substantial damage to the left wing and empennage.
summary: The pilot of a Grumman AA-5A experienced partial engine power loss during initial climb due to a puckered carburetor inlet duct partially blocking the venturi. He executed a forced landing in grass near the runway, sustaining minor injuries and causing substantial damage to the left wing and empennage.

synopsis: During an airshow flyby, the pilot of a Douglas A-20G entered a left turn with the right engine windmilling and decelerated below minimum controllable airspeed. The aircraft impacted terrain short of the runway with gear retracted, causing substantial damage and serious injury to the pilot.
summary: During an airshow flyby, the pilot of a Douglas A-20G entered a left turn with the right engine windmilling and decelerated below minimum controllable airspeed. The aircraft impacted terrain short of the runway with gear retracted, causing substantial damage and serious injury to the pilot.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate clearance from a tree during the low altitude operation.
summary: A pilot and passenger conducting a wildlife management flight in a helicopter hovered at 70 feet when the aircraft shuddered and descended after main and tail rotor blades struck a tree. The pilot executed a precautionary landing in an open field, resulting in substantial damage to the rotor blades with no pre-impact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's poor flight planning and decision making, which resulted in a loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion.
summary: The pilot diverted due to engine power loss, forgot to extend flaps, and initiated a go-around after a fast touchdown. The aircraft subsequently lost all power at 300–400 feet and crashed inverted, caused by fuel exhaustion despite gauges indicating tanks were above half full.

synopsis: The mechanic's failure to properly install the throttle cable hardware resulting in a separation of the cable and loss of engine throttle control.
summary: A pilot and technician flew a local flight to test new avionics when the throttle cable disconnected due to a missing cotter pin after installation. The pilot lost engine power during a practice missed approach at 800 feet, forcing a landing that resulted in substantial damage after striking trees.

synopsis: The inflight collision with debris during takeoff.
summary: Shortly after takeoff from a helipad, a window dislodged from a nearby hangar door and struck the helicopter's main rotor blade, causing loss of lift and excessive vibration. The pilot executed an emergency hard landing, resulting in substantial damage to one main rotor blade with no pre-impact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna T210R experienced a drop in oil pressure at 11,500 feet during cruise, leading to total engine power loss. The pilot executed a forced landing on snow-covered terrain, where the aircraft struck a barbed wire fence, causing substantial damage to the left elevator and horizontal stabilizers.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna T210R experienced a drop in oil pressure at 11,500 feet during cruise, leading to total engine power loss. The pilot executed a forced landing on snow-covered terrain, where the aircraft struck a barbed wire fence, causing substantial damage to the left elevator and horizontal stabilizers.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to secure the coolant cap during the preflight inspection, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to overheating and a subsequent forced landing.
summary: During cruise, the pilot experienced a temperature alarm followed by complete engine power loss, forcing a landing in a vineyard where the aircraft struck a pole. The accident resulted from the pilot failing to re-secure the cooling system expansion tank cap after preflight, causing coolant loss and engine overheating.

synopsis: The failure of the propeller blade due to fatigue that originated from an impact pit sustained at an unknown time. Contributing to the accident was the failure of unknown maintenance personnel to detect and repair the impact pit before painting the propeller, which obscured the damage.
summary: The pilot of a recently purchased airplane experienced a propeller blade separation during the second leg of a cross-country flight, forcing a landing on a rural road. The accident resulted from a fatigue crack originating at an unpainted impact pit, with incomplete maintenance records preventing determination of the damage's history.

synopsis: A Lancair 360 and a Cessna 172S collided at 150 ft AGL over runway intersections at Marana Regional Airport while both were in the traffic pattern. The Lancair pilot was fatally injured and the aircraft destroyed after the Lancair converged on the Cessna during a go-around, while the Cessna occupants escaped with minor aircraft damage.
summary: A Lancair 360 and a Cessna 172S collided at 150 ft AGL over runway intersections at Marana Regional Airport while both were in the traffic pattern. The Lancair pilot was fatally injured and the aircraft destroyed after the Lancair converged on the Cessna during a go-around, while the Cessna occupants escaped with minor aircraft damage.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing roll.
summary: A student pilot practicing touch-and-goes on runway 25 veered left during the fifth landing despite right rudder input. The aircraft exited the runway, striking a sign with the right main gear and causing substantial fuselage damage, with no reported mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: The total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion and the pilot's inadequate preflight inspection.
summary: The pilot reported that during final approach, the engine suffered a total loss of power due to fuel exhaustion, despite gauges reading full during preflight. The pilot attempted a forced landing on a dirt road, impacting trees and terrain, which caused substantial damage to the wings and fuselage.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate preflight planning and decision to maneuver the helicopter at a low altitude, and his subsequent failure to maintain clearance from power lines.
summary: A pilot and passenger flying a helicopter at low altitude over a frozen reservoir struck power lines while searching for wildlife. The impact caused substantial damage to the aircraft, though the lines likely slowed the descent and prevented the helicopter from breaking through the ice.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power for undetermined reasons.
summary: During touch-and-go landings, a pilot experienced sudden total engine power loss on final approach with carburetor heat on, forcing a landing in hay flats that collapsed the right gear and damaged the wing. Post-accident examination found no mechanical failure, and the cause of the power loss remains undetermined.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate maintenance and preflight inspection.
summary: The pilot forgot to reinstall the induction air filter and remove cowling plugs before takeoff. A partially ingested plug obstructed the intake, causing power loss and a forced landing that resulted in substantial damage to the aircraft.

synopsis: The mechanic's incorrect installation of the oil temperature gauge probe in the oil filter adapter and failure to test run the engine for oil leaks after the installation, which resulted in a total loss of oil and the pilot's decision to perform a precautionary landing. Contributing was the pilot's long/fast landing, which resulted in a runway overrun.
summary: A pilot flew an aircraft shortly after a mechanic installed a new oil filter adapter without testing for leaks. A loose oil temperature probe caused total oil loss and engine failure, leading to a runway overrun and substantial damage.

synopsis: The flight instructor's failure to maintain helicopter control during a practice autorotation, which resulted in a hard landing and structural damage to the tail boom and subsequent failure of the tail rotor drive system.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot were involved in a helicopter accident during a hover taxi after a hard landing caused a tail strike. The impact damaged the tail boom and rotor drive system, leading to structural failure and an uncontrolled spin that resulted in terrain impact.

synopsis: The failure of the right main landing gear tubular spring due to a fatigue crack that originated at the airframe connecting bolt hole and progressed to an overstress fracture.
summary: During a simulated short-field takeoff, the right main landing gear collapsed due to a separated tubular spring caused by long-term fatigue and fast fracture. The crack, visible through a cabin floor inspection hole, likely went undetected during previous 100-hour or annual inspections.

synopsis: The unmanned aircraft system's failure to maintain clearance from an obstacle, which resulted in a loss of control and impact with terrain.
summary: During a flight test of an unmanned aircraft system (UAS) to evaluate Safe Contingent Land, the UAS descended to avoid a commercial drone and struck an intentionally placed cart. The UAS subsequently sustained substantial damage to its upper wing struts and fuselage after an unplanned ascent and oscillation, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing roll.
summary: A student pilot in a tailwheel airplane struck a snow berm and sustained substantial damage to the right wing and fuselage while landing on runway 25. The accident occurred when the left main gear contacted snow near the berm during a crosswind landing roll, causing the aircraft to veer left.

synopsis: The pilot undergoing instructions' loss of aircraft control during landing, and the flight instructor's failure to promptly intervene.
summary: A student pilot and flight instructor practicing power-off 180° landings experienced a hard landing with a nosewheel strike after a forward slip resulted in excessive touchdown speed. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the propeller tip and forward fuselage, though the crew remained unaware until after the lesson concluded.

synopsis: A loss of engine power that resulted from fuel contamination when it was treated with a 70% isopropyl alcohol solution (antiseptic) that contained water. Contributing to the accident were vague fuel treatment instructions provided by the operator.
summary: The pilot experienced engine surge during descent while patrolling a pipeline, forcing an off-airport landing that struck a berm and damaged the aircraft. The accident was likely caused by water contamination from an antiseptic fuel additive containing purified water, compounded by vague company instructions on alcohol usage.

synopsis: The flight instructor's failure to avoid wake turbulence from a heavy airplane departing from a parallel runway, which resulted in a loss of airplane control during initial climb after a touch-and-go landing.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot lost control of their aircraft shortly after a touch-and-go departure due to wake turbulence from a departing Boeing C-17. The airplane impacted terrain causing substantial damage, though the controller had issued standard advisories and was not required to provide specific spacing.

synopsis: The airplane's collision with runway lights during takeoff due to reduced airplane climb performance. Contributing to the accident was the shifting winds during takeoff which likely developed into a tailwind.
summary: The pilot rotated late on a 2,000-foot runway in gusty winds, causing the aircraft to drift left and strike runway end lights, which separated the right main tire and damaged the left horizontal stabilator. The pilot attributed the performance loss to a potential tailwind shift and landed safely at the destination.

synopsis: The pilot's improper flare during a bounced water landing, which resulted in a nose-down and submersion of the airplane's open cockpit in the water.
summary: The pilot of an experimental amateur-built amphibious airplane reported that the aircraft bounced on touchdown during a lake landing, causing the open cockpit to flood and the forward fuselage to sustain substantial damage. The pilot attributed the accident to a lack of training on keeping the nose up during water landings, noting no mechanical failures.

aircraft: C K Ing Adventure Llc CCX-2000
synopsis: A separation of the left main landing gear during landing.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane intentionally landed on grass beside the runway, causing the left main gear to collapse and damage the fuselage and wing. Postaccident examination found corrosion-induced stress cracking in the gear tube near the fuselage connection.

synopsis: A private pilot flying a Starduster II, N78WT, crashed near Azle, Texas, while turning from downwind to base for runway 15. The pilot attributed the accident to a tip stall and lack of engine response, resulting in minor injuries and a postcrash fire that destroyed the aircraft.
summary: A private pilot flying a Starduster II, N78WT, crashed near Azle, Texas, while turning from downwind to base for runway 15. The pilot attributed the accident to a tip stall and lack of engine response, resulting in minor injuries and a postcrash fire that destroyed the aircraft.

synopsis: The pilot of an EC 135P2+ air ambulance dropped a night vision goggle case onto the collective during a positioning flight, causing a violent pitch and descent into trees. The helicopter was destroyed, and the pilot, flight paramedic, and flight nurse sustained serious injuries before being rescued.
summary: The pilot of an EC 135P2+ air ambulance dropped a night vision goggle case onto the collective during a positioning flight, causing a violent pitch and descent into trees. The helicopter was destroyed, and the pilot, flight paramedic, and flight nurse sustained serious injuries before being rescued.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power at low altitude due to an accumulation of carburetor ice while in a cruise-power descent, which resulted in a forced landing.
summary: A student pilot experienced a power loss during a solo descent from 2,300 feet, likely caused by carburetor icing despite brief heat application. The aircraft struck trees during a forced landing, but post-accident testing confirmed no mechanical defects.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain an appropriate glide path during the landing approach, which resulted in in the airplane contacting a snowbank short of the runway.
summary: The pilot flying a standard traffic pattern to an ice runway landed too low and slow after using a snowbank as an aiming point. The nose and right gear struck the bank, causing the propeller to hit the ice and the right wing to sustain substantial damage.

synopsis: Delta Air Lines Flight 876, a Boeing 717-200, experienced cabin and cockpit smoke during takeoff from Atlanta, leading to an emergency return, right engine shutdown due to low oil pressure, and evacuation with two minor injuries. The cause is under investigation following maintenance findings of near-zero oil in the right engine.
summary: Delta Air Lines Flight 876, a Boeing 717-200, experienced cabin and cockpit smoke during takeoff from Atlanta, leading to an emergency return, right engine shutdown due to low oil pressure, and evacuation with two minor injuries. The cause is under investigation following maintenance findings of near-zero oil in the right engine.

synopsis: The sUAS operator's failure to see and avoid a helicopter, resulting in a midair collision between the helicopter and the sUAS. The sUAS operator's failure to see and avoid a helicopter, resulting in a midair collision between the helicopter and the sUAS.
summary: During a medical resupply helicopter's final approach, a small unmanned aircraft system (sUAS) likely impacted the upper fuselage, causing substantial damage to a main rotor blade. The sUAS operator lost control of his drone in the area, and investigators concluded the collision was with his sUAS rather than a bird.

synopsis: The pilot's improper decision to continue the visual flight rules flight into instrument meteorological conditions, which resulted in the accumulation of airframe icing and a subsequent aerodynamic stall/spin.
summary: A private pilot without an instrument rating encountered icing and multiple stalls while attempting to navigate clouds during a VFR cross-country flight. The aircraft subsequently entered a spin, collided with trees, and sustained substantial damage, resulting in minor injuries to the pilot and two passengers.

synopsis: A commercial pilot and passenger died when their Robinson R44 helicopter crashed during a low-level aerial survey near Uvalde, Texas. The accident was caused by the separation of the forward right hydraulic servo clevis due to damaged threads and fretting.
summary: A commercial pilot and passenger died when their Robinson R44 helicopter crashed during a low-level aerial survey near Uvalde, Texas. The accident was caused by the separation of the forward right hydraulic servo clevis due to damaged threads and fretting.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control during landing, which resulted in a collision with a snowbank.
summary: The pilot, suffering from unrelieved inner ear pressure during the landing phase, landed normally but pulled the flight control stick fully aft. This caused a loss of directional control, resulting in the left tire striking a snowbank, the aircraft flipping inverted, and substantial rudder damage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to properly identify the proper anchor point for the supplemental harness and the crew's incorrect use of the restraint system structure as an anchor point, which resulted in the separation of the structure.
summary: During an elk capture operation, a gunner fell from a maneuvering helicopter after his harness anchor point separated due to side loads. The manufacturer stated the anchor was not designed for such loads, causing the separation and the gunner's serious injuries.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to lower the landing gear before touchdown.
summary: The pilot of an experimental amateur-built amphibious airplane landed on the hull after forgetting to extend the landing gear during the flare. This resulted in substantial damage to the fuselage, with the pilot reporting no preimpact mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: FedEx flight 3609, a Boeing 767-300F, struck birds during initial climb from Newark, causing right engine fire and severe damage. The crew returned, landed safely, and extinguished the fire with ARFF assistance; no injuries occurred.
summary: FedEx flight 3609, a Boeing 767-300F, struck birds during initial climb from Newark, causing right engine fire and severe damage. The crew returned, landed safely, and extinguished the fire with ARFF assistance; no injuries occurred.

synopsis: The pilot of a Vans RV7 experimental airplane, N902T, sustained fatal injuries when the aircraft crashed near Matheson, Colorado, during a Part 91 personal flight. The accident resulted from a shallow, high-speed impact with the ground while the engine was rotating and flight controls remained functional.
summary: The pilot of a Vans RV7 experimental airplane, N902T, sustained fatal injuries when the aircraft crashed near Matheson, Colorado, during a Part 91 personal flight. The accident resulted from a shallow, high-speed impact with the ground while the engine was rotating and flight controls remained functional.

synopsis: A flight instructor and student pilot in a Cessna 172S experienced a total engine power loss at 180 feet during takeoff due to decreasing fuel flow. The instructor executed an emergency landing that resulted in the aircraft colliding with a fence and nosing over, causing substantial damage but no injuries.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot in a Cessna 172S experienced a total engine power loss at 180 feet during takeoff due to decreasing fuel flow. The instructor executed an emergency landing that resulted in the aircraft colliding with a fence and nosing over, causing substantial damage but no injuries.

synopsis: The failure of the right landing gear leg due to a fatigue crack, which resulted in its separation from the airplane during taxi. Contributing to the accident, was the mechanic's inadequate inspection of the landing gear leg during the last maintenance inspection.
summary: The pilot landed normally, but the right main landing gear leg collapsed during taxiing, damaging the fuselage and wing. Post-accident examination revealed the failure was caused by a fatigue crack and corrosion that should have been detected during recent annual maintenance inspections.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power for a reason that could not be determined.
summary: A helicopter pilot experienced a sudden total engine power loss at 200 feet during takeoff, forcing an autorotation and inverted landing that caused substantial damage. Investigators found fuel present and no mechanical anomalies, leaving the cause of the power loss undetermined.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control of the airplane during the takeoff roll, resulting in a runway excursion.
summary: A student pilot lost directional control during takeoff when the aircraft veered left despite right rudder input, exiting the runway into a ditch. The pilot was uninjured, but the airplane sustained substantial damage, with no preimpact mechanical failures found.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during a gusty crosswind landing.
summary: The pilot landed a single-engine airplane in high crosswinds gusting to 36 knots, causing the aircraft to become uncontrollable and execute a 360° turn off the runway. The airplane sustained substantial right wing damage after coming to rest on a taxiway, with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: An encounter with wind gusts, which resulted in a loss of control and a collapse of the nose landing gear.
summary: The pilot delayed departure due to wind gusts, then encountered a gust during takeoff roll causing the aircraft to leave the runway surface. The airplane pitched nose down, landed hard, and collapsed the nose gear, sustaining substantial damage to the forward fuselage keel beam with no reported mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: A Cessna A150L pilot was fatally injured when the aircraft impacted snow-covered mountainous terrain near Renslow, Washington, during a Part 91 personal flight. A witness reported thunderstorms and gusting winds at the time, though the specific cause of the accident remains undetermined pending further examination.
summary: A Cessna A150L pilot was fatally injured when the aircraft impacted snow-covered mountainous terrain near Renslow, Washington, during a Part 91 personal flight. A witness reported thunderstorms and gusting winds at the time, though the specific cause of the accident remains undetermined pending further examination.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to retract the landing gear prior to landing in water. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's failure to use the manufacturer's provided checklist.
summary: The pilot returned to a lake for a water landing with the landing gear extended. The gear contacted the water, causing the aircraft to nose down, submerge, and sink with substantial damage, though no mechanical failures were found.

synopsis: A complete loss of engine power as a result of carburetor ice due to the pilot's failure to effectively use carburetor heat in conditions conducive to the formation of carburetor ice.
summary: During cruise, a pilot experienced carburetor icing that caused engine roughness and eventual total power loss, leading to a forced landing on a gravel road. A gust of wind pushed the aircraft into trees, causing a wing impact and substantial damage to both wings.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare while attempting to land with a tailwind, which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: The pilot, with limited recent experience, hard-landed a tailwheel aircraft on runway 32 during a practice landing, damaging the aft fuselage and elevator. This prevented an aborted landing, causing the airplane to strike a sign, separate the right main gear, ground loop, and exit the runway.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control while attempting to land in a gusty crosswind, which resulted in a runway excursion.
summary: The pilot attempted a landing in 13-knot gusting crosswinds but encountered a sudden lift loss, possibly from windshear. During the go-around, the aircraft veered off the runway, struck the ground, and separated its empennage, causing substantial damage with no reported mechanical failure.

synopsis: Two pilots operating a Piper PA-28-140 on a personal flight from Pearland Regional Airport experienced a power loss shortly after takeoff due to the use of 87-octane automotive fuel. The aircraft impacted a wood pile and embankment during a forced landing, sustaining substantial damage and a post-impact fire, though both pilots escaped with minor or no injuries.
summary: Two pilots operating a Piper PA-28-140 on a personal flight from Pearland Regional Airport experienced a power loss shortly after takeoff due to the use of 87-octane automotive fuel. The aircraft impacted a wood pile and embankment during a forced landing, sustaining substantial damage and a post-impact fire, though both pilots escaped with minor or no injuries.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed after takeoff due to his distraction by the opening of the cabin door, which resulted in an exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack and an aerodynamic stall/mush condition at too low of an altitude to recover. Contributing to the accident was the airplane's overweight condition, which increased its stall speed and adversely affected its control characteristics.
summary: During takeoff, the pilot became distracted when the cabin door opened on an aircraft loaded 500 lbs over maximum gross weight. The pilot subsequently allowed airspeed to decay, resulting in an aerodynamic stall, ground impact, and a post-crash fire.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain clearance from a truck while taxiing.
summary: A student pilot taxiing a solo aircraft at 10 to 15 mph misjudged wingtip clearance with a parked truck, causing the right wing to strike the vehicle. The airplane pivoted and tipped, damaging the propeller and left wingtip, resulting in substantial damage to the aircraft but no injuries.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll. Contributing to the accident was the soft, wet grass.
summary: A student pilot landed an airplane at 75–80 mph with full flaps, veered left into wet grass and mud 100 feet after touchdown, and nosed over inverted. The accident caused substantial damage to the wings and vertical stabilizer, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: An encounter with an area of moderate clear air turbulence associated with the jet stream during cruise.
summary: During cruise at FL345, Southwest Airlines flight 1425 encountered moderate turbulence, causing a flight attendant to spill hot coffee and sustain second-degree burns while serving in the aft galley. The crew had reviewed weather data indicating potential turbulence but briefed that none was expected, though charts later confirmed the aircraft crossed a jet stream with moderate-to-severe clear air turbulence.

synopsis: The pilot of a Beech A23-19 operating under Part 91 reported a complete engine power loss at 650 feet AGL during initial climb, preceded by a clicking sound. After declaring an emergency and attempting a restart, the pilot executed a forced landing into trees, causing substantial damage to the aircraft and sustaining minor injuries.
summary: The pilot of a Beech A23-19 operating under Part 91 reported a complete engine power loss at 650 feet AGL during initial climb, preceded by a clicking sound. After declaring an emergency and attempting a restart, the pilot executed a forced landing into trees, causing substantial damage to the aircraft and sustaining minor injuries.

synopsis: A commercial pilot, flight paramedic, and flight nurse were killed when their Airbus EC135 P2+ helicopter crashed near Canton, Mississippi, during a Part 135 repositioning flight. The crew reported control problems and an emergency landing before the aircraft impacted trees and was destroyed by a post-crash fire.
summary: A commercial pilot, flight paramedic, and flight nurse were killed when their Airbus EC135 P2+ helicopter crashed near Canton, Mississippi, during a Part 135 repositioning flight. The crew reported control problems and an emergency landing before the aircraft impacted trees and was destroyed by a post-crash fire.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of helicopter control after the door opened during takeoff. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's failure to confirm that the door was properly closed before departure.
summary: During an air tour helicopter takeoff, an unlatched door opened, startling the pilot who inadvertently applied right cyclic while attempting to close it. This caused a dynamic rollover and substantial damage, with the pilot uninjured and two passengers sustaining minor injuries.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control of the tailwheel-equipped airplane while landing in gusty crosswind conditions.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane aborted two landing attempts due to right drift in crosswinds. Remedial actions failed, causing a ground loop that sustained substantial damage to both wings, with no preimpact mechanical malfunctions reported.

synopsis: During a Part 91 sightseeing flight, a Robinson R44 II pilot experienced clutch light illumination and burning rubber smells near Chicago, followed by tail vibration and a loud bang. The pilot autorotated to a golf course, resulting in substantial tail boom damage but no injuries to the pilot or two passengers.
summary: During a Part 91 sightseeing flight, a Robinson R44 II pilot experienced clutch light illumination and burning rubber smells near Chicago, followed by tail vibration and a loud bang. The pilot autorotated to a golf course, resulting in substantial tail boom damage but no injuries to the pilot or two passengers.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control while landing.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane encountered a thermal during landing that deflected the aircraft off the runway centerline. While attempting to realign, the airplane departed the right side of the runway and struck a concrete drainage culvert, causing substantial fuselage damage with no mechanical failures involved.

synopsis: The improper machining of the propeller blade bearing seat, which resulted in an inflight propeller blade fatigue failure. Contributing to the accident was the improper machining of the propeller hub and propeller blade root and machining surface quality control.
summary: During initial climb at 800 ft AGL, a pilot executed a forced landing after a propeller blade separated due to an improperly machined bearing seat in the hub. This manufacturing defect caused uneven load transfer and fatigue cracking, resulting in substantial engine mount damage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain altitude during a low-altitude maneuver which resulted in inadvertent ground contact and a nose over.
summary: The pilot inadvertently descended at low altitude over a remote snow-covered airstrip, causing the nose wheel to contact the snow. The aircraft nosed over and landed inverted, sustaining substantial damage to the right wing and fuselage with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna P210N experienced electrical failures and trim issues during climb near Roswell, New Mexico, following a recent alternator installation. The aircraft landed with collapsed gear and sustained substantial empennage damage after sliding off the runway, though occupants were uninjured.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna P210N experienced electrical failures and trim issues during climb near Roswell, New Mexico, following a recent alternator installation. The aircraft landed with collapsed gear and sustained substantial empennage damage after sliding off the runway, though occupants were uninjured.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain an appropriate airspeed during the landing approach, which resulted in exceedance of the critical angle of attack and an aerodynamic stall, during gusting wind conditions.
summary: The pilot reported that a wind gust on short final to a remote gravel airstrip caused an unstable approach. After attempting to abort, the aircraft stalled and landed hard, sustaining substantial damage to the wings and fuselage with no preaccident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain the airplane's directional control during the takeoff roll.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane drifted left during takeoff roll after riding the left brake, causing the left tire to catch the runway edge and strike a fence. Substantial damage occurred to the wings, fuselage, and empennage, with the pilot reporting no mechanical failures.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power was due to a fracture of the crankshaft at the No. 3 main journal, which originated from a preexisting, thermally induced crack that had gone undetected by maintenance personnel during an inspection performed as part of the engine's most recent overhaul.
summary: During an instructional flight's initial climb, the aircraft engine lost power due to a fractured crankshaft, forcing an off-airport landing that struck a tree. The fracture originated from a preexisting crack at the No. 3 main journal that was likely present but undetected during the last magnetic particle inspection.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power as a result of an excessively rich fuel-to-air ratio due to the pilot's failure to properly lean the engine's fuel air mixture and the inadvertent activation of the auxiliary fuel pump.
summary: The pilot and passenger experienced a total engine power loss at 1,800 feet due to an overly rich mixture caused by inadvertent auxiliary fuel pump activation. This resulted in a forced landing where the left wing struck trees, causing substantial damage and fuel leakage, though both occupants escaped safely.

synopsis: A commercial pilot was fatally injured when a Cessna 525A departed Mesquite Metro Airport and impacted terrain during a right turn while cleared for a left downwind departure. The aircraft descended from 950 feet MSL and crashed into a wooded area 31 seconds after takeoff, resulting in a postimpact fire.
summary: A commercial pilot was fatally injured when a Cessna 525A departed Mesquite Metro Airport and impacted terrain during a right turn while cleared for a left downwind departure. The aircraft descended from 950 feet MSL and crashed into a wooded area 31 seconds after takeoff, resulting in a postimpact fire.

synopsis: A failure of the flight crew to ensure that the landing gear was properly extended before landing.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot landed a training aircraft with the left main and nose gear retracted due to distraction from radio traffic and the instructor's failure to verify gear position. The aircraft struck a runway sign and sustained substantial damage after the gear warning horn and autoextension system activated only upon power reduction during the flare.

synopsis: American Airlines flight crew diverted a Boeing 737-823 to Denver after takeoff engine vibrations and an EGT over-temp. A post-shutdown fire in the No. 2 engine, caused by a leaking fuel fitting and fractured fan blade, forced an evacuation with 12 minor injuries and substantial aircraft damage.
summary: American Airlines flight crew diverted a Boeing 737-823 to Denver after takeoff engine vibrations and an EGT over-temp. A post-shutdown fire in the No. 2 engine, caused by a leaking fuel fitting and fractured fan blade, forced an evacuation with 12 minor injuries and substantial aircraft damage.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of airplane control shortly after climbing into instrument meteorological conditions due to spatial disorientation (somatogyral illusion).
summary: An instrument-rated private pilot departed in IMC, entered a descending spiral, and impacted terrain after losing visual cues. The report attributes the accident to spatial disorientation, noting no mechanical failure but citing potential impairment from diphenhydramine and cardiovascular risk.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to fly at low altitude, at night, and over water, which resulted in the helicopter's collision with power lines.
summary: The helicopter pilot flew low over a reservoir at night, striking power lines at 20–50 feet before impacting the water. The accident resulted from the pilot's decision to operate at low altitude in dark conditions, increasing collision risk with unseen wires.

synopsis: The pilots' inadequate fuel planning and failure to monitor the fuel consumption which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion and a subsequent forced landing into wooded terrain. Contributing to the accident was the flight instructor's inadequate supervision during the instructional flight.
summary: During holding pattern training, a flight instructor and student experienced engine stuttering and total power loss due to fuel exhaustion. The instructor executed a forced landing into wooded terrain, resulting in substantial damage to the wings and empennage.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna 208B lost directional control while lining up on runway 17R at DFW shortly after an Airbus A321 departed. The pilot attributed the left wingtip strike and substantial damage to unexpected wind shear and wake turbulence from the preceding aircraft.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna 208B lost directional control while lining up on runway 17R at DFW shortly after an Airbus A321 departed. The pilot attributed the left wingtip strike and substantial damage to unexpected wind shear and wake turbulence from the preceding aircraft.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain control of the helicopter during a precautionary landing, which resulted in a dynamic roll over and postimpact fire.
summary: A student pilot flying an experimental helicopter experienced left tail rotor pull and rolled the aircraft into mud while attempting to land. Hot exhaust ignited grass and the helicopter, destroying it and consuming the logbooks, though both occupants egressed safely.

synopsis: A non-instrument rated pilot flying a Robinson R44 helicopter was fatally injured when the aircraft impacted the ground in fog near Danville, Virginia. The accident occurred after the pilot departed a convenience store in reduced visibility, with no preimpact mechanical failures found.
summary: A non-instrument rated pilot flying a Robinson R44 helicopter was fatally injured when the aircraft impacted the ground in fog near Danville, Virginia. The accident occurred after the pilot departed a convenience store in reduced visibility, with no preimpact mechanical failures found.

synopsis: The pilot of a Beech V35 operating a Part 91 flight experienced an alternator failure en route but landed normally. Upon touchdown, all landing gear collapsed sequentially, causing the aircraft to depart the runway and sustain substantial damage to the right wing.
summary: The pilot of a Beech V35 operating a Part 91 flight experienced an alternator failure en route but landed normally. Upon touchdown, all landing gear collapsed sequentially, causing the aircraft to depart the runway and sustain substantial damage to the right wing.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airplane control and adequate airspeed during the go-around, resulting in an aerodynamic stall and impact with terrain.
summary: The pilot lost control during the landing flare, causing the aircraft to veer off the runway toward a tree line. While attempting a go-around, the airplane entered an aerodynamic stall and impacted terrain, resulting in substantial damage with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate preflight inspection and fuel planning which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion.
summary: The pilot of a glider experienced total engine power loss enroute due to fuel exhaustion, leading to a forced landing. The aircraft struck a fence and sustained substantial fuselage and rudder damage; the pilot attributed the incident to relying on fuel gauges instead of using a dipstick.

synopsis: A commercial pilot flying an experimental Wild Sky Goat light-sport aircraft, N372WS, sustained fatal injuries when the aircraft collided with a tree during a go-around in gusty weather near Chester, Connecticut. The accident resulted in substantial damage to the fuselage and sail wing, leaving the aircraft on its side at the tree's base.
summary: A commercial pilot flying an experimental Wild Sky Goat light-sport aircraft, N372WS, sustained fatal injuries when the aircraft collided with a tree during a go-around in gusty weather near Chester, Connecticut. The accident resulted in substantial damage to the fuselage and sail wing, leaving the aircraft on its side at the tree's base.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from water while operating at a low altitude.
summary: The pilot and a passenger were flying a helicopter low over a lake when the pilot's depth perception failed, causing the aircraft to impact the water. The accident resulted in substantial damage to the fuselage, tail boom, and main rotor blades.

synopsis: An in-flight collision with a bird during an approach to land.
summary: The right seat pilot reported a bird strike at 5,000 ft MSL over mountains shattered 75% of the windshield, causing substantial damage and minor injuries to the left seat passenger. The flight continued and landed safely with no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The flight instructor's inability to overpower control inputs made by the student pilot during initial climb, which resulted in the airplane impacting powerlines and the ground.
summary: During the takeoff and initial climb of a student's second flight, the nervous student pilot grabbed the controls and applied full left aileron, causing the instructor to lose control. The aircraft struck power lines at 25 feet and crashed, resulting in serious injuries to both occupants and substantial damage to the airplane.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to initiate the flight despite identifying a malfunction in the carburetor heat system during the pre-takeoff engine run-up, which led to a partial loss of engine power during climb out. Contributing to the accident was maintenance personnel's improper rigging of the carburetor heat control cable.
summary: The pilot-owner and a pilot-rated passenger experienced a partial engine power loss during climbout due to a carburetor heat cable that was too long and kinked. This maintenance error, likely from a prior engine reinstall, prevented proper heat control, forcing a landing on a frozen river where the aircraft nosed over and sustained substantial wing damage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing with a gusting crosswind.
summary: The pilot reported that during landing on runway 27, a wind gust pushed the aircraft left, causing the left wheel to catch a downslope edge and pull it into a ditch. Despite unsuccessful rudder recovery, the airplane struck a tree, sustaining substantial left wing damage, with no preaccident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: A commercial pilot flying a Bell 206B II helicopter during a Part 137 agricultural operation was fatally injured when the aircraft struck electrical cables and terrain in a canyon. The impact severed cables and caused substantial damage to the helicopter, with the engine showing no pre-impact mechanical malfunction.
summary: A commercial pilot flying a Bell 206B II helicopter during a Part 137 agricultural operation was fatally injured when the aircraft struck electrical cables and terrain in a canyon. The impact severed cables and caused substantial damage to the helicopter, with the engine showing no pre-impact mechanical malfunction.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a hard, bounced landing and substantial damage to the airplane's fuselage.
summary: A student pilot soloing in the traffic pattern experienced a hard landing with three increasing bounces, causing substantial fuselage damage. The pilot reported no preimpact mechanical malfunctions and taxied off the runway uneventfully after the incident.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane during a go-around, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall.
summary: A student pilot stalled a training aircraft during a go-around after a hard landing and bounce on his third solo attempt. The left wing struck the ground, causing substantial damage, though the pilot reported no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The captain's failure to recognize that the airplane's location did not agree with the assigned departure runway as required per the Southwest Airlines Airplane Operating Manual, and the captain's plan continuation error when he missed several cues that would have informed him that he was not on the assigned departure runway when he initiated takeoff.
summary: Southwest Airlines Flight 3278, a Boeing 737-8H4, initiated a takeoff roll on taxiway H at Orlando International Airport after the captain mistakenly identified it as Runway 17R. The crew rejected the takeoff at 71 knots following alerts from the first officer and air traffic control, returning to the gate with no injuries.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a bounced landing and the nose landing gear collapsing.
summary: The pilot reported that a crosswind gust prior to touchdown caused the aircraft to bounce and porpoise, resulting in nose gear collapse and substantial damage to the fuselage and right wing. The pilot stated there were no preimpact mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: The pilot's exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack while landing and the flight instructor's inadequate remedial action, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall/spin at an altitude too low for recovery.
summary: A student pilot and flight instructor crashed a training aircraft during a power-off 180° accuracy approach when the student likely stalled the airplane while attempting to stretch an undershot glide. The impact caused heavy damage and fire, with no pre-impact mechanical failures found, though the student's unreported medical conditions and medications could not be ruled out as contributing factors.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power due to carburetor icing as a result of the pilot's inadequate use of carburetor heat.
summary: During cruise at 1,500 ft MSL, the pilot experienced total engine power loss and forced landed, colliding with trees and damaging the left wing. The accident was likely caused by carburetor icing due to inadequate carburetor heat application, as the control was found in the Off position.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to land with a quartering tailwind in shifting wind conditions, which resulted in a loss of control and nose-over.
summary: The pilot landed a general aviation aircraft on runway 26 with a quartering tailwind, relying on a limp windsock despite an approaching storm. A sudden wind shift after touchdown caused the airplane to flip and sustain substantial wing damage due to the pilot's underestimation of changing weather conditions.

synopsis: The pilot of a Pilatus PC-12 operating a Part 135 IFR flight reported a left windscreen crack at 27,000 ft, which subsequently blew out at 24,000 ft. The pilot diverted and landed safely at Sleetmute Airport with no injuries, while an examination of the window frame is pending.
summary: The pilot of a Pilatus PC-12 operating a Part 135 IFR flight reported a left windscreen crack at 27,000 ft, which subsequently blew out at 24,000 ft. The pilot diverted and landed safely at Sleetmute Airport with no injuries, while an examination of the window frame is pending.

synopsis: The pilots' overcorrection during the landing roll which resulted in a loss of directional control and runway excursion. Contributing was the flight instructor's inability to correct the pilot's actions because due to brakes only being installed on the pilot's side.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot lost directional control during the flare of a multiengine practice landing, causing the aircraft to veer off the runway and sustain substantial damage. The instructor attributed the accident to delayed intervention and limited braking capability, as the aircraft only had brakes on the pilot's side.

aircraft: Aero Sp Z O O AT-4 LSA
synopsis: A private pilot was fatally injured when an AT-4 LSA, N8548U, descended and struck the ground shortly after departing Bob White Field. The aircraft caught fire on impact, and the pilot had recently requested assistance securing the lower cowling following an annual inspection.
summary: A private pilot was fatally injured when an AT-4 LSA, N8548U, descended and struck the ground shortly after departing Bob White Field. The aircraft caught fire on impact, and the pilot had recently requested assistance securing the lower cowling following an annual inspection.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed during an approach and subsequent descent into terrain. Contributing to the accident was the student pilot's failure to perform a go-around maneuver.
summary: A student pilot flying a gyroplane solo on final approach slowed to follow a landing airplane, causing airspeed and altitude to decay. Full throttle application failed to recover the aircraft, resulting in a right turn into terrain 250 feet from the runway with substantial damage and no mechanical failure.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing, in gusting crosswind conditions.
summary: The pilot reported that during the landing flare on runway 35L, a crosswind gust caused the aircraft to drift right and touch down on the left main gear. The airplane subsequently veered left, exited the runway, and struck a ditch, substantially damaging the fuselage and wings with no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: A commercial pilot flying a Cirrus SF50 experienced FADEC control degradation and unresponsive thrust shortly after a recent fuel control unit replacement. The pilot declared an emergency, landed fast at Kissimmee Gateway Airport, and rolled off the runway into a fence, substantially damaging the aircraft.
summary: A commercial pilot flying a Cirrus SF50 experienced FADEC control degradation and unresponsive thrust shortly after a recent fuel control unit replacement. The pilot declared an emergency, landed fast at Kissimmee Gateway Airport, and rolled off the runway into a fence, substantially damaging the aircraft.

synopsis: The failure of the U.S. Army helicopter pilots to yield the right-of-way to the landing airplane, which resulted in the airplane encountering wake turbulence emitted from the three departing U.S. Army helicopters, a subsequent loss of directional control, and a runway excursion.
summary: Three U.S. Army helicopters departed a taxiway at an uncontrolled airport while two Taylorcraft BC-12D airplanes were landing, violating right-of-way rules. The second airplane encountered wake turbulence without damage, but the third airplane nosed over and sustained substantial damage after encountering unexpected wake turbulence during its landing.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to extend the landing gear before landing due to distraction and his failure to conduct the prelanding checklist.
summary: Shortly after takeoff, a pilot landed gear up due to forgetting the prelanding checklist while distracted by a loose seatbelt and another aircraft. The gear-up landing caused substantial damage to the airplane's belly longerons, though no mechanical failures were reported.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare and subsequent improper recovery from a bounced landing. Contributing to the accident was the gusty crosswind and windshear during landing.
summary: The pilot attempted a landing in gusty crosswinds exceeding her personal limits, resulting in a hard landing, gear collapse, and fractured engine mounts during a go-around. She attributed the accident to the adverse wind conditions and her decision to continue the landing rather than initiating a go-around after the initial bounce.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of airplane control while landing in gusty wind conditions resulting in a hard landing and collapse of the nose landing gear.
summary: The pilot landed a single-engine airplane on runway 13 in gusty crosswinds, bounced twice, and collapsed the nose gear while blowing a right main tire. Unable to maintain directional control, the aircraft exited the runway and sustained substantial fuselage damage.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate fuel planning, which resulted in a total loss of engine power during approach due to fuel exhaustion.
summary: The pilot of an electronic news gathering helicopter experienced an engine power loss at 100 to 150 feet while returning to the airport after a fuel pump caution light illuminated. The subsequent hard landing on the ramp caused substantial fuselage damage, with investigators confirming the fuel tanks were empty.

synopsis: The pilot landed short of the runway.
summary: The pilot landed short of a grass runway at an unfamiliar airport due to inability to distinguish the approach area from the runway threshold. The aircraft struck rising terrain, causing nose gear collapse, propeller strike, and substantial damage to the engine mount, firewall, and right wing.

synopsis: The student pilot's loss of directional control during a hover, which resulted in an impact with terrain.
summary: A student pilot soloing a helicopter jerked the collective during hover, causing a right spin and dynamic rollover into terrain. The instructor observed the event, which resulted in substantial fuselage and drivetrain damage, with the student reporting no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The mechanic's inadequate annual inspection of the airplane and failure to comply with an applicable airworthiness directive, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to oil starvation.
summary: The pilot experienced an engine failure during a cross-country repositioning flight caused by an unaddressed airworthiness directive regarding a loose oil filter adapter. The resulting oil starvation led to catastrophic engine failure, forcing a long, fast landing that resulted in substantial wing damage after the aircraft departed the runway.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control while landing with a crosswind.
summary: The pilot reported that during a crosswind landing, a gust lifted the right wing, and despite full right aileron correction, the left wing struck the ground. The aircraft came to rest inverted with substantial damage to the wings, fuselage, and vertical stabilizer, with no preimpact mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing roll with crosswind conditions.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane veered right during the landing roll on runway 12, causing the left wing and horizontal stabilizer to strike the ground. The pilot reported no preimpact mechanical failures, attributing the substantial damage to the uncorrected veer in 13-knot winds from 170°.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of control during landing roll with gusty winds.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane encountered stronger-than-expected gusty winds during final approach to runway 16. While attempting a three-point landing, the aircraft veered right, causing the right wingtip and elevator to impact the runway and sustain substantial damage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane ground looped during the landing roll on runway 30 while practicing landings. The accident occurred after the pilot overcompensated for a right veer, causing substantial damage to the right wing and empennage with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The failure of the left main landing gear to fully extend and lock as a result of broken downlock switch wires and the failure of the pilots to complete the manual gear extension checklist.
summary: Two pilots flying a simulated instrument approach experienced a left main landing gear collapse after ignoring a missing down-and-locked light.
