Broken wires in the gear's downlock switch prematurely stopped the hydraulic pump, and the pilots' failure to complete the manual extension checklist prevented the gear from locking.

synopsis: Improper alteration of the crankshaft propeller flange at an unknown time, which resulted in an in-flight separation of the propeller assembly.
summary: During an instructional flight, a flight instructor executed a forced landing after the engine lost power due to a fractured crankshaft. The fracture resulted from an unauthorized modification to the crankshaft propeller flange, causing substantial aircraft damage but no injuries.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from an excavator during low-altitude aerial application operations.
summary: An aerial application pilot misjudged the height of a parked excavator during a spray pass, causing the left tire to strike the boom arm. The aircraft subsequently impacted the ground, sustaining substantial damage to the wings, fuselage, and empennage, though the pilot escaped uninjured with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: A loss of separation occurred between US Air Force T38s (DRAGO61) and a Delta Airbus 319 (DAL2983) departing DCA due to a misunderstanding of the "stop departures" hard time between TRACON and Tower controllers. The incident resulted in no injuries or damage, with the T38s instructed to maintain visual separation and climb to 5,000 feet.
summary: A loss of separation occurred between US Air Force T38s (DRAGO61) and a Delta Airbus 319 (DAL2983) departing DCA due to a misunderstanding of the "stop departures" hard time between TRACON and Tower controllers. The incident resulted in no injuries or damage, with the T38s instructed to maintain visual separation and climb to 5,000 feet.

synopsis: The pilot of a Socata TBM700A was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed into a home near Anoka County/Blaine Airport while executing an RNAV runway 9 instrument approach. ADS-B data showed a rapid descent and left turn with no mechanical anomalies found, though icing conditions were probable.
summary: The pilot of a Socata TBM700A was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed into a home near Anoka County/Blaine Airport while executing an RNAV runway 9 instrument approach. ADS-B data showed a rapid descent and left turn with no mechanical anomalies found, though icing conditions were probable.

synopsis: A private pilot flying a Cirrus SR22 under IFR near Princeton, New Jersey, was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed into a wooded area after descending nose-down. The pilot failed to respond to air traffic control climb instructions, and post-accident examination revealed a fractured elevator trim motor with undetermined trim settings.
summary: A private pilot flying a Cirrus SR22 under IFR near Princeton, New Jersey, was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed into a wooded area after descending nose-down. The pilot failed to respond to air traffic control climb instructions, and post-accident examination revealed a fractured elevator trim motor with undetermined trim settings.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll on a snow and ice-covered runway, which resulted in a runway excursion and subsequent nose over.
summary: A student pilot lost directional control during the landing roll on a snow and ice-covered runway, causing the airplane to depart the left side, nose over, and come to rest inverted. The pilot reported no preaccident mechanical malfunctions, resulting in substantial damage to both wings.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from an obstacle while performing an off-airport landing.
summary: The pilot attempted an off-airport landing in a dirt field after departing a public airport. While correcting a left drift during the three-point touchdown, the left main gear struck a tree stump, shearing the wheel assembly and causing the aircraft to nose over and come to rest inverted with substantial damage.

synopsis: Maintenance personnel's inadequate inspection of the exhaust system, which allowed exhaust gases to enter the induction system from cracks in the exhaust manifold, resulting in a total loss of engine power and a subsequent forced landing.
summary: The pilot experienced total engine power loss at 800 ft shortly after maintenance, forcing a landing that flipped the aircraft. The accident was caused by exhaust gases entering the induction system due to a corroded, cracked exhaust system that the mechanic likely failed to detect during the recent annual inspection.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain lateral control of the helicopter during takeoff, which resulted in a dynamic rollover.
summary: A non-certificated helicopter pilot practicing takeoff maneuvers on a grass field inadvertently applied right cyclic while raising the collective. This caused the right skid to dig in, resulting in a dynamic rollover that substantially damaged the main rotor blades and tail boom.

synopsis: The pilot inadvertently turned off the fuel selector valve on takeoff which resulted in a loss of engine power.
summary: During takeoff, a pilot's handheld radio fell under a control cable; upon retrieving it, he inadvertently turned off the fuel selector valve, causing engine power loss. Unable to restart the engine at low altitude, he executed a forced landing on airport property, resulting in substantial fuselage damage.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate preflight inspection, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion and a subsequent forced landing.
summary: The pilot departed assuming the aircraft was fully fueled, but fuel exhaustion caused total engine power loss at 8,000 feet. This forced a landing in a field where the landing gear separated and the airframe sustained substantial damage.

synopsis: The pilot's improper fuel planning and fuel management, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion and subsequent impact with terrain during an autorotation.
summary: The pilot of a helicopter conducting aerial application experienced total engine power loss due to fuel exhaustion while transitioning between spray passes. He performed an autorotation and executed a hard landing that caused substantial damage to the main rotor blades and tailboom.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna 310Q was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed near Midvale, Ohio, while practicing 360° maneuvers. Witnesses observed the twin-engine airplane enter a steep right bank and spiraling nosedive before impacting the ground in a nose-low attitude.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna 310Q was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed near Midvale, Ohio, while practicing 360° maneuvers. Witnesses observed the twin-engine airplane enter a steep right bank and spiraling nosedive before impacting the ground in a nose-low attitude.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain airplane control during an attempted go-around, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall/spin and collision with terrain.
summary: A student pilot soloing a training aircraft aborted a landing due to crosswind drift but stalled and entered a left spin while attempting to climb. The aircraft landed nose-down off the runway with substantial left wing damage, with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: A Cessna 210L with a pilot and flight instructor crashed into a marsh near Houma, Louisiana, during an instrument approach to Runway 18. The flight, conducted for night and instrument proficiency training, lost contact after receiving vectors and an approach clearance in turbulent, low-ceiling conditions.
summary: A Cessna 210L with a pilot and flight instructor crashed into a marsh near Houma, Louisiana, during an instrument approach to Runway 18. The flight, conducted for night and instrument proficiency training, lost contact after receiving vectors and an approach clearance in turbulent, low-ceiling conditions.

aircraft: Costruzioni Aeronautiche Tecna P2002 SIERRA MKII
synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control while landing with a crosswind.
summary: The pilot executed a crosswind landing on runway 36 during gusting winds, but a right gust pushed the aircraft off the left side of the runway upon touchdown. The pilot could not maintain directional control, resulting in the airplane exiting into adjacent grass with substantial damage to the firewall and engine mount.

synopsis: An airline transport pilot operating a Cessna S550 experienced a nose gear collapse upon touchdown at Hilton Head Airport after the gear actuator fractured. The aircraft was substantially damaged with ground-down structure, but the pilot and passenger were not injured.
summary: An airline transport pilot operating a Cessna S550 experienced a nose gear collapse upon touchdown at Hilton Head Airport after the gear actuator fractured. The aircraft was substantially damaged with ground-down structure, but the pilot and passenger were not injured.

synopsis: An encounter with convective turbulence during cruise that was not detected in advance by cockpit weather radar or weather information services.
summary: United Airlines flight crew and cabin crew encountered severe convective turbulence at flight level 400 over the Philippines, causing serious injuries to two flight attendants and minor injuries to three others and one passenger. The sudden event occurred despite no radar returns or weather advisories, but the aircraft sustained no damage and continued to Singapore.

synopsis: A commercial pilot flying a Cessna 182P became disoriented while holding at Lakeland Linder and landed at Orlando Sanford after fuel concerns. The aircraft bounced on runway 36, then collapsed the nose gear on runway 9L during a second attempt due to a wind gust, causing substantial damage and minor pilot injuries.
summary: A commercial pilot flying a Cessna 182P became disoriented while holding at Lakeland Linder and landed at Orlando Sanford after fuel concerns. The aircraft bounced on runway 36, then collapsed the nose gear on runway 9L during a second attempt due to a wind gust, causing substantial damage and minor pilot injuries.

synopsis: Maintenance personnel's reuse of worn hardware during the installation of the landing gear assembly and the hardware's failure and subsequent separation of the gear leg from the landing gear box assembly during taxi.
summary: The pilot reported that the right landing gear collapsed while taxiing for takeoff from a snow-covered lake. The accident was caused by the failure of a worn, re-used bolt and nut that separated the gear leg from the box assembly under load.

synopsis: The flight control system's unanticipated transition to takeoff abort mode due to a software error in the autonomous flight control system, which resulted in a premature throttle reduction and hard landing.
summary: During a landing test of a Pyka Pelican unmanned aircraft, the ground control operator issued a land command, causing the plane to unexpectedly enter takeoff abort mode and crash. The operator attributed the substantial fuselage damage to an error in the autonomous software.

synopsis: A private pilot and passenger sustained serious injuries when their Hiller UH-12E helicopter was substantially damaged after impacting a baseball field near Rockledge, Florida. The accident occurred during a climb to 600 feet when the pilot lost control, experiencing uncommanded turns and vertical descent with yawing before impact.
summary: A private pilot and passenger sustained serious injuries when their Hiller UH-12E helicopter was substantially damaged after impacting a baseball field near Rockledge, Florida. The accident occurred during a climb to 600 feet when the pilot lost control, experiencing uncommanded turns and vertical descent with yawing before impact.

synopsis: The pilot of a Honda HA-420 sustained substantial damage and injuries when the aircraft overran the wet runway at North Bend, Oregon, due to ineffective braking. The pilot entered "wet" conditions into the FMS, but the system calculated a landing distance shorter than the actual 5,910 feet required by the updated performance supplement.
summary: The pilot of a Honda HA-420 sustained substantial damage and injuries when the aircraft overran the wet runway at North Bend, Oregon, due to ineffective braking. The pilot entered "wet" conditions into the FMS, but the system calculated a landing distance shorter than the actual 5,910 feet required by the updated performance supplement.

synopsis: The flight instructor's failure to maintain terrain clearance during an attempted go-around, which resulted in a collision with a fence post.
summary: During a simulated engine failure training flight, a student pilot hesitated and retracted flaps without adding power at 300–400 feet, causing a stall warning and subsequent ground impact with a fence post. The flight instructor attributed the accident to inadequate pre-flight briefing and low go-around altitude, resulting in substantial damage to the aircraft while both occupants escaped uninjured.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a hard, bounced landing which result in the left landing gear collapsing.
summary: During landing, the pilot bounced and attempted a go-around but stalled due to inadequate airspeed. The aircraft landed hard, collapsing the left main gear and sustaining substantial damage to the left-wing spar, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain a stabilized approach and his delayed action to perform a go-around, resulting in a collision with the runway surface.
summary: During landing at 500 ft AGL, the pilot encountered low-level wind shear that shifted a 20-knot headwind to a tailwind, causing a nose dive and propeller strike. A failed go-around attempt led to a second impact, collapsing the nosewheel and sustaining substantial fuselage damage.

synopsis: Separation of the lower nose landing gear down lock link bolt, which resulted in a collapse of the nose landing gear during landing.
summary: A student and flight instructor in a multi-engine airplane experienced a nose landing gear collapse upon landing after a go-around. The accident, which damaged the fuselage, was caused by a missing bolt that prevented the gear from remaining locked in the extended position.

synopsis: The flight instructor's failure to maintain control of the airplane during the go-around which led to the airplane exceeding its critical angle-of-attack and entering an aerodynamic stall at a low altitude. Contributing to the accident was the flight instructor's delayed remedial action and her failure to ensure that the student had relinquished control of the airplane during the go-around.
summary: During a primary instruction landing approach, a flight instructor and student experienced an aerodynamic stall and ground impact after the instructor initiated a go-around while the student likely retained control. The accident resulted in substantial damage to the aircraft, which the instructor attributed to overconfidence and failure to ensure control transfer.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cassutt III M, N5RR, was fatally injured when the aircraft impacted the ground near Haskell, Oklahoma, during a Part 91 personal flight. While performing an aileron roll in the traffic pattern, the pilot lost altitude and could not recover before impact, with witnesses reporting full engine power and no mechanical anomalies.
summary: The pilot of a Cassutt III M, N5RR, was fatally injured when the aircraft impacted the ground near Haskell, Oklahoma, during a Part 91 personal flight. While performing an aileron roll in the traffic pattern, the pilot lost altitude and could not recover before impact, with witnesses reporting full engine power and no mechanical anomalies.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from terrain for reasons which could not be determined.
summary: The pilot maneuvered a single-engine airplane near the airport at altitudes up to 2,000 feet MSL before impacting terrain while turning south at 1,100 feet. No mechanical failure was found, and the pilot did not maintain terrain clearance, though the specific cause for this loss of clearance could not be determined.

synopsis: A pilot and passenger in a Beech A36 suffered minor injuries when the aircraft sustained substantial damage after an engine failure caused by a crankcase hole and fragmented connecting rod. The pilot attempted a field landing but overshot, striking trees and rolling over.
summary: A pilot and passenger in a Beech A36 suffered minor injuries when the aircraft sustained substantial damage after an engine failure caused by a crankcase hole and fragmented connecting rod. The pilot attempted a field landing but overshot, striking trees and rolling over.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control while landing and the flight instructors delayed remedial action.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot landed a single-engine airplane on Runway 17 in a 10-knot crosswind. The aircraft veered right despite control inputs, exited the runway into a ditch, and sustained substantial fuselage damage when the left main gear folded.

synopsis: The pilot of an Aeronca 7AC operating a Part 91 personal flight struck high-voltage powerlines while flying down a valley near Cape Fair, Missouri. The accident caused substantial damage to the aircraft, serious injuries to the pilot, and a fatality to the passenger, with no preimpact mechanical anomalies found.
summary: The pilot of an Aeronca 7AC operating a Part 91 personal flight struck high-voltage powerlines while flying down a valley near Cape Fair, Missouri. The accident caused substantial damage to the aircraft, serious injuries to the pilot, and a fatality to the passenger, with no preimpact mechanical anomalies found.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airplane control during the landing roll.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane lost control during the landing roll on grass adjacent to the runway after hitting a rough spot. The aircraft bounced, nosed over, and came to rest inverted with substantial damage to the vertical stabilizer and rudder, with no preimpact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: A Bell 206L-4 helicopter operating a Part 91 air tour flight broke up in mid-air near Jersey City, killing the pilot and five passengers. Witnesses reported loud bangs before the aircraft separated into three sections and descended into the Hudson River during a southbound leg near the Holland Tunnel.
summary: A Bell 206L-4 helicopter operating a Part 91 air tour flight broke up in mid-air near Jersey City, killing the pilot and five passengers. Witnesses reported loud bangs before the aircraft separated into three sections and descended into the Hudson River during a southbound leg near the Holland Tunnel.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane during a go-around.
summary: During the landing phase of an IFR flight, the pilot initiated a go-around after the nose pitched up below tree tops, but the aircraft failed to climb, drifted left, and struck the ground. The accident caused substantial damage and a postimpact fire, with no preimpact mechanical malfunctions found.

synopsis: Two pilots and a passenger were fatally injured when a Cessna 310R crashed shortly after takeoff from Boca Raton due to a reported rudder failure that prevented right turns. Post-accident examination revealed tension overload fractures in the left rudder cable and separation of the rudder bellcrank attach bracket.
summary: Two pilots and a passenger were fatally injured when a Cessna 310R crashed shortly after takeoff from Boca Raton due to a reported rudder failure that prevented right turns. Post-accident examination revealed tension overload fractures in the left rudder cable and separation of the rudder bellcrank attach bracket.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll in crosswind conditions.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane ground looped during a crosswind landing on runway 21 after losing control while arresting bounces, causing the left main gear to separate and strike the ground. Substantial damage resulted, and while the pilot suspected pre-existing corrosion, the gear leg was altered before inspection, preventing a definitive cause determination.

synopsis: A Mooney M20F pilot, pilot-rated passenger, and passenger were fatally injured when the aircraft crashed into wooded terrain shortly after departing Chattanooga. Witnesses reported strong gusting winds and a weather cell near the accident site, which occurred 13 minutes into the flight.
summary: A Mooney M20F pilot, pilot-rated passenger, and passenger were fatally injured when the aircraft crashed into wooded terrain shortly after departing Chattanooga. Witnesses reported strong gusting winds and a weather cell near the accident site, which occurred 13 minutes into the flight.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental Azalea Saberwing, N121DF, was fatally injured when the aircraft was destroyed near Justin, Texas, during the traffic pattern for runway 35. Witnesses reported the left wing dropped and the airplane inverted into a spin before impacting the ground and burning.
summary: The pilot of an experimental Azalea Saberwing, N121DF, was fatally injured when the aircraft was destroyed near Justin, Texas, during the traffic pattern for runway 35. Witnesses reported the left wing dropped and the airplane inverted into a spin before impacting the ground and burning.

synopsis: A pilot and five passengers were fatally injured when a Mitsubishi MU-2B-40 crashed into terrain near Copake, New York, during an RNAV (GPS) approach to Columbia County Airport. The aircraft descended from a low overcast cloud layer in a steep nose-down attitude after the controller issued a low altitude alert with no pilot response.
summary: A pilot and five passengers were fatally injured when a Mitsubishi MU-2B-40 crashed into terrain near Copake, New York, during an RNAV (GPS) approach to Columbia County Airport. The aircraft descended from a low overcast cloud layer in a steep nose-down attitude after the controller issued a low altitude alert with no pilot response.

synopsis: The pilot's delayed decision to abort the takeoff when the airplane was not attaining sufficient airspeed for takeoff and subsequently departed the end of the lake and collided with terrain.
summary: A pilot departing a frozen lake in a tailwheel-equipped airplane aborted takeoff due to insufficient lift in a 6-knot crosswind. The aircraft slid off the ice into vegetation with substantial right wing damage, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to land on an unsuitable landing surface, which resulted in a nose-over.
summary: The pilot nosed over the airplane during a soft field landing on a snow-covered runway after the nosewheel dug into six inches of snow. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the wings, vertical stabilizer, and fuselage, with no preaccident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna 170A sustained substantial damage during landing at Ak-Chin Regional Airport when the right main landing gear wheel and axle assembly separated. The aircraft veered off the runway after the right wing contacted the surface, though the pilot and passenger were uninjured.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna 170A sustained substantial damage during landing at Ak-Chin Regional Airport when the right main landing gear wheel and axle assembly separated. The aircraft veered off the runway after the right wing contacted the surface, though the pilot and passenger were uninjured.

synopsis: The pilot's exceedance of the airplanes' critical angle of attack resulting in a stall at an altitude too low to recover.
summary: The pilot approached a private grass runway too fast, floated past the intended landing point, and executed a go-around. While turning left to avoid powerlines, the aircraft stalled and impacted the ground, causing substantial damage to the fuselage, wings, and empennage with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control while landing in shifting wind conditions.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane lost rudder control during a go-around on runway 5 in strong, variable winds, causing a ground loop. The right main gear separated and the right wing contacted the ground, resulting in substantial damage to the rear spar with no preimpact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The failure of the left main landing gear down lock to engage and subsequent collapse of the left main landing gear.
summary: The pilot attempted to land an aircraft after routine gear maintenance when the left main landing gear failed to lock despite ground visual confirmation. The gear collapsed during taxi, causing substantial wing damage because the down lock hook was not properly engaged.

synopsis: The airplane's encounter with a dust devil, which resulted in a loss of airplane control at a low altitude.
summary: During a slow flight test in an unregistered airplane, the pilot lost control after a sudden upward push and right wing lift, entering a left descending spiral. The aircraft impacted terrain inverted with substantial damage, likely caused by observed dust devil activity, with no preimpact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: A private pilot flying a Mooney M20J on an Angel Flight diverted to Edinburg due to rising oil temperature, dropping pressure, and engine roughness. The pilot lost engine power while attempting a precautionary landing and landed in a field short of the runway, substantially damaging the aircraft.
summary: A private pilot flying a Mooney M20J on an Angel Flight diverted to Edinburg due to rising oil temperature, dropping pressure, and engine roughness. The pilot lost engine power while attempting a precautionary landing and landed in a field short of the runway, substantially damaging the aircraft.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental Hy-Tek Hurricane HP sustained serious injuries when the engine lost total power at 100 feet during initial climb from Elko Regional Airport. The aircraft subsequently descended rapidly and collided with a metal trash receptacle, causing substantial damage to the fuselage.
summary: The pilot of an experimental Hy-Tek Hurricane HP sustained serious injuries when the engine lost total power at 100 feet during initial climb from Elko Regional Airport. The aircraft subsequently descended rapidly and collided with a metal trash receptacle, causing substantial damage to the fuselage.

synopsis: The pilot's improper fuel management, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel starvation.
summary: During a cross-country climb through 6,300 feet, the pilot experienced total engine power loss after selecting an empty fuel tank while managing electrical issues. This fuel starvation forced a landing on a dirt road where the left wing struck a berm, causing substantial damage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during takeoff roll with a left crosswind.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane ground looped to the right during takeoff on runway 33 while correcting a left veer caused by a 13-knot crosswind. The accident resulted in substantial damage to the left wing and elevator, with no preimpact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna 182L reported engine power loss while climbing to 4,500 ft MSL near Henderson, Nevada, causing the aircraft to lose airspeed and altitude. The pilot executed an emergency landing in a ditch to avoid traffic, resulting in substantial damage to the fuselage and wings, though occupants sustained only minor or no injuries.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna 182L reported engine power loss while climbing to 4,500 ft MSL near Henderson, Nevada, causing the aircraft to lose airspeed and altitude. The pilot executed an emergency landing in a ditch to avoid traffic, resulting in substantial damage to the fuselage and wings, though occupants sustained only minor or no injuries.

synopsis: The pilot of a Bell 206B helicopter practicing takeoffs and landings experienced engine power loss and a chip detector light at 800 feet AGL. He executed an autorotation into an open field, but the tailboom separated upon landing, causing substantial damage to the aircraft.
summary: The pilot of a Bell 206B helicopter practicing takeoffs and landings experienced engine power loss and a chip detector light at 800 feet AGL. He executed an autorotation into an open field, but the tailboom separated upon landing, causing substantial damage to the aircraft.

synopsis: The malfunction of the throttle servo which resulted in the complete loss of engine power.
summary: The UAS operator reported that a throttle servo malfunction caused complete engine power loss during a test flight. The pilot maneuvered the aircraft to a safe location where it impacted terrain, resulting in substantial damage to the fuselage and flight control surfaces.

synopsis: Frontier Airlines flight crew operating an Airbus A321NX sustained nose gear and engine damage during a hard landing at San Juan after a go-around attempt. The nose wheel separated upon touchdown, ingesting debris into the left engine, though all 235 occupants remained uninjured.
summary: Frontier Airlines flight crew operating an Airbus A321NX sustained nose gear and engine damage during a hard landing at San Juan after a go-around attempt. The nose wheel separated upon touchdown, ingesting debris into the left engine, though all 235 occupants remained uninjured.

synopsis: Serious Injury to a flight attendant sustained during an evacuation.
summary: Southwest Airlines flight 3006 experienced a right engine failure during climb-out from Houston, prompting an emergency return and evacuation due to a reported burning odor. One flight attendant sustained a hairline ankle fracture during the evacuation, which the captain initiated after confirming the odor persisted post-landing.

synopsis: The pilot of a Beech A24 experienced total engine power loss at 50 feet AGL during initial climb at Greenville Downtown Airport. While attempting a forced landing to avoid approach lights, the pilot banked right, causing an aerodynamic stall and terrain impact that substantially damaged the aircraft.
summary: The pilot of a Beech A24 experienced total engine power loss at 50 feet AGL during initial climb at Greenville Downtown Airport. While attempting a forced landing to avoid approach lights, the pilot banked right, causing an aerodynamic stall and terrain impact that substantially damaged the aircraft.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane while landing in gusting crosswind conditions.
summary: A student pilot performing solo landings encountered a left crosswind that pushed the aircraft onto its nose gear, flipping it over and damaging the vertical stabilizer. The pilot reported no mechanical failures, noting ATC had previously advised of the crosswind conditions.

synopsis: A Cessna 180 pilot and two passengers were fatally injured when the aircraft struck high-tension powerlines over a river near Fremont, Nebraska, during a personal flight. The pilot ignored advice against flying in low light, collided with the lines, and subsequently crashed into the river while the engine was still running.
summary: A Cessna 180 pilot and two passengers were fatally injured when the aircraft struck high-tension powerlines over a river near Fremont, Nebraska, during a personal flight. The pilot ignored advice against flying in low light, collided with the lines, and subsequently crashed into the river while the engine was still running.

synopsis: A private pilot flying a Cessna 180G was fatally injured with three passengers when the aircraft struck power lines and crashed near Trilla, Illinois. The accident occurred during a visual flight rules flight in misting conditions, with a witness reporting an unusually low engine sound before an explosion.
summary: A private pilot flying a Cessna 180G was fatally injured with three passengers when the aircraft struck power lines and crashed near Trilla, Illinois. The accident occurred during a visual flight rules flight in misting conditions, with a witness reporting an unusually low engine sound before an explosion.

synopsis: The reported loss of engine power for undetermined reasons.
summary: About 20 minutes after departure, a pilot experienced a total engine power loss and performed a forced landing in a cornfield, sustaining substantial wing damage. A mechanic later confirmed fuel flow and magneto operation but could not complete a comprehensive examination to determine the cause.

synopsis: The non-certificated pilot's failure to maintain altitude while maneuvering at low altitude that resulted in a descent and impact into terrain.
summary: A non-certificated pilot flying a private aircraft descended to 200 feet AGL to drop candy but became distracted while looking left, causing the airplane to impact terrain. The left wing spar sustained substantial damage, and the pilot reported no mechanical failure.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain direction control of the airplane during the landing roll.
summary: During a full stall landing in a tailwheel-equipped airplane, the pilot applied the left brake to correct a rightward veer, causing the aircraft to nose over and come to rest inverted. The pilot reported no pre-accident mechanical failures, resulting in substantial damage to the fuselage and empennage with no injuries.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate inflight planning and an encounter with atmospheric conditions where the lift was not sufficient to maintain flight, resulting in an off-airport landing and collision with a fence.
summary: The glider pilot, while returning from a downwind release, attempted to clear a fence during an off-airport landing after losing altitude. Retracting spoilers and pitching up caused a stall, resulting in a fence pole impact and substantial wing damage, which the pilot attributed to the initial downwind release.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental D'Apuzzo Senior Aero Sport experienced a total engine power loss at 1,000 feet AGL during a go-around near Phoenix, Arizona. After failing to restart the engine, the pilot executed a forced landing off-airport, impacting a carport roof and substantially damaging the aircraft.
summary: The pilot of an experimental D'Apuzzo Senior Aero Sport experienced a total engine power loss at 1,000 feet AGL during a go-around near Phoenix, Arizona. After failing to restart the engine, the pilot executed a forced landing off-airport, impacting a carport roof and substantially damaging the aircraft.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to configure the airplane for a water landing.
summary: The pilot of an amphibious airplane touched down on a river with landing gear extended after neglecting to verify gear position. This resulted in the aircraft nosing down and sustaining substantial fuselage damage, with no preimpact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The glider's encounter with atmospheric conditions where the lift was not sufficient to maintain flight.
summary: A flight instructor piloting a glider on final approach experienced a loss of lift and insufficient altitude to reach the airport. The instructor landed in an orchard, striking trees and causing substantial damage to the left wing and horizontal stabilizer, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airplane control during takeoff with a left quartering crosswind.
summary: During takeoff in a free-castering nosewheel airplane with a left quartering crosswind, the pilot corrected right drift with left aileron, causing a nose-down pitch and stall warning. Ground contact damaged the rudder and wings, though the pilot completed the flight and reported no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control while landing with a crosswind.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane reported that during landing rollout in a 9-knot left crosswind, the aircraft veered left and departed the runway into a ditch. Both wings sustained substantial damage, though the pilot reported no pre-accident mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane reported that while on final for runway 9, the aircraft sank and hit the runway about 10 feet above ground level. It subsequently veered left, exited the runway, and impacted trees, causing substantial damage to the wings and fuselage with no preaccident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane during an attempted go around in gusty tailwind conditions, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall and impact with terrain.
summary: During final approach, a pilot encountered sudden strong tailwind gusts and initiated a go-around to avoid obstacles. At approximately 20 feet, another gust caused a right wing stall, resulting in a ground impact that substantially damaged the aircraft, with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during takeoff. Contributing to the accident was the pilot inadvertently using a runway that resulted in a tailwind condition and the flight instructors delayed remedial action.
summary: A student pilot and flight instructor conducting a simulated soft-field takeoff drifted left, settled back on the runway, and struck a directional sign while aborting. The pilot reported no mechanical failures, though winds were variable and gusty prior to the accident that caused substantial left wing damage.

synopsis: The airplane's encounter with moderate turbulence during descent.
summary: During Southwest Flight 2782's descent into Tulsa, a flight attendant sustained serious spinal injuries after leaving her jumpseat to prepare the cabin despite turbulence briefings. The injury occurred when moderate turbulence at 15,000 feet caused her to become airborne and strike the floor.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna T210N experienced alternator failure, smoke, oil spray, and an engine seizure during a personal flight near Fayetteville, Arkansas. The pilot glided back to Drake Field, but the landing gear collapsed on touchdown, causing substantial damage to the fuselage and horizontal stabilizer.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna T210N experienced alternator failure, smoke, oil spray, and an engine seizure during a personal flight near Fayetteville, Arkansas. The pilot glided back to Drake Field, but the landing gear collapsed on touchdown, causing substantial damage to the fuselage and horizontal stabilizer.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane during the takeoff. Contributing was the flight instructor's lack of remedial action.
summary: The pilot, flight instructor, and passenger attempted a takeoff from a 3,400-ft turf runway but lifted off too soon at low speed. The aircraft became uncontrollable after bouncing and striking the ground with the left wing, departing the runway, impacting trees, and burning.

aircraft: Mx Aircraft Tech Pty Ltd MXS
synopsis: A counterweight plug that loosened during the accident flight, jammed the elevator, and resulted in loss of control during landing.
summary: The pilot of an aerobatic airplane lost control during landing approach after a missing left elevator counterweight plug jammed the elevator. The plug, a custom modification lacking installation instructions, likely loosened and contacted stabilizer hardware, causing the aircraft to impact the ground.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the initial climb at night from a confined area landing zone, that resulted in an impact with a tree, a loss of control, and a subsequent impact with terrain.
summary: During a night takeoff from a confined landing zone, the pilot used power lines as a visual reference but drifted rearward, causing the tail rotor to strike a tree. The helicopter crashed and caught fire, sustaining substantial damage, though all three occupants escaped with assistance from ground personnel.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate preflight inspection, and inadequate inflight fuel management, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel starvation and subsequent forced landing.
summary: The pilot of a multi-engine airplane experienced total power loss in both engines at 3,000 ft due to fuel starvation caused by inaccurate fuel indicators and failure to visually check tanks. The aircraft subsequently crashed into wooded terrain, sustaining substantial damage to the fuselage, empennage, and wings.

synopsis: A private pilot flying a Mooney M20TN with two passengers crashed near Sparta, Tennessee, while returning from Alabama. The accident, which fatally injured all on board, was caused by an internal engine catastrophic malfunction involving a fractured No. 3 cylinder connecting rod.
summary: A private pilot flying a Mooney M20TN with two passengers crashed near Sparta, Tennessee, while returning from Alabama. The accident, which fatally injured all on board, was caused by an internal engine catastrophic malfunction involving a fractured No. 3 cylinder connecting rod.

synopsis: Maintenance personnel's failure to identify and remediate water contamination of the airplane's fuel system, which resulted in a partial loss of engine power during initial climb.
summary: The pilot experienced an uncommanded engine power loss during initial climb due to severe water contamination in the fuel system. Post-accident examination attributed the contamination to prolonged outdoor storage and degraded tank seals, which maintenance and preflight inspections failed to adequately identify or remediate.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power on approach due to carburetor ice.
summary: During a tailwheel instructional landing, the student pilot experienced total engine power loss after setting carburetor heat to a prohibited mid-range position, likely causing carburetor ice. The instructor diverted to a field to avoid obstacles, but the aircraft struck a fence, collapsing the right gear and resting on its right wing.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna T207 operating a Part 135 flight for Smokey Bay Air fatally crashed near Nanwalek, Alaska, while attempting a go-around due to a reported object on the runway. The aircraft entered a steep left bank, lost control, and spiraled into the beach, killing the pilot and one passenger while seriously injuring another.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna T207 operating a Part 135 flight for Smokey Bay Air fatally crashed near Nanwalek, Alaska, while attempting a go-around due to a reported object on the runway. The aircraft entered a steep left bank, lost control, and spiraled into the beach, killing the pilot and one passenger while seriously injuring another.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll.
summary: The pilot executed a no-flap approach to runway 35 in 15-knot north winds, veered off the runway, and attempted a go-around that triggered a stall warning. After touching down again, insufficient braking caused the aircraft to exit the runway and strike an agricultural ditch, sustaining substantial damage with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack during the final approach to land, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall and impact with terrain.
summary: A glider pilot returning to a local airport for landing experienced a descent and right wing drop during the final approach, impacting the ground 0.5 miles short of the runway. The pilot reported no mechanical failures, though the right wing sustained substantial damage.

synopsis: The flight instructor's delayed response to an improper landing approach and runway overshoot, which resulted in an impact with an airport perimeter fence and trees.
summary: During an instructional flight, the flight instructor lost control while executing a go-around after overshooting the runway. The aircraft struck a fence post and trees, causing a fire; the student pilot self-extricated, but the instructor remained inside.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane during an aborted landing, which resulted in a runway excursion.
summary: During landing, the pilot pitched up to stop nose gear shaking, causing a hard bounce and aborted landing. The aircraft veered left off the runway, collapsing the nose gear and sustaining substantial damage to the wings and empennage, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a hard landing and the collapse of the nose landing gear.
summary: During a practice landing, a gust caused the pilot to hard-land on the right gear, bounce, and collapse the nose gear, resulting in a post-impact engine fire and substantial fuselage damage. The pilot reported no pre-accident mechanical failures or flight control issues.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control of the airplane while landing in gusting crosswind conditions, which resulted in the left wing impacting the runway.
summary: The pilot of a vintage tailwheel airplane landed on runway 5 in gusty, variable winds despite ATC warnings. The aircraft weathervaned right after touchdown, causing the left wing to strike the runway and sustain substantial damage due to the high crosswind component.

synopsis: The airplane's impact with the ocean for undetermined reasons based on the available evidence.
summary: A pilot flying a float-equipped airplane on a ferry flight from St. John's to Santa Maria disappeared over the Atlantic after reporting ice and climbing to 7,000 ft. ADS-B data showed a rapid descent to the ocean surface followed by a 180-degree turn before signal loss, and the aircraft and pilot remain missing.

synopsis: An improperly tightened B-nut fitting at the fuel flow divider, which resulted in a fuel leak and loss of engine power due to fuel starvation, and the inadequate maintenance inspection, which failed to detect and correct the discrepancy.
summary: The pilot lost all engine power shortly after turning onto the left base leg due to fuel starvation caused by a loose B-nut fitting on the fuel flow divider inlet line. The aircraft struck trees and crashed after the pilot attempted to land in an open area.

synopsis: Two flight crew members on an Amazon Prime Air Boeing 767-319 cargo flight diverted from Lihue to Honolulu due to an inoperative horizontal stabilizer that caused autopilot disconnects and required significant down pressure on the yoke. The crew landed safely after the stabilizer remained stuck despite checklist procedures, with no EICAS warning received.
summary: Two flight crew members on an Amazon Prime Air Boeing 767-319 cargo flight diverted from Lihue to Honolulu due to an inoperative horizontal stabilizer that caused autopilot disconnects and required significant down pressure on the yoke. The crew landed safely after the stabilizer remained stuck despite checklist procedures, with no EICAS warning received.

synopsis: Maintenance personnel's improper maintenance, which resulted in a loss of engine power due to fuel starvation as the result of a loose fuel line B-nut. Contributing to the accident was an inadequate 100-hour inspection performed after the recent maintenance.
summary: During a survey flight, a pilot experienced sudden engine power loss and made an emergency landing, sustaining substantial fuselage damage. Post-accident examination revealed a loose B-nut on the fuel line and multiple maintenance discrepancies, indicating an inadequate 100-hour inspection performed one week prior.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain obstacle clearance which resulted in an in-flight collision with a tree. Contributing to the accident was his impairment from the effects of alcohol consumption.
summary: The pilot departed an unknown airstrip and made an emergency landing at a US Army airfield after the left wing strut was damaged by a tree impact. The pilot appeared under the influence of alcohol, was found with an open container, and was transported to the hospital.

synopsis: A DCA Local Control controller, managing a combined position with a trainee, lost separation between a UH-60 Blackhawk (PAT23) and an Embraer 170 (RPA5825) near DCA. The incident resulted in a closest proximity of 0.4 miles laterally and 200 feet vertically while the helicopter climbed above the Pentagon and the airliner was on approach.
summary: A DCA Local Control controller, managing a combined position with a trainee, lost separation between a UH-60 Blackhawk (PAT23) and an Embraer 170 (RPA5825) near DCA. The incident resulted in a closest proximity of 0.4 miles laterally and 200 feet vertically while the helicopter climbed above the Pentagon and the airliner was on approach.

synopsis: The pilot and passenger of an experimental Van's RV-10 were fatally injured when the aircraft crashed near Simi Valley, California, during an IFR approach. ADS-B data showed erratic heading deviations and altitude changes below a 300-foot cloud layer before the airplane entered a rapid nose-down descent and impacted residential structures.
summary: The pilot and passenger of an experimental Van's RV-10 were fatally injured when the aircraft crashed near Simi Valley, California, during an IFR approach. ADS-B data showed erratic heading deviations and altitude changes below a 300-foot cloud layer before the airplane entered a rapid nose-down descent and impacted residential structures.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper J3C-65 was fatally injured when the aircraft entered an uncontrollable right bank and impacted the ground near Wilson, Kansas, during a personal flight. The pilot reportedly ignored a known right-turning tendency requiring constant left control pressure, which likely caused the loss of control.
summary: The pilot of a Piper J3C-65 was fatally injured when the aircraft entered an uncontrollable right bank and impacted the ground near Wilson, Kansas, during a personal flight. The pilot reportedly ignored a known right-turning tendency requiring constant left control pressure, which likely caused the loss of control.

synopsis: An encounter with hail during descent.
summary: Southwest Airlines flight 2231 encountered hail and turbulence during descent into Nashville, sustaining damage to wing and stabilizer leading edges. The crew entered severe weather not depicted on onboard radar or EFB apps, though the specific cause for this detection failure was undetermined.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate preflight inspection, which resulted in a loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion.
summary: The pilot of a local flight experienced an engine power loss shortly after departure due to fuel exhaustion, despite gauges indicating 10 gallons. He attempted a forced landing in a cabbage field, resulting in substantial damage to the fuselage and right wing after the nose gear collapsed.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing technique that allowed the helicopter's right skid to get caught on the landing platform, which resulted in a dynamic rollover.
summary: After a news gathering flight, the pilot landed a helicopter off-center on a dolly platform. While attempting to back out, the right skid caught, causing a dynamic rollover and substantial damage with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The disconnected throttle control that resulted in a loss of engine power due to improper maintenance.
summary: A student pilot executing a go-around on final approach experienced total engine power loss due to a disconnected throttle cable, forcing a landing that resulted in a nose-over and substantial airframe damage. Post-accident investigation revealed the cable was disconnected after an apprentice replaced the carburetor during a recent 100-hour inspection without full mechanic verification.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental FFF LLC Express 2000 FT was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed near Polk, Ohio, after encountering severe thunderstorms and heavy precipitation. The pilot reported a rough ride and loss of control while attempting to land at Ashland County Airport, leading to an impact with terrain in a right turn.
summary: The pilot of an experimental FFF LLC Express 2000 FT was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed near Polk, Ohio, after encountering severe thunderstorms and heavy precipitation. The pilot reported a rough ride and loss of control while attempting to land at Ashland County Airport, leading to an impact with terrain in a right turn.

synopsis: A Cessna 182P pilot and passenger were injured when the aircraft pitched up uncommanded during initial climb from a grass strip, triggering a stall warning before impacting trees. The pilot reported that control inputs and trim adjustments failed to correct the pitch attitude, resulting in substantial damage to the airplane.
summary: A Cessna 182P pilot and passenger were injured when the aircraft pitched up uncommanded during initial climb from a grass strip, triggering a stall warning before impacting trees. The pilot reported that control inputs and trim adjustments failed to correct the pitch attitude, resulting in substantial damage to the airplane.

synopsis: The student pilot's inadvertent brake application during the touchdown, that resulted in abnormal runway contact and a loss of directional control. Contributing to the accident was the flight instructor's inadequate supervision of the student pilot during the landing.
summary: During a student pilot's landing, the aircraft swerved left and crashed due to suspected inadvertent brake application by the student. The flight instructor could not recover control, resulting in substantial damage to the engine mount, though no mechanical failures were reported.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental Long EZE, N433EZ, reported that left brake failure during the landing roll at Ryan Field Airport caused the aircraft to veer right and exit the runway. The left canard subsequently struck a runway sign, resulting in substantial damage to the aircraft while the pilot remained uninjured.
summary: The pilot of an experimental Long EZE, N433EZ, reported that left brake failure during the landing roll at Ryan Field Airport caused the aircraft to veer right and exit the runway. The left canard subsequently struck a runway sign, resulting in substantial damage to the aircraft while the pilot remained uninjured.

aircraft: Chris Wallen/Michael Pliske JUST ACFT HIGHLANDER
synopsis: The pilot's inadvertent application of brake pressure during landing, which resulted in a nose over.
summary: The pilot inadvertently applied brake pressure during landing due to feet being too high on the rudder pedals. This caused the airplane to nose over, resulting in substantial damage to the vertical stabilizer, empennage, and fuselage with no preimpact mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate roll control of the light sport airplane while on final approach to the airstrip with a crosswind.
summary: The pilot of a light sport airplane experienced a ground impact during final approach to a grass airstrip after a right wind gust caused a left roll. The left wing struck the ground, spinning the aircraft and causing substantial damage, with no preimpact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack during climb out from an aborted landing.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane aborted a landing due to centerline difficulties, then experienced poor climb performance and drift during the go-around. The aircraft subsequently stalled and impacted nose down with substantial wing damage, though the pilot reported no pre-impact mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing roll.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane ground looped left during the landing roll on runway 28R due to incorrect crosswind correction. The right wing impacted the runway, causing substantial damage to the wing and aileron with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control while landing in gusting wind conditions.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane veered left off runway 25 during landing due to a sudden 22-knot gust from 360°. The aircraft struck a fence, causing substantial damage to the right elevator and fuselage after the rudder steering arm separated.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna 180F reported that left rudder input failed to correct right drift during landing rollout at Halliburton Field, causing the aircraft to depart the runway and nose over in soft turf. A post-accident examination revealed a fractured left rudder cable, resulting in substantial damage to the vertical stabilizer, rudder, and wings, though occupants were uninjured.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna 180F reported that left rudder input failed to correct right drift during landing rollout at Halliburton Field, causing the aircraft to depart the runway and nose over in soft turf. A post-accident examination revealed a fractured left rudder cable, resulting in substantial damage to the vertical stabilizer, rudder, and wings, though occupants were uninjured.

synopsis: Two pilots and 11 passengers flew a DeHavilland DHC-6-300 from Arizona to Nevada when they encountered brief turbulence and hail while maneuvering for weather near Boulder City. The encounter caused substantial damage to the wings and stabilizers, though the flight landed uneventfully with no injuries.
summary: Two pilots and 11 passengers flew a DeHavilland DHC-6-300 from Arizona to Nevada when they encountered brief turbulence and hail while maneuvering for weather near Boulder City. The encounter caused substantial damage to the wings and stabilizers, though the flight landed uneventfully with no injuries.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to take off despite having problems controlling the airplane due to his physical stature.
summary: The pilot experienced rudder control issues due to his physical stature, causing his knees to hit the instrument panel and feet to wedge behind the pedals during flight. Unable to control the aircraft, he forced a hard landing over terrain, resulting in substantial damage to the fuselage and left wing with no mechanical failures reported.

aircraft: Diamond Aircraft Ind Inc DA 40 NG
synopsis: The mechanic's re-use of worm drive clamps, which resulted in a separation of the turbocharger air discharge duct and a partial loss of engine power during initial climb.
summary: During a post-annual inspection test flight, a pilot and mechanic experienced partial engine power loss when a reused, worn worm drive clamp failed, separating the turbocharger air discharge duct. The aircraft subsequently impacted a field short of the runway while attempting to avoid trees.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to depart on the flight with known electrical issues and his subsequent loss of situational awareness (geographic position), which resulted in his eventual decision to perform an off-airport landing.
summary: The pilot experienced avionics and radio failures while returning home at night, leading to disorientation and low fuel. He attempted a precautionary landing on a road, resulting in substantial damage to the left wing and fuselage.

synopsis: The commercial pilot's improper fuel management, which resulted in a loss of total engine power due to fuel starvation.
summary: During a night cross-country training flight, a commercial pilot and safety pilot experienced total engine power loss due to fuel starvation caused by the fuel selector being set to the left tank only. The aircraft was forced into a swamp, nosed over, and came to rest inverted.

synopsis: The pilot of an American Champion 7GCBC, N342H, was fatally injured when the aircraft impacted wooded mountainous terrain shortly after departing Big Creek Airport, Idaho. The accident occurred during a Part 91 personal flight, with no witnesses to the sequence and the cause undetermined in the narrative.
summary: The pilot of an American Champion 7GCBC, N342H, was fatally injured when the aircraft impacted wooded mountainous terrain shortly after departing Big Creek Airport, Idaho. The accident occurred during a Part 91 personal flight, with no witnesses to the sequence and the cause undetermined in the narrative.

synopsis: The pilot's exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack during takeoff, which resulted in a stall/spin at an altitude too low for recovery. Contributing to the accident was the opening of the nose baggage door and subsequent distraction of the pilot during a critical phase of flight, as well as the external pressure of the approaching thunderstorms, which likely resulted in the pilot rushing to depart.
summary: The pilot departed a short repositioning flight in rushing conditions, likely failing to secure the nose baggage door. The door opened during takeoff, causing a high angle of attack, stall, and spin that resulted in a fatal crash.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental Just Aircraft Superstol, N128EL, reported a total loss of engine power and smoke from the cowling at 250 feet AGL during the crosswind leg after departing runway 23 at EVW. The pilot attempted a forced landing on a taxiway but struck a hillside, causing substantial fuselage damage with no injuries.
summary: The pilot of an experimental Just Aircraft Superstol, N128EL, reported a total loss of engine power and smoke from the cowling at 250 feet AGL during the crosswind leg after departing runway 23 at EVW. The pilot attempted a forced landing on a taxiway but struck a hillside, causing substantial fuselage damage with no injuries.

synopsis: The failure of the left main landing gear tire casing and tube due to excessive wear which resulted in a loss of directional control during the landing.
summary: A flight instructor and student lost directional control during landing when a worn left tire separated from its rim, causing the aircraft to veer left, strike a runway edge light, and collapse the left main gear. The plane departed the runway and sustained substantial left wing damage.

synopsis: The pilot of a converted Piper PA46-350P experienced total engine power loss at 100 feet AGL during takeoff from Indy South Greenwood Airport. The aircraft impacted a taxiway and embankment, sustaining substantial fuselage damage and causing serious injuries to the pilot and passenger.
summary: The pilot of a converted Piper PA46-350P experienced total engine power loss at 100 feet AGL during takeoff from Indy South Greenwood Airport. The aircraft impacted a taxiway and embankment, sustaining substantial fuselage damage and causing serious injuries to the pilot and passenger.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper PA-18-150 conducting a glider tow from Bergseth Field lost engine power at 200 feet AGL, likely due to fuel exhaustion despite checking controls. After releasing the glider, the pilot forced landed in a field, striking a fence and ground looping, which substantially damaged the aircraft.
summary: The pilot of a Piper PA-18-150 conducting a glider tow from Bergseth Field lost engine power at 200 feet AGL, likely due to fuel exhaustion despite checking controls. After releasing the glider, the pilot forced landed in a field, striking a fence and ground looping, which substantially damaged the aircraft.

synopsis: The pilot's improper fuel planning, which resulted in fuel exhaustion and a total loss of power to both engines.
summary: The pilot of a twin-engine airplane experienced total power loss in both engines during approach, forcing a landing in a cornfield 19.5 miles from the airport. The accident resulted in substantial damage to the fuselage and left wing, with post-recovery fuel checks revealing critically low fuel levels in all tanks.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the glider during takeoff.
summary: The pilot lost control of a glider during aerotow takeoff, causing the left wing to strike the ground and the aircraft to cartwheel after release. The pilot attributed the accident to poor airmanship and rushing preparations without a wing runner, resulting in substantial fuselage damage.

synopsis: A private pilot with no experience in the experimental Chinook Plus 2 was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed near Pittstown, NJ, during its first flight. The pilot lost control on takeoff, struck a runway light, and subsequently descended vertically into a wooded area, resulting in a post-crash fire that destroyed the airplane.
summary: A private pilot with no experience in the experimental Chinook Plus 2 was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed near Pittstown, NJ, during its first flight. The pilot lost control on takeoff, struck a runway light, and subsequently descended vertically into a wooded area, resulting in a post-crash fire that destroyed the airplane.

synopsis: A Beechcraft 95-B55 carrying a pilot and passenger crashed near Broomfield, Colorado, shortly after takeoff when the main cabin door opened. The aircraft entered an inverted dive and impacted the ground, resulting in fatal injuries for both occupants.
summary: A Beechcraft 95-B55 carrying a pilot and passenger crashed near Broomfield, Colorado, shortly after takeoff when the main cabin door opened. The aircraft entered an inverted dive and impacted the ground, resulting in fatal injuries for both occupants.

synopsis: A private pilot and flight instructor in a DB Aerocopter AK1-3 sustained fatal and serious injuries, respectively, when the helicopter struck the ground during a Part 91 instructional flight near Prineville, Oregon. The accident occurred while the aircraft was in the traffic pattern, descending rapidly in a nose-down attitude before impact, with no pre-accident smoke or vapor observed.
summary: A private pilot and flight instructor in a DB Aerocopter AK1-3 sustained fatal and serious injuries, respectively, when the helicopter struck the ground during a Part 91 instructional flight near Prineville, Oregon. The accident occurred while the aircraft was in the traffic pattern, descending rapidly in a nose-down attitude before impact, with no pre-accident smoke or vapor observed.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from an obstacle during taxi operations.
summary: The pilot reported that while taxiing to the ramp, the aircraft's left wing struck a light pole, causing substantial damage to the outboard wing. The pilot stated there were no mechanical anomalies that would have precluded normal operations.

synopsis: An in-flight collision with a bird while enroute.
summary: The pilot reported a bird strike at 1,500 feet AGL that caused the right main landing gear to separate. The pilot returned to the airport and executed a soft field landing in the grass, resulting in substantial damage to the right fuselage.

synopsis: During a Part 91 positioning flight, the pilot of a Grumman TBM-3 reported engine power loss on final approach despite troubleshooting fuel tanks and emergency checklists. The pilot executed a forced landing on a perimeter road, resulting in substantial damage after the aircraft struck a ditch and fence while inverted.
summary: During a Part 91 positioning flight, the pilot of a Grumman TBM-3 reported engine power loss on final approach despite troubleshooting fuel tanks and emergency checklists. The pilot executed a forced landing on a perimeter road, resulting in substantial damage after the aircraft struck a ditch and fence while inverted.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to attain a proper touchdown point, which resulted in a runway overrun and collision with terrain.
summary: The pilot of an airplane conducting a power-off approach landed halfway down a 3,121-foot runway and overran the departure end, striking a berm. This caused nose gear collapse and firewall damage; although the pilot suspected brake failure, inspection found no mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: The pilot of a Beech F33A experienced an abrupt engine speed drop shortly after takeoff, forcing a landing in a wooded area. A post-impact fire consumed the airframe, preventing fuel system examination, though the pilot escaped uninjured.
summary: The pilot of a Beech F33A experienced an abrupt engine speed drop shortly after takeoff, forcing a landing in a wooded area. A post-impact fire consumed the airframe, preventing fuel system examination, though the pilot escaped uninjured.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed and his exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack during the initial climb, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's decision to take off with a known tailwind.
summary: The pilot attempted a downwind water takeoff after three aborted upwind attempts due to water obscuring the cockpit. The aircraft stalled during a left turn at 200 feet, likely caused by insufficient airspeed and excessive angle of attack, resulting in an unrecoverable descent into the water.

synopsis: The pilot's use of engine beta prior to ensuring the tailwheel was on the ground during landing roll.
summary: The pilot reported a fast approach and landing rollout where using engine beta with the tail airborne caused the airplane to nose over. This resulted in substantial damage to the wings, empennage, and engine mounts, with no preaccident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot and passenger of a T-28B were seriously injured when the engine surged during a Part 91 flyover near Marysville, California. The pilot elected to land on a dirt road, where a wing struck a berm, spinning the aircraft and causing substantial damage to the wings and fuselage.
summary: The pilot and passenger of a T-28B were seriously injured when the engine surged during a Part 91 flyover near Marysville, California. The pilot elected to land on a dirt road, where a wing struck a berm, spinning the aircraft and causing substantial damage to the wings and fuselage.

synopsis: The pilot's inadvertent application of brakes during landing, which resulted in a nose over.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane nosed over after inadvertently applying brakes following a bounce during landing on a sandy gravel bar. This resulted in substantial damage to the left wing lift strut, vertical stabilizer, and rudder, with no preaccident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control while landing with a quartering tailwind.
summary: The pilot reported that while landing at night on runway 17R with a quartering tailwind, the airplane veered right twice despite rudder corrections. The aircraft subsequently exited the runway, struck a storm trench, and sustained substantial right wing damage, with no preaccident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: Maintenance personnel's failure to identify and replace damaged rivet nuts at the air conditioning louver assembly, which resulted in the separation of the louver assembly from the helicopter, the louver assembly's impact with the tail rotor, and subsequent loss of helicopter control.
summary: The pilot of a helicopter returning from a patient transport mission lost tail rotor control after an improperly repaired air conditioning louver assembly separated in flight. The detached louver struck the tail rotor, causing its separation and forcing an autorotation landing on a residential lawn.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to extend the landing gear before landing.
summary: The pilot conducting an IFR practice flight landed with the gear retracted due to task saturation and tunnel vision, causing substantial fuselage damage. The landing gear operated normally, but the position warning horn was non-functional.

synopsis: The airplane's collision with a deer on the runway during takeoff.
summary: A flight instructor and student aborted a touch-and-go takeoff at dusk after a deer struck the aircraft's underside during acceleration. The collision caused substantial fuselage damage, though the instructor reported no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's inadvertent movement of the fuel selector to a position that restricted fuel flow to the engine, which resulted in the loss of engine power during takeoff.
summary: During an instructional takeoff from a lake, a flight instructor and student experienced total engine power loss at 200–300 feet due to the fuel selector being out of the right tank detent. The aircraft impacted the water hard, sustaining substantial damage to the left wing strut and fuselage.

synopsis: A Cessna Citation S550 pilot and five passengers were killed when the aircraft struck power lines and a residential area while descending below the minimum crossing altitude on an RNAV (GPS) approach to San Diego. The accident occurred in low visibility with the pilot failing to maintain required altitudes despite ATC instructions and known lighting outages.
summary: A Cessna Citation S550 pilot and five passengers were killed when the aircraft struck power lines and a residential area while descending below the minimum crossing altitude on an RNAV (GPS) approach to San Diego. The accident occurred in low visibility with the pilot failing to maintain required altitudes despite ATC instructions and known lighting outages.

synopsis: A student pilot flying a Robinson R44 II helicopter was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed into terrain near Miami, Texas, during a personal flight in foggy, low-visibility conditions. The accident occurred after the pilot, who had no pre-impact mechanical failures, lost control and descended below the ground while operating without a weather briefing.
summary: A student pilot flying a Robinson R44 II helicopter was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed into terrain near Miami, Texas, during a personal flight in foggy, low-visibility conditions. The accident occurred after the pilot, who had no pre-impact mechanical failures, lost control and descended below the ground while operating without a weather briefing.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate compensation for gusting wind conditions, which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: The pilot reported a hard landing on final approach in gusty winds when the wind suddenly stopped, causing the aircraft to drop. The left main landing gear collapsed, resulting in substantial damage to the wing and fuselage, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate clearance from a fence during taxi.
summary: The pilot reported that while taxiing to the parking area after landing, the aircraft's left wing contacted the airport perimeter fence, causing substantial damage to the wing and aileron. The pilot stated there were no pre-impact mechanical malfunctions or failures.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate preflight planning, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion.
summary: The pilot failed to visually verify fuel quantity before departure, leading to engine power loss at 10,000 feet due to unanticipated headwinds. This resulted in a forced off-airport landing where the aircraft nosed over, causing substantial damage to the wing and tail.

synopsis: During a Part 91 test flight of an experimental Zenith STOL CH701, the pilot and passenger were fatally and seriously injured when the aircraft failed to climb after takeoff. The plane descended in a nose-up attitude and impacted trees near Geneva, Ohio, despite the engine appearing to produce power and controls remaining functional.
summary: During a Part 91 test flight of an experimental Zenith STOL CH701, the pilot and passenger were fatally and seriously injured when the aircraft failed to climb after takeoff. The plane descended in a nose-up attitude and impacted trees near Geneva, Ohio, despite the engine appearing to produce power and controls remaining functional.

synopsis: A private pilot and passenger were fatally injured when their Rockwell Commander 114A entered a steep, high-rate descent near Hankamer, Texas, during a personal flight. ADS-B data showed the aircraft decelerated to 59 knots before impacting terrain in a nose-low attitude, resulting in a destroyed airplane.
summary: A private pilot and passenger were fatally injured when their Rockwell Commander 114A entered a steep, high-rate descent near Hankamer, Texas, during a personal flight. ADS-B data showed the aircraft decelerated to 59 knots before impacting terrain in a nose-low attitude, resulting in a destroyed airplane.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate takeoff performance planning, which resulted in a runway overrun and collision with terrain.
summary: The pilot of an aerial application airplane near maximum gross weight failed to rotate on a 2,650-foot mixed runway, forcing a pull-up to clear an 8-foot dike before settling into a marshy area and contacting trees. The pilot reported no mechanical failures but attributed the accident to loading conditions and variable winds, resulting in substantial fuselage and empennage damage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control of the airplane while attempting to take off in a gusty crosswind, which resulted in a runway excursion.
summary: A student pilot overcompensated with rudder input while correcting for a gusty left quartering crosswind during takeoff roll. The aircraft turned left, departed the runway, and struck lights and terrain, causing substantial damage to the fuselage and left wing strut with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The failure of the left landing gear system and subsequent intentional gear up landing.
summary: The pilot reported that during the third traffic pattern, the left landing gear broke due to a fractured bell crank, possibly damaged in a 1998 gear-up landing. This caused the strut to jam, forcing a gear-up landing that resulted in substantial damage to the lower fuselage.

synopsis: A commercial pilot flying an Aeronca 7AC experienced total engine power loss at 100 feet AGL during takeoff from Forest Hill Airport. The pilot executed a forced landing in a muddy field, causing the aircraft to nose over and sustain substantial wing damage.
summary: A commercial pilot flying an Aeronca 7AC experienced total engine power loss at 100 feet AGL during takeoff from Forest Hill Airport. The pilot executed a forced landing in a muddy field, causing the aircraft to nose over and sustain substantial wing damage.

synopsis: The pilot's inadvertent encounter with soft terrain conditions during the landing which resulted in a loss of directional and a subsequent nose-over.
summary: The pilot landed on a dry grass airstrip where the aircraft encountered soft terrain, pulled toward the runway edge, and nosed over. This caused substantial damage to the left wing and vertical stabilizer, with the pilot attributing the accident to operating on a soft runway rather than mechanical failure.

synopsis: A private pilot flying an experimental Zenith 750 experienced low oil pressure warnings and partial power loss at 2,200 feet MSL.
