synopsis: During a Part 91 departure from Cavanaugh Bay Airport, a Beech A36 pilot and passenger sustained minor injuries when the aircraft's right wing struck trees, causing it to roll into a lake. Witnesses reported high engine RPM and a steep right bank, while the pilot attributed the accident to the wing strike at the runway end.
summary: During a Part 91 departure from Cavanaugh Bay Airport, a Beech A36 pilot and passenger sustained minor injuries when the aircraft's right wing struck trees, causing it to roll into a lake. Witnesses reported high engine RPM and a steep right bank, while the pilot attributed the accident to the wing strike at the runway end.

synopsis: The first officer's failure to maintain proper pitch attitude during flare which resulted in a bounced landing and a tailstrike.
summary: United Airlines flight 2136 sustained a tail strike and substantial fuselage damage while landing at Las Vegas (LAS) after the first officer delayed the flare maneuver. The aircraft bounced, touched down again at 8.2 degrees pitch, and required structural repairs.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to attain a proper touchdown point during landing which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: The pilot of a float-equipped airplane reported an unexpected descent while crossing the shoreline on final approach to a remote lake. The aircraft touched down prematurely in shallow water, striking the rocky bottom and sustaining substantial fuselage damage with no preimpact mechanical failures.

synopsis: A pilot operating a Beech F35, N5009B, was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed into terrain near Eagle Nest, New Mexico, during a personal flight from Angel Fire Airport. The accident occurred after the pilot departed into deteriorating weather conditions and impacted trees in a box canyon, resulting in a post-crash fire that destroyed the airplane.
summary: A pilot operating a Beech F35, N5009B, was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed into terrain near Eagle Nest, New Mexico, during a personal flight from Angel Fire Airport. The accident occurred after the pilot departed into deteriorating weather conditions and impacted trees in a box canyon, resulting in a post-crash fire that destroyed the airplane.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airplane control and clearance from trees during takeoff.
summary: During takeoff rotation, the right-seat pilot unexpectedly commanded a maximum performance climb, causing the left-seat pilot to relinquish control. The aircraft subsequently struck trees and impacted a lake, sustaining substantial damage, with the left-seat pilot reporting no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: A National Guard Sikorsky UH-60 collided with a Texas DPS DJI Mavic 3T drone during flood response operations near Ingram, Texas. The collision, caused by a failure to see or hear traffic despite a verbal deconfliction strategy, damaged the helicopter's tail rotor, though the crew landed safely without injury.
summary: A National Guard Sikorsky UH-60 collided with a Texas DPS DJI Mavic 3T drone during flood response operations near Ingram, Texas. The collision, caused by a failure to see or hear traffic despite a verbal deconfliction strategy, damaged the helicopter's tail rotor, though the crew landed safely without injury.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to turn off the magneto switch before repositioning the propeller by hand which resulted in an inadvertent engine start.
summary: After refueling, a pilot's arm was seriously injured when the engine inadvertently started while he manually repositioned the propeller with the magneto switch ON. The unoccupied aircraft subsequently collided with a large metal sign and came to rest upright.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to land at the manufacturer's recommended approach speed, which resulted in a runway excursion, and impact with trees.
summary: The pilot landed an airplane at 111 knots, exceeding the recommended 85–90 knots, and reported brake failure causing an overrun into trees. Post-accident examination confirmed the brakes functioned properly, indicating the high landing speed caused the runway excursion and substantial damage.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare and failure to maintain pitch control, which resulted in a tail strike. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's failure to initiate a go around after the abnormal runway contact.
summary: During the landing flare, the pilot reported the airplane bounced and subsequently pitched up, causing the tail to strike the surface and sustain substantial fuselage damage. The pilot stated there were no pre-accident mechanical failures or malfunctions.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing, which resulted in a ground loop.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane landing on Runway 22 in 11-knot gusting winds experienced a wing lift after the upwind tire touched down. Despite corrective aileron input, the aircraft turned right and the left wing contacted the ground, causing substantial damage.

synopsis: A Cessna 172 pilot and passenger suffered no injuries when the engine lost power at 1,500 feet MSL during a Part 91 flight. The subsequent forced landing in a peanut field caused the aircraft to nose over, resulting in substantial damage to the vertical stabilizer and rudder.
summary: A Cessna 172 pilot and passenger suffered no injuries when the engine lost power at 1,500 feet MSL during a Part 91 flight. The subsequent forced landing in a peanut field caused the aircraft to nose over, resulting in substantial damage to the vertical stabilizer and rudder.

synopsis: The pilot's inability to maintain directional control during landing due to excessive wear in the tailwheel steering assembly.
summary: During landing, a tailwheel shimmy caused the aircraft to ground loop and sustain left wing damage. Post-accident examination revealed excessive wear on the tailwheel steering arm restricted control, a defect missed during the annual inspection.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to extend the landing gear before landing due to his distraction.
summary: The pilot landed an airplane on the runway with the gear retracted while in the traffic pattern. Distraction from an extended downwind leg and multiple gear configuration changes caused the error, resulting in substantial damage to the lower fuselage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain obstacle clearance during the go-around, that resulted in the tailwheel impacting a taxiway sign, a subsequent loss of control due to the damaged tailwheel, and a runway excursion during the landing.
summary: During a local area flight go-around, the pilot's tailwheel struck a taxiway sign, damaging the rudder and empennage. This damage caused a loss of tailwheel control on landing, resulting in the aircraft departing the runway and sustaining substantial damage, though the pilot egressed safely.

synopsis: The flight instructor's delayed remedial action/lack of supervision. Contributing to the accident was the pilot receiving instructions failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll in gusting wind conditions, which resulted in a ground loop.
summary: A flight instructor and student practicing tailwheel landings ground looped during rollout on runway 13 due to gusting winds lifting the left wing. The student and instructor applied right rudder, but the aircraft veered right and sustained substantial damage to the right wing with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll with a quartering tailwind.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane ground looped to the right during landing on runway 33 due to a right-rear quartering wind gust. The incident caused the left main landing gear to collapse and the left wing to impact the runway, resulting in substantial damage.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna 182B reported premature lift-off at 40 knots during takeoff due to suspected ground effect and a faulty airspeed indicator. The aircraft subsequently bounced on landing and sustained substantial damage to the forward fuselage and engine mount, though occupants were uninjured.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna 182B reported premature lift-off at 40 knots during takeoff due to suspected ground effect and a faulty airspeed indicator. The aircraft subsequently bounced on landing and sustained substantial damage to the forward fuselage and engine mount, though occupants were uninjured.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain direction control during takeoff roll which resulted in a ground loop, and subsequent runway excursion.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane reported that during takeoff, the aircraft veered right despite rudder corrections and increased throttle, leading to a ground loop and runway exit. The plane sustained substantial damage to the right wing and tail, though both occupants escaped uninjured with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot of a Zenith CH601 HDS was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed in Colorado while en route from Wyoming to Kansas. A witness reported the plane descended in a nose-low, wings-level attitude with the engine at full throttle before striking the ground.
summary: The pilot of a Zenith CH601 HDS was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed in Colorado while en route from Wyoming to Kansas. A witness reported the plane descended in a nose-low, wings-level attitude with the engine at full throttle before striking the ground.

synopsis: A Piper PA-25 towplane and a glider were involved in an accident during an aerotow near Hot Springs, South Dakota, resulting in the pilot's death and substantial damage to the towplane. The towplane impacted terrain after the glider pilot failed to release the tow rope due to a binding release cable, causing the towplane to pitch down and crash.
summary: A Piper PA-25 towplane and a glider were involved in an accident during an aerotow near Hot Springs, South Dakota, resulting in the pilot's death and substantial damage to the towplane. The towplane impacted terrain after the glider pilot failed to release the tow rope due to a binding release cable, causing the towplane to pitch down and crash.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane while on approach to land.
summary: During a practice landing, the pilot reported the aircraft suddenly lost altitude below the tree line and struck a wire fence, entangling the right main gear. The taut wire stopped the airplane, causing it to nose over and sustain substantial damage to the wings, struts, and tail, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's excessive braking during the landing roll, resulting in a nose over. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's decision to continue the landing after determining the landing area was unsuitable.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane nosed over during landing at a remote off-airport site after applying heavy brakes due to insufficient stopping distance. The incident caused substantial damage to the rudder and left wing lift strut, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: Two pilots renting a Piper PA-28-180 for personal flight sustained fatal injuries when the aircraft crashed near Needles, California, shortly after landing. The plane came to rest inverted with thermal damage, and the debris path indicated a ground impact approximately 1,200 feet from the runway departure end.
summary: Two pilots renting a Piper PA-28-180 for personal flight sustained fatal injuries when the aircraft crashed near Needles, California, shortly after landing. The plane came to rest inverted with thermal damage, and the debris path indicated a ground impact approximately 1,200 feet from the runway departure end.

synopsis: The flight instructor's inadequate supervision and delayed remedial actions during the landing approach, which resulted in the airplane contacting the runway with the landing gear retracted.
summary: A flight instructor and student in a multi-engine airplane descended with throttles at idle, misinterpreting the landing gear warning horn as a stall warning. The instructor initiated a go-around on short final after realizing the gear was retracted, but the aircraft contacted the runway with substantial fuselage damage.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate fuel planning, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion.
summary: The pilot of a newly purchased aircraft experienced an engine power loss on short final due to empty fuel tanks after failing to recalculate fuel for headwinds and weather rerouting. He performed a forced landing on railroad tracks, causing substantial damage to the wings, nose gear, and firewall.

aircraft: Moyes Liteflite Pty Ltd C DRAGONFLY
synopsis: During a glider tow descent near Charleston, New Hampshire, the pilot of a Moyes Liteflite Dragonfly experienced a total loss of engine power after releasing the glider at 3,500 feet. The aircraft impacted a grass field, sustaining substantial damage and causing serious injury to the pilot, though post-accident inspection found no fuel contamination or control cable failures.
summary: During a glider tow descent near Charleston, New Hampshire, the pilot of a Moyes Liteflite Dragonfly experienced a total loss of engine power after releasing the glider at 3,500 feet. The aircraft impacted a grass field, sustaining substantial damage and causing serious injury to the pilot, though post-accident inspection found no fuel contamination or control cable failures.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate preflight fuel planning, which resulted in fuel exhaustion and a subsequent total loss of engine power to one of the airplane's two engines. Contributing to the outcome was the pilot's loading of the airplane beyond its maximum gross weight.
summary: The pilot of a multi-engine airplane experienced a rear engine power loss due to fuel exhaustion three miles from the destination. The subsequent impact with a tree and substantial damage resulted from incorrect range calculations and operating the aircraft more than 500 pounds over maximum gross weight.

synopsis: The pilot of a Game Composites GB-1 Gamebird, N588AF, executed a go-around after formation instruction while cleared to land at K57, colliding with a Vans RV-8, N931KZ, rolling out on the runway. The Gamebird's rudder contacted the RV-8's propeller, causing substantial damage to the Gamebird and minor damage to the RV-8 with no injuries.
summary: The pilot of a Game Composites GB-1 Gamebird, N588AF, executed a go-around after formation instruction while cleared to land at K57, colliding with a Vans RV-8, N931KZ, rolling out on the runway. The Gamebird's rudder contacted the RV-8's propeller, causing substantial damage to the Gamebird and minor damage to the RV-8 with no injuries.

synopsis: The airplane's reduced climb performance during takeoff in mountainous terrain, which resulted in the airplane's inability to climb and impact with terrain.
summary: The pilot departed a down-sloping grass airstrip in mountainous terrain, but the aircraft failed to climb above 20 to 40 feet and impacted the ground. The pilot attributed the accident to a possible downdraft or temperature inversion reducing climb performance, noting no mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from a creek bank while maneuvering to land.
summary: The pilot misjudged height during short final to a remote beach, causing landing gear to strike a creek bank. This impact separated the right main gear and damaged the right wing and fuselage, though the pilot reported no preimpact mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's excessive braking during the landing roll, resulting in a nose over.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane nosed over during the landing roll after bouncing on rough terrain and applying heavy braking. This resulted in substantial damage to the rudder and right wing lift strut, with no preaccident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the helicopter during the landing.
summary: During a water landing approach, the pilot raised the collective with his hand too high, preventing the governor from increasing throttle to maintain rotor RPM. The helicopter impacted the water, sustaining substantial tail boom damage, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to attain a proper airspeed and climb attitude during takeoff, which led to the airplane exceeding its critical angle of attack and experiencing an aerodynamic stall. Contributing to the accident were the student pilot's lack of experience and poor judgement.
summary: A student pilot with a passenger attempted a takeoff from a sloped 2,000-ft grass strip, stalled shortly after liftoff, and crashed with substantial damage. The pilot attributed the accident to not extending flaps for density altitude, while instructors noted the aircraft was inappropriate for training and no current endorsements were provided.

synopsis: The pilot's exceedance of the airplane's never-exceed speed (VNE) during maneuvering, which resulted in the in-flight separation of the left flaperon.
summary: During a steep turn, the pilot reported the aircraft pitched down, exceeded VNE, and experienced buffeting. This caused the left flaperon to separate in-flight and damaged the left wing, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental Rans S7 experienced engine vibration and oil pressure loss, forcing a landing in a wheat field where the aircraft nosed over. The accident caused substantial damage to the rudder and engine components, though the pilot was not injured.
summary: The pilot of an experimental Rans S7 experienced engine vibration and oil pressure loss, forcing a landing in a wheat field where the aircraft nosed over. The accident caused substantial damage to the rudder and engine components, though the pilot was not injured.

synopsis: A flight instructor, student pilot, and passenger were injured when a Cessna 172S crashed near Sisters, Oregon, during a takeoff for a discovery flight. The instructor reported insufficient engine power and a high angle of attack, leading to a stall and collision with trees before the aircraft caught fire.
summary: A flight instructor, student pilot, and passenger were injured when a Cessna 172S crashed near Sisters, Oregon, during a takeoff for a discovery flight. The instructor reported insufficient engine power and a high angle of attack, leading to a stall and collision with trees before the aircraft caught fire.

synopsis: Impact with the ocean for reasons that could not be determined because the pilot and airplane were not located.
summary: A pilot flying a single-engine aircraft lost radio contact after acknowledging landing clearance for runway 28R at the destination airport. ADS-B data showed the airplane deviated from the approach and flew 470 nautical miles southwest before contact was lost, resulting in a suspended search with no wreckage found.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental Murphy Moose SR3500 experienced a total engine power loss and vibration during cruise flight from Sekiu to Olympia, Washington. The pilot attempted a forced landing in forested terrain, resulting in substantial damage, one fatality, and injuries to the pilot and another passenger.
summary: The pilot of an experimental Murphy Moose SR3500 experienced a total engine power loss and vibration during cruise flight from Sekiu to Olympia, Washington. The pilot attempted a forced landing in forested terrain, resulting in substantial damage, one fatality, and injuries to the pilot and another passenger.

synopsis: Failure of the engine mount which resulted in a collapse of the nose landing gear.
summary: The pilot reported a nose gear collapse and runway excursion during landing, causing substantial wing damage. Post-accident inspection found a broken engine mount, and the mechanic admitted missing a required service bulletin inspection for cracks after 138 flight hours.

synopsis: A private pilot flying a Beech K35 with a recently remanufactured engine experienced rough running and altitude loss due to suspected cylinder issues. The pilot declared an emergency and conducted a forced landing into wooded terrain near Sylacauga, Alabama, resulting in substantial damage to the aircraft and serious injuries.
summary: A private pilot flying a Beech K35 with a recently remanufactured engine experienced rough running and altitude loss due to suspected cylinder issues. The pilot declared an emergency and conducted a forced landing into wooded terrain near Sylacauga, Alabama, resulting in substantial damage to the aircraft and serious injuries.

synopsis: A commercial pilot flying a Piper PA-46-310P experienced engine roughness, low oil pressure, and oil spray during cruise, leading to a forced landing on a golf course. Post-accident inspection revealed a fractured connecting rod, crankcase holes, and only 3/4 quart of oil remaining in the engine.
summary: A commercial pilot flying a Piper PA-46-310P experienced engine roughness, low oil pressure, and oil spray during cruise, leading to a forced landing on a golf course. Post-accident inspection revealed a fractured connecting rod, crankcase holes, and only 3/4 quart of oil remaining in the engine.

synopsis: The flight crew's failure to use the airplane pre-landing checklist and failure to extend the airplane's landing gear before landing.
summary: A flight instructor and student landed a retractable gear aircraft with the gear retracted after the instructor was distracted by traffic and a student question, missing prelanding checks. The accident caused substantial fuselage damage, prompting the flight school to implement additional training and crew procedures for gear verification.

synopsis: SkyWest Flight 3005, an Embraer 170, initiated a go-around at Monterey Regional Airport due to a closed runway indicated by a lighted "X" and a NOTAM. The crew landed uneventfully on a second approach after airport operations temporarily removed the closure markers and confirmed the runway was open.
summary: SkyWest Flight 3005, an Embraer 170, initiated a go-around at Monterey Regional Airport due to a closed runway indicated by a lighted "X" and a NOTAM. The crew landed uneventfully on a second approach after airport operations temporarily removed the closure markers and confirmed the runway was open.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to establish and maintain the airstrip centerline during takeoff, which resulted in the airplane's right wingtips contacting the corn that bordered the airstrip.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel agricultural biplane departing a 100-ft-wide grass airstrip reported that the right wingtips struck bordering corn during the takeoff run. This contact caused the aircraft to veer, spin, and sustain substantial damage to the wings, fuselage, and empennage with no preimpact mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain pitch control during takeoff. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's inexperience in the accident gyroplane.
summary: During a post-inspection test flight of a gyroplane, a pilot with no experience in this specific model lost control due to unexpectedly high backstick forces caused by a modified, heavier trim spring. The aircraft pitched up to 60 degrees, rolled left, and impacted the ground with substantial damage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain proper airspeed and altitude during the approach which resulted in a runway overshoot and subsequent landing in a lake. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's delayed remedial action to abort the landing.
summary: During approach to a turf runway, a pilot attempted to correct a high and fast condition but raised flaps instead of advancing throttle, causing the aircraft to overshoot the runway, land in a lake, and nose over. The pilot reported no mechanical failures and attributed the accident to improper speed management and flap selection.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control while landing with a crosswind.
summary: The pilot reported that during the landing roll of a Phase 1 test flight on runway 27, the aircraft pitched down and veered left despite right rudder input. The plane exited the runway into grass, collapsing the nose gear and damaging the right wing, with the pilot citing no mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to attain an appropriate touchdown point during landing, which resulted in a runway overrun and collision with a fence.
summary: During a pre-flight systems check, the pilot was too high and fast on final approach, resulting in a mid-field touchdown. Despite heavy braking, the aircraft overran the runway and struck a perimeter fence, substantially damaging both wings with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: A Piper PA-28-180 carrying a pilot and two pilot-rated passengers crashed into wooded terrain near West Yellowstone, Montana, during a night personal flight. The accident resulted in substantial damage and fatal injuries, following a departure where the aircraft drifted left of the runway centerline and failed to maintain clear radio communication.
summary: A Piper PA-28-180 carrying a pilot and two pilot-rated passengers crashed into wooded terrain near West Yellowstone, Montana, during a night personal flight. The accident resulted in substantial damage and fatal injuries, following a departure where the aircraft drifted left of the runway centerline and failed to maintain clear radio communication.

synopsis: The ground crews improper parking of N247BZ, which left its tail protruding into the taxiway, and the JA986A flight crew's failure to maintain adequate clearance while taxiing. The ground crews improper parking of N247BZ, which left its tail protruding into the taxiway, and the JA986A flight crew's failure to maintain adequate clearance while taxiing.
summary: All Nippon Airways B787-10 JA986A collided with parked Breeze Airways A220 N247BZ while taxiing on taxiway M at Charleston International Airport. The JA986A left wingtip struck the N247BZ rudder, causing substantial damage to both aircraft and two minor passenger injuries, due to the A220 being parked beyond the ramp clearance line.

synopsis: The pilot's aggressive brake application which resulted in a loss of directional control and a ground loop.
summary: The pilot ground looped while landing on runway 36L after braking hard to avoid a preceding aircraft that landed short and decelerated rapidly. The maneuver caused the right wing and elevator to strike the ground, resulting in substantial damage with no reported mechanical anomalies.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare and subsequent failure to maintain directional control during the landing in a crosswind condition.
summary: The pilot flared too high during landing on runway 28L, likely due to a runway width illusion, causing a bounce and weathervaning into an 8-knot crosswind. Despite control inputs, the aircraft ground looped, scraping the right wing and aileron, resulting in substantial damage with no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: A pilot operating a Kolb Firestar, N55161, was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed into a soybean field near Meadow Grove, Nebraska, during a personal flight. The accident resulted in total destruction of the airplane, with damage consistent with high-impact ground forces.
summary: A pilot operating a Kolb Firestar, N55161, was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed into a soybean field near Meadow Grove, Nebraska, during a personal flight. The accident resulted in total destruction of the airplane, with damage consistent with high-impact ground forces.

synopsis: A private pilot was fatally injured when his Piper PA-46-500TP Meridian, N819MA, pitched down and impacted a cornfield 20 seconds after takeoff from Lancaster Regional Airport. The aircraft suffered substantial damage following an unexplained sudden descent to -1600 feet per minute at 650 feet mean sea level.
summary: A private pilot was fatally injured when his Piper PA-46-500TP Meridian, N819MA, pitched down and impacted a cornfield 20 seconds after takeoff from Lancaster Regional Airport. The aircraft suffered substantial damage following an unexplained sudden descent to -1600 feet per minute at 650 feet mean sea level.

synopsis: The ground vehicle operator's failure to maintain clearance from the airplane.
summary: A ground vehicle operator struck the left fuselage of a taxiing airplane while driving behind it. The collision caused substantial damage after the operator failed to see the aircraft turn off the taxiway toward the ramp.

synopsis: The pilot's mismanagement of the available fuel, which resulted in fuel starvation and a total loss of engine power.
summary: During a go-around after a float landing, the pilot experienced engine power loss at 50 feet due to fuel starvation from the left tank. The aircraft impacted the runway overrun area with substantial damage because the pilot could not restore power before impact.

synopsis: The failure of the left brake to release due to corrosion and pitting of the caliper piston and bore, which resulted in a runway excursion.
summary: The pilot reported that during landing, the airplane pulled left and exited the runway, collapsing the nose gear and resting inverted in a cornfield. Post-accident examination revealed corroded brake caliper pistons likely caused the left brake to fail to release, resulting in the excursion and substantial damage.

synopsis: The failure of the pilot to set the flaps to the proper configuration for takeoff.
summary: The pilot attempted takeoff with flaps extended beyond the 10° setting, causing insufficient airspeed and a nose gear collapse upon impact. This resulted in the aircraft veering off the runway with substantial fuselage damage, attributed to the pilot's failure to verify flap configuration.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from powerlines, which resulted in a wire strike.
summary: The pilot flying over a river to inspect a gravel bar lost altitude while searching for powerlines and collided with a line striking the vertical stabilizer. The aircraft subsequently impacted terrain near the riverbank, sustaining substantial damage to the wings and fuselage with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna TR182 experienced engine power loss due to empty fuel tanks while en route, despite preflight verification and in-flight tank switching. He executed a forced landing with gear stowed, resulting in substantial damage to the right wing and left elevator, though no injuries occurred.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna TR182 experienced engine power loss due to empty fuel tanks while en route, despite preflight verification and in-flight tank switching. He executed a forced landing with gear stowed, resulting in substantial damage to the right wing and left elevator, though no injuries occurred.

synopsis: During a Part 91 instructional flight in a Cessna 425 at 26,000 feet, both engines lost power followed by total electrical failure. The pilot executed a forced landing in the desert where the main landing gear separated, causing substantial damage to the left wing while both occupants remained uninjured.
summary: During a Part 91 instructional flight in a Cessna 425 at 26,000 feet, both engines lost power followed by total electrical failure. The pilot executed a forced landing in the desert where the main landing gear separated, causing substantial damage to the left wing while both occupants remained uninjured.

synopsis: The departing pilot's failure to see and avoid the landing airplane during the takeoff, which resulted in a mid-air collision. The departing pilot's failure to see and avoid the landing airplane during the takeoff, which resulted in a mid-air collision.
summary: A Cirrus on final approach collided with an RV-8 that took off from the runway threshold, striking the Cirrus's empennage at 50 to 100 feet. The Cirrus crashed with substantial damage while the RV-8 landed safely, with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot of a Questair Venture N53TL landed on main gear at Oshkosh after three green lights indicated gear down, but the nose gear was retracted, causing the propeller to strike the runway. A popped circuit breaker prevented nose gear extension until reset during recovery, resulting in substantial engine mount damage.
summary: The pilot of a Questair Venture N53TL landed on main gear at Oshkosh after three green lights indicated gear down, but the nose gear was retracted, causing the propeller to strike the runway. A popped circuit breaker prevented nose gear extension until reset during recovery, resulting in substantial engine mount damage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to avoid power lines during an aerial application flight.
summary: A pilot flying a helicopter during an aerial application spray pass collided with a lower power line while attempting to fly underneath it to avoid drifting onto a car. The pilot lost control, impacting a field and sustaining substantial damage to the fuselage and tail boom, noting he was unaware of the lines despite prior flights.

synopsis: The pilot's mismanagement of the airplane's available fuel supply, which resulted in fuel starvation and a subsequent total loss of engine power.
summary: During cruise at 11,500 feet, a pilot experienced engine vibration followed by total power loss due to fuel starvation from an empty left tank. The pilot executed a forced landing to a field, resulting in substantial damage to the horizontal stabilizer.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to attain a positive climb rate due to airplane's improper takeoff configuration.
summary: The aerial application pilot accidentally extended flaps during a second takeoff from a grass strip, causing the aircraft to veer into tall grass and lose speed. The airplane subsequently settled into a soybean field, sustaining substantial left wing damage, which the pilot attributed to the speed loss rather than mechanical failure.

synopsis: A USAF B-52H conducting a flyby experienced loss of separation with an arriving SkyWest ERJ-170 and a Piper PA-28 near Minot International Airport. The incident involved conflicting ATC instructions and coordination errors between the tower and radar approach control, resulting in closest proximities of 1.25 miles and 0.33 miles.
summary: A USAF B-52H conducting a flyby experienced loss of separation with an arriving SkyWest ERJ-170 and a Piper PA-28 near Minot International Airport. The incident involved conflicting ATC instructions and coordination errors between the tower and radar approach control, resulting in closest proximities of 1.25 miles and 0.33 miles.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing.
summary: The pilot reported a mild bounce and left drift during landing, which he unsuccessfully countered with right rudder and brakes. The aircraft swerved left, causing the right main landing gear to separate and resulting in substantial damage to the fuselage and right wing.

synopsis: The student pilot's excessing pitch attitude during takeoff, which resulted in a loss of aircraft control and aerodynamic stall.
summary: A student pilot with 0.6 hours of solo experience stalled left and impacted a parking lot while attempting a soft field takeoff. The accident resulted from an extreme nose-high attitude and left yaw, causing substantial damage with no mechanical failures found.

synopsis: During an instructional flight in an Aero Vodochody L-39C, an engine failure occurred after smoke and grinding noises were reported at FL200. The flight instructor ejected and survived with serious injuries, but the student pilot failed to eject and was fatally injured when the aircraft impacted terrain short of the runway.
summary: During an instructional flight in an Aero Vodochody L-39C, an engine failure occurred after smoke and grinding noises were reported at FL200. The flight instructor ejected and survived with serious injuries, but the student pilot failed to eject and was fatally injured when the aircraft impacted terrain short of the runway.

synopsis: A pilot and pilot-rated passenger were killed when their Van's RV-14A, N21KL, impacted a storage building near Lowell, Michigan, during a descending turn while approaching non-towered airport 24C. Witnesses reported no pre-impact smoke or engine anomalies, and the aircraft was destroyed by a post-impact fire.
summary: A pilot and pilot-rated passenger were killed when their Van's RV-14A, N21KL, impacted a storage building near Lowell, Michigan, during a descending turn while approaching non-towered airport 24C. Witnesses reported no pre-impact smoke or engine anomalies, and the aircraft was destroyed by a post-impact fire.

synopsis: The glider's encounter with atmospheric conditions where the lift was not sufficient to maintain flight.
summary: The glider pilot performed a forced landing at an alternate airport with a closed runway due to insufficient altitude. The right wing struck a vegetation-covered fence post and the left wing hit barbed wire, causing substantial damage with no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: A Cessna T188C pilot conducting aerial application operations was fatally injured when the aircraft struck powerlines and crashed near Oregon, Illinois. The accident occurred shortly after departure following a partial chemical load, resulting in substantial damage and a post-impact fire.
summary: A Cessna T188C pilot conducting aerial application operations was fatally injured when the aircraft struck powerlines and crashed near Oregon, Illinois. The accident occurred shortly after departure following a partial chemical load, resulting in substantial damage and a post-impact fire.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from powerlines while maneuvering at low altitude.
summary: During a clean-up pass following aerial application, the pilot misjudged altitude and collided with a power line. The aircraft subsequently lost control and impacted terrain, sustaining substantial damage to the left wing and empennage with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The failure of the left rudder assembly which resulted in a runway excursion and ground loop.
summary: The pilot lost left rudder control immediately after touchdown when a rudder bar weld failed, causing the aircraft to ground loop and sustain substantial left wing damage. Post-accident examination revealed preexisting cracking at the weld, which was missed during maintenance despite increased pedal forces from ski operations.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from power lines during low-level maneuvering.
summary: The pilot of an agricultural airplane struck power lines estimated at 50 feet and impacted terrain during a midday flight. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the wings and fuselage, with the pilot reporting no mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: During a Part 137 aerial application flight, the pilot of a Robinson R66 helicopter reported a turbine engine flameout while turning 5 to 10 feet above corn. The pilot executed a forced landing that resulted in substantial damage and tailboom separation, though he remained uninjured.
summary: During a Part 137 aerial application flight, the pilot of a Robinson R66 helicopter reported a turbine engine flameout while turning 5 to 10 feet above corn. The pilot executed a forced landing that resulted in substantial damage and tailboom separation, though he remained uninjured.

synopsis: The failure of the left main landing gear lateral pushrod end fitting which resulted in a landing gear collapse during the landing roll.
summary: The pilot reported that the left main landing gear collapsed during the landing roll due to a failed lateral pushrod end fitting. This caused the left wing and horizontal stabilizer to strike the ground, resulting in substantial damage to the aircraft.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane while landing with a tailwind.
summary: During a landing at the EAA AirVenture air show, a homebuilt aircraft bounced and landed hard in a variable tailwind, causing the right main gear to collapse and the nose gear to separate. The pilot reported no mechanical failures, attributing the substantial damage to the hard landing and runway departure.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance to powerlines during an agricultural application pass.
summary: During a pesticide application flight, a helicopter pilot misjudged the flight path and struck a static power line with the right landing skid. This contact caused the skid to separate, followed by main rotor blade strikes that resulted in loss of control and the accident.

synopsis: The pilot and passenger of a Cessna T210N experienced fuel loss and engine power reduction shortly after departing IAH, causing an off-field landing into a water retention pond. A post-impact fire damaged the engine cowling and fuselage, but both occupants egressed without injury.
summary: The pilot and passenger of a Cessna T210N experienced fuel loss and engine power reduction shortly after departing IAH, causing an off-field landing into a water retention pond. A post-impact fire damaged the engine cowling and fuselage, but both occupants egressed without injury.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane during takeoff with a tailwind from a wet turf airstrip.
summary: The pilot of an aerial application aircraft struck crops shortly after takeoff from a grass strip due to tall grass, soft ground from rain, and a tailwind. Although no mechanical failure occurred, the pilot attributed the accident to insufficient weight reduction for the conditions, resulting in substantial damage to the fuselage, empennage, and right wing.

synopsis: The student pilot's improper landing flare and the flight instructor's delayed remedial action during landing that resulted in a loss of control and impact with terrain.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot experienced a bounced landing and left turn during the flare phase at a narrow runway. The instructor took control to abort, but a left wing stall caused the aircraft to impact the ground with substantial damage, with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The ramp worker's premature entry into the jet blast hazard area of an operating engine due to his failure to maintain situational awareness and his misinterpretation of the marshaller's hand signals.
summary: United Airlines flight 2428 experienced electrical faults at Santa Barbara, delaying left engine shutdown. A ramp agent entered the jet blast zone prematurely, misinterpreting marshaller signals, and sustained serious injuries from the operating engine's exhaust.

synopsis: The airplane's encounter with unanticipated moderate turbulence.
summary: Republic Airways flight 5826 encountered unanticipated moderate turbulence while climbing through 10,000 feet near Jacksonville, causing a flight attendant to fall and sustain a broken ankle. The crew diverted to Washington Dulles after the captain determined the injured attendant could not perform duties.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control of the airplane while landing in a crosswind.
summary: The pilot of a vintage tailwheel airplane veered left during a wheel landing in an 8-knot crosswind despite applying full right rudder. The aircraft departed the runway, causing the right main gear to collapse and the right wing to sustain substantial damage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from the crops during an aerial application flight.
summary: During an aerial application spray pass, the pilot reported the airplane contacted the crop, pulling it down and striking the ground. The left wing was substantially damaged, with no preaccident mechanical malfunctions reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to properly configure the airplane during a go-around which resulted in the airplane exceeding its critical angle of attack and an aerodynamic stall at a low altitude.
summary: During a go-around after overshooting the runway, the pilot mistakenly advanced the mixture control instead of the throttle, causing a loss of power. The aircraft subsequently descended, impacting a road and building with substantial wing damage, though the pilot reported no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from a tree during low-level maneuvering.
summary: During low altitude aerial spray application, the pilot flew too close to a tree, causing the left wingtip to strike it and the airplane to impact the ground. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the wings and fuselage, with no preaccident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: An inadvertent encounter with severe turbulence during descent.
summary: Endeavor Air flight 4985 encountered severe turbulence while descending through 17,400 feet into CVG after passing through a cumulus cloud not detected by weather radar. The event injured two flight attendants and one passenger, despite the seat belt sign being on and no active SIGMETs or PIREPs existing.

synopsis: A Yakutat Air Cessna 210-5 pilot operating a Part 135 charter flight reported that the aircraft failed to accelerate properly on a wet, soft beach. The right wing stalled shortly after takeoff, causing the gear to strike sand and driftwood, resulting in substantial damage to the fuselage, wings, and empennage.
summary: A Yakutat Air Cessna 210-5 pilot operating a Part 135 charter flight reported that the aircraft failed to accelerate properly on a wet, soft beach. The right wing stalled shortly after takeoff, causing the gear to strike sand and driftwood, resulting in substantial damage to the fuselage, wings, and empennage.

synopsis: SkyWest flight 3751, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24, departed from closed runway 14 at MBS International Airport despite the crew reviewing NOTAMs and receiving clearance from Great Lakes approach. The flight arrived safely at Detroit with no injuries, though the crew reported no visible cues indicating the runway closure.
summary: SkyWest flight 3751, a Bombardier CL-600-2D24, departed from closed runway 14 at MBS International Airport despite the crew reviewing NOTAMs and receiving clearance from Great Lakes approach. The flight arrived safely at Detroit with no injuries, though the crew reported no visible cues indicating the runway closure.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate fuel management, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel starvation.
summary: The pilot experienced total engine power loss on short final due to an empty left fuel tank, despite switching tanks and activating the boost pump. The aircraft landed short of the runway and nosed over, causing substantial damage, which the operator attributed to improper prelanding checklist use.

aircraft: Rotorsport Uk Ltd ROTORSPORT UK CAVALO
synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain pitch control during takeoff, which resulted in an unintended liftoff from the runway and a subsequent loss of control.
summary: A student pilot flying a gyroplane veered left and rolled onto its right side during the takeoff ground roll, sustaining substantial drivetrain damage. The pilot attributed the accident to moving the control stick forward too early and failing to abort the takeoff, reporting no mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper J3C-65 operating a Part 91 flight was fatally injured when the aircraft stalled and crashed shortly after a touch-and-go at Dillingham Airport. Witnesses reported momentary engine power loss at 200 feet, followed by a left wing stall and uncontrolled descent that resulted in substantial damage.
summary: The pilot of a Piper J3C-65 operating a Part 91 flight was fatally injured when the aircraft stalled and crashed shortly after a touch-and-go at Dillingham Airport. Witnesses reported momentary engine power loss at 200 feet, followed by a left wing stall and uncontrolled descent that resulted in substantial damage.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of direction control during landing due to an unapproved tailwheel assembly and tail spring that resulted in a tailwheel shimmy and a subsequent ground loop.
summary: The pilot experienced severe tailwheel shimmy during landing, leading to a ground loop and substantial damage to the right wing and empennage. Postaccident examination attributed the loss of control to an unapproved tailwheel assembly and spring that created a negative castor angle, exacerbated by a rear passenger's weight.

synopsis: A pilot and passenger were fatally injured when their Grumman AA-5, N1342R, failed to become airborne during takeoff from a grass runway near West Glacier, Montana. Witnesses reported the aircraft moved slowly despite high engine RPM and collided with trees and terrain at the runway's end, resulting in a postimpact fire.
summary: A pilot and passenger were fatally injured when their Grumman AA-5, N1342R, failed to become airborne during takeoff from a grass runway near West Glacier, Montana. Witnesses reported the aircraft moved slowly despite high engine RPM and collided with trees and terrain at the runway's end, resulting in a postimpact fire.

synopsis: An airline transport pilot flying a Piper PA-28RT-201T experienced fluctuating fuel flow during departure from Brookings Regional Airport. After returning for a precautionary landing, the engine suffered a total power loss during the base-to-final turn, forcing a landing that resulted in substantial damage to the left wing and flaps.
summary: An airline transport pilot flying a Piper PA-28RT-201T experienced fluctuating fuel flow during departure from Brookings Regional Airport. After returning for a precautionary landing, the engine suffered a total power loss during the base-to-final turn, forcing a landing that resulted in substantial damage to the left wing and flaps.

synopsis: The pilot of a Beech 95-B55, N8976R, was fatally injured with two passengers when the aircraft crashed into the ocean near Pacific Grove, California, during an ILS 10R approach to Monterey. The accident occurred after the pilot descended below minimum vectoring altitude, acknowledged a go-around, and subsequently entered a descending left turn into the water.
summary: The pilot of a Beech 95-B55, N8976R, was fatally injured with two passengers when the aircraft crashed into the ocean near Pacific Grove, California, during an ILS 10R approach to Monterey. The accident occurred after the pilot descended below minimum vectoring altitude, acknowledged a go-around, and subsequently entered a descending left turn into the water.

synopsis: A pilot and two passengers were fatally injured when their Mooney M20J crashed near Nampa, Idaho, shortly after departing runway 29. The aircraft impacted a storage structure following a climb to 338 feet AGL, with the report noting high density altitude but citing no specific mechanical or operational cause.
summary: A pilot and two passengers were fatally injured when their Mooney M20J crashed near Nampa, Idaho, shortly after departing runway 29. The aircraft impacted a storage structure following a climb to 338 feet AGL, with the report noting high density altitude but citing no specific mechanical or operational cause.

synopsis: A Piper PA-22-150 pilot and passenger were involved in a fatal accident during a local Part 91 flight when the aircraft struck a powerline and inverted. The investigation found no pre-impact mechanical anomalies, concluding the crash resulted from the initial impact with the powerline.
summary: A Piper PA-22-150 pilot and passenger were involved in a fatal accident during a local Part 91 flight when the aircraft struck a powerline and inverted. The investigation found no pre-impact mechanical anomalies, concluding the crash resulted from the initial impact with the powerline.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental Lancair 360 and a passenger sustained minor injuries when the aircraft impacted trees short of the runway at Breckenridge Airport due to engine power loss. The pilot attributed the accident to fuel exhaustion, noting the fuel totalizer indicated approximately 6 gallons on final approach.
summary: The pilot of an experimental Lancair 360 and a passenger sustained minor injuries when the aircraft impacted trees short of the runway at Breckenridge Airport due to engine power loss. The pilot attributed the accident to fuel exhaustion, noting the fuel totalizer indicated approximately 6 gallons on final approach.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to extend the landing gear before landing due to his distraction of other traffic and failure to follow his landing procedures.
summary: The pilot landed an aircraft with the gear retracted after being distracted by a helicopter in the traffic pattern. The fuselage contacted the runway, causing substantial damage, which the pilot attributed to failing to follow landing procedures.

synopsis: The pilot of a Lancair 320 experienced rapid fuel depletion and total engine power loss during a personal flight from Mesa, Arizona. He performed an off-field landing near Wink, Texas, resulting in substantial damage to the empennage and fuselage, though post-accident inspection found fuel in the header tank and lines.
summary: The pilot of a Lancair 320 experienced rapid fuel depletion and total engine power loss during a personal flight from Mesa, Arizona. He performed an off-field landing near Wink, Texas, resulting in substantial damage to the empennage and fuselage, though post-accident inspection found fuel in the header tank and lines.

synopsis: The pilot's inability to stop the airplane on the runway during a rejected takeoff for undetermined reasons, which resulted in the airplane's impact with a ditch.
summary: During takeoff roll, the pilot aborted due to a non-functioning airspeed indicator, but the aircraft overran the runway after brakes failed to slow it as expected. The plane impacted a culvert and was destroyed by a post-crash fire, preventing determination of the specific causes for the instrument and brake failures.

aircraft: Hartline J Bon HARTLINE KITFOX III
synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airplane control during takeoff in variable wind and high density altitude conditions.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane experienced sluggish controls and a delayed lift-off during takeoff on runway 28 due to high density altitude and near-maximum gross weight. The aircraft drifted right, landed hard off-heading, and sustained substantial damage to the right wing and fuselage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from wires while maneuvering at a low altitude, and the ground crew failure to inform the pilot that the support truck had been moved.
summary: During agricultural spraying, a helicopter pilot struck wires with the main rotor blades on final approach to a support vehicle. The pilot attributed the incident to the vehicle driver moving the truck 50 feet closer to the wires without notification, resulting in substantial blade damage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane on the ground, which resulted in a collision with a parked airplane.
summary: The pilot of a cargo airplane lost braking action during taxi after engine start, causing a collision with a parked aircraft. Post-accident examination found the left main landing gear brake pads worn beyond limits, though the system was otherwise functional and braking should have remained available.

aircraft: Orlican S R O M-8 EAGLE
synopsis: During a Part 91 test flight of an Orlican M-8 to calibrate a new propeller, the pilot and flight instructor experienced total engine power loss one minute after departure. They executed a forced landing onto a roadway where the aircraft struck a tree and vehicle, causing substantial damage and minor injuries to occupants and five people on the ground.
summary: During a Part 91 test flight of an Orlican M-8 to calibrate a new propeller, the pilot and flight instructor experienced total engine power loss one minute after departure. They executed a forced landing onto a roadway where the aircraft struck a tree and vehicle, causing substantial damage and minor injuries to occupants and five people on the ground.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate preflight planning, which resulted in a rejected takeoff and subsequent runway excursion.
summary: The pilot rejected takeoff on a 2,799-ft runway after using 2,100 ft without reaching rotation speed but could not stop, causing the aircraft to exit the runway and impact a perimeter fence. The pilot reported no mechanical failures and admitted he should not have attempted departure from the shorter available runway.

synopsis: The collision with a deer during takeoff.
summary: During a night takeoff from a turf runway, the pilot collided with a deer, causing left flap and elevator damage that led to controllability issues. The pilot executed a safe no-flap landing, though the airport directory had previously warned of deer in the vicinity.

synopsis: A pilot and flight instructor in a Beechcraft Bonanza V35 experienced engine power loss at 400 feet AGL while approaching Runway 26 at Astoria Regional Airport. The instructor executed a forced landing on a gravel road, resulting in substantial fuselage damage after the aircraft overran an embankment.
summary: A pilot and flight instructor in a Beechcraft Bonanza V35 experienced engine power loss at 400 feet AGL while approaching Runway 26 at Astoria Regional Airport. The instructor executed a forced landing on a gravel road, resulting in substantial fuselage damage after the aircraft overran an embankment.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane bounced twice on touchdown while landing runway 24 in 11-knot winds. Braking caused the aircraft to veer, exit the runway, and ground loop, resulting in substantial left aileron damage with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental Lancair Evolution, N505RF, suffered an engine power loss due to low oil pressure while turning to the base leg near Coeur d'Alene, Idaho. This forced a road landing that resulted in gear separation, a skid, and a post-crash fire that destroyed the aircraft, leaving the pilot and two passengers with minor injuries.
summary: The pilot of an experimental Lancair Evolution, N505RF, suffered an engine power loss due to low oil pressure while turning to the base leg near Coeur d'Alene, Idaho. This forced a road landing that resulted in gear separation, a skid, and a post-crash fire that destroyed the aircraft, leaving the pilot and two passengers with minor injuries.

synopsis: The failure of the airplane's left main landing gear tires and wheels during the takeoff roll due to the thermal relief plugs melting and releasing tire pressure, which resulted in abnormal airplane handling characteristics and led the flight crew to reject the takeoff at high speed.
summary: American Airlines Flight 3023 experienced left main landing gear tire and wheel failures during takeoff roll at Denver, causing a rejected takeoff, fire, and emergency evacuation. The crew attributed the incident to high temperatures and heavy weight, resulting in substantial aircraft damage but no injuries.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna 182P reported a loud pop and flames during taxi after advancing the throttle. Post-accident examination revealed the engine fuel primer line had melted and fused to the alternator output wire, destroying the aircraft.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna 182P reported a loud pop and flames during taxi after advancing the throttle. Post-accident examination revealed the engine fuel primer line had melted and fused to the alternator output wire, destroying the aircraft.

synopsis: A Lancair IVP, N49BX, was destroyed near Greenwood, Indiana, during a Part 91 personal flight, resulting in the pilot's fatal injury. The accident occurred shortly after takeoff when the aircraft entered a tightening left turn followed by a rapid descent to the right, while engine parameters remained steady until impact.
summary: A Lancair IVP, N49BX, was destroyed near Greenwood, Indiana, during a Part 91 personal flight, resulting in the pilot's fatal injury. The accident occurred shortly after takeoff when the aircraft entered a tightening left turn followed by a rapid descent to the right, while engine parameters remained steady until impact.

synopsis: The pilot's inability to maintain directional control following a collision with a boulder during an off airport precautionary landing.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane made a precautionary off-airport landing due to elevated engine exhaust gas temperatures. The left main gear struck a hidden boulder, breaking the cabane V and causing the wing to strike the ground, resulting in the aircraft nosing over into a creek with substantial damage.

synopsis: During a low-level agricultural flight, the pilot of an Ayres S2R-T34 experienced a sudden total engine power loss at 70 feet AGL with no prior warning. The pilot executed a forced landing in a soybean field to avoid populated areas, but the aircraft nosed over on wet ground, sustaining substantial damage and causing serious injuries to the pilot.
summary: During a low-level agricultural flight, the pilot of an Ayres S2R-T34 experienced a sudden total engine power loss at 70 feet AGL with no prior warning. The pilot executed a forced landing in a soybean field to avoid populated areas, but the aircraft nosed over on wet ground, sustaining substantial damage and causing serious injuries to the pilot.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper PA-28-181 substantially damaged the aircraft after overrunning runway 10 at Block Island State Airport during a personal flight. The accident occurred when a gust lifted the right wing upon touchdown, leaving insufficient runway for a go-around, causing the airplane to impact trees.
summary: The pilot of a Piper PA-28-181 substantially damaged the aircraft after overrunning runway 10 at Block Island State Airport during a personal flight. The accident occurred when a gust lifted the right wing upon touchdown, leaving insufficient runway for a go-around, causing the airplane to impact trees.

synopsis: During a Part 91 instructional flight in a Cessna 172S, a private pilot and flight instructor experienced a catastrophic engine failure at 1,900 feet MSL, causing oil to obscure the windshield. The crew performed a forced landing on a road, impacting a car, after the engine's top crankcase broke and the number 2 connecting rod released.
summary: During a Part 91 instructional flight in a Cessna 172S, a private pilot and flight instructor experienced a catastrophic engine failure at 1,900 feet MSL, causing oil to obscure the windshield. The crew performed a forced landing on a road, impacting a car, after the engine's top crankcase broke and the number 2 connecting rod released.

synopsis: Delta Air Lines flight 56, an Airbus A330-941, encountered severe turbulence and an upset event at FL370 near Creston, Wyoming, after accepting an ATC left turn deviation. The incident caused injuries to 20 cabin crew and passengers, minor aircraft damage, and an emergency diversion to Minneapolis-St Paul.
summary: Delta Air Lines flight 56, an Airbus A330-941, encountered severe turbulence and an upset event at FL370 near Creston, Wyoming, after accepting an ATC left turn deviation. The incident caused injuries to 20 cabin crew and passengers, minor aircraft damage, and an emergency diversion to Minneapolis-St Paul.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance with the ground while hovering, which resulted in a dynamic rollover.
summary: The helicopter pilot practicing low-level maneuvers around a cone lost altitude awareness, causing the right skid to contact the ground and trigger a dynamic rollover. The accident substantially damaged the tailboom, with the pilot reporting no pre-impact mechanical failures.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power due to fuel starvation, which resulted from attitude-inducing unporting of the fuel.
summary: The aerial application helicopter pilot experienced total engine power loss at 100 ft AGL due to fuel starvation caused by low fuel levels and pitch attitude changes. The pilot performed an autorotation, but the hard landing collapsed the right skid and severed the tail boom, resulting in substantial damage.

synopsis: The flight instructor's inadequate supervision of the flight and improper decision to continue with a takeoff after the airplane swerved off the runway. Contributing to the accident was the student pilot's failure to maintain directional control of the tailwheel-equipped airplane.
summary: A flight instructor and student in a tailwheel airplane swerved off the runway during a full-stop landing due to a left turn followed by a right turn. The aircraft struck a fence after entering waist-high grass, causing substantial damage to wing struts and an engine mount tube with no reported mechanical failure.

synopsis: During a Part 91 instructional flight near Soldotna, Alaska, a Cessna 150J substantially damaged after pitching up to 300 ft agl, rotating left, and descending nose-down into runway 25. The instructor sustained minor injuries and the student was seriously injured while practicing short and soft field landings.
summary: During a Part 91 instructional flight near Soldotna, Alaska, a Cessna 150J substantially damaged after pitching up to 300 ft agl, rotating left, and descending nose-down into runway 25. The instructor sustained minor injuries and the student was seriously injured while practicing short and soft field landings.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper J5C suffered a fatal accident with a passenger during a Part 91 flight after the engine surged and lost power due to fuel contamination from dirt in the gasolator. The pilot attempted a forced landing on a street but struck a tree and impacted the ground, substantially damaging the aircraft.
summary: The pilot of a Piper J5C suffered a fatal accident with a passenger during a Part 91 flight after the engine surged and lost power due to fuel contamination from dirt in the gasolator. The pilot attempted a forced landing on a street but struck a tree and impacted the ground, substantially damaging the aircraft.

synopsis: The pilot of a Schleicher ASW27-18 glider was fatally injured when the aircraft impacted a mountain slope near Morgan, Utah, shortly after release from a tow. The glider struck the terrain at 6,625 feet MSL and was subsequently consumed by a post-crash fire.
summary: The pilot of a Schleicher ASW27-18 glider was fatally injured when the aircraft impacted a mountain slope near Morgan, Utah, shortly after release from a tow. The glider struck the terrain at 6,625 feet MSL and was subsequently consumed by a post-crash fire.

synopsis: A student pilot flying a Cessna 152 Part 91 personal flight was fatally injured when the aircraft impacted terrain near Hornell, New York. Witnesses reported the engine-operating airplane entered a descending right turn and struck trees in densely wooded terrain.
summary: A student pilot flying a Cessna 152 Part 91 personal flight was fatally injured when the aircraft impacted terrain near Hornell, New York. Witnesses reported the engine-operating airplane entered a descending right turn and struck trees in densely wooded terrain.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to continue an unstabilized approach, which resulted in a landing touchdown with insufficient runway remaining and a subsequent runway overrun and a collision with a fence.
summary: The pilot executed a steep straight-in arrival without decelerating to normal landing speed, causing a fast midfield touchdown. The aircraft overran the runway, struck a perimeter fence, and crossed six traffic lanes before stopping in a grass field with substantial right wing lift strut damage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance during approach in gusting wind conditions to a remote airstrip, resulting in a collision with brush.
summary: During a circling approach in gusty winds, the pilot landed short after a sudden headwind dissipation, causing the right wing to strike brush. The aircraft veered, spun 180°, and exited the runway with substantial damage to the right wing and elevators, with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from terrain while maneuvering at low altitude.
summary: The pilot conducting a low-level search for a gravel bar landing site inadvertently struck rough terrain with the tailwheel, causing a hard landing. The main gear then hit a 3-foot gravel berm and collapsed, resulting in substantial damage to the fuselage and left wing lift struts due to overload forces.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from obstacles during an aborted landing, while flying in tailwind conditions. Contributing to the accident was the high density altitude weather condition.
summary: The pilot landed on runway 07 at 70 knots, aborted due to insufficient deceleration, and collided with a residential structure during the go-around. The accident caused substantial damage to the wings, fuselage, and elevator, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: A flight instructor and student in a Cessna 172P experienced sudden engine power loss at 250-300 feet AGL during initial climb, likely due to carburetor icing. The aircraft was forced to land in a field, nosed over, and was substantially damaged, though both occupants escaped without injury.
summary: A flight instructor and student in a Cessna 172P experienced sudden engine power loss at 250-300 feet AGL during initial climb, likely due to carburetor icing. The aircraft was forced to land in a field, nosed over, and was substantially damaged, though both occupants escaped without injury.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to confirm the fuel quantity before flight which resulted in a loss of engine power due to fuel starvation.
summary: The pilot experienced an engine power loss 20 minutes after takeoff due to fuel exhaustion, despite gauges indicating near-full tanks. He executed a forced landing to a road where the right wing struck a tree, causing substantial damage, attributed to reliance on unreliable fuel gauges without visual verification.

synopsis: The flight instructor's inadequate supervision and delayed remedial action which resulted in a skid contacting the terrain. Contributing to the accident was the flight instructor's improper judgement to allow the student pilot to manipulate the flight controls at a low altitude/hover.
summary: During a low-altitude instructional hover, a student pilot lost control of a helicopter, causing it to drift, descend, and roll over into terrain. The flight instructor attributed the substantial damage to his delayed intervention rather than any mechanical failure.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airplane control during an aborted takeoff.
summary: The pilot aborted a takeoff after the aircraft settled back to the runway, then abruptly pulled back on the stick to avoid nosing over. This caused the airplane to balloon, strike trees, and rest in a ditch with substantial damage, though no mechanical failures were reported.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to operate the airplane with a known deficiency of the floats, which resulted in an accumulation of water in the forward compartments of the floats, a forward center of gravity, and subsequent nose over during a water landing.
summary: The pilot of an amphibious airplane nosed over during a water landing after excessive water accumulation in the forward float compartments shifted the center of gravity forward. The pilot had previously observed significant water in these compartments but continued flying, resulting in substantial fuselage damage.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of airplane control following an encounter with a microburst during takeoff.
summary: The pilot reported that during takeoff on runway 17, a microburst caused a strong crosswind that rolled the aircraft right, dragging the wingtip and causing it to exit the runway, cartwheel into a ditch, and sustain substantial damage to the right wing and tail.

synopsis: A student pilot flying a Piper PA28-180 solo experienced a loud bang and total power loss at 7,500 feet due to a missing propeller blade. Although the emergency landing on a highway was initially uneventful, damaged rudder pedals caused a loss of directional control, resulting in a collision with a median curb and substantial engine mount damage.
summary: A student pilot flying a Piper PA28-180 solo experienced a loud bang and total power loss at 7,500 feet due to a missing propeller blade. Although the emergency landing on a highway was initially uneventful, damaged rudder pedals caused a loss of directional control, resulting in a collision with a median curb and substantial engine mount damage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to extend the landing gear during landing. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's failure to use a pre-landing checklist.
summary: The pilot landed a training aircraft with the gear retracted during touch-and-go practice, causing the airplane to slide and sustain substantial lower fuselage damage. The incident resulted from the pilot's failure to use a pre-landing checklist, with no mechanical malfunctions reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to detect the inadvertent deployment of the spoilers, which resulted in a prolonged, excessive descent rate. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's decision to conduct a downwind approach versus a straight in approach to the diversionary airport, which resulted in an off-airport landing.
summary: A glider pilot encountered turbulence and rotor wave activity during a tow near mountains, leading to rapid sink after release. Although the pilot retracted inadvertently extended spoilers and attempted a diversion, insufficient altitude forced a field landing where tall grass caused a ground loop and substantial tail boom damage.

synopsis: A flight instructor and student pilot in a Cessna 172N experienced severe engine vibration and power loss at 1,800 feet during a Part 91 instructional flight. The instructor performed a forced landing to a dirt road, but the aircraft veered off, impacted terrain, and sustained substantial damage to the fuselage, wings, and engine.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot in a Cessna 172N experienced severe engine vibration and power loss at 1,800 feet during a Part 91 instructional flight. The instructor performed a forced landing to a dirt road, but the aircraft veered off, impacted terrain, and sustained substantial damage to the fuselage, wings, and engine.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to adequately compensate for a wind gust during the departure roll, which resulted in a loss of directional control and a runway excursion.
summary: During takeoff, a large wind gust pushed the aircraft left off the runway, causing the left wing to strike trees. The pilot reported substantial damage to the wings and fuselage but stated no mechanical malfunctions occurred prior to impact.

synopsis: The pilot's improper pedal application during an approach to a hover.
summary: The pilot reported that while transitioning a helicopter into a 4 ft hover, a wind gust caused an overreaction with right pedal input, leading to a dynamic rollover and terrain impact. The aircraft sustained substantial fuselage and tailboom damage with no preaccident mechanical failures.

synopsis: A private pilot flying a Jabiru J-230-D experienced repeated engine power drops during climb and approach, leading to a total power loss at 1,400 feet. Unable to reach the airport or land safely on a crowded beach, the pilot ditched the aircraft into the water, sustaining minor injuries while the airplane was substantially damaged.
summary: A private pilot flying a Jabiru J-230-D experienced repeated engine power drops during climb and approach, leading to a total power loss at 1,400 feet. Unable to reach the airport or land safely on a crowded beach, the pilot ditched the aircraft into the water, sustaining minor injuries while the airplane was substantially damaged.

synopsis: A Beech 300 operating a Part 135 positioning flight crashed near Chinle, Arizona, killing the pilot, co-pilot, and two medical crew members. The aircraft entered a knife-edge attitude and pitched up before impacting terrain while on the base leg for runway 36.
summary: A Beech 300 operating a Part 135 positioning flight crashed near Chinle, Arizona, killing the pilot, co-pilot, and two medical crew members. The aircraft entered a knife-edge attitude and pitched up before impacting terrain while on the base leg for runway 36.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from trees while taxiing, which resulted in a wing strike.
summary: The pilot taxied the aircraft on the far left side of the runway to avoid soft terrain and rocks after a full-stop landing. The left wing struck a tree during this maneuver, causing substantial damage, with no mechanical malfunctions reported.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: During a practice landing, the pilot intentionally flew slow and forgot to focus on the horizon during the flare, causing the aircraft to stall and land hard. This resulted in substantial fuselage damage, with no pre-accident mechanical malfunctions reported.

synopsis: A private pilot flying a Lewinski Sonex, N67BG, suffered serious burns and substantial aircraft damage after the airplane pulled left and stalled shortly after takeoff near Tellico Plains, Tennessee. The pilot attributed the loss of control to a suspected nose wheel bearing issue noted during prior taxi tests, though he reported no engine or flight control malfunctions.
summary: A private pilot flying a Lewinski Sonex, N67BG, suffered serious burns and substantial aircraft damage after the airplane pulled left and stalled shortly after takeoff near Tellico Plains, Tennessee. The pilot attributed the loss of control to a suspected nose wheel bearing issue noted during prior taxi tests, though he reported no engine or flight control malfunctions.

synopsis: A student pilot flying an Aeronca 7AC under Part 91 sustained serious injuries when the aircraft impacted Runway 13 at Willow Airport in a nosed-down, near-vertical attitude. Initial examination found no pre-impact mechanical failures, though the cause remains pending further wreckage analysis.
summary: A student pilot flying an Aeronca 7AC under Part 91 sustained serious injuries when the aircraft impacted Runway 13 at Willow Airport in a nosed-down, near-vertical attitude. Initial examination found no pre-impact mechanical failures, though the cause remains pending further wreckage analysis.

synopsis: During a Part 137 agricultural flight near Slayton, Minnesota, the pilot of an Ayres S2R-G6 reported that flight controls locked up at 200 feet while turning for a spray pass. Unable to recover with rudder inputs, the aircraft impacted terrain in a left-wing-low attitude, causing substantial damage and serious injury to the pilot.
