summary: During a Part 137 agricultural flight near Slayton, Minnesota, the pilot of an Ayres S2R-G6 reported that flight controls locked up at 200 feet while turning for a spray pass. Unable to recover with rudder inputs, the aircraft impacted terrain in a left-wing-low attitude, causing substantial damage and serious injury to the pilot.

synopsis: The pilot of a Stolp Starduster SA 300 experienced a sudden total loss of power 40 minutes after departing Smith Field Airport. He performed an off-airport landing, striking a fence post with the right wing, which caused the aircraft to flip and sustain substantial damage.
summary: The pilot of a Stolp Starduster SA 300 experienced a sudden total loss of power 40 minutes after departing Smith Field Airport. He performed an off-airport landing, striking a fence post with the right wing, which caused the aircraft to flip and sustain substantial damage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during takeoff roll, which resulted in a runway excursion and collision with haybales.
summary: The pilot lost directional control during takeoff roll on a short asphalt runway, causing the aircraft to turn left and strike haybales. An FAA inspector found no mechanical malfunctions, noting the airplane lacked rudder trim and the pilot had been using heavy right rudder.

synopsis: An Air Tractor AT-301 pilot suffered serious injuries when the aircraft sustained substantial damage during a forced landing in a cornfield near Davenport, North Dakota. The accident occurred during an aerial application return climb at 500 feet after the engine lost power due to low fuel, despite the pilot's attempt to manually restore flow.
summary: An Air Tractor AT-301 pilot suffered serious injuries when the aircraft sustained substantial damage during a forced landing in a cornfield near Davenport, North Dakota. The accident occurred during an aerial application return climb at 500 feet after the engine lost power due to low fuel, despite the pilot's attempt to manually restore flow.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain helicopter clearance from the powerline during the powerline maintenance operation for reasons that could not be determined.
summary: A pilot and lineman were performing maintenance on a powerline when the helicopter's tail struck the line, causing the tailboom to separate and the cockpit to hit the line. The aircraft fell onto a barge and caught fire; the pilot had chosen to use the helicopter platform over a rope despite safety concerns.

synopsis: A Cessna T182T pilot and passenger were involved in a fatal accident near Augusta, Arkansas, during a Part 91 personal flight. The aircraft crashed inverted in a cornfield after a recorded track showed erratic turns, with post-accident examination revealing no pre-existing mechanical failures in the engine or flight controls.
summary: A Cessna T182T pilot and passenger were involved in a fatal accident near Augusta, Arkansas, during a Part 91 personal flight. The aircraft crashed inverted in a cornfield after a recorded track showed erratic turns, with post-accident examination revealing no pre-existing mechanical failures in the engine or flight controls.

synopsis: The pilot of a Vans RV4 reported an electrical voltage spike to 20 volts at 1,000 feet AGL, causing total instrument and engine power loss with smoke. He executed a forced landing on a golf course, resulting in substantial damage to the fuselage and engine mount, though both occupants were uninjured.
summary: The pilot of a Vans RV4 reported an electrical voltage spike to 20 volts at 1,000 feet AGL, causing total instrument and engine power loss with smoke. He executed a forced landing on a golf course, resulting in substantial damage to the fuselage and engine mount, though both occupants were uninjured.

synopsis: During a Part 91 instructional flight in a Cirrus SR22 at 10,500 ft, the engine lost power while the student pilot performed a lean test. The instructor activated the CAPS parachute at 1,500 ft agl, but the subsequent hard landing caused substantial damage to the fuselage and wings, seriously injuring the student and passenger.
summary: During a Part 91 instructional flight in a Cirrus SR22 at 10,500 ft, the engine lost power while the student pilot performed a lean test. The instructor activated the CAPS parachute at 1,500 ft agl, but the subsequent hard landing caused substantial damage to the fuselage and wings, seriously injuring the student and passenger.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain airspeed and altitude resulting in a collision with the ground during the base to final turn.
summary: A solo student pilot flying a glider on the base leg became task saturated and failed to maintain altitude and airspeed, causing the aircraft to impact the ground during the turn to final. The pilot escaped uninjured, but the glider sustained substantial damage to the fuselage and right wing with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The student pilot's inadequate landing flare and recovery from a bounced landing.
summary: A student pilot performing a solo cross-country flight executed a hard landing due to improper flare and failure to add power to correct oscillation. The aircraft porpoised on the runway, sustaining firewall damage, with no pre-impact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The captain's decision to continue the landing after the bounce and the subsequent misapplication of pitch controls. Contributing to the accident was the ongoing "land and hold short" operations that may have created an urgency to land.
summary: Republic Airways flight 5783 sustained substantial tail strike damage during landing at Boston Logan after a bounce and subsequent hard touchdown. The captain's increased back pressure raised the pitch attitude to 14° with compressed gear, causing the tail cone to contact the runway.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from rising terrain while maneuvering at low altitude.
summary: The pilot of a float-equipped airplane encountered a downdraft while orbiting at 500 feet AGL to view wildlife, forcing a landing on rocky terrain. The impact collapsed the float struts and spreaderbars, causing substantial fuselage damage, with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from a tree which resulted in the right wing impacting the tree and a subsequent collision with trees and terrain. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's decision to operate the airplane at a low altitude over trees.
summary: The pilot of a privately owned aircraft struck a standing dead tree with the right wing while turning from downwind to base leg between two backcountry airstrips. The pilot attributed the accident to operating at too low an altitude and insufficient attention to tree proximity, resulting in substantial damage to the airframe.

synopsis: During takeoff of an Air Tractor AT-502 agricultural flight, the pilot reported low torque and could not jettison the load due to a migrated handgrip blocking the switch. The aircraft impacted a field and came to rest inverted with substantial damage after the pilot failed to maintain altitude.
summary: During takeoff of an Air Tractor AT-502 agricultural flight, the pilot reported low torque and could not jettison the load due to a migrated handgrip blocking the switch. The aircraft impacted a field and came to rest inverted with substantial damage after the pilot failed to maintain altitude.

synopsis: The pilot of a Rockwell International 112 experienced sudden engine power loss on the downwind leg for runway 10 at Burlington Airport. The aircraft landed 15 feet short of the runway, impacted a berm, and sustained substantial damage to the left wing spar, though the pilot was uninjured.
summary: The pilot of a Rockwell International 112 experienced sudden engine power loss on the downwind leg for runway 10 at Burlington Airport. The aircraft landed 15 feet short of the runway, impacted a berm, and sustained substantial damage to the left wing spar, though the pilot was uninjured.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain aircraft control during the landing and go-around with variable wind direction and speed.
summary: During the landing flare, the pilot experienced sudden pitch and yaw deviations, leading to a 90° right yaw, ground impact, and substantial left wing damage. The pilot attributed the upset to a suspected dust devil or surface wind trough, reporting no preimpact mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate monitoring of the airplane during taxi which resulted in collision with a sign.
summary: The pilot, while taxiing for departure after a touch-and-go, looked at a tablet to load a route and ran off the pavement into a sign. This collision caused substantial damage to the right wing underside, with no preimpact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: During a night cross-country training flight in a Piper PA-28-151, the engine lost power at 300–400 feet AGL during a go-around at DeKalb-Peachtree Airport. The flight instructor attributed the accident to fuel exhaustion, resulting in an off-airport landing where the aircraft struck powerlines and a tree, causing serious injuries to the pilots.
summary: During a night cross-country training flight in a Piper PA-28-151, the engine lost power at 300–400 feet AGL during a go-around at DeKalb-Peachtree Airport. The flight instructor attributed the accident to fuel exhaustion, resulting in an off-airport landing where the aircraft struck powerlines and a tree, causing serious injuries to the pilots.

synopsis: A pilot and passenger were seriously injured when their T-28C crashed near West Wendover, Utah, during climb-out due to an engine failure. Investigators found fractured articulating rods and metallic debris in the oil system, indicating internal engine damage caused the loss of power and subsequent impact.
summary: A pilot and passenger were seriously injured when their T-28C crashed near West Wendover, Utah, during climb-out due to an engine failure. Investigators found fractured articulating rods and metallic debris in the oil system, indicating internal engine damage caused the loss of power and subsequent impact.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental Kitfox N300KF suffered serious injuries when the engine abruptly lost all power on the base leg. The pilot performed a forced landing in a pasture, where the aircraft nosed over and came to rest inverted, causing substantial damage to the vertical stabilizer and rudder.
summary: The pilot of an experimental Kitfox N300KF suffered serious injuries when the engine abruptly lost all power on the base leg. The pilot performed a forced landing in a pasture, where the aircraft nosed over and came to rest inverted, causing substantial damage to the vertical stabilizer and rudder.

synopsis: The pilot's abrupt maneuver to avoid a powerline during an aerial application flight, which resulted in the helicopter's impact with terrain.
summary: During an aerial application flight, a helicopter pilot executed a hard right turn to avoid powerlines perceived as too low to cross. The maneuver caused the helicopter to lose lift, resulting in ground contact with the spray boom and main rotor, a rollover, and substantial damage to the fuselage and tail boom.

synopsis: The pilot's premature rotation at insufficient airspeed during takeoff to avoid an unexpected animal on the runway, which resulted in a loss of control and subsequent nose-over during the aborted takeoff. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's excessive brake application.
summary: During departure from a private grass airstrip, a pilot aborted takeoff after an animal entered the runway and the aircraft bounced due to insufficient airspeed. Heavy braking on the remaining runway caused the airplane to nose over, resulting in substantial damage to the rudder and vertical stabilizer.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll with crosswind.
summary: The pilot ground looped the airplane while landing on runway 13 in 11-knot winds from 110°, causing the right wing and horizontal stabilizer to strike the ground. The aircraft subsequently went nose down and came to rest upright, resulting in substantial damage to the right wing and horizontal stabilizer.

synopsis: The captain of a DHC-6-300 operating a Part 135 flight to Grand Canyon Bar Ten Airstrip lost directional control on landing due to strong gusting westerly winds. The aircraft veered off the runway, struck a ditch, and sustained substantial damage to the left wing and forward fuselage, though all occupants were evacuated with only minor injuries to six passengers.
summary: The captain of a DHC-6-300 operating a Part 135 flight to Grand Canyon Bar Ten Airstrip lost directional control on landing due to strong gusting westerly winds. The aircraft veered off the runway, struck a ditch, and sustained substantial damage to the left wing and forward fuselage, though all occupants were evacuated with only minor injuries to six passengers.

synopsis: During a Part 135 air medical flight, the pilot of an Airbus AS350 B3 damaged the tail rotor by contacting a parking sign while performing a left pedal turn in a hover near the Las Cruces helipad. The pilot reported no mechanical failures, and all four occupants were uninjured.
summary: During a Part 135 air medical flight, the pilot of an Airbus AS350 B3 damaged the tail rotor by contacting a parking sign while performing a left pedal turn in a hover near the Las Cruces helipad. The pilot reported no mechanical failures, and all four occupants were uninjured.

synopsis: The pilot of a North American T-28B, N28XT, was fatally injured when the aircraft was substantially damaged during an emergency landing in a bean field near Monticello, Iowa. The accident occurred after the pilot reported a propeller governor failure followed by a total loss of engine power while returning to the airport.
summary: The pilot of a North American T-28B, N28XT, was fatally injured when the aircraft was substantially damaged during an emergency landing in a bean field near Monticello, Iowa. The accident occurred after the pilot reported a propeller governor failure followed by a total loss of engine power while returning to the airport.

synopsis: A DHC-6-300 air taxi flight with two pilots and 16 passengers suffered substantial damage upon landing at San Clemente Island when the left engine propeller beta ring fragmented. The failure caused a hard left yaw and pitch-down, resulting in a runway excursion with no injuries.
summary: A DHC-6-300 air taxi flight with two pilots and 16 passengers suffered substantial damage upon landing at San Clemente Island when the left engine propeller beta ring fragmented. The failure caused a hard left yaw and pitch-down, resulting in a runway excursion with no injuries.

synopsis: Failure of the left main landing gear due to the loss of the protective paint coating and a change in the local surface finish from impermissible grinding, which resulted in fatigue cracking.
summary: During the landing roll at 15 mph, the pilot reported the airplane veered right, and corrective braking caused the left main landing gear to collapse, damaging the fuselage and wing. The NTSB determined the gear fractured due to fatigue cracking from impermissible surface grinding that removed protective paint.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to obtain a proper touchdown point while attempting to land on a very short and rough turf runway, which resulted in a runway overrun and collision with vegetation and terrain.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane rejected a second landing on a short, rough turf strip after bouncing over humps. While attempting to clear reeds at the runway end, the propeller struck the vegetation, causing the aircraft to decelerate, nose over, and come to rest inverted with substantial damage.

synopsis: The pilot's unstable approach to the runway, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall at low altitude and impact with terrain.
summary: The pilot reported the airplane was too high during approach, leading to an idle power descent where airspeed decayed and a stall warning sounded. The aircraft rolled left, impacted terrain beside the runway, and caught fire, though all occupants escaped before the plane was destroyed by postaccident fire.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental Vans RV-7A was fatally injured when the aircraft struck a tree during a go-around at Ryan Field Airport. summary: The pilot forgot to extend the landing gear while in the traffic pattern and did not hear the warning horn. The aircraft landed gear-up, sustaining substantial fuselage damage near the nose wheel well, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's improper fuel planning, which resulted in fuel exhaustion and a subsequent forced landing.
summary: The pilot experienced engine power loss during cruise at 2,400 feet due to fuel exhaustion, forcing a landing that damaged the left wing. Post-accident investigation found less than one gallon of fuel onboard despite the pilot's estimate of 18 gallons, with no mechanical engine failure identified.

summary: A Cessna 172L pilot conducting a personal flight near Walters, Oklahoma, was killed when the aircraft impacted terrain nose-down at high speed. Radar data showed the airplane descending and accelerating before impact, with wreckage indicating a high-speed, nose-down collision.

summary: The pilot of a Cessna 180K experienced a ground loop and left main landing gear collapse while taxiing after landing at Lake Riverside Estates Airport. summary: A pilot and passenger were fatally injured when their Beech M35, N951T, impacted wooded terrain on Sierra Grande Mountain near Des Moines, New Mexico, during a Part 91 personal flight. summary: Air Canada Rouge flight ROU1717, an Airbus A319, touched down short of runway 20L at Nashville International Airport during a rain-affected RNAV (GPS) approach. synopsis: During a Part 91 instructional takeoff on runway 19, a Piper PA-12 yawed left despite full right rudder input and departed the runway. The aircraft struck a berm and perimeter fence, causing substantial damage and serious injuries to the pilot.
summary: During a Part 91 instructional takeoff on runway 19, a Piper PA-12 yawed left despite full right rudder input and departed the runway. The aircraft struck a berm and perimeter fence, causing substantial damage and serious injuries to the pilot.

summary: Two pilots operating a Cessna 560XL experienced an uncommanded steep climb and multiple stalls after takeoff due to a bent elevator pushrod contacting a structural member. synopsis: During a Part 91 instructional flight in a Cessna 172, the engine failed to respond to power addition while in the traffic pattern due to automotive fuel contamination. The flight instructor attempted a return to the runway, but the aircraft struck trees half a mile from the airport, causing substantial damage and injuries.
summary: During a Part 91 instructional flight in a Cessna 172, the engine failed to respond to power addition while in the traffic pattern due to automotive fuel contamination. synopsis: The pilot's failure to assemble the glider's elevator control before takeoff.
summary: During preflight assembly, the pilot failed to connect the elevator control on the glider. After takeoff, the pilot released from the tow plane upon realizing the lack of control, causing the glider to nose down and impact the ground with substantial damage to the fuselage and tail boom.

synopsis: A student pilot and passenger in a Cessna 140 were fatally and seriously injured, respectively, when the aircraft impacted the ocean shortly after departing Shelter Cove Airport. The passenger reported the plane entered low coastal fog during a right turn, was violently pushed down by turbulence, and struck the water before the wreckage was recovered.
summary: A student pilot and passenger in a Cessna 140 were fatally and seriously injured, respectively, when the aircraft impacted the ocean shortly after departing Shelter Cove Airport. synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane during landing, which resulted in a runway excursion and subsequent nose over.
summary: A solo student pilot bounced hard on landing, veered off the runway into grass, and nosed over inverted after failing to gain altitude. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the wings, fuselage, tail, and engine mount with no reported pre-impact mechanical failures.

summary: A pilot operating a Lancair NLA-275-FR-C on a Part 91 flight was fatally injured when the aircraft was destroyed near Bradley, Arkansas. ADS-B data showed the airplane entered a rapid right spiraling descent from 11,800 feet before impacting terrain and burning.

summary: The pilot of a banner tow aircraft experienced a loud bang, vibrations, and total engine power loss due to a failed No. 2 cylinder exhaust valve. He executed a forced landing that resulted in a ground loop, fence impact, and substantial damage to the left elevator.

summary: During an aerial application flight, a Grumman G-164-B experienced total engine failure due to a severed fuel control unit sensing line. The pilot landed in a bean field, sustaining substantial damage to the wings and fuselage, but was not injured.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain airplane directional control during the approach and subsequent go-around.
summary: A student pilot conducting a solo flight in a single-engine airplane drifted left during the third landing attempt despite rudder and go-around inputs. The aircraft impacted the ground nose-down with substantial damage to the left wing, firewall, and rudder, with no mechanical failure reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll with a crosswind.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane bounced on touchdown during a crosswind landing on runway 03, causing the aircraft to drift, exit the runway, and pivot in the grass. The left landing gear separated and the left wing struck the ground, resulting in substantial damage with no preaccident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: During an enroute descent, the pilot of a Robinson R44 II helicopter experienced loud vibration and lost tail rotor authority while the alternator warning light illuminated. summary: During an enroute descent, the pilot of a Robinson R44 II helicopter experienced loud vibration and lost tail rotor authority while the alternator warning light illuminated. The pilot executed an autorotation that resulted in a hard landing, causing the main rotor to strike the tail boom and substantially damage the aircraft.

synopsis: The failure of the left main landing gear mount due to extensive corrosion while landing in an area of rough terrain.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane reported that the main landing gear collapsed upon landing at a remote airstrip due to rough terrain, causing substantial damage. Investigation revealed the left gear fractured at the fuselage attach point, likely caused by a fatigue crack initiated by extensive corrosion.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain a rate of climb sufficient to clear obstacles during takeoff, resulting in a collision with tree-covered terrain.
summary: The pilot reported that shortly after takeoff from a remote, wet, gravel airstrip, the airplane unexpectedly descended and settled into trees despite recovery attempts. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the horizontal stabilizer, wings, and fuselage, with no preaccident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's excessive use of brakes during landing roll, which resulted in a nose-over.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane nosed over during the landing roll after inadvertently applying excessive braking. This resulted in substantial damage to the rudder, with no preaccident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll with a quartering tailwind.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane experienced a left wing strike during the landing roll on runway 02 while correcting for a low wing. The aircraft veered off the runway, struck rough terrain, and nosed over inverted, causing substantial damage to the left wing and rudder with no reported mechanical failures.

aircraft: Dassault/Sud FAN JET FALCON SER D
synopsis: During a Part 91 positioning descent, a Dassault Falcon D experienced a loud bang and vibration, causing the flightcrew to divert to Martinsburg. summary: During a Part 91 positioning descent, a Dassault Falcon D experienced a loud bang and vibration, causing the flightcrew to divert to Martinsburg. synopsis: The pilot's inadequate landing flare at night, which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: The pilot experienced restricted elevator control during the landing flare of a personal night flight, resulting in a flat touchdown and substantial damage to the firewall and lower fuselage. Post-accident examination determined the control binding was caused by a bent pivot point from the hard landing, with no pre-existing mechanical failures found.

synopsis: A commercial pilot flying a Vans RV-6A for familiarization experienced total engine power loss near Warrensburg, Missouri, despite checking fuel and mixture. The aircraft stalled during a forced landing into a cornfield, sustaining substantial fuselage damage while the pilot suffered minor injuries.
summary: A commercial pilot flying a Vans RV-6A for familiarization experienced total engine power loss near Warrensburg, Missouri, despite checking fuel and mixture. synopsis: Separation of the right landing gear wheel assembly during landing.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane experienced a right landing gear wheel assembly separation during touchdown, causing the aircraft to veer and nose over. The probable cause was insufficient bolt torque or loosening, which allowed the wheel to detach and damage the airframe.

aircraft: Jmb Aircraft S R O VL-3LSA-912
synopsis: The flight instructors inadequate supervision of the flight and delayed remedial action and the pilot's improper landing flare during which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: During a commercial pilot training landing, a student pilot initiated a go-around due to wind gusts, but the flight instructor simultaneously pulled back on the controls without a clear transfer of command. This conflicting input caused an abrupt pitch-up, resulting in a tail strike, aerodynamic stall, and substantial fuselage damage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain elevator control during the landing, which resulted in a nose over.
summary: During the landing roll on a dry grass strip, the pilot released elevator back pressure before braking, causing the airplane to nose over and come to rest inverted. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the left wing, vertical stabilizer, and rudder, with the pilot attributing the incident to premature control input release.

summary: The pilot landed on a non-approved grass surface between the runway and taxiway, causing the aircraft to nose over despite control inputs and braking. The plane came to rest inverted with substantial damage to the vertical stabilizer, rudder, left wing, and lift struts, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of control after a rejected takeoff, which resulted in a noseover.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane aborted a takeoff from a remote airstrip after encountering rough terrain and insufficient airspeed. The aircraft bounced, nosed over during heavy braking, and came to rest inverted with substantial damage to the wings and vertical stabilizer.

aircraft: Vu Holdings Llc/Dba Vanilla Un VA 001
synopsis: A Platform Aerospace VA 001 UAS, N246VU, sustained substantial damage after impacting a beachside cliff near Ninilchik, Alaska, during an off-airport emergency landing. summary: A Platform Aerospace VA 001 UAS, N246VU, sustained substantial damage after impacting a beachside cliff near Ninilchik, Alaska, during an off-airport emergency landing. synopsis: A commercial pilot flying a Beech A36 from Little Rock to Clarksburg experienced total engine power loss at 6,000 feet due to fuel exhaustion. The pilot performed a forced landing in a field, sustaining substantial right wing damage, though all four occupants were uninjured.
summary: A commercial pilot flying a Beech A36 from Little Rock to Clarksburg experienced total engine power loss at 6,000 feet due to fuel exhaustion. The pilot performed a forced landing in a field, sustaining substantial right wing damage, though all four occupants were uninjured.

synopsis: A pilot ferrying a Cessna A185F from Europe to the US was fatally injured when the aircraft ground looped left during a visual approach to Bangor International Airport runway 33. The pilot attributed the incident to flat light conditions that obscured terrain height, noting no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain helicopter control which resulted in an uncontrolled descent and impact with terrain.
summary: During a rotorcraft external load firefighting refill, a pilot lost control when a nearby helicopter's wake turbulence caused a left pitch in 15-knot gusts. The aircraft descended into the lake, sustaining substantial main rotor blade damage, with no mechanical failure reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from terrain while maneuvering at low altitude.
summary: During low-altitude aerial application, the pilot maneuvered under power lines and impacted terrain while attempting to pull up. The fuselage and left wing sustained substantial damage, with no preaccident mechanical malfunctions reported.

synopsis: The front seat passenger's inadvertent movement of the cyclic control resulting in a dynamic rollover after landing. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's decision to leave the dual flight controls installed with a non-pilot passenger in the front seat.
summary: The pilot of an OH-58A helicopter experienced a dynamic rollover during landing in gusty winds after a passenger inadvertently contacted the cyclic control. This interference caused the aircraft to roll onto its right side, resulting in substantial damage to the main rotor and fuselage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing with a gusting crosswind. Contributing to the accident was the closure of the wind aligned runway 27.
summary: The pilot of a Cirrus SR22T executing a crosswind landing on Runway 18 ballooned and drifted left due to gusts exceeding the manual's limit, resulting in a grass impact and substantial left wing damage. The pilot attributed the accident to the closure of Runway 27 and the failure to select an alternate airport with suitable wind conditions.

synopsis: The pilot receiving instruction's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll. Contributing to the accident was the flight instructor's delayed remedial action.
summary: A tailwheel-endorsed pilot and flight instructor ground looped a tailwheel-equipped airplane during a three-point landing after the pilot bounced and lost directional control. The incident caused substantial damage to the right wing and elevator, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

summary: A commercial pilot flying a Cessna 310Q on an IFR approach to Milledgeville descended below the cleared 3,000 ft minimum after a low altitude alert. The aircraft impacted trees and terrain with retracted gear, destroying the airplane and fatally injuring the pilot.

summary: The pilot of a Rans S-12 Airaile was fatally injured when the aircraft entered a nose-down spiral descent near Concordia, Kansas, after struggling to gain altitude. synopsis: The flight instructor's distraction during landing, which resulted in a long landing and subsequent runway excursion.
summary: A student pilot's tablet interfered with controls during landing flare, causing the flight instructor to divert attention and resulting in a runway overrun. The instructor steered the aircraft off the left end to avoid trees, causing nose gear collapse and substantial fuselage damage with no mechanical malfunction.

summary: The pilot of a Cirrus aircraft experienced fuel exhaustion during the engine break-in phase after forgetting to switch tanks as intended. He activated the CAPS system, resulting in a hard landing and substantial right wing damage, while 14 gallons of fuel remained in the breached right tank.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll with a quartering tailwind.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane ground looped and nosed over while landing on runway 32, causing substantial damage to the rudder, fuselage, and wing strut. The pilot attributed the accident to a left quartering tailwind rather than any mechanical failure.

synopsis: The pilot of a Raytheon A36, N855DC, suffered serious injuries when the aircraft impacted trees and ground during approach to Gulf Shores, Alabama, after the engine lost power due to fuel exhaustion. The accident occurred because the pilot switched to a fuel tank that was empty, despite the aircraft having tip tanks that were not filled prior to departure.
summary: The pilot of a Raytheon A36, N855DC, suffered serious injuries when the aircraft impacted trees and ground during approach to Gulf Shores, Alabama, after the engine lost power due to fuel exhaustion. summary: The pilot experienced a landing gear malfunction enroute due to a cracked hydraulic fitting causing fluid loss. Despite a low pass confirming the gear appeared down, the gear collapsed on touchdown, resulting in substantial fuselage damage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to detect and remove water contamination from the airplane's fuel system before the flight, which resulted in a total loss of engine power during initial climb.
summary: The pilot-owner of an experimental amateur-built aircraft experienced a total engine power loss at 300 feet during a demonstration flight due to water contamination in the fuel. The water entered the right tank from a tipped fuel barrel and was not drained during preflight, causing a forced landing in a wooded area with substantial wing damage.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper PA-28-180 reported a partial engine power loss and vibration during climb-out after a low pass at Chicken Airport. The aircraft impacted terrain half a mile northwest of the airfield, causing substantial damage and minor injuries to the pilot and one passenger.
summary: The pilot of a Piper PA-28-180 reported a partial engine power loss and vibration during climb-out after a low pass at Chicken Airport. The aircraft impacted terrain half a mile northwest of the airfield, causing substantial damage and minor injuries to the pilot and one passenger.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate takeoff performance planning, which resulted in a runway excursion and collision with terrain.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane overran the takeoff area at a remote airstrip due to miscalculating performance abilities. The aircraft struck terrain, causing substantial fuselage damage, with no preaccident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: During a post-maintenance test flight of a Sportcruiser N538SF, the pilot and mechanic encountered an engine problem after takeoff from runway 35. The aircraft could not maintain altitude during a turn back attempt, impacting a field and causing substantial damage and serious injury to the pilot.
summary: During a post-maintenance test flight of a Sportcruiser N538SF, the pilot and mechanic encountered an engine problem after takeoff from runway 35. The aircraft could not maintain altitude during a turn back attempt, impacting a field and causing substantial damage and serious injury to the pilot.

synopsis: A student pilot flying a Piper PA28-140 instructional flight experienced engine misfire and shutdown at 600 feet AGL during the downwind-to-base turn. summary: A student pilot flying a Piper PA28-140 instructional flight experienced engine misfire and shutdown at 600 feet AGL during the downwind-to-base turn. synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing roll in a crosswind, which resulted in a runway excursion and a subsequent ground loop.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane lost directional control during deceleration after landing in crosswind conditions, causing the aircraft to veer off the runway and ground-loop. The pilot reported no mechanical failures, but the airplane sustained substantial damage to the right wingtip and aileron.

summary: The pilot of an amphibious airplane landed on the hull instead of the hard surface runway after becoming distracted and failing to extend the landing gear. This resulted in substantial damage to the composite structure, with no preimpact mechanical malfunctions reported.

synopsis: The pilot of a Bell 407 GTX conducting a Part 135 air medical flight crashed near Lincoln, Montana, while landing in a parking lot at night. Despite confirming visibility through dust, the helicopter's tail struck a sign at 10 feet AGL during a steep approach, causing substantial damage to the airframe and rotors.
summary: The pilot of a Bell 407 GTX conducting a Part 135 air medical flight crashed near Lincoln, Montana, while landing in a parking lot at night. Despite confirming visibility through dust, the helicopter's tail struck a sign at 10 feet AGL during a steep approach, causing substantial damage to the airframe and rotors.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper PA-28-181 experienced partial engine power loss at 1,700 feet after switching fuel tanks, likely due to improper valve selection. He executed a forced landing on Interstate 805, where the left wing struck a sign post, causing substantial damage to the aircraft with no injuries.
summary: The pilot of a Piper PA-28-181 experienced partial engine power loss at 1,700 feet after switching fuel tanks, likely due to improper valve selection. synopsis: The pilot's failure to see and avoid the light pole, which resulted in a collision with the light pole and subsequent ground impact.
summary: The pilot reported that while hovering 10 feet prior to departure, the helicopter struck a light pole while maneuvering away from a parked vehicle. The subsequent ground impact caused substantial damage to the tailboom and fuselage, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's selection of an unsuitable landing area resulting in an on-ground collision with an obscured log and a main landing gear separation.
summary: The pilot reported that while landing a tailwheel-equipped airplane on tidal grass, the left main gear struck a log obscured by tall grass during rollout. This impact caused the left main gear to separate and sustain substantial damage to the gearbox assembly, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll, in gusting crosswind conditions.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane ground looped and exited the runway during landing on Runway 17 due to a right wind gust. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the left wing and aileron, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

summary: A student pilot performing a solo landing on a turf runway 18 struck a bump, causing the aircraft to porpoise and collapse the nose gear. The incident resulted in substantial fuselage damage, with the pilot reporting no pre-accident mechanical failures.

summary: The pilot of a Cessna 172S experienced excessive nose-down pitch requiring emergency declaration and assistance from other aircraft. Despite troubleshooting attempts, the pilot lost control during a spiraling descent and impacted terrain near Los Banos, California, resulting in the aircraft's destruction and the pilot's death.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna 120 operating under Part 91 experienced total engine power loss during approach near Taylor, Arizona, after 1 hour and 25 minutes of flight. The accident, which caused substantial fuselage damage but no injuries, resulted from fuel exhaustion in the selected right tank despite the pilot's preflight dipstick check.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna 120 operating under Part 91 experienced total engine power loss during approach near Taylor, Arizona, after 1 hour and 25 minutes of flight. The accident, which caused substantial fuselage damage but no injuries, resulted from fuel exhaustion in the selected right tank despite the pilot's preflight dipstick check.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing roll, which resulted in a runway excursion and collision with an object.
summary: The pilot of a vintage bi-wing tailwheel aircraft veered off the runway into grass during landing rollout after a wind gust struck at 5 knots. The left wing struck a precision approach path indicator light, causing substantial damage, though the pilot reported no preimpact mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed during landing in gusting wind conditions, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall and impact with terrain.
summary: During a STOL competition landing on Runway 20, the pilot allowed airspeed to decay at 20 ft AGL, causing a left wing stall and loss of control. The aircraft impacted the ground with substantial damage to the left wing and fuselage, with no preaccident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot and passenger of a Cessna 340A were fatally injured when the aircraft collided with terrain near Kearney, Missouri, during a low and slow approach. The airplane rolled left after dipping wings while descending below normal traffic pattern altitude, resulting in substantial damage and a postimpact fire.
summary: The pilot and passenger of a Cessna 340A were fatally injured when the aircraft collided with terrain near Kearney, Missouri, during a low and slow approach. The airplane rolled left after dipping wings while descending below normal traffic pattern altitude, resulting in substantial damage and a postimpact fire.

aircraft: Air Fly Balonismo E Inflaveis AF-SS-94
synopsis: The balloon pilot's failure to see and avoid powerlines during an off-field airport landing.
summary: During a local sightseeing flight, a hot air balloon pilot executed an off-airport landing after spotting a powerline. To avoid basket contact, the pilot vented the envelope, causing the riser cable and envelope to arc against the wires, resulting in substantial equipment damage but no injuries.

synopsis: The pilot's inadvertent entanglement of a lightweight Kevlar long line into the helicopters operating main rotor system, resulting in a severe imbalance and separation of the main rotor gearbox.
summary: A helicopter pilot operating in mountainous terrain exited the aircraft with the engine running to coil a Kevlar long line. The line snagged on rocks, then recoiled into the main rotor, causing severe imbalance that ripped the rotor system from the helicopter and resulted in substantial damage.

synopsis: The accident was the pilot's failure to properly configure the airplane for a soft-field takeoff, which resulted in his decision to abort the takeoff and the subsequent runway overrun.
summary: The pilot aborted a soft-field takeoff on a grass runway after the aircraft failed to lift off and skidded into a fence. The accident likely resulted from retracted flaps, contrary to handbook procedures, which prevented sufficient lift and acceleration in rough conditions.

synopsis: The pilot's fuel system mismanagement which resulted in a loss of engine power due to fuel starvation.
summary: The pilot experienced engine power loss during cruise at 6,500 ft after switching fuel tanks, leading to a forced landing that caused substantial airframe damage. Investigators determined the pilot likely ran the right tank dry and failed to restore fuel flow from the left tank.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna TR182 reported a landing gear malfunction during descent to Montgomery-Gibbs Executive Airport after the hydraulic system lost fluid due to a failed pressure hose. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the left horizontal stabilizer upon landing with the main gear retracted, though the pilot and passenger were uninjured.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna TR182 reported a landing gear malfunction during descent to Montgomery-Gibbs Executive Airport after the hydraulic system lost fluid due to a failed pressure hose. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the left horizontal stabilizer upon landing with the main gear retracted, though the pilot and passenger were uninjured.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental Jabirwatt, N824DW, reported an engine power loss at 1,500 ft MSL near Albany Municipal Airport. The pilot executed an off-airport landing in a field, but the aircraft exited the field and impacted a hazelnut grove, causing substantial wing damage.
summary: The pilot of an experimental Jabirwatt, N824DW, reported an engine power loss at 1,500 ft MSL near Albany Municipal Airport. The pilot executed an off-airport landing in a field, but the aircraft exited the field and impacted a hazelnut grove, causing substantial wing damage.

synopsis: A Cessna 210D carrying two pilots crashed into a cornfield near Kearney, Nebraska, while executing an RNAV (GPS) Runway 18 approach after diverting due to low ceilings. Both pilots were fatally injured when the aircraft impacted the ground following a loss of radar contact and communication with Minneapolis ARTCC.
summary: A Cessna 210D carrying two pilots crashed into a cornfield near Kearney, Nebraska, while executing an RNAV (GPS) Runway 18 approach after diverting due to low ceilings. Both pilots were fatally injured when the aircraft impacted the ground following a loss of radar contact and communication with Minneapolis ARTCC.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a hard, bounced landing and substantial damage to the airplane's fuselage.
summary: A student pilot on a solo touch-and-go landing in the traffic pattern bounced the aircraft multiple times, causing substantial damage to the fuselage underside. The pilot reported no preimpact mechanical malfunctions or failures.

synopsis: The pilot's improper judgment to circumnavigate convective activity which resulted in extensive hail damage to the airplane.
summary: An airline transport pilot and an unqualified commercial pilot flew a two-pilot required aircraft into heavy turbulence and hail at FL 410, causing substantial damage to the wings, empennage, and windshield. The pilot attributed the accident to failing to divert around the weather and noted the aircraft was later found unreported in a hangar.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a hard, bounced landing.
summary: During solo night training, a pilot bounced the aircraft 3 to 4 times on landing, causing substantial lower fuselage damage. The chief pilot attributed the incident to insufficient training on night illusions, noting no mechanical failures occurred.

synopsis: The abrupt maneuver required to comply with a traffic alert and collision avoidance system resolution advisory during descent.
summary: During a Delta A320 descent from FL290 to FL280 en route to DCA, a TCAS resolution advisory caused the captain to level off at FL285. The sudden maneuver injured a flight attendant with fractured kneecaps and two others with minor injuries while they were preparing the cabin.

synopsis: The airplane's encounter with convective turbulence that resulted in serious injuries to a passenger who was out of their seat when the seatbelt sign was illuminated.
summary: SkyWest flight 5971 encountered sudden severe turbulence at FL390 while en route to Houston, injuring two passengers and two flight attendants. The crew declared an emergency and diverted to Austin after a post-accident examination revealed a malfunctioning outflow valve caused a cabin altitude warning.

synopsis: The pilot's improper decision-making for the attempted landing, which resulted in a runway overrun due to inadequate runway landing distance with a quartering tailwind. Contributing to the accident was the wet condition of the runway.
summary: The pilot landed an airplane long on a wet, recently rolled grass runway where braking was ineffective. The aircraft overran the runway, skidded into vegetation while turning left, and sustained substantial fuselage damage due to insufficient available landing distance.

synopsis: The inflight engine compartment fire for reasons that could not be determined.
summary: The pilot experienced radio crackling, blank displays, and total engine power loss while in the traffic pattern, forcing a landing. Smoke and flames appeared during the flare, resulting in substantial fire damage to the engine, fuselage, and empennage, though the exact fire source could not be determined.

synopsis: Maintenance personnel's failure to detect and address water contamination of the airplane's fuel system, which resulted in a total loss of engine power during initial climb.
summary: The pilot/owner experienced total engine power loss during initial climb after a touch-and-go due to water contamination in the fuel system. The aircraft struck a fence and inverted, causing substantial damage, likely because a mechanic failed to document or properly address the water issue during prior maintenance.

synopsis: Unidentified burned debris in an aft galley oven, which generated smoke and odor in the cabin and led to an air turnback and subsequent evacuation, during which a serious injury occurred.
summary: Air Canada flight 1038 crew and passengers experienced smoke and electrical odor during climb out, causing an emergency return to Denver. Post-landing evacuation resulted in one passenger sustaining a serious ankle injury, with the cause identified as burned debris in an aft galley oven.

synopsis: A Cessna 172M conducting an RNAV GPS approach collided midair with an Extra 300 on final approach at Fort Morgan Municipal Airport. The impact destroyed both aircraft, fatally injuring the Extra 300's safety pilot and seriously injuring its pilot, while the Cessna occupants sustained minor injuries.
summary: A Cessna 172M conducting an RNAV GPS approach collided midair with an Extra 300 on final approach at Fort Morgan Municipal Airport. The impact destroyed both aircraft, fatally injuring the Extra 300's safety pilot and seriously injuring its pilot, while the Cessna occupants sustained minor injuries.

synopsis: A Piper PA28-200R, N1147X, carrying a pilot and passenger, crashed into terrain in Little Cottonwood Canyon, Utah, during a personal flight. The pilot seriously injured and the passenger fatally injured after the aircraft struck a tree while climbing the canyon, with the nose dropping and impacting the north valley face.
summary: A Piper PA28-200R, N1147X, carrying a pilot and passenger, crashed into terrain in Little Cottonwood Canyon, Utah, during a personal flight. The pilot seriously injured and the passenger fatally injured after the aircraft struck a tree while climbing the canyon, with the nose dropping and impacting the north valley face.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control of the airplane during takeoff, which resulted in a runway excursion and collision with a sign.
summary: The pilot of a personal flight departed with incorrect flap settings, preventing climb and causing the aircraft to drift off the runway in crosswind. The airplane struck a taxiway sign, sustaining substantial damage to the left horizontal stabilizer, before landing uneventfully in a nearby field.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental Zenith Zodiac 601 HDS suffered an engine failure at 420 feet AGL during a personal flight after refueling with 89 octane automotive fuel. The subsequent forced landing resulted in the aircraft nosing over and coming to rest inverted, causing substantial damage and minor injuries to the occupants.
summary: The pilot of an experimental Zenith Zodiac 601 HDS suffered an engine failure at 420 feet AGL during a personal flight after refueling with 89 octane automotive fuel. The subsequent forced landing resulted in the aircraft nosing over and coming to rest inverted, causing substantial damage and minor injuries to the occupants.

synopsis: A Piper PA-28-180 operating a Part 91 personal flight crashed in mountainous terrain near Wolf, Wyoming, while en route from Sheridan to Boise. The accident resulted in substantial damage to the aircraft, one fatality, and serious injuries to the pilot and another passenger.
summary: A Piper PA-28-180 operating a Part 91 personal flight crashed in mountainous terrain near Wolf, Wyoming, while en route from Sheridan to Boise. The accident resulted in substantial damage to the aircraft, one fatality, and serious injuries to the pilot and another passenger.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to verify the wind direction and maintain an appropriate approach speed, which resulted in a long landing and subsequent runway excursion.
summary: The pilot overflew the airport at sunset, misinterpreting a dim windsock and assuming a favorable runway due to another aircraft's alignment. He executed a go-around, then landed with a 6-knot tailwind, causing a bounce, skid, and runway overrun that resulted in substantial wing damage.

synopsis: The collision with a deer during the aborted landing in night visual meteorological conditions.
summary: A flight instructor and student aborted a night landing to avoid a deer, but a second deer struck the left wing during the subsequent takeoff. The aircraft sustained substantial damage due to wildlife on the runway at an airport lacking exclusion fencing.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to continue the night landing without runway lights which resulted in the runway overrun.
summary: The pilot renting the aircraft for night cross-country training attempted to land on a turf runway after failing to activate pilot-controlled lights. Despite an on-speed approach, the airplane overran the runway and struck trees, sustaining substantial left wing damage with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's mismanagement of available fuel, which resulted in a loss of engine power due to fuel starvation.
summary: The pilot of a single-engine aircraft experienced an engine power loss at 200–300 feet AGL during a touch-and-go, forcing a landing that caused substantial damage. The pilot attributed the incident to failing to switch the fuel selector to the tank containing available fuel.

synopsis: The flight crew's failure to properly identify the heliport in dark night conditions, which resulted in the flight crew attempting to land and a subsequent impact with trees and terrain.
summary: During a night helicopter flight to a private heliport, the crew likely misidentified the landing site due to dark conditions and failed to properly verify location using navigation data. The aircraft impacted trees and terrain after the captain lost visual references, sustaining substantial damage with no pre-impact mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing in crosswind conditions.
summary: A flight instructor landing a crosswind on runway 16R experienced a bounce and gust, causing the aircraft to veer right and ground loop despite corrective rudder and brake inputs. The left wing contacted the runway, sustaining substantial damage, with no preimpact mechanical malfunctions reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from obstacles during an aborted landing. Contributing to the accident was the high density altitude weather condition.
summary: The pilot, unfamiliar with landing at this airport, executed two go-arounds due to people on the grass runway and a hard bounce. During the second go-around, the aircraft struck a wire fence and powerlines, sustaining substantial damage to the wings and fuselage.

synopsis: During a Part 91 scenic flight in an American Champion 8KCAB, the pilot-rated passenger reported a lack of engine response while maneuvering at 2,000 ft agl. The pilot executed a precautionary landing on rough terrain, striking a tree and sustaining substantial damage to the aircraft.
summary: During a Part 91 scenic flight in an American Champion 8KCAB, the pilot-rated passenger reported a lack of engine response while maneuvering at 2,000 ft agl. The pilot executed a precautionary landing on rough terrain, striking a tree and sustaining substantial damage to the aircraft.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper PA-24-250 experienced a sudden engine power loss during a Part 91 flight from Charlevoix to Toledo, Michigan. The aircraft crashed and burned near Richmond Field Airport after the pilot attempted a forced landing, with post-accident examination revealing seized accessory case shafts consistent with fire damage.
summary: The pilot of a Piper PA-24-250 experienced a sudden engine power loss during a Part 91 flight from Charlevoix to Toledo, Michigan. The aircraft crashed and burned near Richmond Field Airport after the pilot attempted a forced landing, with post-accident examination revealing seized accessory case shafts consistent with fire damage.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate fuel planning which resulted in a total loss of power due to fuel exhaustion. Contributing to the accident was the landing zone being unlit.
summary: The helicopter pilot experienced fuel exhaustion and total power loss while enroute to an unlit landing zone, causing an autorotation that resulted in a collision with a power pole. The pilot attributed the accident to inadequate fuel monitoring and the lack of lighting at the intended landing site.

synopsis: An encounter with convective turbulence during descent that resulted in a serious injury to a flight attendant.
summary: World Atlantic Airlines flight 261 encountered severe turbulence at 12,000 ft during descent into Miami, injuring a flight attendant who was attempting to fasten her seat belt. The crew landed safely, but the attendant suffered a concussion and rib contusion, prompting the airline to issue a safety bulletin on turbulence procedures.

synopsis: A Cessna 172H pilot experienced partial engine power loss at 300 feet AGL during initial climb, forcing a landing where the right wing struck a light pole. The pilot attributed the power loss to a spider nest found in the left fuel vent after the accident.
summary: A Cessna 172H pilot experienced partial engine power loss at 300 feet AGL during initial climb, forcing a landing where the right wing struck a light pole. The pilot attributed the power loss to a spider nest found in the left fuel vent after the accident.

synopsis: During ground operations at Portland International Airport, a Gulfstream G-V's nose gear retracted after the pilot activated the power transfer unit following a low hydraulic pressure indication. The forward fuselage impacted the ground, causing substantial damage to the pressure bulkhead, though all occupants evacuated safely.
summary: During ground operations at Portland International Airport, a Gulfstream G-V's nose gear retracted after the pilot activated the power transfer unit following a low hydraulic pressure indication. The forward fuselage impacted the ground, causing substantial damage to the pressure bulkhead, though all occupants evacuated safely.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to remove the tow bar before flight.
summary: The pilot diverted after a landing gear circuit breaker tripped, but the aircraft veered right and struck a ditch during landing due to a forgotten tow bar. This caused substantial empennage damage, though the pilot reported no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: A in-flight collision with a bird during the descent for landing.
summary: The pilot reported a bird strike with a black vulture while descending four miles from the destination airport. The aircraft landed safely, but substantial damage was found on the right wing.

synopsis: The Cessna 150 pilot's decision to taxi in front of an oncoming Cessna 172, which resulted in a ground collision. Contributing to the accident was the Cessna 150 pilot's momentary distraction, which delayed his recognition of the impending collision. The Cessna 150 pilot's decision to taxi in front of an oncoming Cessna 172, which resulted in a ground collision. Contributing to the accident was the Cessna 150 pilot's momentary distraction, which delayed his recognition of the impending collision.
summary: A Cessna 150 pilot and a Cessna 172 student pilot with an instructor collided while taxiing in a non-movement area. The Cessna 150 pulled into the path of the Cessna 172 after the pilot glanced at instruments, causing the Cessna 150 propeller to strike the Cessna 172 right wing spar.

synopsis: The pilot of a Beech K35 sustained fatal injuries when the aircraft crashed near Cambridge, Minnesota, while approaching a non-towered airport. The fuel selector was found in the auxiliary position, which is prohibited for landing, and the engine fuel system contained no fuel at impact.
summary: The pilot of a Beech K35 sustained fatal injuries when the aircraft crashed near Cambridge, Minnesota, while approaching a non-towered airport. The fuel selector was found in the auxiliary position, which is prohibited for landing, and the engine fuel system contained no fuel at impact.

synopsis: A Gulfstream G150 pilot and copilot substantially damaged the aircraft during a wet runway 34 landing at Chicago Executive Airport. The accident occurred because the crew failed to deploy air brakes, landed long with excessive speed, and exceeded the available runway distance.
summary: A Gulfstream G150 pilot and copilot substantially damaged the aircraft during a wet runway 34 landing at Chicago Executive Airport. The accident occurred because the crew failed to deploy air brakes, landed long with excessive speed, and exceeded the available runway distance.

synopsis: A private pilot was fatally injured when his Czech Sport Aircraft Sportcruiser crashed near Fryeburg, Maine, during a personal repositioning flight. The aircraft entered an uncontrolled descent and spin after a loud noise, with the ballistic parachute partially deploying before impact.
summary: A private pilot was fatally injured when his Czech Sport Aircraft Sportcruiser crashed near Fryeburg, Maine, during a personal repositioning flight. The aircraft entered an uncontrolled descent and spin after a loud noise, with the ballistic parachute partially deploying before impact.

synopsis: A flight instructor and student pilot were fatally injured when their Beech P35 crashed near Englewood, Colorado, during a Part 91 instructional flight. The aircraft descended with the engine silent, banked left then right, and impacted an industrial driveway after the engine stopped completely.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot were fatally injured when their Beech P35 crashed near Englewood, Colorado, during a Part 91 instructional flight. The aircraft descended with the engine silent, banked left then right, and impacted an industrial driveway after the engine stopped completely.

synopsis: During a checkride in a Piper PA-44, a private pilot and DPE attempted a go-around after an unstable approach, but the right engine failed to produce power because it had not been fully restarted following a simulated shutdown. The aircraft descended and impacted a field, sustaining substantial damage while both occupants received minor injuries.
summary: During a checkride in a Piper PA-44, a private pilot and DPE attempted a go-around after an unstable approach, but the right engine failed to produce power because it had not been fully restarted following a simulated shutdown. The aircraft descended and impacted a field, sustaining substantial damage while both occupants received minor injuries.

synopsis: A Robinson R66 helicopter carrying a pilot and passenger crashed near Lakeville, Minnesota, during a personal flight en route to New Richmond. Witnesses reported the aircraft turned sharply right and pitched nose-low before impacting the ground, resulting in a post-impact fire that destroyed the helicopter and fatally injured both occupants.
summary: A Robinson R66 helicopter carrying a pilot and passenger crashed near Lakeville, Minnesota, during a personal flight en route to New Richmond. Witnesses reported the aircraft turned sharply right and pitched nose-low before impacting the ground, resulting in a post-impact fire that destroyed the helicopter and fatally injured both occupants.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare and subsequent improper recovery from a bounced landing, which resulted in substantial damage to the engine mounts.
summary: A private pilot reported that a high-speed final approach with 10-degree flaps caused the airplane to bounce and porpoise on touchdown, collapsing the nose gear and damaging engine mounts. The pilot stated no pre-accident mechanical malfunctions occurred.

synopsis: The pilot of a Beech 35-C33 reported moderate vibration, a bang, and reduced RPM shortly after takeoff, leading to a forced landing in a grass clearing. The aircraft was destroyed by a post-impact fire, while the pilot and two passengers sustained minor injuries.
summary: The pilot of a Beech 35-C33 reported moderate vibration, a bang, and reduced RPM shortly after takeoff, leading to a forced landing in a grass clearing. The aircraft was destroyed by a post-impact fire, while the pilot and two passengers sustained minor injuries.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control while landing.
summary: The pilot experienced a nose gear collapse and substantial damage during the second landing after the airplane ballooned due to a wind gust. The pilot attributed the accident to being late in initiating a go-around and noted that increased approach airspeed might have prevented the incident.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper PA-23-160 sustained serious injuries when the aircraft impacted terrain shortly after takeoff from runway 10. The pilot reported a left yaw and decreasing engine noise, assumed the left engine failed, and drifted left while attempting to maintain control below 50 feet.
summary: The pilot of a Piper PA-23-160 sustained serious injuries when the aircraft impacted terrain shortly after takeoff from runway 10. The pilot reported a left yaw and decreasing engine noise, assumed the left engine failed, and drifted left while attempting to maintain control below 50 feet.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from a moving vehicle during an evasive maneuver from a perceived conflict with another airplane. Contributing to the accident was the pilot of the other airplane's non-standard phraseology and inaccurate position report.
summary: A pilot in the traffic pattern for a grass landing heard another aircraft report "short final" but could not see it. The pilot executed a forward slip, struck a vehicle on an adjacent roadway, and landed hard inverted, causing substantial damage to the airframe.

synopsis: The pilot's exceedance of the helicopter's available power while landing in a remote confined area, which resulted in rotor droop and a hard landing.
summary: A helicopter pilot transporting three passengers to a mountainous landing zone initiated a steep approach without a planned flyover after becoming distracted by a guide. The aircraft descended despite full collective input, impacted the ground, and rolled over, sustaining substantial damage with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The airplane's encounter with a downdraft while maneuvering at low altitude, which resulted in a forced landing and collision with terrain.
summary: The pilot reported that a strong downdraft during approach to a remote mountain airstrip forced the airplane into rough terrain, causing substantial damage to the wings and lift struts. No preimpact mechanical failures were reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to extend the landing gear before landing.
summary: The pilot landed with the landing gear retracted during an instrument approach after forgetting to extend it. The aircraft slid on the runway and sustained substantial damage to the lower fuselage.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to takeoff from an unsuitable runway due to large puddles of water, which resulted in a nose over.
summary: The pilot reported that during the takeoff roll, the aircraft contacted a puddle of standing water, causing resistance that forced the nose down and resulted in a nose-over. This incident caused substantial damage to the right wing lift strut, vertical stabilizer, and rudder, with no pre-impact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The flight instructor's improper landing flare which resulted in a bounced landing and loss of control.
summary: During a student pilot training flight, the aircraft bounced and turned sharply left upon touchdown while the flight instructor controlled the airplane on final approach. The instructor attempted a go-around but could not regain airspeed or directional control, reporting no mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilots encounter with an obstructed dip in the landing surface during the landing roll out on a remote airstrip, which resulted in a noseover.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane nosed over and inverted while landing on a remote airstrip after encountering an obstructed dip. The pilot could not arrest the nose-down pitch during rollout, causing substantial damage to the rudder and left wing with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to raise the landing gear before landing on the water.
summary: The pilot of an amphibious airplane forgot to raise the landing gear before a planned water landing at a nearby river. The extended gear contacted the water, causing the aircraft to nose over and sustain substantial damage to the forward fuselage.

synopsis: The pilot's exceedance of the glider's critical angle of attack which resulted in a loss of control while maneuvering to return for landing after a runway overshoot.
summary: A student pilot conducting a solo glider flight in the traffic pattern entered a slip to lose altitude but floated past the runway threshold. The glider stalled during a subsequent turn, contacting the ground with substantial damage to the fuselage and left wing, with no mechanical failures reported.

aircraft: Larocca Roch B ERACER MK II
synopsis: The failure of the nose gear actuator bolt during the landing roll, which resulted in the collapse of the nose landing gear and subsequent runway excursion.
summary: The pilot of an experimental amateur-built airplane reported a nose gear collapse during the landing roll caused by a failed actuator bolt. The aircraft veered off the runway, impacted uneven terrain, and sustained substantial right wing damage.

synopsis: A flight instructor and student pilot were seriously injured when their Bell 206, N992MR, was destroyed during a Part 91 hover training exercise near Monroe, Georgia. The helicopter violently turned right at 10-15 feet AGL, crashed, and caught fire, with the instructor reporting no prior erratic maneuvers before the incident.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot were seriously injured when their Bell 206, N992MR, was destroyed during a Part 91 hover training exercise near Monroe, Georgia. The helicopter violently turned right at 10-15 feet AGL, crashed, and caught fire, with the instructor reporting no prior erratic maneuvers before the incident.

synopsis: A flat left main landing gear tire, which resulted in a loss of directional control and runway excursion during landing.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot experienced a runway excursion during landing when the aircraft veered left due to a flat left main tire. The left wing struck a sign causing substantial damage before the airplane stopped upright in the grass.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control of the airplane during a touch-and-go landing.
summary: A pilot and flight instructor in a tailwheel airplane ground looped left during the fourth touch-and-go landing, departing the runway into a ditch. The fuselage and left wing were substantially damaged, with the pilot reporting no preimpact mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: The pilot's distraction and failure to monitor the airplane's flight path, which resulted in controlled flight into a lake.
summary: The pilot of a vintage amphibious airplane impacted a lake while maneuvering after using a mobile phone to obtain a radio frequency. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the fuselage, hull, wing, and sponsons, with the pilot reporting no preaccident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's exceedance of the critical angle of attack which resulted in an aerodynamic stall at an altitude too low to recover.
summary: The pilot reported the airplane became airborne before reaching intended airspeed. Increasing pitch to clear power lines caused an aerodynamic stall, resulting in a crash into trees and substantial damage to the wings and fuselage with no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's delayed go-around from an unstabilized approach that resulted in an impact with terrain.
summary: The pilot, flying with 40° flaps on final approach to Runway 05, executed a go-around after floating, but aborted it due to low airspeed and stall warnings. The aircraft subsequently bounced, impacted a dirt mound, and nosed over, sustaining substantial damage to the wings and vertical stabilizer.

synopsis: The pilot's encounter with gusting crosswind conditions during takeoff, which resulted in a loss of control and subsequent impact with terrain.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane encountered a strong crosswind shortly after takeoff from a remote airstrip, causing the aircraft to veer right. Attempting to correct the attitude resulted in a stall with insufficient altitude for recovery, leading to a ground impact and substantial damage to the fuselage and wings.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to extend the landing gear prior to landing. Contributing to the accident was a malfunction of the landing gear's electrical retraction/extension system, which tripped the circuit breaker.
summary: The pilot of a multi-engine airplane returned to the departure airport after alternator failure caused electrical issues and a tripped landing gear circuit breaker. The nose gear failed to extend, causing the gear to collapse on touchdown and resulting in substantial fuselage damage.

synopsis: A commercial pilot and line technician were fatally injured when their Hughes 369D helicopter was destroyed during a Part 133 external load flight near a transmission tower in Jim Thorpe, Pennsylvania. The aircraft impacted the tower while the technician was positioned on a skid plate to mark a fiber optic wire, resulting in severe structural separation.
summary: A commercial pilot and line technician were fatally injured when their Hughes 369D helicopter was destroyed during a Part 133 external load flight near a transmission tower in Jim Thorpe, Pennsylvania. The aircraft impacted the tower while the technician was positioned on a skid plate to mark a fiber optic wire, resulting in severe structural separation.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental Zenith CH801 reported engine power decay from 4,500 to 3,700 rpm shortly after takeoff from Jackpot Airport, Nevada, forcing a landing in a field. The left main gear collapsed during the landing roll, causing substantial damage to the left wing, though no occupants were injured.
summary: The pilot of an experimental Zenith CH801 reported engine power decay from 4,500 to 3,700 rpm shortly after takeoff from Jackpot Airport, Nevada, forcing a landing in a field. The left main gear collapsed during the landing roll, causing substantial damage to the left wing, though no occupants were injured.

aircraft: Lawson Thomas O LANCAIR SUPER ES
synopsis: The pilot of an experimental Lancair Super ES, N905ET, was fatally injured when the aircraft impacted mountainous terrain near Mount Hamilton, California, during a personal flight. Witnesses reported the airplane descending to 300 feet and banking right before striking a tree and the hillside at full engine power.
summary: The pilot of an experimental Lancair Super ES, N905ET, was fatally injured when the aircraft impacted mountainous terrain near Mount Hamilton, California, during a personal flight. Witnesses reported the airplane descending to 300 feet and banking right before striking a tree and the hillside at full engine power.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the takeoff roll.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane departing a remote strip encountered a strong left crosswind during takeoff, causing the aircraft to veer right and depart the runway. The plane impacted a river rut, collapsing the left main gear and damaging the left wing, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: A commercial pilot flying a Maule M5-235C under Part 91 sustained serious injuries when the aircraft impacted the ground near Point McKenzie, Alaska. The accident occurred on the base leg at 300-400 feet AGL when the plane rolled left immediately after the pilot added the second notch of flaps at 65 knots.
summary: A commercial pilot flying a Maule M5-235C under Part 91 sustained serious injuries when the aircraft impacted the ground near Point McKenzie, Alaska. The accident occurred on the base leg at 300-400 feet AGL when the plane rolled left immediately after the pilot added the second notch of flaps at 65 knots.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control of the airplane during a gusty crosswind landing.
summary: The pilot of an experimental amateur-built airplane departed the left runway edge during the landing flare due to a right wind gust. The aircraft descended an embankment and nosed over, sustaining substantial damage to the rudder and right-wing lift strut.

synopsis: The flight instructor's failure to maintain directional control during landing in the tailwheel equipped airplane.
summary: A flight instructor flying a tailwheel aircraft as sole manipulator lost directional control during the landing roll, causing the airplane to veer left, exit the runway, and strike the ground with the right wing. The incident resulted in substantial damage to the right wing and elevator, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate fuel planning and failure to monitor the fuel consumption which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion.
summary: The pilot of a multi-engine airplane misjudged fuel quantity before a night flight, believing 53 gallons were available when only 36 were usable. This miscalculation caused total engine power loss on final approach, resulting in a forced landing into a perimeter fence and substantial right wing damage.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power for reasons that could not be determined.
summary: During a training flight over Lake Michigan, a Cirrus aircraft suffered an engine oil pressure drop leading to total power loss.
