The crew elected to perform the required maneuver themselves after failing to coordinate with an experienced test pilot, despite the Pilot's Operating Manual warning of potential unacceptable stall characteristics.
summary: The captain and co-pilot of a Raytheon Hawker 800XP were killed when the aircraft stalled and impacted terrain during a post-maintenance stall test flight. The crew elected to perform the required maneuver themselves after failing to coordinate with an experienced test pilot, despite the Pilot's Operating Manual warning of potential unacceptable stall characteristics.

synopsis: A pilot operating a Beech V35 on a Part 91 personal flight was fatally injured when the aircraft impacted mountainous terrain near Austin, Nevada. The accident occurred while the airplane was flying at approximately 11,100 feet MSL, resulting in substantial damage to the aircraft.
summary: A pilot operating a Beech V35 on a Part 91 personal flight was fatally injured when the aircraft impacted mountainous terrain near Austin, Nevada. The accident occurred while the airplane was flying at approximately 11,100 feet MSL, resulting in substantial damage to the aircraft.

synopsis: The pilot of a Kitfox II, N8610X, was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed into an embankment southeast of runway 35 at Avery County Airport during a Part 91 personal flight. Witnesses observed the airplane executing a takeoff roll parallel to runway 17 before impacting terrain in a nose-low attitude, with the engine showing no pre-impact anomalies.
summary: The pilot of a Kitfox II, N8610X, was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed into an embankment southeast of runway 35 at Avery County Airport during a Part 91 personal flight. Witnesses observed the airplane executing a takeoff roll parallel to runway 17 before impacting terrain in a nose-low attitude, with the engine showing no pre-impact anomalies.

synopsis: A flight instructor and student pilot were fatally injured when their JMB VL-3LSA-912, N594TT, entered a nose-low spin and impacted the ground during a go-around at Erie Municipal Airport. The accident occurred after the aircraft failed to touch down on its fifth approach, and the airframe parachute did not deploy because its safety pin remained installed.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot were fatally injured when their JMB VL-3LSA-912, N594TT, entered a nose-low spin and impacted the ground during a go-around at Erie Municipal Airport. The accident occurred after the aircraft failed to touch down on its fifth approach, and the airframe parachute did not deploy because its safety pin remained installed.

synopsis: A Piper PA-23-250 pilot and two passengers were fatally injured when the aircraft crashed in mountainous terrain near Condon, Montana, during a Part 91 flight. The pilot declared an emergency due to icing and a left engine issue, subsequently losing radar contact before the aircraft was located at 5,286 ft msl.
summary: A Piper PA-23-250 pilot and two passengers were fatally injured when the aircraft crashed in mountainous terrain near Condon, Montana, during a Part 91 flight. The pilot declared an emergency due to icing and a left engine issue, subsequently losing radar contact before the aircraft was located at 5,286 ft msl.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain a proper glidepath during landing which resulted in a landing short of the runway.
summary: The pilot reported that during the landing phase after an agricultural spray operation, the airplane descended too low and impacted a soybean crop off the runway end. The pilot attributed the accident to pilot error, which caused landing gear collapse and substantial fuselage damage.

synopsis: The pilot of an amateur-built RV-8, N3545W, was seriously injured when the aircraft impacted terrain near McKinney, Texas, during a Part 91 personal flight. Witnesses reported the pilot experienced an engine issue while attempting to land, though the specific circumstances remain unknown.
summary: The pilot of an amateur-built RV-8, N3545W, was seriously injured when the aircraft impacted terrain near McKinney, Texas, during a Part 91 personal flight. Witnesses reported the pilot experienced an engine issue while attempting to land, though the specific circumstances remain unknown.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to ensure that the landing gear was properly extended before landing. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's unfamiliarity with the landing gear warning horn and failure to verify the gear was extended with the cockpit position indicators.
summary: The pilot landed an aircraft on its belly during the downwind leg after failing to verify gear extension despite a warning horn. A tripped circuit breaker caused partial gear extension, resulting in substantial fuselage damage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from a power line during a descent for landing.
summary: The balloon pilot reported that during approach, the balloon descended faster than anticipated and collided with powerlines, damaging an aluminum frame tube. The pilot stated there were no pre-accident mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: The pilot of a Flight Design CTSW, N531CT, experienced total engine power loss during cruise due to suspected fuel starvation despite preflight checks. The pilot declared a mayday and performed an off-airport landing in desert scrub, resulting in a nose-over that substantially damaged the aircraft while the pilot sustained minor injuries.
summary: The pilot of a Flight Design CTSW, N531CT, experienced total engine power loss during cruise due to suspected fuel starvation despite preflight checks. The pilot declared a mayday and performed an off-airport landing in desert scrub, resulting in a nose-over that substantially damaged the aircraft while the pilot sustained minor injuries.

aircraft: Hawker Aircraft Ltd HAWKER HUNTER MK.58
synopsis: A complete loss of engine power for reasons that could not be determined.
summary: A pilot conducting military adversary training at flight level 220 experienced a complete engine power loss after reducing power to conserve fuel. Unable to restart the engine or safely land due to low altitude and overcast conditions, the pilot ejected over the Pacific Ocean, and the aircraft was not recovered.

synopsis: The pilot receiving instruction's failure to maintain directional control during landing and the flight instructor's delayed remedial action, which resulted in a runway excursion.
summary: A flight instructor and student in a tailwheel airplane experienced a bounce on landing, leading to a failed go-around and a second touchdown off the runway centerline. The instructor took control but the aircraft ground looped, causing substantial right wing damage, with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's improper runway alignment and failure to maintain clearance from powerlines. Contributing to the accident was sun glare, which obscured the pilot's view of the runway.
summary: During a cross-country approach, the pilot misidentified an irrigation canal as a runway due to sun glare and struck high-tension transmission lines while attempting to fly under them. This impact separated the rudder and vertical stabilizer, causing substantial damage, though the pilot successfully diverted and landed the aircraft.

synopsis: During a Part 91 instructional takeoff of an EXTRA 300L, the canopy separated seconds after roll initiation, damaging the rudder and stabilizers. The instructor rejected the takeoff, attributing the event to a likely mechanical malfunction where the left-side locking mechanism failed to engage.
summary: During a Part 91 instructional takeoff of an EXTRA 300L, the canopy separated seconds after roll initiation, damaging the rudder and stabilizers. The instructor rejected the takeoff, attributing the event to a likely mechanical malfunction where the left-side locking mechanism failed to engage.

synopsis: A worn tailwheel steering mechanism, which resulted in a locked tailwheel and a ground loop during a landing roll.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane experienced a stuck right rudder pedal and steering arm during takeoff, causing a ground loop and substantial damage upon landing. The NTSB attributed the accident to a worn tailwheel locking/steering mechanism with no recorded maintenance history.

synopsis: A commercial pilot flying a Raytheon G58 reported an unspecified engine issue while en route to Lafayette, Louisiana, before entering a right spin and impacting terrain. Post-accident examination found no mechanical anomalies, though the right engine propeller was unfeathered and the aircraft was destroyed with three fatalities.
summary: A commercial pilot flying a Raytheon G58 reported an unspecified engine issue while en route to Lafayette, Louisiana, before entering a right spin and impacting terrain. Post-accident examination found no mechanical anomalies, though the right engine propeller was unfeathered and the aircraft was destroyed with three fatalities.

aircraft: Roderick James Willmore KITFOX S7 SUPERSPORT
synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the takeoff. Contributing to the accident was the separation of the control stick grip.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane lost control during takeoff on a dirt road after forgetting to reset pitch trim and having the control stick grip slip. The aircraft veered right, exited the runway, and sustained substantial left wing damage upon ground impact.

synopsis: A private pilot flying a Cirrus SR22 was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed into trees near Ruston, Louisiana, while hand-flying after requesting a go-around due to autopilot programming difficulties. The pilot lost control in a left bank and nose-low attitude, and the airframe parachute system failed to deploy fully before impact.
summary: A private pilot flying a Cirrus SR22 was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed into trees near Ruston, Louisiana, while hand-flying after requesting a go-around due to autopilot programming difficulties. The pilot lost control in a left bank and nose-low attitude, and the airframe parachute system failed to deploy fully before impact.

synopsis: The pilot's inadvertent application of brakes during the landing roll, which resulted in a noseover.
summary: A private pilot receiving tailwheel instruction nosed over and inverted the aircraft shortly after touchdown during a touch-and-go landing. The accident occurred when the pilot inadvertently applied brakes instead of rudder to correct a drift, causing substantial damage with no preimpact mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control and the flight instructor's lack of proper remedial action during the practice autorotation that resulted in the helicopter impacting terrain. Contributing to the accident was the presence of the gusting wind condition and the presence of speed shear.
summary: A flight instructor and student practicing autorotations in a helicopter drifted off airport property due to uncorrected wind gusts and shear. The instructor failed to initiate a timely power recovery, resulting in a terrain impact that caused substantial damage to the aircraft.

synopsis: The plot's failure to account sufficiently for the decrease in the airplane's takeoff performance due to the wet turf runway, which resulted in a collision with a log barrier and subsequent nose over after aborting the takeoff.
summary: The pilot attempted a short field takeoff on a wet 2,005-ft turf runway in a tailwheel airplane but aborted when the aircraft failed to climb into ground effect. The airplane slid on the wet grass, impacted a log barrier, and nosed over inverted, sustaining substantial damage due to reduced acceleration from the wet runway.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental Rutan Long-EZ experienced total engine power loss due to decreasing fuel flow while en route to Compton/Woodley Airport. He attempted a forced landing in a park near Long Beach, striking a pedestrian and sustaining substantial damage to the aircraft.
summary: The pilot of an experimental Rutan Long-EZ experienced total engine power loss due to decreasing fuel flow while en route to Compton/Woodley Airport. He attempted a forced landing in a park near Long Beach, striking a pedestrian and sustaining substantial damage to the aircraft.

synopsis: A Robinson R66 helicopter, N67GA, carrying a pilot and three passengers, crashed near Ekalaka, Montana, while flying low over the Chalk Buttes during a Part 91 personal flight. The aircraft was substantially damaged and all occupants were fatally injured after the pilot lost visual contact with a trailing Cessna 182 and the helicopter descended out of sight.
summary: A Robinson R66 helicopter, N67GA, carrying a pilot and three passengers, crashed near Ekalaka, Montana, while flying low over the Chalk Buttes during a Part 91 personal flight. The aircraft was substantially damaged and all occupants were fatally injured after the pilot lost visual contact with a trailing Cessna 182 and the helicopter descended out of sight.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to extend the landing gear before landing due to distraction and his failure to conduct the Before Landing checklist.
summary: The pilot landed an aircraft with the gear retracted after confusing the flap lever for the gear lever and misidentifying the landing gear warning horn as a stall warning. This distraction and checklist omission caused substantial lower fuselage damage during the wheels-up landing.

synopsis: A collision with terrain during takeoff.
summary: A non-certificated pilot crashed a tailwheel-equipped airplane on takeoff from a remote gravel bar. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to both wing lift struts, but the pilot did not report the accident or provide a statement.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of helicopter control during landing approach in strong wind conditions, which resulted in tail rotor contact with the ground during landing.
summary: Two pilots repositioning a vintage experimental helicopter in 30-knot winds experienced a severe shake during a low-altitude approach to a movable skid. The pilot executed an immediate grass landing, resulting in substantial damage to the tail rotor and drive system due to ground contact.

synopsis: A cascading shutoff of multiple aft motors due to a sudden increase in motor loads during maneuvering, resulting in a loss of control.
summary: A remote pilot operating an Air VEV Zero 2 eVTOL lost control during landing at Indiantown Airport when an aft motor shutdown, triggered by a current spike from maneuvering loads, caused a cascade failure. The resulting thrust imbalance pitched the aircraft up and sideways, leading to a crash and fire with no injuries.

synopsis: A pilot flying a Cirrus SR22T at night to an unfamiliar airport in Lincoln, Montana, was killed when the aircraft stalled and crashed into trees. The accident occurred after the pilot descended below minimum safe altitudes, triggering TAWS alerts, followed by a steep left bank and loss of airspeed.
summary: A pilot flying a Cirrus SR22T at night to an unfamiliar airport in Lincoln, Montana, was killed when the aircraft stalled and crashed into trees. The accident occurred after the pilot descended below minimum safe altitudes, triggering TAWS alerts, followed by a steep left bank and loss of airspeed.

synopsis: The pilot of a Beech 35-33 suffered serious injuries when the aircraft crashed shortly after takeoff due to total engine power loss caused by the fuel selector valve being in the off position. Post-accident examination confirmed the valve was off, likely preventing fuel flow, while the pilot's leg position obstructed access to the control.
summary: The pilot of a Beech 35-33 suffered serious injuries when the aircraft crashed shortly after takeoff due to total engine power loss caused by the fuel selector valve being in the off position. Post-accident examination confirmed the valve was off, likely preventing fuel flow, while the pilot's leg position obstructed access to the control.

aircraft: Rans Employee Flying Club RANS S-6ES COYOTE II
synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control of the airplane during the initial climb in gusting crosswind conditions.
summary: The pilot departed a 2,395-ft turf runway when a wind gust lifted the right wing, causing the airplane to turn left and impact trees. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the right wing and empennage, with the pilot reporting no preaccident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper PA46-310P reported an engine failure during climb near El Paso, Texas, caused by a crankcase hole and dislodged magneto. The pilot executed an emergency landing on a dirt road where landing gear separated after passing a hole, resulting in substantial damage to the wings and fuselage with no injuries.
summary: The pilot of a Piper PA46-310P reported an engine failure during climb near El Paso, Texas, caused by a crankcase hole and dislodged magneto. The pilot executed an emergency landing on a dirt road where landing gear separated after passing a hole, resulting in substantial damage to the wings and fuselage with no injuries.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to properly set the elevator trim prior to takeoff, which resulted in her inability to effectively control the airplane's pitch and a collision with trees at the end of the runway during initial climb.
summary: A student pilot on her second solo flight struck trees at the end of an 8,001-foot runway during initial climb. The accident likely resulted from the elevator trim being set near full nose-down, causing difficulty controlling pitch despite normal instrumentation.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper PA-28-140 experienced a partial loss of engine power at 600 feet during the fourth takeoff at Fayette County Airport. Unable to restore power, the pilot executed a 180° turn and landed in a grassy area, where the aircraft struck a perimeter fence and sustained substantial damage.
summary: The pilot of a Piper PA-28-140 experienced a partial loss of engine power at 600 feet during the fourth takeoff at Fayette County Airport. Unable to restore power, the pilot executed a 180° turn and landed in a grassy area, where the aircraft struck a perimeter fence and sustained substantial damage.

synopsis: The pilot and passenger of a Denney Kitfox III, N5241N, suffered no injuries during a Part 91 flight near Chilton, Texas, when the engine lost power due to violent shuddering. The pilot executed a forced landing in a field, but the aircraft nosed over and sustained substantial damage while avoiding an unseen fence line.
summary: The pilot and passenger of a Denney Kitfox III, N5241N, suffered no injuries during a Part 91 flight near Chilton, Texas, when the engine lost power due to violent shuddering. The pilot executed a forced landing in a field, but the aircraft nosed over and sustained substantial damage while avoiding an unseen fence line.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control in gusting wind conditions during the takeoff roll.
summary: The pilot reported that during takeoff in gusting crosswinds, the airplane veered off the left runway side, struck a berm, and nosed over. The aircraft sustained substantial fuselage damage, with the pilot stating no mechanical malfunctions precluded normal operation.

synopsis: The low-wing pilot's inadequate visual lookout, which resulted in a collision with another airplane while taxiing. The low-wing pilot's inadequate visual lookout, which resulted in a collision with another airplane while taxiing.
summary: A pilot of a tailwheel low-wing airplane taxiing for departure collided with a stationary high-wing airplane holding a takeoff clearance at the runup area. The low-wing pilot failed to see the high-wing aircraft until underneath its wing, causing substantial damage to both propellers and wings with no mechanical failures involved.

synopsis: The pilot's improper recovery from a practice autorotation, which resulted in a hard landing. Contributing to the accident was the flight instructor's inadequate supervision of the pilot receiving instruction.
summary: During night helicopter training, the pilot prematurely increased collective power during an autorotation, causing a hard landing that damaged the tail boom. The crew completed the flight unaware of the damage, which was discovered the next day, with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper Arrow PA-28R-200 experienced total oil pressure loss and an engine explosion during descent from 5,000 feet. After declaring an emergency and attempting a power-off landing at Brackett Field, the aircraft stalled 15–20 feet above the runway, resulting in a hard landing and substantial damage.
summary: The pilot of a Piper Arrow PA-28R-200 experienced total oil pressure loss and an engine explosion during descent from 5,000 feet. After declaring an emergency and attempting a power-off landing at Brackett Field, the aircraft stalled 15–20 feet above the runway, resulting in a hard landing and substantial damage.

synopsis: A pilot and flight instructor were fatally and seriously injured, respectively, when a Mooney M20E lost engine power during initial climb due to a failed engine-driven fuel pump. The aircraft impacted a tree and burned after the instructor attempted a turn back to the airport.
summary: A pilot and flight instructor were fatally and seriously injured, respectively, when a Mooney M20E lost engine power during initial climb due to a failed engine-driven fuel pump. The aircraft impacted a tree and burned after the instructor attempted a turn back to the airport.

synopsis: JetBlue Flight 1230 experienced a pitch excursion at 35,000 feet, causing a 100-foot altitude loss and minor injuries to 22 people. Airbus identified a possible ELAC software design issue, prompting mandatory airworthiness directives while the NTSB investigation continues.
summary: JetBlue Flight 1230 experienced a pitch excursion at 35,000 feet, causing a 100-foot altitude loss and minor injuries to 22 people. Airbus identified a possible ELAC software design issue, prompting mandatory airworthiness directives while the NTSB investigation continues.

synopsis: The collapse of the left main landing gear due to the fatigue fracture of the lower landing gear actuator bolt.
summary: Following a maintenance test flight, a flight crew experienced a left main landing gear collapse upon touchdown due to a sheared actuator attachment bolt. The failure, caused by reverse bending fatigue, resulted in the aircraft veering off the runway and sustaining substantial damage to the left wing and hull.

synopsis: During a Part 91 instructional flight in an experimental Just Highlander, the flight instructor and student pilot were seriously injured after a forced landing. The accident occurred when the propeller stopped turning despite normal engine indications, causing partial power loss and fluid leakage before the aircraft impacted rough terrain inverted.
summary: During a Part 91 instructional flight in an experimental Just Highlander, the flight instructor and student pilot were seriously injured after a forced landing. The accident occurred when the propeller stopped turning despite normal engine indications, causing partial power loss and fluid leakage before the aircraft impacted rough terrain inverted.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain a proper approach path during landing which resulted in a collision with terrain short of the runway. Contributing to the accident was the improper flap position during landing, and the pilot being fatigued.
summary: The pilot landed an aircraft short of the runway threshold, impacting a berm and causing substantial damage to the left wing and fuselage. The accident resulted from the pilot mistakenly setting improper flaps, which altered the approach path, and was likely exacerbated by fatigue.

aircraft: Hugh Nunnally Farrior COZY MK IV
synopsis: The pilot's failure to extend the nose landing gear, which resulted in a nose gear up landing. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's inappropriate decision to continue to fly with known delamination damage to the propeller.
summary: The pilot of an experimental airplane experienced progressive vibration in cruise at 1,700 feet due to a delaminating composite propeller damaged by engine exhaust heat. He forgot to extend the nose gear during a precautionary landing, causing substantial fuselage damage, despite prior warnings from the manufacturer to stop flying.

synopsis: The pilot of a Maule M-7-235A, N9234N, reported that a right main landing gear weld fracture caused gear failure and a ground loop during a crosswind landing at Friday Harbor Airport. The accident resulted in substantial damage to the wings and fuselage, though the pilot was not injured.
summary: The pilot of a Maule M-7-235A, N9234N, reported that a right main landing gear weld fracture caused gear failure and a ground loop during a crosswind landing at Friday Harbor Airport. The accident resulted in substantial damage to the wings and fuselage, though the pilot was not injured.

synopsis: The pilot of a Funk B85C was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed into a tree near Anderson, Indiana, during the landing phase of a personal flight. The pilot lost engine power, landed in a field, and impacted a tree, resulting in a post-impact fire, though no pre-crash mechanical anomalies were identified.
summary: The pilot of a Funk B85C was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed into a tree near Anderson, Indiana, during the landing phase of a personal flight. The pilot lost engine power, landed in a field, and impacted a tree, resulting in a post-impact fire, though no pre-crash mechanical anomalies were identified.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cirrus SR-22 reported partial engine power loss shortly after rotation, followed by further power loss and airspeed decrease during climb. Unable to return to the runway, the pilot deployed the CAPS, resulting in substantial damage to the fuselage and empennage upon landing in desert terrain.
summary: The pilot of a Cirrus SR-22 reported partial engine power loss shortly after rotation, followed by further power loss and airspeed decrease during climb. Unable to return to the runway, the pilot deployed the CAPS, resulting in substantial damage to the fuselage and empennage upon landing in desert terrain.

synopsis: A commercial pilot flying a Grumman American AA-5B experienced total engine power loss during initial climb after departing runway 26. The pilot executed an off-airport landing in a vineyard, resulting in substantial damage to the left horizontal stabilizer and ruptured fuel tanks upon impact with grapevines and fence posts.
summary: A commercial pilot flying a Grumman American AA-5B experienced total engine power loss during initial climb after departing runway 26. The pilot executed an off-airport landing in a vineyard, resulting in substantial damage to the left horizontal stabilizer and ruptured fuel tanks upon impact with grapevines and fence posts.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to adjust his seat during the takeoff roll, which resulted in the seat sliding aft and a subsequent loss of directional control.
summary: During takeoff roll, the pilot attempted to adjust his seat forward, but it slid fully aft, preventing him from reaching the pedals to maintain directional control. The airplane subsequently departed the runway and nosed over, causing serious injury to the pilot and substantial damage to the fuselage, wings, and empennage.

synopsis: UPS Flight 2976, an MD-11F, crashed shortly after takeoff from Louisville when the left engine and pylon separated from the wing, causing a fire and loss of control. The accident killed all three crewmembers and 11 people on the ground, with wreckage examination revealing fractures in the pylon aft mount lugs and spherical bearing.
summary: UPS Flight 2976, an MD-11F, crashed shortly after takeoff from Louisville when the left engine and pylon separated from the wing, causing a fire and loss of control. The accident killed all three crewmembers and 11 people on the ground, with wreckage examination revealing fractures in the pylon aft mount lugs and spherical bearing.

synopsis: During a local Part 91 flight, a commercial pilot flying an experimental Rotorway 162F helicopter experienced a left turn with no anti-torque pedal response while raising the collective for landing. The helicopter drifted, rolled onto its left side, and was destroyed by a post-impact fire, leaving the pilot with minor injuries.
summary: During a local Part 91 flight, a commercial pilot flying an experimental Rotorway 162F helicopter experienced a left turn with no anti-torque pedal response while raising the collective for landing. The helicopter drifted, rolled onto its left side, and was destroyed by a post-impact fire, leaving the pilot with minor injuries.

synopsis: The collision with a white-tail deer during the landing in dark night visual conditions.
summary: During a night final approach, a pilot executed a go-around after spotting a deer, but the animal struck the right horizontal stabilizer, causing substantial damage and reduced climb performance. The pilot safely diverted to a nearby airport, noting the airport's proximity to a wildlife area and lack of exclusion fencing as contributing factors.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain situational awareness and clearance from terrain while maneuvering to avoid birds.
summary: During an agricultural application flight, a pilot lost situational awareness while turning to avoid birds and inadvertently impacted the terrain. The airplane sustained substantial damage to the right wing and fuselage, with no mechanical malfunctions reported prior to the accident.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to extended to landing gear before landing.
summary: During a local flight practicing an instrument approach, the pilot was distracted by birds and forgot to extend the landing gear, ignoring the warning horn. The aircraft landed gear-up, sustaining substantial fuselage damage, with no mechanical malfunctions reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane during landing, which resulted in a nose over.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane nosed over while practicing touch-and-go landings on a private turf runway, sustaining substantial damage to the vertical stabilizer, rudder, and fuselage. The pilot reported no mechanical failures, and post-accident tests confirmed the parking brake was removed and wheel brakes functioned normally.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to compensate for gusty crosswind conditions, which resulted in a loss of control of the airplane and subsequent collision with terrain.
summary: During a simulated power-off 180-degree turn practice, a crosswind gust caused the left wing to rise, leading to an uncontrollable right turn and ground impact. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the wings and fuselage, though the pilot reported no preimpact mechanical failures.

synopsis: The change in wind direction during landing, which resulted in a tailwind condition and runway overrun.
summary: A private pilot landing a small aircraft on runway 19 at a remote mountain grass strip encountered a wind shift to a tailwind after touchdown. This caused excessive ground speed, preventing a stop before the runway end, resulting in the aircraft striking a tree and sustaining substantial wing damage.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to continue an approach that resulted in a long landing and inability to stop prior to the end of the runway. Contributing to the accident were the light conditions and a road with vehicles on it immediately adjacent to the end of the runway.
summary: During landing, the pilot experienced sun glare and a long float, then turned sharply left to avoid two cars on a road beyond the runway. This maneuver caused the left wheel assembly to separate and the wing to strike the ground, substantially damaging the aircraft.

synopsis: A private pilot was fatally injured when an Extra 330/SC, N330SL, impacted the ground inverted near Keystone Heights, Florida, during an aerobatic practice flight. The accident occurred after the pilot entered an uncontrolled flat inverted spin during a maneuver and lacked sufficient altitude to recover.
summary: A private pilot was fatally injured when an Extra 330/SC, N330SL, impacted the ground inverted near Keystone Heights, Florida, during an aerobatic practice flight. The accident occurred after the pilot entered an uncontrolled flat inverted spin during a maneuver and lacked sufficient altitude to recover.

synopsis: An Air Methods Airbus EC130 T2 air medical crew suffered a fatal accident near Lebanon, Tennessee, when the pilot became unresponsive during a return-to-base flight. The flight paramedic attempted to control the aircraft but the helicopter struck trees and impacted the ground, killing the nurse and seriously injuring the pilot and paramedic.
summary: An Air Methods Airbus EC130 T2 air medical crew suffered a fatal accident near Lebanon, Tennessee, when the pilot became unresponsive during a return-to-base flight. The flight paramedic attempted to control the aircraft but the helicopter struck trees and impacted the ground, killing the nurse and seriously injuring the pilot and paramedic.

aircraft: Czech Sport Aircraft A S SPORTCRUISER
synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from trees and terrain while maneuvering for a precautionary landing, at low altitude and at night.
summary: During a night VFR flight, a pilot encountered elevated engine cylinder head temperatures at 10,000 ft and diverted to an airport. While distracted by the engine issue, he failed to tune the correct frequency to activate runway lights, resulting in a collision with trees and the ground.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during takeoff at night, while distracted by an animal approaching the runway, which resulted in collision with a runway light.
summary: A pilot departing a multi-engine airplane at night was distracted by an animal during the takeoff roll, causing a rudder input error. The aircraft struck a runway edge light, resulting in substantial damage to the left aileron, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: Failure of the nose landing gear link which resulted in a loss of directional.
summary: The pilot aborted takeoff due to extreme vibration caused by a fractured nose landing gear upper retract link assembly. The aircraft veered off the runway, the nose gear collapsed, and propellers contacted the ground, resulting in substantial fuselage damage.

synopsis: An inadvertent hard landing in high wind conditions resulting in serious injury of one of the pilots.
summary: During an instructional balloon flight, a student pilot sustained serious injuries after the balloon bounced upon landing in 14-knot winds and dragged across the ground. The pilot attributed the accident to high wind conditions rather than mechanical failure.

synopsis: A pilot and passenger were fatally injured when their Beech King Air B100 crashed into a pond near Coral Springs, Florida, during the climb phase of a relief supply flight. The aircraft entered a steep nose-down descent while in clouds after takeoff, with no evidence of engine failure or smoke prior to impact.
summary: A pilot and passenger were fatally injured when their Beech King Air B100 crashed into a pond near Coral Springs, Florida, during the climb phase of a relief supply flight. The aircraft entered a steep nose-down descent while in clouds after takeoff, with no evidence of engine failure or smoke prior to impact.

synopsis: An in-flight collision with a bird.
summary: During a training flight at 2,500 ft, a student pilot attempted to avoid a bird by turning left, but the bird struck the right wing, causing substantial damage. The flight instructor then took control and landed the aircraft uneventfully.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental ICP Savannah amphibian reported that the propeller separated from the engine during cruise flight, forcing a landing in a grassy field. The aircraft nosed over and came to rest inverted, sustaining substantial damage to the wings and fuselage, while the pilot and passenger remained uninjured.
summary: The pilot of an experimental ICP Savannah amphibian reported that the propeller separated from the engine during cruise flight, forcing a landing in a grassy field. The aircraft nosed over and came to rest inverted, sustaining substantial damage to the wings and fuselage, while the pilot and passenger remained uninjured.

synopsis: The pilot's improper starting procedure which resulted in the airplane's unexpected movement and subsequent impact with an airport fence.
summary: The pilot hand-propped the engine after a dead battery, then removed the chock while re-entering the aircraft. The throttle lock loosened, causing the unoccupied airplane to accelerate forward and impact an airport fence, resulting in substantial damage to the engine mount.

synopsis: During cruise flight, a Piper PA-28-235 pilot experienced total engine power loss despite applying carburetor heat, forcing a landing on a road. The left wing struck a car, causing substantial aircraft damage and minor injuries to one passenger.
summary: During cruise flight, a Piper PA-28-235 pilot experienced total engine power loss despite applying carburetor heat, forcing a landing on a road. The left wing struck a car, causing substantial aircraft damage and minor injuries to one passenger.

synopsis: A pilot flying a Cessna 172M from Bishop Airport struck terrain in a canyon while climbing toward a mountain range. The accident, which fatally injured two passengers and seriously injured the pilot, resulted from the aircraft impacting a 7,000 ft msl slope after the last ADS-B return at 6,850 ft msl.
summary: A pilot flying a Cessna 172M from Bishop Airport struck terrain in a canyon while climbing toward a mountain range. The accident, which fatally injured two passengers and seriously injured the pilot, resulted from the aircraft impacting a 7,000 ft msl slope after the last ADS-B return at 6,850 ft msl.

synopsis: During a night approach in a Cirrus SR20, the pilot extended flaps to 100% below 100 knots, causing an uncommanded yaw and roll that led to loss of control. The pilot deployed the CAPS parachute after the aircraft entered a steep spiral, resulting in substantial damage and minor injuries to both occupants.
summary: During a night approach in a Cirrus SR20, the pilot extended flaps to 100% below 100 knots, causing an uncommanded yaw and roll that led to loss of control. The pilot deployed the CAPS parachute after the aircraft entered a steep spiral, resulting in substantial damage and minor injuries to both occupants.

synopsis: A Cessna TU206F taxiing across runway 24 at taxiway B collided with a Hawker B300 on landing roll during a simulated single-engine approach at Muscatine Regional Airport. Both pilots reported making radio calls but not hearing the other, resulting in substantial damage to the TU206F empennage and B300 right wing with no injuries.
summary: A Cessna TU206F taxiing across runway 24 at taxiway B collided with a Hawker B300 on landing roll during a simulated single-engine approach at Muscatine Regional Airport. Both pilots reported making radio calls but not hearing the other, resulting in substantial damage to the TU206F empennage and B300 right wing with no injuries.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cirrus SR22 experienced an in-flight engine failure with oil venting and zero RPM, likely caused by crankcase holes and cylinder separation linked to prior oil leaks. He deployed the CAPS parachute, but the aircraft sustained substantial damage after colliding with trees during descent.
summary: The pilot of a Cirrus SR22 experienced an in-flight engine failure with oil venting and zero RPM, likely caused by crankcase holes and cylinder separation linked to prior oil leaks. He deployed the CAPS parachute, but the aircraft sustained substantial damage after colliding with trees during descent.

synopsis: The pilot's improper application of left brake pedal during the landing roll, which resulted in a loss of directional control and a ground loop.
summary: The pilot ground looped the aircraft to the left while decelerating after landing and applying hard left rudder. This caused the right main landing gear to collapse and the right wing to strike the pavement, resulting in substantial damage with no preimpact mechanical failures.

aircraft: Jabiru Usa Sport Aircraft Llc J230-SP
synopsis: A sport pilot and passenger were fatally injured when their Jabiru J230-SP crashed near New Bavaria, Ohio, during a low-altitude maneuver. The aircraft struck the ground with its left wingtip after executing a steep left turn with a near 90° bank angle while flying over a residence.
summary: A sport pilot and passenger were fatally injured when their Jabiru J230-SP crashed near New Bavaria, Ohio, during a low-altitude maneuver. The aircraft struck the ground with its left wingtip after executing a steep left turn with a near 90° bank angle while flying over a residence.

synopsis: A commercial pilot flying a Piper PA-32R-301T experienced engine surging and total power loss during a Part 91 positioning flight. The pilot attempted a forced landing on a pasture but struck a powerline with the left wing, causing substantial damage to the airframe and landing gear.
summary: A commercial pilot flying a Piper PA-32R-301T experienced engine surging and total power loss during a Part 91 positioning flight. The pilot attempted a forced landing on a pasture but struck a powerline with the left wing, causing substantial damage to the airframe and landing gear.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control while landing in a strong quartering headwind, which resulted in a runway excursion and collision with an airport sign.
summary: During landing in a 12-knot right-quartering headwind, a strong gust lifted the right wing, causing the left wingtip to strike the runway. The aircraft veered left and hit an airport sign, damaging the engine mount, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: During a Part 91 instructional flight in a Piper PA 28-181 near Mesa, Arizona, an uncommanded power loss on base leg forced the flight instructor to execute a forced landing on a gravel road. The aircraft struck a cinder block fence during the landing roll, sustaining substantial damage to the fuselage, stabilizer, and wings, though both occupants were uninjured.
summary: During a Part 91 instructional flight in a Piper PA 28-181 near Mesa, Arizona, an uncommanded power loss on base leg forced the flight instructor to execute a forced landing on a gravel road. The aircraft struck a cinder block fence during the landing roll, sustaining substantial damage to the fuselage, stabilizer, and wings, though both occupants were uninjured.

aircraft: Michael W Verzwyvelt SS-7 SUPER SPORT
synopsis: The pilot's operation of the airplane while intoxicated, resulting in its impact with obstacles while on approach.
summary: The pilot of an airplane crashed into a traffic light and roadway 2,500 feet northwest of the airport, sustaining substantial damage and minor injuries to both occupants. Law enforcement reported the pilot showed signs of alcoholic impairment with breath alcohol levels of .21 and .17, while the pilot claimed no mechanical failures occurred.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna 172S reported a nosewheel bounce upon touchdown during a straight-in approach to runway 06. Subsequent inspection revealed a flat nosewheel tire, propeller ground damage, and substantial structural damage to the tunnel and floorboards.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna 172S reported a nosewheel bounce upon touchdown during a straight-in approach to runway 06. Subsequent inspection revealed a flat nosewheel tire, propeller ground damage, and substantial structural damage to the tunnel and floorboards.

synopsis: The failure of the left main landing gear actuator rods, which resulted in a gear up landing.
summary: Pilots conducting an instructional flight diverted after the left main landing gear failed to extend due to open circuit breakers and failed actuator rods. They performed a gear-up landing, which caused substantial fuselage damage and confirmed the left gear door was damaged from runway contact.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of airplane control during a go-around, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's improper recovery from an aerodynamic stall.
summary: During a practice instrument approach, the pilot slowed excessively, initiated a go-around, and entered an aerodynamic stall. The pilot's subsequent control input caused the aircraft to bank left and impact terrain, resulting in substantial damage to the empennage and fuselage with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to extend the landing gear prior to landing.
summary: The pilot performed a short field landing but failed to extend the landing gear before touchdown. The aircraft came to rest upright with the gear retracted, causing substantial damage to the lower fuselage without any preimpact mechanical failures.

synopsis: A private pilot flying a Cessna 172N experienced an engine power loss at 1,500 feet MSL during a practice emergency descent, likely due to fuel starvation after switching tanks. The pilot executed a forced landing to a road, but the aircraft struck a traffic sign and sustained substantial damage.
summary: A private pilot flying a Cessna 172N experienced an engine power loss at 1,500 feet MSL during a practice emergency descent, likely due to fuel starvation after switching tanks. The pilot executed a forced landing to a road, but the aircraft struck a traffic sign and sustained substantial damage.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control when the airplane encountered snow and ice on the runway while landing at night in gusting crosswind conditions.
summary: The pilot reported that during the landing roll at night in gusting crosswinds, the right main gear struck ice and a snow drift, causing the aircraft to veer right and impact a snow berm. This collision collapsed the nose gear and caused substantial damage to the nose and fuselage, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The flight instructor's failure to arrest the airplane's descent rate during a takeoff simulated engine failure which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: During a night instructional flight, a student's slow response to a simulated engine failure caused airspeed decay, leading to a hard landing despite the instructor's recovery attempt. The instructor attributed the accident to inadequate night training on the attitude directional indicator and potential wind disturbances from nearby terrain.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the initial climb, which resulted in abnormal contact with the water and a subsequent collision with vegetation.
summary: The pilot of an amphibious airplane lost control during an eastbound departure over ocean waters due to a strong southeast gust. The aircraft entered a steep left bank, striking the water and shoreline vegetation, which caused substantial right wing damage with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The airplane's encounter with downdrafts in mountainous terrain, which resulted in a collision with terrain. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's decision to continue the flight through mountainous terrain in marginal weather conditions.
summary: A pilot flying cross-country diverted due to weather but encountered low ceilings and strong downdrafts over mountainous terrain. Unable to maintain altitude, the aircraft impacted rising terrain, causing substantial damage, which the pilot attributed to not stopping at an earlier airport.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper PA-28R-201 diverted to Pittsfield due to fuel issues and fog but crashed while attempting a visual approach. The accident resulted in substantial damage, a fatality, and serious injuries, caused by the pilot descending below the cleared 2,500 ft minimum altitude in low visibility.
summary: The pilot of a Piper PA-28R-201 diverted to Pittsfield due to fuel issues and fog but crashed while attempting a visual approach. The accident resulted in substantial damage, a fatality, and serious injuries, caused by the pilot descending below the cleared 2,500 ft minimum altitude in low visibility.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain an appropriate decent rate during approach, resulting in a hard landing.
summary: A helicopter pilot performing an air tour landing at a fairground experienced a sudden drop from 10 to 15 feet while executing a pedal turn. The aircraft landed hard, causing substantial fuselage damage, though the pilot reported no preimpact mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: The pilot's improper throttle input during an approach, which resulted in a rapid descent, hard landing and runway excursion.
summary: The pilot of an experimental amateur-built airplane reduced all engine power during an approach after five go-arounds, causing a rapid descent and hard landing. The aircraft departed the left side of the dirt strip and nosed over, sustaining substantial damage to the empennage, wings, and fuselage with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper PA-14 operating under Part 91 lost all engine power shortly after applying full carburetor heat while descending near Talkeetna, Alaska. He executed a forced landing on a gravel bar where the left main gear collapsed, causing substantial damage to the left wing and fuselage.
summary: The pilot of a Piper PA-14 operating under Part 91 lost all engine power shortly after applying full carburetor heat while descending near Talkeetna, Alaska. He executed a forced landing on a gravel bar where the left main gear collapsed, causing substantial damage to the left wing and fuselage.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate preflight inspection, and inadequate inflight fuel management, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel starvation and subsequent forced landing.
summary: The pilot mistakenly set the fuel selector to off instead of both prior to takeoff, causing total engine power loss shortly after departure. Unable to return to the runway, he performed a forced landing on a road, resulting in substantial wing damage.

synopsis: The pilot and pilot-rated passenger of a Socata TBM 700 were killed when the aircraft impacted mining equipment near Monroe, Wisconsin, during a missed approach in fog below landing minimums. The accident resulted from a high-speed, nose-down impact with the flaps and gear retracted, causing airframe fragmentation and an explosion.
summary: The pilot and pilot-rated passenger of a Socata TBM 700 were killed when the aircraft impacted mining equipment near Monroe, Wisconsin, during a missed approach in fog below landing minimums. The accident resulted from a high-speed, nose-down impact with the flaps and gear retracted, causing airframe fragmentation and an explosion.

synopsis: A commercial pilot flying a Cessna 401A at 17,000 ft experienced dual engine failure after switching fuel tanks during an aerial observation flight. The pilot executed a forced landing in a field, resulting in substantial damage when the nose gear collapsed.
summary: A commercial pilot flying a Cessna 401A at 17,000 ft experienced dual engine failure after switching fuel tanks during an aerial observation flight. The pilot executed a forced landing in a field, resulting in substantial damage when the nose gear collapsed.

synopsis: A private pilot flying an experimental Long EZ, N82MT, experienced progressive engine roughness and total power loss at 500 feet AGL near Beaufort, South Carolina. Despite troubleshooting attempts, the pilot performed a forced landing in a stream, resulting in substantial damage to the aircraft.
summary: A private pilot flying an experimental Long EZ, N82MT, experienced progressive engine roughness and total power loss at 500 feet AGL near Beaufort, South Carolina. Despite troubleshooting attempts, the pilot performed a forced landing in a stream, resulting in substantial damage to the aircraft.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control of the airplane during the landing roll.
summary: The pilot of a multi-engine airplane veered right off the runway during landing after ineffective braking, impacting a taxiway sign. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the nose gear bulkhead and fuselage, with the pilot reporting no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper PA-46-701TP Fury sustained serious injuries when the aircraft crashed in Provo, Utah, after the pitch trim became stuck in a full nose-up position. The accident occurred during the climb phase when the pilot could not overcome extreme control forces to prevent a pitch-up, leading to a high-speed landing and subsequent fire.
summary: The pilot of a Piper PA-46-701TP Fury sustained serious injuries when the aircraft crashed in Provo, Utah, after the pitch trim became stuck in a full nose-up position. The accident occurred during the climb phase when the pilot could not overcome extreme control forces to prevent a pitch-up, leading to a high-speed landing and subsequent fire.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from a power line during an approach to land.
summary: The pilot reported that while turning from base to final, the airplane struck a powerline with the main landing gear, causing substantial damage to the right aileron. The pilot regained control and landed safely, noting no pre-accident mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: The pilot's improper decision to take off with the airplane over its maximum allowable gross weight, which degraded its climb performance and led to a subsequent off airport landing.
summary: The pilot conducted a flight test in an aircraft over maximum gross weight by 25 lbs due to full fuel tanks. Poor climb performance necessitated a forced landing in a short field, resulting in a hard landing and substantial damage to the wings and fuselage with no mechanical failure reported.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental Lancair IV-P experienced an engine explosion and power loss at 16,500 feet while en route to Sarasota. After a precautionary shutdown and failed glide attempt, the pilot deployed the ballistic parachute, landing on a golf course with substantial airframe damage but no injuries.
summary: The pilot of an experimental Lancair IV-P experienced an engine explosion and power loss at 16,500 feet while en route to Sarasota. After a precautionary shutdown and failed glide attempt, the pilot deployed the ballistic parachute, landing on a golf course with substantial airframe damage but no injuries.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper PA-24-180 experienced total engine power loss during cruise to Lakeland, Florida, likely due to fuel exhaustion despite switching tanks. The pilot declared an emergency and performed a forced landing with gear retracted, resulting in substantial damage to the right wing and stabilator after striking a fence.
summary: The pilot of a Piper PA-24-180 experienced total engine power loss during cruise to Lakeland, Florida, likely due to fuel exhaustion despite switching tanks. The pilot declared an emergency and performed a forced landing with gear retracted, resulting in substantial damage to the right wing and stabilator after striking a fence.

synopsis: A Cessna 172N carrying a flight instructor and student crashed into Lake Pontchartrain near New Orleans while on an ILS approach to runway 18R. The aircraft was destroyed and both occupants were fatally injured after executing a tight descending left turn in instrument meteorological conditions.
summary: A Cessna 172N carrying a flight instructor and student crashed into Lake Pontchartrain near New Orleans while on an ILS approach to runway 18R. The aircraft was destroyed and both occupants were fatally injured after executing a tight descending left turn in instrument meteorological conditions.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental RG12 ferry flight experienced severe airframe vibration and control issues caused by loose right wing drag wires. Unable to land safely at a diversion airport, the pilot attempted a landing in high winds at Benton Harbor, where the aircraft veered off the runway, nosed over, and sustained substantial damage.
summary: The pilot of an experimental RG12 ferry flight experienced severe airframe vibration and control issues caused by loose right wing drag wires. Unable to land safely at a diversion airport, the pilot attempted a landing in high winds at Benton Harbor, where the aircraft veered off the runway, nosed over, and sustained substantial damage.

synopsis: The elevator control restriction was caused by the failure of an elevator autopilot servo control cable which failed due to cyclic fatigue. The slack in the cable wrapped around the servo mount in such a way that it interfered with the rotation of the servo mount. The servo mount remained connected to the aft side of the elevator control quadrant by the intact aft cables. This condition resulted in the limited rotation of the elevator control quadrant in one direction.
summary: SkyWest Airlines flight 4229, a CRJ550, experienced nose-up pitch restriction during landing at KHIB due to a broken elevator autopilot servo control cable. The aircraft landed safely with no injuries or damage, and maintenance attributed the failure to cyclic fatigue in the cable.

synopsis: A newly certified private pilot and passenger were fatally injured when their American Aviation AA-1A crashed into a mountainous slope near Alamogordo, New Mexico, during a Part 91 personal flight. The aircraft struck trees and caught fire after departing Alamogordo-White Sands Regional Airport and failing to return.
summary: A newly certified private pilot and passenger were fatally injured when their American Aviation AA-1A crashed into a mountainous slope near Alamogordo, New Mexico, during a Part 91 personal flight. The aircraft struck trees and caught fire after departing Alamogordo-White Sands Regional Airport and failing to return.

synopsis: The flight instructors failure to extend the landing gear before landing.
summary: A flight instructor landed an aircraft with the gear retracted after failing to extend it, causing the plane to slide off the runway and sustain substantial lower fuselage damage. The instructor reported the gear warning horn did not activate, though post-accident examination found no mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing.
summary: The pilot overcorrected a gust during a go-around, causing the aircraft to veer off the runway and strike a distance remaining sign. This impact jammed the elevator nose-up and damaged the left wing strut and stabilizer, though the pilot regained control at 400 feet and landed safely.

synopsis: The collision with two deer during takeoff which resulted in a loss of control and impact with terrain.
summary: The pilot struck two deer during takeoff from a private airstrip, causing a thump to the right main gear and aggressive nose-down pitch. Despite corrective inputs, the aircraft veered off the runway, struck trees, and sustained substantial left wing damage with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from power lines during low-level maneuvering along a river.
summary: A witness observed an aircraft maneuvering 30 to 50 feet above a river before banking and striking a powerline estimated at 40 to 45 feet high. The pilot was seriously injured and the airplane sustained substantial damage, but the pilot has not yet provided a statement regarding the cause.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airplane control during an attempted go-around.
summary: The pilot executed a go-around after a bounced landing on runway 27 due to runway length concerns. During the climb, the aircraft yawed left, struck a tree, and impacted the ground, causing substantial damage with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The balloon landing in increased wind, and the pilot's inability to maintain the proper descent rate, which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: A hot air balloon pilot and eight passengers encountered unexpected 19-knot gusts and a downdraft, forcing a diversion to an open area. Despite activating the rapid-deflation system, the balloon landed hard at 23 knots, dragging and causing a serious injury to one passenger.

synopsis: United Airlines flight crew's failure to maintain adequate clearance from the parked Envoy Airlines airplane while taxiing in winter weather conditions. United Airlines flight crew's failure to maintain adequate clearance from the parked Envoy Airlines airplane while taxiing in winter weather conditions.
summary: United Airlines A320 flight 2333 collided with a stationary Envoy Airlines ERJ-175 flight 4028 while taxiing at Chicago O'Hare in heavy snow obscuring taxiway markings. The A320's left winglet struck the ERJ-175's right horizontal stabilizer and elevator, causing substantial damage to the Envoy aircraft and minor damage to the United aircraft with no injuries.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control on takeoff. Contributing to the accident was the aircraft design that did not incorporate differential braking.
summary: The pilot of an amateur-built tailwheel airplane without differential braking drifted left during takeoff in a mild right crosswind and struck a sign, causing substantial left wing damage. Postaccident examination found no mechanical malfunctions with the tailwheel or brake system.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to attain a proper touchdown point while landing with a quartering tailwind, which resulted in a long landing and subsequent runway excursion.
summary: The pilot reported that during a nighttime visual approach landing in wet conditions with a right quartering tailwind, a gust caused the aircraft to become airborne briefly before overrunning the runway. The airplane impacted a perimeter fence, sustaining substantial wing damage, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control while landing in a crosswind.
summary: The pilot landed a tailwheel-equipped airplane in a 13-knot right crosswind gusting to 20 knots. The aircraft departed the left side of the runway and struck the perimeter fence, causing substantial damage to the fuselage and wings with no preaccident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain altitude and clearance from trees while maneuvering at night.
summary: A solo student pilot flying at night diverted from a straight-in approach to avoid a departing aircraft but unintentionally descended and struck a tree. The subsequent stall caused a second impact with trees before the airplane nosed over into a river, sustaining substantial damage with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot of a Mooney M20K experienced total engine power loss during a Part 91 personal flight near Foley, Alabama, likely due to fuel management issues. The pilot attempted an off-field landing in a pasture, where the aircraft struck a fence and sustained substantial damage.
summary: The pilot of a Mooney M20K experienced total engine power loss during a Part 91 personal flight near Foley, Alabama, likely due to fuel management issues. The pilot attempted an off-field landing in a pasture, where the aircraft struck a fence and sustained substantial damage.

synopsis: A pilot operating a Hughes 369D helicopter on a Part 91 aerial observation flight was fatally injured when the aircraft substantially damaged after flipping over and falling to the ground. Witnesses reported the helicopter suddenly pitched up to a near-inverted attitude while hovering near a power line to monitor a "sock" device, then pitched straight down into an open field.
summary: A pilot operating a Hughes 369D helicopter on a Part 91 aerial observation flight was fatally injured when the aircraft substantially damaged after flipping over and falling to the ground. Witnesses reported the helicopter suddenly pitched up to a near-inverted attitude while hovering near a power line to monitor a "sock" device, then pitched straight down into an open field.

synopsis: The pilot's exceedance of the critical angle of attack during initial climb which resulted in an aerodynamic stall.
summary: The pilot departed a night IFR flight in an aircraft likely at or above maximum takeoff weight due to fuel discrepancies. The airplane entered an aerodynamic stall shortly after rotation, causing an uncontrollable left yaw and impact with trees, resulting in substantial damage.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare which resulted in a hard landing. Contributing to the accident was the pilot being in a rush and failing to note the wind direction and speed.
summary: The pilot diverted due to fog and landed on runway 35 with a 10-knot right quartering tailwind. The aircraft dropped from 20 feet, hit on the left gear, and nosed over, causing substantial damage; the pilot attributed the accident to rushing the landing and ignoring wind conditions.

synopsis: The flight instructor's inadequate fuel quantity inspection, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion.
summary: During a cross-country instructional flight, the flight instructor performed a forced landing after total engine power loss, striking trees and sustaining substantial damage. The instructor attributed the accident to fuel exhaustion caused by relying on inaccurate avionics fuel indications instead of visually verifying tank quantities.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airplane control of the airplane during an aborted landing, resulting in a runway excursion and collision with terrain.
summary: During the landing flare at 5 ft AGL, the pilot experienced a stall and bounced, then aborted due to excursion concerns. Improper elevator and rudder inputs caused the aircraft to yaw and roll left, striking a drainage ditch and damaging the fuselage with no pre-impact mechanical failures.

synopsis: The flight crew's failure to adequately manage the available fuel onboard the airplane, which resulted in a total loss of power due to fuel starvation.
summary: A pilot and flight instructor flying a multi-engine airplane experienced dual engine power loss at 1,500 ft AGL due to fuel starvation caused by inaccurate fuel gauges. The aircraft crashed onto an interstate highway, striking a vehicle and sustaining substantial damage.

synopsis: The collision with a deer during takeoff.
summary: A student pilot and flight instructor experienced a runway incursion during takeoff when a second deer struck the propeller after the first was avoided. The impact damaged the left main landing gear, causing it to collapse and resulting in substantial damage to the left wing as the aircraft skidded to a stop.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing in crosswind conditions. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's lack of recent flight experience.
summary: A pilot landing a tailwheel airplane on runway 19 in light crosswinds failed to apply appropriate control inputs, causing the left wing to strike the runway. The aircraft subsequently ground looped and exited the runway, resulting in substantial damage to the left wing and aileron.

synopsis: The pilot's improper securing hardware installation, which resulted in a loss of throttle control and a loss of engine power.
summary: The pilot of an amateur-built helicopter experienced engine power loss during landing at 30 ft due to a disconnected throttle cable caused by a missing retaining nut. This resulted in a hard autorotative landing that damaged the tailboom and tail rotor blades.

synopsis: A commercial pilot flying a Cessna TU206F on a Part 91 aerial observation flight experienced sudden total engine power loss after fuel gauge fluctuations. The pilot executed an emergency field landing, causing substantial fuselage damage, nose gear collapse, and partial empennage separation.
summary: A commercial pilot flying a Cessna TU206F on a Part 91 aerial observation flight experienced sudden total engine power loss after fuel gauge fluctuations. The pilot executed an emergency field landing, causing substantial fuselage damage, nose gear collapse, and partial empennage separation.

synopsis: A commercial pilot was fatally injured when his American Champion Decathlon, N157WB, crashed shortly after departing runway 18 at Roy E. Ray Airfield. The aircraft pitched up, rolled left 270 degrees, and impacted a wooded area while carrying two repacked parachutes.
summary: A commercial pilot was fatally injured when his American Champion Decathlon, N157WB, crashed shortly after departing runway 18 at Roy E. Ray Airfield. The aircraft pitched up, rolled left 270 degrees, and impacted a wooded area while carrying two repacked parachutes.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate visual lookout while taxing, which resulted in the airplane striking a light pole.
summary: The pilot reported that a lowered seat reduced forward visibility during taxi, causing the aircraft's left wing to strike a light pole and sustain substantial damage. The pilot stated no pre-accident mechanical malfunctions occurred.

synopsis: The pilot of a Sonerai II (N28MD) experienced abnormal engine sounds and fluctuating RPMs during a downwind turn after a high-speed pass. He attempted an emergency landing but overran the runway, striking a tree in a ravine, which caused substantial damage and serious injury.
summary: The pilot of a Sonerai II (N28MD) experienced abnormal engine sounds and fluctuating RPMs during a downwind turn after a high-speed pass. He attempted an emergency landing but overran the runway, striking a tree in a ravine, which caused substantial damage and serious injury.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll.
summary: A student pilot returning from a solo cross-country flight reported the right wheel caught during landing roll, causing the aircraft to veer right. Despite applying opposite rudder, the airplane exited the runway and nosed over, sustaining substantial damage to the vertical stabilizer and rudder with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to extend the landing gear prior to landing.
summary: During a maintenance test flight, the pilot landed with the gear retracted after failing to confirm the dim LED gear-down advisory lights, which were obscured by sunlight. This resulted in substantial damage to the lower fuselage composite structure, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The biplane pilot's failure to maintain adequate clearance from the low-wing airplane while taxiing. The biplane pilot's failure to maintain adequate clearance from the low-wing airplane while taxiing.
summary: While taxiing behind a stopped low-wing airplane, a tailwheel biplane pilot performing s-turns lost sight of the lead aircraft and collided despite evasive braking. The biplane's wing and propeller struck the low-wing airplane's rudder and empennage, causing substantial damage to both aircraft with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot of a Bell 505 helicopter reported a loud bang and cyclic shake shortly after takeoff, causing uncommanded pitching and partial loss of control. He executed a forced landing over land, resulting in the aircraft rolling onto its left side with substantial main rotor damage and serious pilot injury.
summary: The pilot of a Bell 505 helicopter reported a loud bang and cyclic shake shortly after takeoff, causing uncommanded pitching and partial loss of control. He executed a forced landing over land, resulting in the aircraft rolling onto its left side with substantial main rotor damage and serious pilot injury.

synopsis: The pilot's improper pitch control that resulted in a hard landing, and his improper recovery from multiple bounced landings. Contributing to the accident was the safety pilot's delayed response to the initial bounced landing which led to the runway excursion.
summary: During a proficiency flight, the pilot bounced twice after flaring high and failing to add power. The safety pilot took over, applied maximum power, but lost directional control, causing the aircraft to veer off, hit a fence and trees, and sustain substantial damage.

synopsis: The pilot of a Beechcraft G36 experienced engine oil pressure loss and failure at 17,000 feet following a recent overhaul, causing smoke and rough running. Unable to reach the requested airport, the pilot attempted an emergency glide landing but landed short in an irrigation canal, sustaining minor injuries and substantial aircraft damage.
summary: The pilot of a Beechcraft G36 experienced engine oil pressure loss and failure at 17,000 feet following a recent overhaul, causing smoke and rough running. Unable to reach the requested airport, the pilot attempted an emergency glide landing but landed short in an irrigation canal, sustaining minor injuries and substantial aircraft damage.

synopsis: Tail rotor blade impact from an unidentified object at an undetermined time.
summary: The aircrew conducted an air medical helicopter flight transporting a patient between facilities. A post-flight inspection revealed substantial dents on the vertical stabilizer and a tail rotor blade, though the time and source of the damage were undetermined.

synopsis: A Piper PA-30 pilot and passenger were fatally injured when the aircraft crashed shortly after takeoff from runway 20R near West Chicago, Illinois. The plane drifted right, banked steeply to 90°, and impacted terrain while witnesses reported normal engine sounds and no pre-accident control anomalies.
summary: A Piper PA-30 pilot and passenger were fatally injured when the aircraft crashed shortly after takeoff from runway 20R near West Chicago, Illinois. The plane drifted right, banked steeply to 90°, and impacted terrain while witnesses reported normal engine sounds and no pre-accident control anomalies.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna Citation 550, accompanied by six passengers, fatally crashed near Statesville, North Carolina, shortly after takeoff. The accident resulted from a post-takeoff descent and loss of control following reported flight instrument and audio malfunctions, leading to impact with approach lights and a subsequent fire.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna Citation 550, accompanied by six passengers, fatally crashed near Statesville, North Carolina, shortly after takeoff. The accident resulted from a post-takeoff descent and loss of control following reported flight instrument and audio malfunctions, leading to impact with approach lights and a subsequent fire.

synopsis: The pilot of a Mooney M20J sustained serious injuries when the aircraft crashed near Silver Springs, Nevada, during a go-around attempt in strong gusts. The accident occurred after the pilot landed on runway 6 without wind information due to an out-of-service AWOS, resulting in a failed climb and stall.
summary: The pilot of a Mooney M20J sustained serious injuries when the aircraft crashed near Silver Springs, Nevada, during a go-around attempt in strong gusts. The accident occurred after the pilot landed on runway 6 without wind information due to an out-of-service AWOS, resulting in a failed climb and stall.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental Velocity V-Twin, N22EU, suffered minor injuries when the aircraft substantially damaged a house and vehicle during a Part 91 traffic pattern turn. The pilot reported the airplane steepened its bank and nosed down uncontrollably despite full power, with no preimpact mechanical failures observed.
summary: The pilot of an experimental Velocity V-Twin, N22EU, suffered minor injuries when the aircraft substantially damaged a house and vehicle during a Part 91 traffic pattern turn. The pilot reported the airplane steepened its bank and nosed down uncontrollably despite full power, with no preimpact mechanical failures observed.

synopsis: The flight instructor's inadequate supervision during the approach and delayed remedial action, which resulted in a loss of control.
summary: During a hydraulic training maneuver, a student pilot's excessive sink rate caused a helicopter to bounce, slide off the runway, and roll onto its side, damaging the rotor systems. The chief flight instructor attributed the accident to the instructor's failure to recognize the high descent rate and intervene, noting no mechanical failures occurred.

synopsis: The pilots' failure to ensure that the airplane's landing gear was extended before landing. Contributing was the flight instructor's inadequate supervision during the landing approach.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot landed a twin-engine aircraft with gear retracted after the instructor, distracted by traffic, skipped the before-landing checklist. The landing gear warning horn was inaudible because its circuit breaker remained pulled from a prior simulated engine failure, causing substantial fuselage damage.

synopsis: A pilot and passenger in a Cirrus SR22 experienced engine roughness and total power loss during cruise at 8,000 feet, forcing a landing on US 65. The aircraft struck a road sign and caught fire, sustaining substantial damage, though both occupants escaped uninjured.
summary: A pilot and passenger in a Cirrus SR22 experienced engine roughness and total power loss during cruise at 8,000 feet, forcing a landing on US 65. The aircraft struck a road sign and caught fire, sustaining substantial damage, though both occupants escaped uninjured.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate preflight inspection and fuel planning, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion.
summary: The pilot of a single-engine airplane experienced a total engine power loss during the return leg of a cross-country flight due to fuel exhaustion. He executed a forced landing in a vineyard, sustaining substantial damage to the wing struts and horizontal stabilizers after striking ground stakes.

aircraft: Mark O Treidel American Ranger AR-1
synopsis: The pilot's failure to attain rotor RPM and maintain proper rotor disc angle during takeoff which resulted in a rotor strike with the rudder.
summary: During a windy takeoff roll, a gyroplane pilot experienced rotor flap at 130–140 RPM, causing the rotor to strike and damage the rudder. The pilot returned to land safely, attributing the incident to insufficient pre-rotation speed rather than mechanical failure.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel biplane lost directional control during a three-point landing, causing the aircraft to ground-loop off the runway. Both lower wings struck the ground, resulting in substantial damage to the left wing and aileron due to pilot control inputs.
