summary: The pilot of a Piper PA-30 reported that upon landing at Big Bear City Airport, the nose gear collapsed despite appearing extended, causing the aircraft to slide and sustain substantial fuselage damage. No injuries occurred, and the pilot noted the green landing gear light failed to illuminate before the collapse.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control of the airplane during the landing roll, which resulted in a runway excursion and collision with a ditch.
summary: The pilot reported that during landing after annual inspection, the airplane veered left upon nose wheel touchdown despite rudder inputs, exiting the runway and impacting a ditch with substantial damage. A post-accident mechanic examination found no pre-accident mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain proper airspeed during landing and exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall and impact with the runway. Contributing to the accident was the flight instructor's delayed remedial action.
summary: During a landing on runway 12 in gusty winds, a student pilot's delayed response to a headwind loss caused a stall and hard landing. The flight instructor's corrective power addition was insufficient, resulting in substantial damage to the left wing and lift strut with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot of a Raytheon G58 experienced landing gear indication failures and an inoperative gear motor during approach to Savannah. After manually extending the gear for a soft field landing, the gear collapsed on touchdown, causing substantial fuselage damage.
summary: The pilot of a Raytheon G58 experienced landing gear indication failures and an inoperative gear motor during approach to Savannah. After manually extending the gear for a soft field landing, the gear collapsed on touchdown, causing substantial fuselage damage.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental Peck Jodel-F12, N30P, sustained fatal injuries when the aircraft crashed into Beaver Lake during a personal ferry flight from Ozark Aerodrome to Springdale. A witness reported a rough-running engine and observed the airplane enter a nose-down descent after failing to land on a nearby private airstrip.
summary: The pilot of an experimental Peck Jodel-F12, N30P, sustained fatal injuries when the aircraft crashed into Beaver Lake during a personal ferry flight from Ozark Aerodrome to Springdale. A witness reported a rough-running engine and observed the airplane enter a nose-down descent after failing to land on a nearby private airstrip.

synopsis: The captain's inadequate compensation for gusting crosswind wind conditions while attempting to land and a subsequent go-around.
summary: Endeavor Air flight 5304, a CRJ700, sustained minor wingtip damage during a go-around at Atlanta due to pilot overcontrol while correcting a wind-induced balloon. The captain overcorrected the aircraft's roll after a gust at 30 feet, causing both wings to strike the runway before the first officer completed a safe landing.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare and subsequent loss of directional control while attempting to land during high crosswind conditions.
summary: The pilot reported a hard landing and runway departure on approach to Runway 21 due to windshear in 28-knot crosswinds gusting to 44 knots. This caused substantial damage to the fuselage and left wing, with the pilot admitting he should not have attempted the landing in those conditions.

synopsis: The flight crew's failure to maintain adequate clearance from the blast fence during taxi to the runway for departure, and their inadequate inspection of the airplane after it contacted the blast fence.
summary: The SIC of a business jet struck a jet blast fence while taxiing, damaging the right elevator. Later, in cruise, the crew experienced severe buffeting and pitch alerts, leading to a diversion where the partially detached elevator was discovered.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental Vans RV-8, N80AR, was fatally injured when the aircraft impacted terrain near Hurricane, Utah, during a formation flight at 500 feet AGL. Witnesses reported the airplane pitched up and rolled left before the pilot attempted recovery, resulting in substantial damage to the aircraft.
summary: The pilot of an experimental Vans RV-8, N80AR, was fatally injured when the aircraft impacted terrain near Hurricane, Utah, during a formation flight at 500 feet AGL. Witnesses reported the airplane pitched up and rolled left before the pilot attempted recovery, resulting in substantial damage to the aircraft.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper PA-22-150 was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed into a tree and sloping terrain while on the downwind leg for runway 35 at Paradise Airport Skypark. The accident occurred during a personal flight to initiate an annual inspection, resulting in the destruction of the airplane.
summary: The pilot of a Piper PA-22-150 was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed into a tree and sloping terrain while on the downwind leg for runway 35 at Paradise Airport Skypark. The accident occurred during a personal flight to initiate an annual inspection, resulting in the destruction of the airplane.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airplane control during takeoff, which resulted in a runway excursion and collision with terrain.
summary: During a soft field takeoff, the pilot reported the airplane drifted left in ground effect, causing the left wing to strike trees and damage the fuselage, wing, and horizontal stabilizer. The pilot stated no pre-accident mechanical failures occurred.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from trees on takeoff from a rural road.
summary: The pilot landed in an adjacent field due to sun glare while attempting to land on a private grass runway. During a subsequent takeoff attempt from a nearby paved road, the airplane collided with trees, causing substantial damage to the wings and fuselage with no reported mechanical failures.

aircraft: Morris Bradley D ZENITH STOL CH-701
synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during takeoff, which resulted in a runway excursion and impact with trees.
summary: An inexperienced pilot reported that during takeoff, the aircraft lifted off with a nose-high attitude and uncontrolled left turn, causing it to depart the runway and impact trees. The pilot attributed the substantial damage to the wings and fuselage to a lack of experience rather than any preimpact mechanical malfunction.

synopsis: The pilot's improper fuel planning and his failure to adequately monitor the fuel level during flight, which resulted in fuel exhaustion, and a total loss of engine power. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's lack of attention performing the task, which led to a loss of situational awareness.
summary: The pilot of an aerial application airplane experienced total engine power loss due to fuel exhaustion while returning to a private airstrip. The pilot executed a forced landing in a wooded area, escaping uninjured, though the aircraft sustained substantial damage.

synopsis: The captain's inadvertent activation of the takeoff/go around switch at touchdown that caused an increase in the airplane pitch attitude that was not corrected before the lower fuselage contacted the runway.
summary: All Nippon Airways flight 114 tailstruck during a CAT III autoland at Houston after the captain inadvertently pressed the TOGA switch while reaching for thrust reversers. This activated go-around pitch mode, raising the nose to 7.9° and causing substantial fuselage damage despite no injuries.

synopsis: United Airlines flight 2127, a Boeing 787-9, experienced a left engine surge, fire, and compressor stall during climb from LAX. The crew returned, landed safely, and evacuated after observing fire, with post-incident inspection revealing thermal damage to the engine core and high-pressure turbine.
summary: United Airlines flight 2127, a Boeing 787-9, experienced a left engine surge, fire, and compressor stall during climb from LAX. The crew returned, landed safely, and evacuated after observing fire, with post-incident inspection revealing thermal damage to the engine core and high-pressure turbine.

synopsis: The flight instructor's inadequate supervision of a dual student who attempted a go-around using one engine which resulted in a loss of control and impact with the ground.
summary: During a simulated single-engine landing training flight, the student pilot initiated a go-around using only the left engine, causing an uncontrolled right turn and collision with a hangar. The flight instructor attributed the accident to a briefing omission regarding the use of both engines for go-arounds, noting no mechanical failures occurred.

synopsis: During a Part 91 practice quick stop maneuver, a Bell 206L-3 pilot lost collective control and entered an autorotation from 50 feet, resulting in a tailboom collapse upon taxiway contact. The pilot and passenger were uninjured, but the helicopter sustained substantial damage before being sold for salvage.
summary: During a Part 91 practice quick stop maneuver, a Bell 206L-3 pilot lost collective control and entered an autorotation from 50 feet, resulting in a tailboom collapse upon taxiway contact. The pilot and passenger were uninjured, but the helicopter sustained substantial damage before being sold for salvage.

aircraft: Remos Acft Gmbh Flugzeugbau REMOS GX
synopsis: The solo student pilot's improper landing flare and subsequent improper recovery from a bounced landing.
summary: A solo student pilot conducting touch-and-go landings bounced multiple times and applied forward elevator inputs, causing a nose-low touchdown. This resulted in bent nose gear, a propeller strike, and substantial fuselage damage, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to operate the airplane with a known mechanical defect, and the improper application of the main wheel brakes, which resulted in the airplane nosing over.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane nosed over while landing at a backcountry airstrip after the tailwheel assembly separated during taxi. The pilot attributed the accident to excessive main-wheel braking used to keep the tail off the ground, resulting in substantial damage to the airframe.

synopsis: Propeller separation due to failure of the propeller attachment bolts.
summary: The unregistered pilot operating an uncertificated aircraft experienced a pusher propeller separation during straight and level flight, causing engine overspeed and a forced landing. The accident resulted in substantial damage when the propeller struck the left wing and the right main gear separated, attributed to inadequate inspection of hidden propeller bolts.

synopsis: A flight instructor and student pilot in a Cessna 172N experienced zero oil pressure and total engine power loss after a touch-and-go at New York Stewart International Airport. The instructor ditched the aircraft in the Hudson River, striking submerged structures and causing substantial damage, though both occupants escaped with minor injuries.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot in a Cessna 172N experienced zero oil pressure and total engine power loss after a touch-and-go at New York Stewart International Airport. The instructor ditched the aircraft in the Hudson River, striking submerged structures and causing substantial damage, though both occupants escaped with minor injuries.

synopsis: A control system anomaly, which resulted in the overload and failure of one of the propulsion motor systems during the transition from hover to forward flight.
summary: An unmanned aircraft experienced control and estimation anomalies during a test flight transition, leading to a motor pod failure from high load. The aircraft departed controlled flight and impacted an adjacent taxiway, resulting in total destruction with no injuries or property damage.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in hard, bounced landing and subsequent tail strike.
summary: The pilot reported a hard landing and bounce during the flare of a visual approach, causing the empennage to strike the runway and the nose wheel to blow out. This resulted in substantial empennage damage, though the pilot stated no mechanical malfunctions occurred.

synopsis: The hot air balloon's encounter with downdraft wind conditions in mountainous terrain and subsequent impact with terrain.
summary: A hot air balloon pilot conducting a sightseeing flight encountered mountain downdrafts that caused an uncontrolled sink and ground speed increase. The basket struck a rock, damaging structural components and causing a minor injury to one standing passenger, though the pilot attributed the event to weather rather than mechanical failure.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate fuel planning and improper in-flight decision-making, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion.
summary: The pilot of a single-engine airplane experienced total engine power loss due to fuel exhaustion during a night cross-country flight. This resulted in a forced landing into trees and substantial damage, caused by inadequate fuel planning for weather and route deviations.

synopsis: During a Part 91 instructional flight in a Piper PA-28-140 near Phoenix, the flight instructor and student experienced engine power loss at 1,700 feet AGL. The aircraft subsequently crashed into residential homes after the engine failed completely, causing substantial damage and injuries to the crew and a ground person.
summary: During a Part 91 instructional flight in a Piper PA-28-140 near Phoenix, the flight instructor and student experienced engine power loss at 1,700 feet AGL. The aircraft subsequently crashed into residential homes after the engine failed completely, causing substantial damage and injuries to the crew and a ground person.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna T210M conducting an RNAV 16 approach to Chicago Executive Airport ignored ATC low altitude alerts and drifted west of course before impacting trees and a townhouse. The pilot was fatally injured, and the aircraft sustained substantial damage with the engine operating at impact.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna T210M conducting an RNAV 16 approach to Chicago Executive Airport ignored ATC low altitude alerts and drifted west of course before impacting trees and a townhouse. The pilot was fatally injured, and the aircraft sustained substantial damage with the engine operating at impact.

synopsis: During a post-maintenance test flight, a Cessna 551 crew encountered a right main landing gear extension failure on an ILS approach. Despite troubleshooting, the gear collapsed upon landing, causing substantial wing damage, while subsequent tests confirmed the actuator only extended to 45°.
summary: During a post-maintenance test flight, a Cessna 551 crew encountered a right main landing gear extension failure on an ILS approach. Despite troubleshooting, the gear collapsed upon landing, causing substantial wing damage, while subsequent tests confirmed the actuator only extended to 45°.

synopsis: The solo student pilot's improper landing flare and subsequent improper recovery from a bounced landing which resulted in substantial damage to the airplane.
summary: A student pilot experienced a bounced landing during a solo practice flight, resulting in a hard nose-first touchdown. The event caused substantial fuselage damage, though the pilot reported no pre-accident mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: The pilot of a BN-2B-27 Islander taxiing at Benjamin Rivera Noriega Airport lost right braking action, causing the aircraft to veer off the taxiway onto grass and a drain. Subsequent inspection revealed a buckled left wing and a leaking right brake caliper seal, resulting in substantial damage.
summary: The pilot of a BN-2B-27 Islander taxiing at Benjamin Rivera Noriega Airport lost right braking action, causing the aircraft to veer off the taxiway onto grass and a drain. Subsequent inspection revealed a buckled left wing and a leaking right brake caliper seal, resulting in substantial damage.

synopsis: A loss of thermal lift during a glider flight, which resulted in a collision with trees during a landing approach to a diversionary airport.
summary: The glider pilot, while attempting to cross a ridge line after an aerotow, discovered an unseen private turf runway and initiated a landing approach. The glider struck trees 200 feet short of the runway, causing substantial damage to the fuselage and wings, with no preimpact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to extend the landing gear before landing.
summary: The pilot landed an aircraft with the gear retracted on final approach due to distraction by a preceding aircraft. Although the gear warning horn functioned, noise-canceling headsets prevented the crew from hearing it, resulting in substantial fuselage damage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed during takeoff, which resulted in a loss of control and hard landing.
summary: The pilot reported a takeoff accident where the aircraft stalled, drifted left, and crashed into terrain, collapsing the right main gear. Although the pilot suspected water intrusion caused erroneous airspeed indications, maintenance testing found the pitot/static system and indicator within normal limits.

synopsis: The pilot and passenger of a Columbia LC41-550FG were fatally injured when the aircraft impacted a tree near Albuquerque after the pilot reported losing power and declared an emergency during descent. The accident occurred while the pilot attempted to find an area for an emergency landing following the power loss.
summary: The pilot and passenger of a Columbia LC41-550FG were fatally injured when the aircraft impacted a tree near Albuquerque after the pilot reported losing power and declared an emergency during descent. The accident occurred while the pilot attempted to find an area for an emergency landing following the power loss.

synopsis: The overstress failure of the left main landing gear lower drag brace links during takeoff which resulted in a runway excursion during landing due to the left main landing gear collapsing.
summary: Key Lime Air Flight 143, a Part 135 cargo flight, excused the runway at Denver International Airport due to a collapsed left main landing gear caused by fractured drag brace links. The pilot landed with an unsafe gear indication and icing, lost directional control upon touchdown, and sustained substantial damage to the left wing and gear while remaining uninjured.

synopsis: A pilot and passenger were fatally injured when their Beechcraft A36 crashed into water near Gulf Shores, Alabama, during an RNAV runway 9 approach. The accident occurred after the pilot failed to maintain the cleared heading and altitude, entering a steep descending turn following ATC instructions to rejoin the final approach course.
summary: A pilot and passenger were fatally injured when their Beechcraft A36 crashed into water near Gulf Shores, Alabama, during an RNAV runway 9 approach. The accident occurred after the pilot failed to maintain the cleared heading and altitude, entering a steep descending turn following ATC instructions to rejoin the final approach course.

synopsis: The pilot and crew member of a Bell 505 helicopter, N911FW, suffered no injuries during a Part 91 public use flight near Fort Worth, Texas. The pilot reported engine power decreased to idle during climbout, necessitating a forced landing that caused substantial damage to the vertical stabilizer.
summary: The pilot and crew member of a Bell 505 helicopter, N911FW, suffered no injuries during a Part 91 public use flight near Fort Worth, Texas. The pilot reported engine power decreased to idle during climbout, necessitating a forced landing that caused substantial damage to the vertical stabilizer.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate visual lookout, which resulted in a collision with a helicopter dolly during taxi.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane struck a helicopter dolly while taxiing between a parked van and the dolly on the ramp. This collision caused substantial damage to the fuselage underside, with the pilot reporting no preimpact mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: During a tailwheel endorsement training flight in a Piper PA-12, the student pilot and instructor attempted a takeoff from a grassy area with insufficient runway remaining. A loud bang occurred after rotation, causing the aircraft to wobble and dip, leading to a collision with a fence and tree that substantially damaged the airplane.
summary: During a tailwheel endorsement training flight in a Piper PA-12, the student pilot and instructor attempted a takeoff from a grassy area with insufficient runway remaining. A loud bang occurred after rotation, causing the aircraft to wobble and dip, leading to a collision with a fence and tree that substantially damaged the airplane.

synopsis: An in-flight collision with a bird while enroute.
summary: A flight instructor flying at 1,000 ft MSL attempted to evade a large black bird but sustained a strike on the left wing's leading edge. Despite substantial wing damage, she delayed flap deployment until over the runway and executed a safe long landing.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from trees while on final approach for landing. Contributing to the accident were the flight instructor's inadequate remedial actions.
summary: A pilot and flight instructor in a training flight struck trees with the right wing at 50–60 feet AGL during a short field landing approach due to being right of centerline and poor visibility. The pilot executed a go-around, but the wing sustained substantial damage with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot and passenger of a Piper PA-28-140 were seriously injured when the engine cut out at 1,000 feet AGL during climb, causing a forced landing where the left wing struck a tree. The FAA found the fuel selector was correctly set to the right tank with fuel present, and no engine failure signatures were observed.
summary: The pilot and passenger of a Piper PA-28-140 were seriously injured when the engine cut out at 1,000 feet AGL during climb, causing a forced landing where the left wing struck a tree. The FAA found the fuel selector was correctly set to the right tank with fuel present, and no engine failure signatures were observed.

synopsis: An MD Helicopters 369FF pilot was fatally injured when the helicopter was destroyed during a Part 133 external load power line rope stringing operation near Mojave, California. Witnesses reported a pop sound followed by a rapid descent and rotor stoppage before the aircraft struck the ground and erupted in flames, with no contact with obstructions.
summary: An MD Helicopters 369FF pilot was fatally injured when the helicopter was destroyed during a Part 133 external load power line rope stringing operation near Mojave, California. Witnesses reported a pop sound followed by a rapid descent and rotor stoppage before the aircraft struck the ground and erupted in flames, with no contact with obstructions.

synopsis: Maintenance personnel's decision to conduct an engine run at takeoff power in front of an active taxiway, and their failure to notify ATC, which resulted in the accident pilot's loss of control during taxi due to an encounter with a jet blast.
summary: A Cessna 182 taxiing for departure flipped over due to jet blast from a parked CRJ 700 undergoing unannounced engine testing by mechanics. The accident occurred because the mechanics failed to notify ATC or move the aircraft, placing the Cessna within the dangerous 290-foot blast zone at a distance of 240 feet.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control during landing, which resulted in a runway excursion and collision with terrain.
summary: During landing, the pilot bounced, attempted to stop due to insufficient runway for a go-around, and veered off the surface. The nosewheel struck snow, causing the aircraft to nose over inverted with substantial damage, which the pilot attributed to delaying the go-around.

synopsis: An encounter with a downdraft while maneuvering at a low altitude, which resulted in an impact with terrain.
summary: The pilot maneuvering at low altitude searching for an off-airport landing site encountered a downdraft during a left turn, causing a perceived loss of control. Despite leveling wings and applying full power, the aircraft impacted terrain, sustaining substantial damage to the fuselage, wings, and empennage with no prior mechanical anomalies.

synopsis: During a Part 91 instructional and engine break-in flight, a Rockwell 114 experienced total engine power loss at 2,700 feet MSL. The student pilot executed a forced landing where the landing gear separated, causing substantial damage to the fuselage and left wing while injuring the flight instructor and student.
summary: During a Part 91 instructional and engine break-in flight, a Rockwell 114 experienced total engine power loss at 2,700 feet MSL. The student pilot executed a forced landing where the landing gear separated, causing substantial damage to the fuselage and left wing while injuring the flight instructor and student.

synopsis: The pilot's improper approach, which resulted in a long landing, runway excursion, and a nose over.
summary: A pilot landing at an unfamiliar airport bounced on touchdown, overshot the paved runway, and lost steering traction on the dirt overrun. The aircraft nosed over and came to rest inverted with substantial right wing damage, with the pilot reporting no mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to extend the landing gear before landing.
summary: The pilot felt rushed during an instrument approach and extended speed brakes to descend rapidly, skipping the 500 ft before-landing check. Consequently, the aircraft touched down with landing gear retracted, causing substantial fuselage damage without any preimpact mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane while in the run-up area in high wind conditions.
summary: While parked in the run-up area facing 350° winds gusting to 25 knots, a gust tipped the aircraft onto its side, causing substantial left wing damage. The pilot reported using proper flight control inputs and noted no preimpact mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control during a crosswind takeoff, which resulted in a runway excursion and impact with a drainage ditch.
summary: The pilot departed in 9-knot crosswinds with 19-knot gusts, but the aircraft veered left immediately after liftoff with ineffective control inputs. The pilot executed a forced landing on adjacent grass, impacting a ditch and sustaining substantial damage, though post-accident inspection found no mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's improper decision to continue the flight into icing conditions, which resulted in the accumulation of airframe icing and a subsequent aerodynamic stall.
summary: A pilot flying a Cirrus aircraft under IFR encountered IMC and airframe icing while climbing to 12,000 ft, leading to a stall during descent. The pilot deployed the CAPS after the stall, resulting in a terrain impact with substantial damage to the elevator and rudder.

synopsis: The flight instructor's decision to conduct a training flight in strong, gusting crosswinds, which resulted in the airplane's right wing impacting the ground during taxi.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot experienced a ground accident during taxi for departure when 48-knot gusts exceeded the aircraft's 20-knot crosswind limit, causing a skid and right wing impact. The instructor attributed the substantial damage to extreme wind conditions and recommended implementing maximum wind gust limits for training flights.

synopsis: An in-flight collision with a bird during initial climb.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot experienced a bird strike during the climb phase after takeoff, causing substantial damage to the right wing. The instructor landed safely on a parallel runway, reporting no pre-impact mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: The pilot's improper flare, which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: A student pilot performing solo landings bounced on the first attempt and subsequently touched down on the nose gear on the second attempt. This resulted in substantial damage to the firewall and fuselage side skins, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot of an Aero Commander 500-B operating a Part 135 cargo flight was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed near Chesterfield, Missouri, shortly after departing runway 26L. The airplane entered a modified traffic pattern at altitudes between 500 and 850 feet MSL before impacting the ground and burning, though the investigation remains ongoing.
summary: The pilot of an Aero Commander 500-B operating a Part 135 cargo flight was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed near Chesterfield, Missouri, shortly after departing runway 26L. The airplane entered a modified traffic pattern at altitudes between 500 and 850 feet MSL before impacting the ground and burning, though the investigation remains ongoing.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate fuel planning, and improper in-flight decision making which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion.
summary: The pilot of an amphibious airplane without a seaplane rating experienced total engine power loss due to fuel exhaustion about 10 miles from destination. He made a forced water landing one mile short, causing substantial damage to the hull and engine pylon.

synopsis: The inaccurate obstacle height entered into mission planning that resulted in the aircraft wing's impact with a tree during descent, resulting resulted in a loss of control.
summary: A Pyka Pelican Cargo UAS was substantially damaged during an autonomous landing at Summit Point, West Virginia, after striking a tree and powerline at 60 feet. The accident resulted from incorrect obstacle height data in mission planning software and a missed taller tree, compounded by the lack of LIDAR for collision avoidance.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to extend the landing gear before landing.
summary: The pilot landed an aircraft with the gear retracted during a straight-in approach, causing substantial lower fuselage damage. Post-accident examination confirmed the landing gear system and warning horn functioned normally, with no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: A student pilot was killed when his Piper PA-28-140 crashed into a field near Rock Falls, Illinois, during a solo instructional flight. The aircraft was destroyed upon impact, with the investigation noting flight control cable separations and flap system jamming consistent with the crash forces.
summary: A student pilot was killed when his Piper PA-28-140 crashed into a field near Rock Falls, Illinois, during a solo instructional flight. The aircraft was destroyed upon impact, with the investigation noting flight control cable separations and flap system jamming consistent with the crash forces.

synopsis: The pilot of a Beechcraft B200GT operating a Part 91 flight from Fort Lauderdale to Dallas was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed near Sharp, Louisiana. Following an autopilot disconnect at FL280, the airplane entered an uncontrolled steep right turn and high-speed descent, impacting a swamp.
summary: The pilot of a Beechcraft B200GT operating a Part 91 flight from Fort Lauderdale to Dallas was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed near Sharp, Louisiana. Following an autopilot disconnect at FL280, the airplane entered an uncontrolled steep right turn and high-speed descent, impacting a swamp.

synopsis: Jazz Aviation flight 646, a CRJ-900, collided with ARFF vehicle R35 while landing on runway 4 at LaGuardia Airport after the vehicle entered the runway on ATC clearance. The crash fatally injured both pilots and caused substantial damage to the aircraft, with 39 people transported to hospitals.
summary: Jazz Aviation flight 646, a CRJ-900, collided with ARFF vehicle R35 while landing on runway 4 at LaGuardia Airport after the vehicle entered the runway on ATC clearance. The crash fatally injured both pilots and caused substantial damage to the aircraft, with 39 people transported to hospitals.

synopsis: A pilot operating a Beech A36 on a Part 91 cross-country flight reported a turbocharger problem and subsequently crashed into a lake near Olympic Valley, California. The aircraft was substantially damaged and the pilot was fatally injured after striking trees and coming to rest partially submerged.
summary: A pilot operating a Beech A36 on a Part 91 cross-country flight reported a turbocharger problem and subsequently crashed into a lake near Olympic Valley, California. The aircraft was substantially damaged and the pilot was fatally injured after striking trees and coming to rest partially submerged.

synopsis: A flight instructor and student pilot were fatally injured when their Robinson R44 helicopter crashed into a warehouse during a VFR instructional flight. The accident resulted from the separation of the upper right push-pull tube from its rod end, likely due to corrosion and loose fasteners, causing a loss of flight control.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot were fatally injured when their Robinson R44 helicopter crashed into a warehouse during a VFR instructional flight. The accident resulted from the separation of the upper right push-pull tube from its rod end, likely due to corrosion and loose fasteners, causing a loss of flight control.

synopsis: During the initial climb of a Cessna 172P aerial observation flight, the pilot experienced partial engine power loss and attempted an emergency landing. The aircraft struck trees while trying to clear them after the pilot determined insufficient runway remained, resulting in substantial damage and injuries to both occupants.
summary: During the initial climb of a Cessna 172P aerial observation flight, the pilot experienced partial engine power loss and attempted an emergency landing. The aircraft struck trees while trying to clear them after the pilot determined insufficient runway remained, resulting in substantial damage and injuries to both occupants.

synopsis: During a max performance takeoff of an Aerospatiale SA341G Gazelle from Winslow, Arizona, the pilot observed a torque caution light and engine over-temperature event. The instructor directed a collective reduction, but the helicopter settled hard, sustaining substantial tailboom damage and causing minor injuries to the pilot and passenger.
summary: During a max performance takeoff of an Aerospatiale SA341G Gazelle from Winslow, Arizona, the pilot observed a torque caution light and engine over-temperature event. The instructor directed a collective reduction, but the helicopter settled hard, sustaining substantial tailboom damage and causing minor injuries to the pilot and passenger.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper PA-28-140 experienced a partial engine power loss at 5,800 feet MSL while returning to South Valley Regional Airport. Unable to restore power, the pilot made an off-airport landing where rough terrain caused the nose and right gear to collapse, substantially damaging the right wing and aileron.
summary: The pilot of a Piper PA-28-140 experienced a partial engine power loss at 5,800 feet MSL while returning to South Valley Regional Airport. Unable to restore power, the pilot made an off-airport landing where rough terrain caused the nose and right gear to collapse, substantially damaging the right wing and aileron.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper PA-12, N7632H, suffered substantial damage to the right wing when the aircraft departed the shoreline and entered the Willamette River during takeoff from an unimproved surface on Goat Island. Postaccident examination revealed the left main landing gear separated due to tears and cracking at its attach points.
summary: The pilot of a Piper PA-12, N7632H, suffered substantial damage to the right wing when the aircraft departed the shoreline and entered the Willamette River during takeoff from an unimproved surface on Goat Island. Postaccident examination revealed the left main landing gear separated due to tears and cracking at its attach points.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate clearance from trees during landing.
summary: During a cross-country flight, a pilot landed an airplane in an unimproved grassy meadow in mountainous terrain. The aircraft touched down with high ground speed, drifted left, struck a juniper tree, and ground looped, causing substantial right wing damage with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll with a quartering tailwind.
summary: The pilot landing a tailwheel airplane on Runway 08 encountered an unexpected tailwind despite calm automated reports. A gust lifted the right wing after touchdown, causing the aircraft to exit the runway, ground loop, and sustain substantial damage to the left wing and fuselage.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate fuel management which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel starvation.
summary: During a local flight, the pilot experienced total engine power loss after selecting the empty left fuel tank instead of the right. This error caused a forced landing in a grass field where the right wing struck trees, resulting in substantial damage to the aircraft.

synopsis: The pilot's improper recovery from a bounced landing, which resulted in a tail strike.
summary: A student pilot conducting a solo cross-country landing flared hard, causing a bounce. She continued the landing attempt with added power in a nose-low attitude, resulting in propeller and nose gear impact, a tail strike, and substantial rudder damage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll. Contributing to the accident was nose wheel misalignment at touchdown.
summary: During touch-and-go landings, a gyrocopter pilot reported the aircraft rolled over after the nose wheel contacted the runway, causing substantial damage to the empennage and main rotor. The pilot attributed the loss of control to potential nose wheel misalignment at touchdown, noting no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing rollout, which resulted in a ground loop.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane reported that a strong wind gust during landing rollout caused the aircraft to veer right and ground loop despite corrective inputs. The left wing contacted the ground, resulting in substantial damage, with no mechanical malfunctions reported.

synopsis: The biplane pilot's failure to maintain an adequate visual lookout while taxiing, which included the failure to perform S-turns to compensate for limited forward visibility. The biplane pilot's failure to maintain an adequate visual lookout while taxiing, which included the failure to perform S-turns to compensate for limited forward visibility.
summary: A tailwheel biplane pilot taxiing to a hangar collided with a single-engine low-wing airplane conducting a preflight run-up. The biplane pilot attributed the impact to poor forward visibility preventing S-turns, resulting in substantial damage to both aircraft with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain proper airspeed during takeoff and exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall and impact with terrain.
summary: The pilot reported a vibration and mushy controls during takeoff rotation, causing a left wing stall and loss of control. The pilot aborted the takeoff, leveled the wings, and impacted a ditch, resulting in substantial damage to the fuselage and wings with no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The tug drivers improper positioning of the airplane during pushback, which resulted in the airplane's jet blast impacting an active gate area during taxi and the subsequent injury to a maintenance technician. Contributing to the accident was the captain's decision to accept the tug driver's incorrect release location.
summary: During pushback at Washington Dulles, United Airlines Flight 1303 was positioned north of the taxiway centerline due to construction constraints. As the aircraft turned to align, jet blast displaced a ladder, causing a maintenance technician to fall and sustain serious injuries.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental Airshark N220AS was fatally injured when the aircraft struck a tree and crashed during a local flight near Statesboro, Georgia. The investigation found the left fuel tank screen was partially obstructed by solder and water was present in the gascolator, though no definitive cause was established.
summary: The pilot of an experimental Airshark N220AS was fatally injured when the aircraft struck a tree and crashed during a local flight near Statesboro, Georgia. The investigation found the left fuel tank screen was partially obstructed by solder and water was present in the gascolator, though no definitive cause was established.

synopsis: A private pilot operating a Lancair Legacy, N212LG, sustained substantial damage when the nose landing gear collapsed during deceleration on runway 31L. The pilot attributed the failure to a violent shimmy following touchdown, while flight data indicated a gear fault developed shortly after weight-on-wheels was detected.
summary: A private pilot operating a Lancair Legacy, N212LG, sustained substantial damage when the nose landing gear collapsed during deceleration on runway 31L. The pilot attributed the failure to a violent shimmy following touchdown, while flight data indicated a gear fault developed shortly after weight-on-wheels was detected.

synopsis: During a Part 91 aerial observation flight, a Robinson R44 II helicopter suffered an uncontrolled descent after a loud "pop" caused a loss of anti-torque pedal control and rapid clockwise rotation. The pilot and passenger were seriously injured, and the aircraft sustained substantial damage to the fuselage, main rotor, and tail systems.
summary: During a Part 91 aerial observation flight, a Robinson R44 II helicopter suffered an uncontrolled descent after a loud "pop" caused a loss of anti-torque pedal control and rapid clockwise rotation. The pilot and passenger were seriously injured, and the aircraft sustained substantial damage to the fuselage, main rotor, and tail systems.

synopsis: A pilot flying a Piper PA28-140 experienced total engine power loss during initial climb over the runway near Atlanta, Texas. The pilot landed straight ahead in a grassy area, where the aircraft struck a perimeter fence, causing substantial fuselage damage despite no fuel contamination being found.
summary: A pilot flying a Piper PA28-140 experienced total engine power loss during initial climb over the runway near Atlanta, Texas. The pilot landed straight ahead in a grassy area, where the aircraft struck a perimeter fence, causing substantial fuselage damage despite no fuel contamination being found.

synopsis: During a Part 135 sightseeing flight near Haena, Hawaii, a Hughes 369D helicopter experienced high-frequency vibration and uncommanded right yaw during a turn, causing it to rotate and impact the water. The accident resulted in substantial damage to the aircraft, three fatalities, and serious injuries to the pilot and one passenger.
summary: During a Part 135 sightseeing flight near Haena, Hawaii, a Hughes 369D helicopter experienced high-frequency vibration and uncommanded right yaw during a turn, causing it to rotate and impact the water. The accident resulted in substantial damage to the aircraft, three fatalities, and serious injuries to the pilot and one passenger.

synopsis: The airplane's encounter with turbulence resulted in serious injuries to a flight attendant who was not seated due to completion of arrival compliance checks.
summary: JetBlue flight 1245 encountered severe turbulence while descending into Palm Beach International Airport between 7,000 and 9,000 feet, injuring three flight attendants. The crew reported no weather radar returns or relevant advisories, yet one attendant suffered a fractured pelvis and vertebrae requiring hospitalization.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control during landing roll due to contact with wind hardened snow berm and subsequent failure of main landing gear.
summary: The pilot of a wheel ski-equipped airplane reported that after landing on a snow-covered lake, the right ski struck a wind-hardened snow berm, shearing the right main landing gear axle. This caused the ski to impact the right wing, resulting in substantial damage to the wing and fuselage.

synopsis: Maintenance personnel's failure to ensure that the throttle cable was properly secured to the carburetor, which resulted an inflight separation of the throttle cable and the pilots' inability to control the engine.
summary: Pilots lost engine power control during landing due to a missing cotter pin on the throttle cable, causing an off-airport landing with left wing damage. The failure resulted from mechanics forgetting to install the pin during recent maintenance and annual inspection.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control during the landing roll.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane in the traffic pattern landed on an opposite direction runway after a wind shift. During the flare, the aircraft veered left despite rudder inputs, struck trees, and sustained substantial wing damage with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna T206H sustained minor injuries when the aircraft struck trees after a soft-field takeoff from a turf runway. The accident occurred because the empennage dragged during the roll, causing the airplane to drift right and exit the runway before impacting obstacles.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna T206H sustained minor injuries when the aircraft struck trees after a soft-field takeoff from a turf runway. The accident occurred because the empennage dragged during the roll, causing the airplane to drift right and exit the runway before impacting obstacles.

synopsis: The pilot's excessive application of brakes, which resulted in the airplane tipping forward onto its nose.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane tipped the aircraft forward onto its nose during the landing roll on a narrow runway after applying additional braking due to insufficient stopping distance. The left wing subsequently struck the ground, sustaining substantial damage, with no preaccident mechanical failures reported.

aircraft: Paul D Cannon Kitfox Light Squared
synopsis: The pilot's failure to properly flare the airplane during landing, which resulted in a hard landing and separation of the main landing gear. Contributing to the accident was the improper installation and over torquing of the landing gear attachment hardware, which reduced the load-carrying capacity of the landing gear clamping brackets.
summary: The pilot of an amateur-built airplane experienced a hard landing during touch-and-go operations due to improper flare, causing main landing gear separation and a runway excursion. Post-accident examination revealed the aftermarket gear was improperly installed with overtorqued bolts, which reduced load capacity and allowed the attachment to fail under stress.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate clearance from a jet blast fence during taxi.
summary: While taxiing to the run-up area, the pilot focused on right wing clearance and failed to monitor the left wingtip, causing it to strike a jet blast fence. This resulted in substantial damage to the left wing, with no pre-accident mechanical malfunctions reported.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna 421B reported that despite green landing gear lights, the aircraft yawed right and exited the runway during landing at Sedona, Arizona. All three landing gear legs collapsed, causing substantial damage to the wing, stabilizer, and fuselage, though the pilot and passenger were uninjured.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna 421B reported that despite green landing gear lights, the aircraft yawed right and exited the runway during landing at Sedona, Arizona. All three landing gear legs collapsed, causing substantial damage to the wing, stabilizer, and fuselage, though the pilot and passenger were uninjured.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing with a quartering headwind. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's runway selection based on the variable and gusting wind conditions.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane landing on runway 36 in gusting crosswinds lost directional control after touchdown, causing the left wingtip to strike the ground and the aircraft to exit the runway. The left main gear separated and the airframe sustained substantial damage, with the pilot attributing the accident to not selecting the more favorably aligned turf runway.

synopsis: An unanticipated encounter with clear air turbulence while in cruise flight.
summary: United Airlines flight 115 encountered moderate clear air turbulence at FL300 while en route to Tahiti, causing two flight attendants to fall and one to sustain a serious injury. The event occurred after crossing an unknown subtropical jet stream, with no weather radar returns or active advisories indicating the hazard.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control of the airplane during takeoff in gusty wind conditions, which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: The pilot departed in gusty crosswinds, deviated from the flight path, and landed on an adjacent grass runway where the left main gear collapsed, causing substantial wing and fuselage damage. The pilot attributed the accident to wind conditions and a lack of conservative personal minimums, noting no mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the takeoff in gusting wind conditions.
summary: During a touch-and-go on runway 26, a gyroplane drifted left despite pilot corrections and tipped over upon rotation attempt, causing substantial mast and empennage damage. The pilot reported no mechanical failures, noting 10-knot winds gusting to 19 knots at the time.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from terrain during the hover taxi.
summary: A helicopter pilot drifted off a taxiway and impacted the ground while distracted by entering a transponder code during a hover taxi. The accident caused damage to the tail rotor, stabilizer, and skids, with the pilot attributing the cause to the distraction rather than mechanical failure.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the hover taxi with a quartering tailwind.
summary: While hover taxiing north in an 18-knot quartering tailwind, the pilot reported the helicopter spun and touched down hard after a power reduction attempt. The hard landing collapsed the left skid and grounded the main rotor blades, causing substantial damage with no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane during an aborted landing, which resulted in a runway excursion, collision with a fence, and a hard landing .
summary: The pilot overflew the destination airport and entered the traffic pattern, but bounced on short final due to a late flare. He added power too quickly without right rudder, causing a violent left turn that led to a fence impact and substantial damage to the wings and fuselage.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to land on an unsuitable snow-covered runway and his failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll which resulted in a nose over.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane nosed over during the landing roll on a snow-covered runway when the main wheels encountered soft snow. This resulted in substantial damage to the rudder, wings, wing struts, and fuselage, with no pre-accident mechanical malfunctions reported.

synopsis: A pilot flying a Cessna 150G for personal training sustained serious injuries when the aircraft impacted the ground near Ellicott, Colorado, shortly after takeoff. The pilot lost consciousness during an uncommanded left bank, causing the plane to crash 500 feet left of the runway centerline with substantial damage to the airframe.
summary: A pilot flying a Cessna 150G for personal training sustained serious injuries when the aircraft impacted the ground near Ellicott, Colorado, shortly after takeoff. The pilot lost consciousness during an uncommanded left bank, causing the plane to crash 500 feet left of the runway centerline with substantial damage to the airframe.

synopsis: An in-flight collision with a bird during cruise flight.
summary: The pilot reported a loud bang and right wing leading edge damage at 1,800 ft during cruise, prompting a safe return to the departure airport. Post-accident examination confirmed the damage was consistent with a bird strike.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control of the airplane during landing in gusty wind conditions.
summary: The pilot landing on runway 15 encountered a wind gust during flare that raised the left wing. Despite corrective inputs, the right wing struck the runway, causing loss of control, runway departure into a ditch, and substantial damage with no mechanical failure reported.

synopsis: A flight instructor and student pilot in a Piper PA-28-181 suffered substantial damage after an engine power loss during descent near Philadelphia. The student pilot lost engine response at 1,400 feet, leading to an emergency landing where the aircraft struck a tree, with post-accident testing revealing external leakage from the fuel selector.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot in a Piper PA-28-181 suffered substantial damage after an engine power loss during descent near Philadelphia. The student pilot lost engine response at 1,400 feet, leading to an emergency landing where the aircraft struck a tree, with post-accident testing revealing external leakage from the fuel selector.

synopsis: The airplane's encounter with uneven terrain during takeoff, which resulted in a runway excursion and impact with water.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot lost control during a soft-field takeoff on a turf runway when the left main gear likely struck uneven ground caused by ant hills and mole tunnels. The aircraft veered left, exited the runway, struck adjacent water, and sustained substantial elevator damage.

synopsis: An in-flight collision with a bird while enroute.
summary: During the enroute phase, the pilot descended to 1,000 ft for departing traffic when a bird struck the left windshield and roof, causing substantial damage. The pilot declared an emergency and landed uneventfully at a nearby airport.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during a gusting crosswind landing, and the flight instructor's delayed remedial action.
summary: A student pilot and flight instructor lost directional control during a landing roll on runway 36 in gusty crosswinds, causing the aircraft to veer right. The instructor attempted to avoid a runway light, but the left wingtip struck the ground, resulting in the airplane overturning with substantial damage.

synopsis: During a touch-and-go takeoff in a Cessna 172M, the pilot reported an uncontrollable pitch-up caused by flaps being left down. Despite emergency maneuvers, the aircraft bounced on landing, impacted a berm, and nosed over inverted, sustaining substantial damage while occupants remained uninjured.
summary: During a touch-and-go takeoff in a Cessna 172M, the pilot reported an uncontrollable pitch-up caused by flaps being left down. Despite emergency maneuvers, the aircraft bounced on landing, impacted a berm, and nosed over inverted, sustaining substantial damage while occupants remained uninjured.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate clearance from the terrain while performing a low-altitude circling takeoff maneuver, which resulted in a dynamic rollover.
summary: A pilot and passenger practicing off-airport landings in a helicopter experienced a dynamic rollover during a low-altitude circling takeoff intended to gain translational lift. The left skid contacted the terrain as the aircraft accelerated, causing substantial damage to the fuselage and rotor systems with no reported mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: The airplane's encounter with unexpected low-level wind shear during final approach, which resulted in a hard impact with the runway.
summary: A pilot and flight instructor conducting an instrument proficiency check experienced a hard landing and gear failure during a simulated engine-out approach, likely caused by low-level wind shear. The aircraft subsequently departed the runway, sustaining substantial fuselage damage after the right wing impacted the ground.

synopsis: An in-flight collision with a bird while descending to land at an airport.
summary: A flight instructor and student experienced a bird strike on the left wing leading edge while descending through 1,400 feet MSL. The student landed safely, but a post-accident examination revealed substantial damage to the left wing.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain directional control while landing, which resulted in a runway excursion and nose over.
summary: A solo student pilot reported that during the landing roll, the aircraft pulled left, and he allowed it to veer into a wet ravine to avoid abrupt rudder input. The nosewheel stuck in mud, causing the airplane to nose over and come to rest inverted with substantial damage to the left wing and vertical stabilizer.

synopsis: The pilot of a Sonex-A, N106D, experienced rising exhaust gas temperatures and partial power loss at 2,500 feet shortly after takeoff from Eastern WV Regional Airport. Unable to return, he made an emergency field landing, overran the field, and struck fences, causing substantial fuselage damage while both occupants remained uninjured.
summary: The pilot of a Sonex-A, N106D, experienced rising exhaust gas temperatures and partial power loss at 2,500 feet shortly after takeoff from Eastern WV Regional Airport. Unable to return, he made an emergency field landing, overran the field, and struck fences, causing substantial fuselage damage while both occupants remained uninjured.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper PA-31T1 landed on Runway 6 at Ocean City Municipal Airport relying on AWOS calm wind reports, but encountered an unreported 15-knot tailwind. Ineffective braking caused the aircraft to overrun the runway, collapse the right main gear, and spin 180 degrees, resulting in substantial damage with no injuries.
summary: The pilot of a Piper PA-31T1 landed on Runway 6 at Ocean City Municipal Airport relying on AWOS calm wind reports, but encountered an unreported 15-knot tailwind. Ineffective braking caused the aircraft to overrun the runway, collapse the right main gear, and spin 180 degrees, resulting in substantial damage with no injuries.

synopsis: The failure of the landing gear weldment that resulted in separation of the right main landing gear.
summary: A student pilot and flight instructor experienced a right main landing gear separation during rollout after a normal landing. The gear weldment fractured due to undetected prior damage, corrosion, and overstress, causing the aircraft to land in the grass and sustain substantial damage.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a bounced landing and a subsequent runway excursion.
summary: The pilot of a locally purchased airplane in the traffic pattern bounced during a hard landing and aborted a go-around due to insufficient clearance over trees. The aircraft overran the runway and struck brush, causing substantial wing damage, which the pilot attributed to an incorrect flap configuration.

synopsis: The pilot of a Lancair IV, N94PT, conducted a personal flight from PVG to ONX when the engine suffered a complete power loss due to throttle creep and rough running. The pilot executed a forced landing on Scotland Road with gear retracted, causing substantial damage to the fuselage, exhaust, and propeller, though both occupants were uninjured.
summary: The pilot of a Lancair IV, N94PT, conducted a personal flight from PVG to ONX when the engine suffered a complete power loss due to throttle creep and rough running. The pilot executed a forced landing on Scotland Road with gear retracted, causing substantial damage to the fuselage, exhaust, and propeller, though both occupants were uninjured.

synopsis: The flight crew's failure to ensure that the rear cargo door was properly latched before flight.
summary: A flight instructor and student in a Cessna 206 experienced an in-flight opening of the aft cargo door due to a lower latch that appeared latched but failed to engage the fuselage plate. The aircraft sustained substantial fuselage damage but completed an uneventful no-flap landing.

synopsis: A pilot and passenger sustained minor injuries when a Cessna T-41B veered left during takeoff roll near Fort Mohave, Arizona, due to a loss of directional control at approximately 30 mph. The aircraft exited the runway, crossed a berm, and impacted a garage wall, sustaining substantial damage to the wings and forward fuselage.
summary: A pilot and passenger sustained minor injuries when a Cessna T-41B veered left during takeoff roll near Fort Mohave, Arizona, due to a loss of directional control at approximately 30 mph. The aircraft exited the runway, crossed a berm, and impacted a garage wall, sustaining substantial damage to the wings and forward fuselage.

synopsis: During a Part 91 instructional flight in a Cessna 150G near Phoenix, the engine failed to respond after a power-off stall maneuver at 4,000 feet. The flight instructor executed a forced landing on uneven terrain, causing the aircraft to nose over and sustain substantial damage, though both occupants were uninjured.
summary: During a Part 91 instructional flight in a Cessna 150G near Phoenix, the engine failed to respond after a power-off stall maneuver at 4,000 feet. The flight instructor executed a forced landing on uneven terrain, causing the aircraft to nose over and sustain substantial damage, though both occupants were uninjured.

synopsis: A pilot and passenger were killed when their Piper PA-32R-301T crashed after overshooting the final approach at Marana Regional Airport. The aircraft bounced on touchdown, failed to stop on the remaining runway, and impacted a concrete drainage culvert, resulting in substantial damage and a post-crash fire.
summary: A pilot and passenger were killed when their Piper PA-32R-301T crashed after overshooting the final approach at Marana Regional Airport. The aircraft bounced on touchdown, failed to stop on the remaining runway, and impacted a concrete drainage culvert, resulting in substantial damage and a post-crash fire.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental Just Aircraft Highlander N563JA lost total engine power during a steep approach to a private grass airstrip near Great Falls, Montana. The aircraft overshot the landing zone, nosed over, and was substantially damaged after the pilot applied full aft stick and brakes.
summary: The pilot of an experimental Just Aircraft Highlander N563JA lost total engine power during a steep approach to a private grass airstrip near Great Falls, Montana. The aircraft overshot the landing zone, nosed over, and was substantially damaged after the pilot applied full aft stick and brakes.

synopsis: A pilot and pilot-rated passenger were fatally injured when their Sling 2, N166TW, impacted terrain near Avalon, California, during a personal flight to Santa Catalina Island. The aircraft was flying less than 100 feet above ground in a canyon before the crash, with the ballistic parachute undeployed and flaps fully retracted.
summary: A pilot and pilot-rated passenger were fatally injured when their Sling 2, N166TW, impacted terrain near Avalon, California, during a personal flight to Santa Catalina Island. The aircraft was flying less than 100 feet above ground in a canyon before the crash, with the ballistic parachute undeployed and flaps fully retracted.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control while maneuvering onto the runway for takeoff. Contributing to the accident was the presence of heavy, wet snow adjacent to the runway.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane lost directional control while applying power during a turn onto the runway, causing the aircraft to depart the surface and nose over in heavy, wet snow. This resulted in substantial damage to the left wing lift strut, with no preaccident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot of a Republic RC-3 experienced an engine power loss and propeller overspeed at 2,500 feet due to a separated exhaust tail pipe. He executed a gear-up forced landing on a road, causing substantial damage to the fuselage and left wing after striking a water valve.
summary: The pilot of a Republic RC-3 experienced an engine power loss and propeller overspeed at 2,500 feet due to a separated exhaust tail pipe. He executed a gear-up forced landing on a road, causing substantial damage to the fuselage and left wing after striking a water valve.

synopsis: During a Part 91 instructional flight in an L-39, the engine lost thrust at 8,500 feet while configuring for landing. The crew executed a forced gear-up landing in a field after relight attempts failed, resulting in substantial damage to the fuselage and wings.
summary: During a Part 91 instructional flight in an L-39, the engine lost thrust at 8,500 feet while configuring for landing. The crew executed a forced gear-up landing in a field after relight attempts failed, resulting in substantial damage to the fuselage and wings.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane during the landing rollout, which resulted in a nose-over.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane lost control during a second landing attempt, causing the aircraft to nose over and come to rest inverted. The pilot reported no pre-accident mechanical failures, and the airplane sustained substantial damage to the rudder assembly and both wing struts.

synopsis: Two pilots operating a Cessna T182 for a pre-purchase inspection exited the runway during landing due to nosewheel shimmy caused by a loose bearing. The aircraft struck an adjacent ditch, sustaining substantial damage to both wings, though both pilots remained uninjured.
summary: Two pilots operating a Cessna T182 for a pre-purchase inspection exited the runway during landing due to nosewheel shimmy caused by a loose bearing. The aircraft struck an adjacent ditch, sustaining substantial damage to both wings, though both pilots remained uninjured.

aircraft: Alexander Schleicher Gmbh & Co ASH 31 MI
synopsis: The pilot of an experimental Alexander Schleicher ASH 31 Mi motorglider, N77UK, sustained minor injuries when the engine lost power at 200 feet AGL during climbout. While attempting a right turn back to the runway to avoid power lines, the right wingtip struck terrain, causing substantial damage to the fuselage and wings.
summary: The pilot of an experimental Alexander Schleicher ASH 31 Mi motorglider, N77UK, sustained minor injuries when the engine lost power at 200 feet AGL during climbout. While attempting a right turn back to the runway to avoid power lines, the right wingtip struck terrain, causing substantial damage to the fuselage and wings.

synopsis: A flight instructor and commercial pilot were fatally injured when their Beechcraft 58 crashed near New Market, Tennessee, during an instrument competency check. ADS-B data and witness reports indicated the aircraft entered a steep descent with erratic engine power before impacting the ground in a nose-down attitude.
summary: A flight instructor and commercial pilot were fatally injured when their Beechcraft 58 crashed near New Market, Tennessee, during an instrument competency check. ADS-B data and witness reports indicated the aircraft entered a steep descent with erratic engine power before impacting the ground in a nose-down attitude.

synopsis: A Cessna 172S and a King Air B200 collided near Marathon, Florida, while the King Air descended from 11,000 ft and the Cessna operated at 5,500 ft. The King Air's left engine and wing struck the Cessna's left wing, causing substantial damage to the Cessna and minor damage to the King Air, though all six occupants were uninjured.
summary: A Cessna 172S and a King Air B200 collided near Marathon, Florida, while the King Air descended from 11,000 ft and the Cessna operated at 5,500 ft. The King Air's left engine and wing struck the Cessna's left wing, causing substantial damage to the Cessna and minor damage to the King Air, though all six occupants were uninjured.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper J3C-65 lost all engine power at 200 ft agl during a climb after a low approach. While attempting to avoid power lines and trees, the right wing struck a tree, causing the aircraft to impact the ground with substantial damage and injuring both occupants.
summary: The pilot of a Piper J3C-65 lost all engine power at 200 ft agl during a climb after a low approach. While attempting to avoid power lines and trees, the right wing struck a tree, causing the aircraft to impact the ground with substantial damage and injuring both occupants.

synopsis: A flight instructor and student pilot were seriously injured when their Piper Cherokee PA-28-180 struck power lines and impacted a road during a touch-and-go practice at Corpus Christi International Airport. The accident occurred on short final for runway 13 after an engine issue, resulting in a postimpact fire.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot were seriously injured when their Piper Cherokee PA-28-180 struck power lines and impacted a road during a touch-and-go practice at Corpus Christi International Airport. The accident occurred on short final for runway 13 after an engine issue, resulting in a postimpact fire.

synopsis: The front and back seat pilots of an experimental SW-51 sustained minor and serious injuries, respectively, after the aircraft sustained minor damage during a local flight. The accident occurred shortly after takeoff from Lincoln County Regional Airport when the slip/skid indicator showed erratic movement, prompting an off-field landing.
summary: The front and back seat pilots of an experimental SW-51 sustained minor and serious injuries, respectively, after the aircraft sustained minor damage during a local flight. The accident occurred shortly after takeoff from Lincoln County Regional Airport when the slip/skid indicator showed erratic movement, prompting an off-field landing.

synopsis: The pilot's improper recovery from a practice autorotation, which resulted in a hard landing. Contributing to the accident was the flight instructor's inadequate supervision of the pilot receiving the instruction.
summary: A pilot and flight instructor conducting a night vision goggle training flight experienced a hard landing during an autorotation maneuver. The pilot applied collective too early, causing rotor RPM decay and substantial damage to the tailboom and vertical stabilizers, with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate fuel planning, which resulted in fuel exhaustion and a total loss of engine power.
summary: The pilot of a single-engine airplane experienced total engine power loss due to fuel exhaustion after deviating from the planned altitude and course, which increased fuel consumption and flight duration. This resulted in a forced landing on a road that caused substantial damage to the fuselage and wings.

synopsis: The pilot of a DeHavilland DHC-3 amphibious aircraft nosed over into the water during a water takeoff attempt near Dry Tortugas, Florida, after the airplane failed to lift off and yawed right. The accident caused substantial damage to the right wing, and the investigation found the elevator trim was set to full nose-down with no other mechanical failures.
summary: The pilot of a DeHavilland DHC-3 amphibious aircraft nosed over into the water during a water takeoff attempt near Dry Tortugas, Florida, after the airplane failed to lift off and yawed right. The accident caused substantial damage to the right wing, and the investigation found the elevator trim was set to full nose-down with no other mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilots' inadequate preflight fuel planning and improper in-flight fuel management, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion and subsequent forced landing to a field.
summary: Two commercial pilots conducting a night cross-country flight experienced an engine power loss due to fuel exhaustion after relying on a faulty fuel gauge that read 2.5 to 3 gallons high. The right-seat pilot executed a forced landing in a field, causing substantial fuselage damage, while post-accident inspection confirmed no mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's inadvertent retraction of the landing gear lever during the landing roll, which resulted in a gear collapse and runway excursion.
summary: During the landing roll, the pilot inadvertently retracted the landing gear while attempting to retract flaps, causing the gear to collapse. The aircraft slid off the runway into a drainage ditch, sustaining substantial left wing damage, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

aircraft: Diamond Aircraft Ind Gmbh DA 42 NG
synopsis: Maintenance personnel's installation of an oversized tire, which prevented the left main landing gear from extending resulting in a precautionary gear up landing.
summary: During approach, the pilot reported the left main landing gear failed to extend due to oversized tires installed by maintenance two days prior, which wedged the gear in the wheel well. The pilot performed a gear-up landing, resulting in substantial damage to both engine mounts.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a hard, porpoised landing.
summary: A student pilot reported that during landing, a light wind gust caused the airplane to balloon, touch down hard, and porpoise, resulting in substantial fuselage damage. The pilot stated there were no preaccident mechanical malfunctions or failures.

synopsis: An oil line separation at a barbed fitting in an experimental airplane, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to oil starvation.
summary: During approach, an amphibious airplane suffered total engine power loss due to a separated oil line, forcing a hard water landing that damaged the left wing and empennage. Investigators suspect a missing clamp on the oil line, possibly installed incorrectly during an engine upgrade one year prior, caused the separation.

synopsis: A private pilot was fatally injured when his Rajchl Vladimir Swing 06 crashed near O'Brien, Florida, shortly after departing for a traffic pattern. The aircraft pitched nose down and impacted terrain following a popping noise, with post-accident examination revealing all three propeller blades separated from the hub.
summary: A private pilot was fatally injured when his Rajchl Vladimir Swing 06 crashed near O'Brien, Florida, shortly after departing for a traffic pattern. The aircraft pitched nose down and impacted terrain following a popping noise, with post-accident examination revealing all three propeller blades separated from the hub.

synopsis: The airplane's encounter with turbulence during descent resulting in a serious injury to a flight attendant.
summary: Southwest flight 2392 encountered unexpected moderate turbulence at 14,000 ft during descent to Boston, injuring four flight attendants while they prepared the cabin. The crew noted no weather radar returns or SkyPath reports, though a SIGMET existed 75 miles away, and the aircraft landed safely with medical assistance.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of control during takeoff, due to the seat sliding aft.
summary: The pilot reported that during the takeoff roll, the crew seat slid aft despite preflight checks, causing the aircraft to pitch up, yaw left, and impact terrain with substantial wing damage. Investigation found no mechanical failure, but noted the pilot may not have locked the seat or that the uninstalled secondary latch service bulletin contributed to the incident.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain situational awareness while taxiing which resulted in a collision with fence poles on either side of a gate which was not intended for airplanes.
summary: A student pilot taxiing behind another aircraft left the taxiway, crossed hangars, and struck a narrow vehicle gate with both wings, causing substantial damage. The pilot attributed the incident to forgetting the aircraft had wings, with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain proper main rotor rpm during a low-level turn, which resulted in the main rotor rpm drooping, a loss of control at an altitude too low for recovery, and a subsequent impact with terrain.
summary: During a low-level aerial hunting flight in a Robinson helicopter, the pilot experienced a simultaneous decrease in engine and main rotor RPM while maneuvering at 75 ft AGL. The pilot executed a forced landing into a canyon, resulting in substantial damage to the airframe, though no pre-impact mechanical failure was reported.

synopsis: A pilot operating a Mooney M20J Part 91 flight was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed near Ironton, Ohio, shortly after takeoff from Ashland Regional Airport. The accident occurred after the airplane descended to 500 feet MSL and pitched up before impacting a field, resulting in extensive post-crash fire damage.
summary: A pilot operating a Mooney M20J Part 91 flight was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed near Ironton, Ohio, shortly after takeoff from Ashland Regional Airport. The accident occurred after the airplane descended to 500 feet MSL and pitched up before impacting a field, resulting in extensive post-crash fire damage.

synopsis: The pilot and three passengers were fatally injured when a Mooney M20J crashed shortly after takeoff from Union County Airport. The aircraft banked right, rolled left, and descended into wooded terrain at approximately 200 feet above ground level, resulting in a post-impact fire that destroyed the airplane.
summary: The pilot and three passengers were fatally injured when a Mooney M20J crashed shortly after takeoff from Union County Airport. The aircraft banked right, rolled left, and descended into wooded terrain at approximately 200 feet above ground level, resulting in a post-impact fire that destroyed the airplane.

synopsis: A commercial pilot was fatally injured when a Cessna 401B crashed near Land O' Lakes, Florida, shortly after takeoff from runway 32. The aircraft climbed to 200 feet AGL before dropping out of the sky, resulting in a post-impact fire that destroyed the fuselage and rendered instrument data unreliable.
summary: A commercial pilot was fatally injured when a Cessna 401B crashed near Land O' Lakes, Florida, shortly after takeoff from runway 32.
