The aircraft climbed to 200 feet AGL before dropping out of the sky, resulting in a post-impact fire that destroyed the fuselage and rendered instrument data unreliable.

synopsis: The pilot's inability to maintain climb performance and clearance from terrain due to the airplane's encounter with windshear during takeoff.
summary: The pilot attempted to depart a remote 2,040 ft airstrip but encountered windshear during initial climb, causing a decreasing vertical speed. Unable to clear terrain, the pilot executed a forced landing in sagebrush, resulting in the aircraft nosing over inverted with substantial damage to the wings and fuselage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane while landing on a wet runway with a tailwind.
summary: A pilot flying VFR with flight following descended below clouds and landed at an incorrect airport 29 miles north of his destination. After a go-around, the aircraft overran the wet runway in gusty winds, striking a fence and sustaining damage to the fuselage, engine, and wing.

synopsis: A private pilot flying a Piper PA-28-181 instructional flight experienced sudden engine power loss at 3,500 feet MSL, likely due to fuel exhaustion despite reporting 40 gallons. The pilot attempted a forced landing in a marsh, resulting in substantial damage when the aircraft nosed over and inverted.
summary: A private pilot flying a Piper PA-28-181 instructional flight experienced sudden engine power loss at 3,500 feet MSL, likely due to fuel exhaustion despite reporting 40 gallons. The pilot attempted a forced landing in a marsh, resulting in substantial damage when the aircraft nosed over and inverted.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power for reasons that could not be determined because the airplane was not recovered from the ocean.
summary: The pilot reported an enroute total engine power loss at 1,300 feet MSL over water, forcing a ditching two miles from shore. The aircraft sank after remaining upright for two minutes, and the cause of the power loss remains undetermined as the airplane was not recovered.

synopsis: During a Part 91 instructional flight in a Cirrus SR22, the engine lost total power at 500 feet AGL while turning left. The flight instructor deployed the CAPS, resulting in a substantial damage landing in a residential area after the engine failed to produce maximum power despite full throttle and mixture settings.
summary: During a Part 91 instructional flight in a Cirrus SR22, the engine lost total power at 500 feet AGL while turning left. The flight instructor deployed the CAPS, resulting in a substantial damage landing in a residential area after the engine failed to produce maximum power despite full throttle and mixture settings.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper PA-30 Twin Comanche experienced decreasing engine RPMs during descent, likely due to fuel tank selection issues, forcing a diversion to Auburn. The aircraft impacted a soil mound during a forced landing in a dirt field, sustaining substantial damage and causing minor injuries to the pilot and passenger.
summary: The pilot of a Piper PA-30 Twin Comanche experienced decreasing engine RPMs during descent, likely due to fuel tank selection issues, forcing a diversion to Auburn. The aircraft impacted a soil mound during a forced landing in a dirt field, sustaining substantial damage and causing minor injuries to the pilot and passenger.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna 172S operating under Part 91 near Whiteman Airport was seriously injured when the aircraft impacted powerlines and terrain short of Runway 12. ADS-B data showed the airplane descended to 1,000 feet and slowed to 55 knots before losing contact 0.4 nautical miles from the threshold.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna 172S operating under Part 91 near Whiteman Airport was seriously injured when the aircraft impacted powerlines and terrain short of Runway 12. ADS-B data showed the airplane descended to 1,000 feet and slowed to 55 knots before losing contact 0.4 nautical miles from the threshold.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing roll. Contributing to the accident was the rotor wash from a nearby helicopter.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane veered off runway 16 during landing, likely due to helicopter rotor wash, and subsequently nosed over while braking to avoid a fuel island. This resulted in substantial damage to the wings and rudder, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

aircraft: Aeroprakt Mfg Sp Z O O A32
synopsis: The flight instructor's improper in-flight fuel management, which resulted in fuel starvation, a total loss of engine power, and a forced landing to rough terrain.
summary: A flight instructor conducting practice maneuvers experienced an engine power loss after incorrectly isolating fuel tanks, violating Pilot Operating Handbook procedures. The resulting forced landing in a rough field caused substantial left wing damage due to fuel starvation.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to extend the landing gear before landing.
summary: During a touch-and-go landing in a busy traffic pattern, the pilot forgot to extend the landing gear due to distraction by slower traffic. The aircraft skidded on the runway with gear retracted and exited into grass, causing substantial fuselage damage, while the gear warning horn remained inaudible due to headset noise cancellation and wiring issues.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airplane control during recovery from a bounced landing.
summary: During landing, the pilot reported the airplane dropped and bounced at idle power, then veered left after applying full power, impacting terrain off the runway. This caused substantial damage to the wings and fuselage, with no preaccident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna 421C reported an asymmetric power condition during takeoff from Richmond International Airport, causing the aircraft to veer right despite rudder input. After reducing throttles, the plane departed the runway and struck a sign with the left wing, resulting in substantial damage but no injuries.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna 421C reported an asymmetric power condition during takeoff from Richmond International Airport, causing the aircraft to veer right despite rudder input. After reducing throttles, the plane departed the runway and struck a sign with the left wing, resulting in substantial damage but no injuries.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed during the flare which resulted in the airplane exceeding its critical angle of attack and aerodynamic stall at a low altitude and loss of airplane control.
summary: A student pilot practicing solo touch-and-go landings stalled on short final when the stall horn sounded. The aircraft drifted right, landed off the runway on sloping terrain, and sustained substantial wing damage with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll in gusting wind conditions, which resulted in a ground loop.
summary: The pilot reported that during a touch-and-go landing on a gravel bar in a tailwheel airplane, a strong gust lifted the left wing, causing the aircraft to roll left and rest inverted. Substantial damage occurred to the left wing, rudder, and wings, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot of a Maule M-7-235 reported a perceived engine power loss shortly after rotation during a personal takeoff near Wasilla, Alaska. Unable to reject the takeoff, the pilot selected one notch of flaps to clear obstacles, but the aircraft impacted trees 1,500 feet down the runway, sustaining substantial damage.
summary: The pilot of a Maule M-7-235 reported a perceived engine power loss shortly after rotation during a personal takeoff near Wasilla, Alaska. Unable to reject the takeoff, the pilot selected one notch of flaps to clear obstacles, but the aircraft impacted trees 1,500 feet down the runway, sustaining substantial damage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control of the airplane during the aborted landing, which resulted in a runway excursion, collision with a runway sign, and nose over.
summary: During landing, the pilot flared high, bounced, and aborted with full power, causing the aircraft to veer left, exit the runway, hit a sign, and nose over. The pilot reported no pre-accident mechanical failures, resulting in substantial damage to the wings, fuselage, and empennage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane during the landing, which resulted in a runway excursion and collision with taxiway sign.
summary: The pilot executed an unstable, high-speed approach and floated before losing directional control during the landing roll, causing the aircraft to depart the runway and strike a taxiway sign. The pilot attributed the incident to continuing the unstable approach instead of performing a go-around, noting no mechanical failures.

synopsis: The flight instructor's failure to maintain airplane control during a takeoff attempt, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall, runway excursion, and on-ground collision with an object. Contributing to the accident was the flight instructor's decision to continue the takeoff on a closed, unsuitable runway.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot conducting soft field takeoff training on a closed turf runway at Dupont/Lapeer Airport experienced reduced acceleration and two aerodynamic stalls. The instructor aborted the takeoff after the aircraft overran the runway, struck an object in a parking lot, and sustained substantial right wing damage.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna 185 reported that the left wheel/ski assembly separated from the main landing gear leg during takeoff from a snow-covered site. The aircraft overturned and sustained substantial damage after the exposed gear leg struck the runway during an emergency landing at Aniak Airport.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna 185 reported that the left wheel/ski assembly separated from the main landing gear leg during takeoff from a snow-covered site. The aircraft overturned and sustained substantial damage after the exposed gear leg struck the runway during an emergency landing at Aniak Airport.

synopsis: A pilot and passenger were fatally injured when their Beechcraft F33A crashed shortly after departing runway 32 at Crystal Airport with landing gear down. The aircraft turned left, descended behind trees, and impacted the ground nose-down, resulting in a postimpact fire.
summary: A pilot and passenger were fatally injured when their Beechcraft F33A crashed shortly after departing runway 32 at Crystal Airport with landing gear down. The aircraft turned left, descended behind trees, and impacted the ground nose-down, resulting in a postimpact fire.

synopsis: The pilot receiving instruction's failure to maintain aircraft directional control during the takeoff roll. Contributing was the flight crew's failure to ensure a positive exchange of flight controls during the takeoff roll.
summary: During a training takeoff, a student pilot overcorrected rudder inputs, causing the aircraft to veer off the runway and strike the precision approach path indicator. The flight instructor reported no mechanical failures, but the incident resulted in substantial damage to the right horizontal stabilizer and landing gear separation.

synopsis: Fracture of the left main landing gear trunnion during landing, which resulted in a loss of directional control during landing and subsequent runway excursion.
summary: The pilot reported that during landing, the aircraft made an uncontrolled right turn after touchdown, veering off the runway and impacting trees despite corrective inputs. Post-accident examination found a bent right main gear axle and a cracked left main gear trunnion consistent with overstress separation, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate preflight and inflight fuel planning, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel starvation and subsequent forced landing into trees.
summary: The pilot of a multiengine airplane conducting a proficiency flight experienced total power loss in both engines during the traffic pattern due to fuel exhaustion from miscalculating consumption. The aircraft impacted trees short of the runway, sustaining substantial damage, with no preimpact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: A pilot and passenger in a Cirrus SR22T suffered minor injuries after an engine failure en route to Sikeston, Missouri, forced an emergency parachute deployment. The aircraft was substantially damaged when the parachute dragged it through fences and a truck, causing the engine and empennage to separate before it came to rest.
summary: A pilot and passenger in a Cirrus SR22T suffered minor injuries after an engine failure en route to Sikeston, Missouri, forced an emergency parachute deployment. The aircraft was substantially damaged when the parachute dragged it through fences and a truck, causing the engine and empennage to separate before it came to rest.

aircraft: Czech Sport Aircraft As PIPER SPORT
synopsis: The pilot's failure to correctly identify the runway, which resulted in a landing on a residential driveway and collision with a gate.
summary: An enroute pilot became ill and, after being vectored by ATC, mistakenly landed on a residential driveway instead of the intended airport. The aircraft struck a gate extension, causing substantial right wing damage, with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of of directional control during landing roll following an encounter with a dust devil.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane experienced a violent right wing lift and ground loop during the landing roll on runway 16 due to a dust element. Despite initiating a go-around, the left wing impacted the ground, causing substantial damage with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: A loss of electrical power as a result of broken stator leads within the alternator, which resulted in the pilot's inability to extend the airplane's landing gear.
summary: The pilot experienced an alternator failure causing total electrical loss while in the traffic pattern, preventing full landing gear extension via the hand crank. The nose gear collapsed on landing, sustaining substantial fuselage damage due to the unsecured gear.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain airplane control while landing in gusting crosswind conditions.
summary: A student pilot soloing in the traffic pattern exited the runway during landing on Runway 24 when gusty winds from 300° at 16 knots lifted the right wing. The pilot's correction attempt caused the left wing to strike the ground, resulting in substantial damage to the wing and aileron with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's delayed decision to deflate the balloon during a static display in windy conditions, which resulted in a loss of control and impact with a building. Contributing to the accident was the proximity of the balloon from structures during a static display.
summary: The pilot of a balloon secured for a static display reported that wind shifts caused tether line failures, allowing the balloon to drift toward and collide with a building and trees. The pilot applied burner to clear the structure, but the balloon subsequently impacted powerlines during the approach to a field.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to extend the landing gear before landing due to distraction and his failure to conduct the before landing checklist.
summary: The pilot became distracted by traffic and runway length during the approach, failing to complete the checklist or extend the landing gear. The gear warning horn did not sound due to high engine RPM, resulting in a gear-up landing that caused substantial lower fuselage damage.

synopsis: The in-flight separation of a turn lock fastener stud, which resulted in substantial damage to one tail rotor blade.
summary: The pilot reported that a missing turn lock fastener stud on the tail rotor driveshaft cover likely separated in-flight and damaged a tail rotor blade. The fastener was not found, and the helicopter had been inspected 77 flight hours prior to the incident.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from a tree stump during landing in mountainous terrain.
summary: During a personal flight in mountainous terrain, a helicopter pilot struck a tree stump with the tail rotor and vertical stabilizer while landing. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to those components but came to rest upright with no preimpact mechanical failures.

synopsis: A private pilot flying a Cessna 421C reported pitot tube icing and inoperative pitot heat while descending to 4,000 feet. The aircraft subsequently broke up in flight and crashed near Wimberley, Texas, killing the pilot and four passengers.
summary: A private pilot flying a Cessna 421C reported pitot tube icing and inoperative pitot heat while descending to 4,000 feet. The aircraft subsequently broke up in flight and crashed near Wimberley, Texas, killing the pilot and four passengers.

synopsis: Failure of the volunteer fire department personnel to properly monitor and secure a stretcher, which resulted in it rolling into the helicopter's tail rotor.
summary: During an air medical helicopter ground operation, two volunteer firefighters left an unsecured stretcher in the rotor disk area. The stretcher rolled into the spinning tail rotor, causing substantial damage to both tail rotor blades and minor damage to the tail boom.

synopsis: United Airlines flight crew operating a Boeing 767-400 struck a light pole on the New Jersey Turnpike during final approach to runway 29 at Newark due to the aircraft being low and slow. The airplane sustained substantial damage and injured a truck driver, but all 231 occupants on board deplaned without injury.
summary: United Airlines flight crew operating a Boeing 767-400 struck a light pole on the New Jersey Turnpike during final approach to runway 29 at Newark due to the aircraft being low and slow. The airplane sustained substantial damage and injured a truck driver, but all 231 occupants on board deplaned without injury.

synopsis: During an agricultural flight, the pilot of an Air Tractor AT-602 experienced uncommanded propeller feathering at low altitude, causing thrust loss and a forced landing. The pilot intentionally ground looped to avoid overrunning the field, resulting in collapsed landing gear and substantial fuselage damage.
summary: During an agricultural flight, the pilot of an Air Tractor AT-602 experienced uncommanded propeller feathering at low altitude, causing thrust loss and a forced landing. The pilot intentionally ground looped to avoid overrunning the field, resulting in collapsed landing gear and substantial fuselage damage.

synopsis: A private pilot and flight instructor in a Beechcraft C23 experienced total engine power loss during a Part 91 instructional flight near Bangor, Maine. The aircraft overran the runway and impacted an embankment after the instructor could not lose sufficient altitude following the power loss, resulting in substantial damage.
summary: A private pilot and flight instructor in a Beechcraft C23 experienced total engine power loss during a Part 91 instructional flight near Bangor, Maine. The aircraft overran the runway and impacted an embankment after the instructor could not lose sufficient altitude following the power loss, resulting in substantial damage.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna 182D experienced partial engine power loss described as "sputtering" at 3,000 feet MSL while returning to Lancaster, Ohio. The subsequent emergency landing in a field resulted in the aircraft striking trees and terrain, causing substantial damage and minor injuries to the pilot and passenger.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna 182D experienced partial engine power loss described as "sputtering" at 3,000 feet MSL while returning to Lancaster, Ohio. The subsequent emergency landing in a field resulted in the aircraft striking trees and terrain, causing substantial damage and minor injuries to the pilot and passenger.

synopsis: The pilot of a North American Navion, N8618H, suffered minor injuries when the engine lost all power at 1,700 feet during a Part 91 flight. Unable to restart the engine, he ditched in Quabbin Reservoir, striking trees before impact, which caused substantial damage to the aircraft.
summary: The pilot of a North American Navion, N8618H, suffered minor injuries when the engine lost all power at 1,700 feet during a Part 91 flight. Unable to restart the engine, he ditched in Quabbin Reservoir, striking trees before impact, which caused substantial damage to the aircraft.

synopsis: The flight instructor's inadequate preflight inspection which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot experienced a total engine power loss at 250 feet during a climb after 39 minutes of pattern work due to undetected empty fuel tanks. The instructor executed a forced landing causing substantial fuselage damage, attributed to relying on difficult-to-read cabin sight gauges instead of checking fuel caps as required.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed and exceedance of the airplanes critical angle of attack while maneuvering at a low altitude, which resulted in a subsequent stall and impact with trees during stall recovery.
summary: During a low-altitude cattle search, the pilot stalled the airplane while turning right. The left wing struck a tree during recovery, causing loss of control and terrain impact with substantial wing damage, though no mechanical failures were reported.

synopsis: The pilot's inability to maintain directional control during the landing roll due to a flat tire.
summary: The pilot of a weight-shift control trike reported that a flat right rear tire likely caused oscillations and a rollover during landing, resulting in substantial damage to the wing and mast. No other pre-accident mechanical failures were identified.

synopsis: During an aerial application flight, a Hiller UH-12E pilot experienced a main rotor hop and a control rotor blade separation, forcing a landing that severed the tail boom. The pilot reported the blade separated despite maintenance records showing compliance with Airworthiness Directive 97-10-16 during a recent annual inspection.
summary: During an aerial application flight, a Hiller UH-12E pilot experienced a main rotor hop and a control rotor blade separation, forcing a landing that severed the tail boom. The pilot reported the blade separated despite maintenance records showing compliance with Airworthiness Directive 97-10-16 during a recent annual inspection.

synopsis: The passenger's improper hand placement on the basket upright during landing, which resulted in injury when the upright fractured during the basket's bounce and drag sequence.
summary: The pilot and a passenger conducting a local balloon flight experienced a serious injury during a steep approach and bounced touchdown. The passenger held a basket upright that fractured upon impact, despite pre-flight briefings, with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain aircraft control during takeoff resulting in a collision with a building during takeoff.
summary: During takeoff and initial climb, the pilot encountered a wind disturbance causing an uncommanded left roll that led to the left wing striking a shed. The aircraft yawed left, crossed a road, and inverted in a cornfield; the pilot attributed the accident to downdrafts from nearby structures and reported no mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental Tundrair King, N62TK, was seriously injured when the aircraft was destroyed near Palmer, Alaska, during a Part 91 personal flight. Witnesses reported the airplane encountered a 20-knot gusting crosswind off the glacier while climbing in a steep left bank, causing a sharp bank increase and nose-down impact with terrain.
summary: The pilot of an experimental Tundrair King, N62TK, was seriously injured when the aircraft was destroyed near Palmer, Alaska, during a Part 91 personal flight. Witnesses reported the airplane encountered a 20-knot gusting crosswind off the glacier while climbing in a steep left bank, causing a sharp bank increase and nose-down impact with terrain.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna 421C experienced a right windshield failure and rapid decompression at flight level 200 during cruise. The pilot declared an emergency and landed safely, attributing the failure to the windshield exceeding recommended inspection intervals and potential grommet deterioration.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna 421C experienced a right windshield failure and rapid decompression at flight level 200 during cruise. The pilot declared an emergency and landed safely, attributing the failure to the windshield exceeding recommended inspection intervals and potential grommet deterioration.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from a power line after takeoff.
summary: A pilot flying a tailwheel STOL aircraft from a private grass airstrip collided with an unmarked power line shortly after departure, impacting terrain and causing a post-crash fire. Although the pilot knew the lines existed, the specific cause of the collision could not be determined.

synopsis: An in-flight collision with a bird during cruise flight.
summary: During cruise, the flight crew encountered a flock of geese causing slight vibration, but initial checks showed no damage. A post-flight inspection revealed substantial damage to the right horizontal stabilizer's leading edge from a bird impact, though the flight landed safely with no pre-existing mechanical failures.

synopsis: The glider pilot's encounter with a strong sink/loss of lift, which resulted in a forced landing to unsuitable terrain.
summary: A glider pilot participating in a race encountered strong sink and could not find thermals, forcing a landing in a field. The left wing struck a swale, causing the glider to spin and the tailboom to separate, though the pilot reported no preimpact mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: The flight instructor's inadequate supervision of the pilot receiving the instruction and the pilot's improper recovery from a practice autorotation in shifting wind conditions, which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: During a practice autorotation in a helicopter, the student pilot overshot the landing point and flared with low rotor RPM, causing a hard landing that collapsed the skids and separated the tail boom. The crew attributed the accident to an unexpected wind shift opposite the windsock, with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: A flight instructor and student pilot were fatally injured when their Cessna 182T crashed into a steep canyon hillside near Armistead, California, during a Part 91 instructional flight. The aircraft impacted the terrain in a left-wing-low attitude while flying up a narrow canyon, resulting in a post-impact fire that destroyed the airplane.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot were fatally injured when their Cessna 182T crashed into a steep canyon hillside near Armistead, California, during a Part 91 instructional flight. The aircraft impacted the terrain in a left-wing-low attitude while flying up a narrow canyon, resulting in a post-impact fire that destroyed the airplane.

synopsis: A flight instructor and student pilot in a Cessna 162 sustained substantial fuselage damage when the nose landing gear collapsed during landing at Seattle Paine Field. The collapse occurred after a loud clunking sound on takeoff and visual confirmation of gear damage during low-altitude passes.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot in a Cessna 162 sustained substantial fuselage damage when the nose landing gear collapsed during landing at Seattle Paine Field. The collapse occurred after a loud clunking sound on takeoff and visual confirmation of gear damage during low-altitude passes.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to retract the flaps during takeoff following a touch-and-go landing, which resulted in degraded climb performance and an impact with an object during an off-field landing.
summary: During a touch-and-go takeoff, the pilot departed with flaps fully extended instead of retracting them to 20°, causing reduced climb performance. The aircraft subsequently impacted a sign during an off-field landing, resulting in substantial damage to the right wing and fuselage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing with a crosswind.
summary: The pilot reported that a tailwheel airplane veered left upon landing on runway 35R, leading to a go-around where both wings struck the ground and the aircraft spun 180°. The pilot attributed the substantial wing damage to the veering and noted no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate preflight inspection, which resulted in him taking off with the fuel selector in the OFF position, and the subsequent total loss of engine power due to fuel starvation.
summary: The pilot lost engine power shortly after takeoff while turning left due to inadvertently leaving the fuel selector in the OFF position. This resulted in a forced landing where the aircraft struck a fence and signpost, collapsing the left gear and sustaining substantial damage to the right wing and fuselage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane while landing, which resulted in a ground loop and subsequent nose over.
summary: The pilot of an experimental exhibition airplane reported a hard landing, bounce, and porpoise on touchdown during the first flight. The pilot delayed a go-around, causing the aircraft to ground loop and nose over, resulting in substantial fuselage and empennage damage with no mechanical failures.

synopsis: The student pilot's improper landing flare and the flight instructor's inadequate remedial action, which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: A student pilot and flight instructor were involved in a hard landing during a cross-country training flight. The student flared too early, causing an excessive sink rate and substantial fuselage damage, which the instructor attributed to his failure to intervene with a go-around on the unstable approach.

synopsis: The pilot's improper flare during landing that resulted in a hard landing.
summary: The pilot reported a hard landing on a turf runway during a straight-in approach, resulting in a nose-over with collapsed gear and bent propeller blades. The aircraft sustained substantial right wing damage, though the pilot attributed the incident to an unexpected event rather than mechanical malfunction.

synopsis: A Cessna A185F seaplane operated by the Maine Warden Service crashed into wooded terrain near Schoolhouse Pond while conducting a fish stocking mission. The pilot was fatally injured when the aircraft impacted rising ground during a right turn, resulting in substantial damage to the airframe and engine.
summary: A Cessna A185F seaplane operated by the Maine Warden Service crashed into wooded terrain near Schoolhouse Pond while conducting a fish stocking mission. The pilot was fatally injured when the aircraft impacted rising ground during a right turn, resulting in substantial damage to the airframe and engine.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from trees while maneuvering in mountainous terrain prior to encountering a downdraft.
summary: The pilot flying near Monroe Mountain encountered a downdraft at 1,000 ft AGL and collided with an unseen tree while maneuvering to avoid another. The aircraft impacted terrain and burned, with the pilot reporting no mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to land at night on a runway without illuminated runway lights. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's failure to review NOTAMs for a nightly airport closure.
summary: A pilot conducting night currency training attempted to land without runway lights after failing to activate them and missing a NOTAM regarding airport closure. He lost visual contact, misjudged his position, and struck a perimeter fence during a go-around, causing substantial damage to the aircraft.

synopsis: The pilot of a Stinson 108-3 experienced engine roughness 15 minutes after departure, followed by an explosion, oil spray, and fire. He executed an off-field landing in a grassy field where the aircraft impacted a ditch, sustaining substantial damage to the fuselage and empennage.
summary: The pilot of a Stinson 108-3 experienced engine roughness 15 minutes after departure, followed by an explosion, oil spray, and fire. He executed an off-field landing in a grassy field where the aircraft impacted a ditch, sustaining substantial damage to the fuselage and empennage.

synopsis: The pilot of a North American F-51D was fatally injured when the aircraft impacted terrain during an aerobatic Split-S maneuver at Vicksburg Tallulah Regional Airport. Witnesses and video showed the engine running normally as the inverted aircraft dived and struck a drainage embankment, with no pre-impact mechanical anomalies found.
summary: The pilot of a North American F-51D was fatally injured when the aircraft impacted terrain during an aerobatic Split-S maneuver at Vicksburg Tallulah Regional Airport. Witnesses and video showed the engine running normally as the inverted aircraft dived and struck a drainage embankment, with no pre-impact mechanical anomalies found.

synopsis: The pilot's collision with a hole in the runway surface during the landing roll, which resulted in a nose over.
summary: During the landing roll on a grass strip, the pilot reported the nose landing gear struck a runway hole, causing the airplane to nose over and come to rest inverted. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the vertical stabilizer and rudder, with no preaccident mechanical malfunctions reported.

synopsis: The captain and first officer of a Cessna 750 landed with gear retracted near Fort Myers after the captain interrupted the before landing checklist due to a master caution and ATC clearance. The aircraft sustained substantial fuselage damage from the gear-up landing, though both crew members were uninjured.
summary: The captain and first officer of a Cessna 750 landed with gear retracted near Fort Myers after the captain interrupted the before landing checklist due to a master caution and ATC clearance. The aircraft sustained substantial fuselage damage from the gear-up landing, though both crew members were uninjured.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain situational awareness and clearance from the helipad surveillance camera during liftoff.
summary: An air medical helicopter pilot and crew departed a helipad at night when the aircraft drifted backward during a right turn, causing the tail rotor to strike a surveillance camera. The pilot landed with substantial damage to the tail rotor and skid, though the operator reported no mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: The pilot's improper decision to attempt an intersection takeoff and delay to abort the takeoff which resulted in a subsequent runway excursion.
summary: During a personal flight intersection takeoff, the pilot aborted when the aircraft failed to reach rotation speed, causing it to veer off the runway and strike a light. The pilot attributed the accident to insufficient runway length for a safe stop, noting no mechanical failures.

synopsis: During the landing of an experimental Bearhawk Four, the pilot reported a dragging right brake caused the aircraft to deviate right and nose over while compensating. The inverted crash resulted in substantial damage to the rudder, wings, and strut, with the pilot uninjured and the passenger sustaining minor injuries.
summary: During the landing of an experimental Bearhawk Four, the pilot reported a dragging right brake caused the aircraft to deviate right and nose over while compensating. The inverted crash resulted in substantial damage to the rudder, wings, and strut, with the pilot uninjured and the passenger sustaining minor injuries.

synopsis: The photographer's failure to remain clear of an active taxiway.
summary: During a glider experience flight, the pilot landed and rolled onto a taxiway where the left wing struck a photographer taking pictures. The glider rotated 90° left and stopped, causing fatal injuries to the photographer, with the pilot reporting no mechanical failures.

synopsis: A Beech C90 air ambulance carrying two pilots and two flight nurses crashed into terrain near Ruidoso, New Mexico, while on a visual approach. The accident occurred after military GPS jamming caused navigation loss, leading the crew to descend below the Capitan Mountains despite the absence of a local altimeter setting.
summary: A Beech C90 air ambulance carrying two pilots and two flight nurses crashed into terrain near Ruidoso, New Mexico, while on a visual approach. The accident occurred after military GPS jamming caused navigation loss, leading the crew to descend below the Capitan Mountains despite the absence of a local altimeter setting.

synopsis: A Cessna 172S pilot reported that during takeoff near Denton, Texas, the aircraft struck a gas cap, causing early rotation and a stuck yoke. Unable to lower the nose while drifting left at 5 to 7 feet, the pilot reduced power, resulting in a ground impact with substantial damage but no injuries.
summary: A Cessna 172S pilot reported that during takeoff near Denton, Texas, the aircraft struck a gas cap, causing early rotation and a stuck yoke. Unable to lower the nose while drifting left at 5 to 7 feet, the pilot reduced power, resulting in a ground impact with substantial damage but no injuries.

synopsis: A flight instructor and student pilot were fatally injured when their Piper PA-28-180 entered a steep, uncontrolled descent during a go-around at Akron, Ohio, in high winds. The aircraft impacted a residential garage, causing a fire, though the three occupants inside escaped uninjured.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot were fatally injured when their Piper PA-28-180 entered a steep, uncontrolled descent during a go-around at Akron, Ohio, in high winds. The aircraft impacted a residential garage, causing a fire, though the three occupants inside escaped uninjured.

synopsis: The pilot's inability to maintain directional control due to a plastic foreign object jammed in the rudder pedals, while landing with a gusting left crosswind.
summary: The pilot reported that a plastic foreign object stuck in the right rudder pedal caused the pedal to jam during landing on runway 21. This resulted in the aircraft yawing right, exiting the runway, and sustaining substantial damage when the left wing struck an airport sign.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control while hovering in gusty wind conditions, resulting in the helicopter rolling onto its side.
summary: A pilot maneuvering a helicopter near an airport while practicing hovering and evaluating left lateral cyclic trim encountered wind gusts to 17 knots, causing the aircraft to roll onto its left side. The main rotor blades severed the tail boom, though the pilot reported no pre-impact mechanical failures.

synopsis: A pilot and passenger were killed when their Piper PA-32-300 entered a right descending spiral and crashed near Empire, Nevada, after the pilot reported being in clouds. The accident occurred during a Part 91 flight in icing conditions with a freezing level at 6,300 ft, resulting in substantial damage to the aircraft.
summary: A pilot and passenger were killed when their Piper PA-32-300 entered a right descending spiral and crashed near Empire, Nevada, after the pilot reported being in clouds. The accident occurred during a Part 91 flight in icing conditions with a freezing level at 6,300 ft, resulting in substantial damage to the aircraft.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper PA-28 experienced engine power loss and rough running near Chandler, Arizona, forcing an emergency landing in a field. The aircraft sustained substantial damage when the nose gear separated after crossing a berm and encountering soft terrain.
summary: The pilot of a Piper PA-28 experienced engine power loss and rough running near Chandler, Arizona, forcing an emergency landing in a field. The aircraft sustained substantial damage when the nose gear separated after crossing a berm and encountering soft terrain.

aircraft: Bigham Jack L MARQUART M 5 CHARGER
synopsis: The pilot of an experimental Marquart M5 Charger experienced total engine power loss at 1,000 feet AGL during a Part 91 flight. While attempting to avoid a vehicle on a road, the pilot turned away and struck a pole, causing substantial wing damage and a subsequent fuel leak.
summary: The pilot of an experimental Marquart M5 Charger experienced total engine power loss at 1,000 feet AGL during a Part 91 flight. While attempting to avoid a vehicle on a road, the pilot turned away and struck a pole, causing substantial wing damage and a subsequent fuel leak.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to extend the main landing gear prior to landing, which resulted in a gear up landing. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's distraction during the approach.
summary: The pilot landed gear-up on the runway after forgetting to extend the main landing gear due to distraction from an approach control instruction to change runways. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the fuselage keel beams, with no preaccident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control during the landing flare with a gusting crosswind.
summary: The pilot encountered a 40-knot crosswind gust during the landing flare on runway 17, causing the right wing to lift. After initiating a go-around, the left wingtip struck the ground, spinning the aircraft 180° and sustaining substantial damage to the right wing, with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control during a precautionary landing following a partial reduction in engine rpm.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane experienced an engine RPM drop during initial climb due to a degraded No. 3 cylinder ignition lead. After returning for a precautionary landing, the aircraft nosed over during the roll, sustaining substantial damage to the right wing lift strut and rudder.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll, in gusting crosswind conditions.
summary: The gyrocopter pilot reported that during landing on runway 31, a gusting crosswind pushed the aircraft right after a hard right gear touchdown. The gyrocopter exited the runway, rolled over, and sustained substantial damage to the fuselage and main rotor driveshaft with no mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate fuel management, which resulted in a loss of engine power due to fuel starvation.
summary: The pilot of a local flight experienced engine power loss due to fuel exhaustion in the left tank after failing to switch to the right tank. He executed a forced landing in a field, sustaining substantial wing damage, with no pre-impact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: During a Part 91 diversion due to gusty winds, the pilot of a Downer 14-19-3 experienced rough engine operation and could not maintain altitude, forcing a landing in a construction area. The aircraft nosed over, sustaining substantial damage, while the pilot and one passenger suffered minor injuries and a second passenger died 13 days later.
summary: During a Part 91 diversion due to gusty winds, the pilot of a Downer 14-19-3 experienced rough engine operation and could not maintain altitude, forcing a landing in a construction area. The aircraft nosed over, sustaining substantial damage, while the pilot and one passenger suffered minor injuries and a second passenger died 13 days later.

synopsis: The pilot of a Vertical Aviation Technologies 300L Hummingbird helicopter lost control during a low hover near Lee's Summit, Missouri, after a sudden engine RPM increase caused a counterclockwise rotation. The aircraft impacted sloped terrain on its right side, sustaining substantial damage to the stabilizers while one passenger suffered minor injuries.
summary: The pilot of a Vertical Aviation Technologies 300L Hummingbird helicopter lost control during a low hover near Lee's Summit, Missouri, after a sudden engine RPM increase caused a counterclockwise rotation. The aircraft impacted sloped terrain on its right side, sustaining substantial damage to the stabilizers while one passenger suffered minor injuries.

synopsis: During a post-maintenance test flight of a Cessna 172N, the pilot was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed after the right aileron control cable fractured. Witnesses reported the airplane rolled right and nosed down, while the investigation found the cable failure and an obstructed fuel tank vent line.
summary: During a post-maintenance test flight of a Cessna 172N, the pilot was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed after the right aileron control cable fractured. Witnesses reported the airplane rolled right and nosed down, while the investigation found the cable failure and an obstructed fuel tank vent line.

synopsis: The student pilot's excessive pitch up attitude during takeoff, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall and loss of control.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot stalled a light aircraft during a soft field takeoff after the student aggressively applied excessive aft yoke input. The instructor could not overpower the student's control, causing the airplane to pitch up, roll left, and impact the ground with substantial damage.

synopsis: Contamination of the left wheel brake system with debris, which resulted in a loss of directional control during takeoff.
summary: The pilot of an experimental amateur-built tailwheel airplane ground looped during takeoff roll after the aircraft turned hard left despite right rudder input. The excursion caused substantial damage, and post-accident inspection revealed a seized left wheel due to grooved brake pads and debris in the rotor.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll with a right crosswind.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane ground looped and nosed over inverted during a full-stop landing on runway 24 in an 18-knot right crosswind. The accident occurred after the right wing lifted on touchdown and a go-around attempt failed due to insufficient airspeed, causing substantial damage to the left-wing strut and rudder.

synopsis: The pilot's inability to maintain climb performance and clearance from mountainous terrain due to a downdraft.
summary: The pilot of a cross-country flight diverted to Elko, Nevada, after finding snow at Wells, then crossed a mountain range exceeding 10,000 ft. The aircraft encountered an unclimbable down-draft headwind, impacting terrain 500 ft below the summit, causing substantial damage and serious injuries despite pre-flight weather forecasts indicating hazardous conditions.

synopsis: The pilot of a Mooney M20J experienced engine roughness after refueling at Lake Havasu City, which temporarily improved when leaning the mixture. During the subsequent takeoff climb at 200 feet AGL, insufficient power forced a turn back, resulting in a ground impact short of the runway that substantially damaged the aircraft and seriously injured the occupants.
summary: The pilot of a Mooney M20J experienced engine roughness after refueling at Lake Havasu City, which temporarily improved when leaning the mixture. During the subsequent takeoff climb at 200 feet AGL, insufficient power forced a turn back, resulting in a ground impact short of the runway that substantially damaged the aircraft and seriously injured the occupants.

synopsis: A commercial pilot substantially damaged an experimental Thorp T-18 during takeoff at Hendersonville Airport after a lackadaisical preflight inspection left the pitch trim set nose-down. The aircraft climbed steeply, became uncontrollable despite forward stick input, and impacted trees because the trim system was not properly configured for departure.
summary: A commercial pilot substantially damaged an experimental Thorp T-18 during takeoff at Hendersonville Airport after a lackadaisical preflight inspection left the pitch trim set nose-down. The aircraft climbed steeply, became uncontrollable despite forward stick input, and impacted trees because the trim system was not properly configured for departure.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane experienced a ground loop after the right brake failed to function during landing rollout, causing the aircraft to veer left and strike a runway light. Post-accident checks showed the brake required pumping to engage, though no mechanical anomalies were found in the wheel or brake assemblies.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate fuel planning, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion.
summary: The pilot of a twin-engine experimental airplane experienced dual engine power loss due to fuel exhaustion while 5 to 10 minutes from his destination. He conducted a forced landing in a muddy field, resulting in substantial damage to the fuselage and left wing after the left wheel flange separated.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control of the airplane during landing, which resulted in a touchdown off the paved runway surface and a collision with terrain during the subsequent aborted landing.
summary: During landing approach, the pilot reported the airplane drifted left, briefly touched down off the runway, and failed to accelerate during a go-around attempt. The aircraft subsequently impacted the ground, nosed over, and came to rest inverted with substantial damage, though the pilot reported no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot of a Mooney M20J ferrying the aircraft after maintenance reported a cylinder running 100°F hotter than others before departing. The airplane subsequently banked sharply, flipped, and impacted the ground near Woodlake, California, resulting in the pilot's fatal injury and a postaccident fire.
summary: The pilot of a Mooney M20J ferrying the aircraft after maintenance reported a cylinder running 100°F hotter than others before departing. The airplane subsequently banked sharply, flipped, and impacted the ground near Woodlake, California, resulting in the pilot's fatal injury and a postaccident fire.

synopsis: A private pilot and passenger in a Sling LSA N83PF experienced engine failure near Kalaupapa Airport due to a fractured No. 2 cylinder exhaust valve stem. The pilot attempted a water landing to avoid rocky terrain, resulting in an inverted crash, substantial aircraft damage, and minor injuries to both occupants.
summary: A private pilot and passenger in a Sling LSA N83PF experienced engine failure near Kalaupapa Airport due to a fractured No. 2 cylinder exhaust valve stem. The pilot attempted a water landing to avoid rocky terrain, resulting in an inverted crash, substantial aircraft damage, and minor injuries to both occupants.

synopsis: The pilot's excessive approach speed, which resulted in a hard, bounced landing and nose-over.
summary: The pilot conducting glider tow operations landed on a rough grassy area adjacent to the runway, experiencing a firm touchdown that caused the aircraft to bounce and nose over inverted. The pilot attributed the accident to rushing the approach and landing in a distracted environment rather than mechanical failure.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to extend the landing gear prior to landing.
summary: A pilot approaching the traffic pattern became distracted by another aircraft taking off and entering downwind, causing him to forget the before landing checklist. He subsequently landed without extending the landing gear, resulting in substantial damage to the lower fuselage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain sufficient altitude and aircraft control during the base to final turn, which resulted in the airplane impacting the water. Contributing to the accident was reported downdraft wind conditions.
summary: The pilot encountered a strong downdraft while turning from base to final for a lake landing, causing the aircraft to descend and impact the water left-wing low. The pilot attributed the accident to insufficient altitude and a tight turn, noting no mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental Fokker DR1 was fatally injured when the aircraft stalled and impacted the runway during a low-altitude traffic pattern. Post-accident examination revealed a fractured throttle cable and a closed throttle slide, which likely caused a loss of power leading to the stall.
summary: The pilot of an experimental Fokker DR1 was fatally injured when the aircraft stalled and impacted the runway during a low-altitude traffic pattern. Post-accident examination revealed a fractured throttle cable and a closed throttle slide, which likely caused a loss of power leading to the stall.

synopsis: The flight instructor's failure to maintain helicopter control while manipulating the engine governor reference rpm adjustment during hover operations, which resulted in a loss of control and impact with the ground.
summary: A flight instructor flying a helicopter from the left seat lost control during an initial hover while adjusting the governor reference rpm, causing the aircraft to pitch up, descend, and impact the taxiway. The helicopter subsequently spun, became airborne, and crashed again, resulting in the separation of the tailboom and main rotor system.

synopsis: During an aerotow departure at 200 feet, a Schleicher ASW27 glider climbed above the Piper PA-25-235 towplane, causing a nose-down upset that the pilot could not recover from. The towplane impacted the runway and burned, killing the pilot, while the glider pilot successfully released and landed safely.
summary: During an aerotow departure at 200 feet, a Schleicher ASW27 glider climbed above the Piper PA-25-235 towplane, causing a nose-down upset that the pilot could not recover from. The towplane impacted the runway and burned, killing the pilot, while the glider pilot successfully released and landed safely.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll with gusting crosswind conditions.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane ground looped left during the landing roll on Runway 1 due to a gusty west-northwest wind. The right main landing gear collapsed and the right wing struck the ground, causing substantial damage, with no preaccident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: During a Part 91 instructional flight in a Textron 172S, the flight instructor and student experienced a total engine power loss at 1,800 feet MSL while practicing a climb. The instructor executed an emergency landing in a plowed field, resulting in substantial damage to the right wing, though both occupants were uninjured.
summary: During a Part 91 instructional flight in a Textron 172S, the flight instructor and student experienced a total engine power loss at 1,800 feet MSL while practicing a climb. The instructor executed an emergency landing in a plowed field, resulting in substantial damage to the right wing, though both occupants were uninjured.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna A188B operating a Part 137 agricultural flight reported a total loss of engine power while en route to apply fertilizer. He executed a forced landing into a field, striking trees and sustaining substantial damage to the fuselage and wings, though he was not injured.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna A188B operating a Part 137 agricultural flight reported a total loss of engine power while en route to apply fertilizer. He executed a forced landing into a field, striking trees and sustaining substantial damage to the fuselage and wings, though he was not injured.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airplane control during the go-around.
summary: The pilot executed a crosswind landing in a 11-knot wind but initiated a go-around when a tailwind shift increased airspeed. The aircraft failed to climb out of ground effect, sank, and sustained substantial damage after the nose gear collapsed upon impacting terrain beyond the runway.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna A188B attempted a go-around at Blair Executive Airport after an unsatisfactory landing but experienced engine power loss due to a disconnected throttle cable. The aircraft was forced into an adjacent field, sustaining substantial left wing damage following recent throttle body maintenance.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna A188B attempted a go-around at Blair Executive Airport after an unsatisfactory landing but experienced engine power loss due to a disconnected throttle cable. The aircraft was forced into an adjacent field, sustaining substantial left wing damage following recent throttle body maintenance.

synopsis: The flight crew's decision to continue the landing approach into adverse weather conditions, which resulted in a loss visual reference and loss airplane control during landing.
summary: The business jet flight crew landed in heavy rain, lost visual reference, and veered off the runway, damaging the right wing. The pilot attributed the incident to unanticipated visibility loss from precipitation despite a stabilized approach and no mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's improper engine power application during the landing flare, which resulted in a hard, bounced landing and nose over.
summary: The pilot reduced engine power too early on final approach, causing a hard bounced landing where the nose gear collapsed and the aircraft nosed over. The pilot attributed the substantial damage to the vertical stabilizer, rudder, wings, and struts to pilot error rather than mechanical issues.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare and subsequent loss of directional control during landing.
summary: A solo student pilot lost directional control during the flare of a touch-and-go landing, causing the aircraft to balloon, exit the runway, and nose over into a drainage ditch. The pilot reported no mechanical malfunctions, and the accident resulted in substantial damage to the left wing and rudder.

synopsis: A flight instructor and student pilot in a Rainbow Cheetah XLS suffered serious injuries when the aircraft struck a tree and semi-trailer during a low approach at Raleigh East Airport. The accident occurred after the engine repeatedly sputtered upon power application, preventing a climb over obstacles and forcing an unsuccessful attempt to land in an open field.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot in a Rainbow Cheetah XLS suffered serious injuries when the aircraft struck a tree and semi-trailer during a low approach at Raleigh East Airport. The accident occurred after the engine repeatedly sputtered upon power application, preventing a climb over obstacles and forcing an unsuccessful attempt to land in an open field.

synopsis: The pilot in command's decision to continue the takeoff when the airplane was not airborne at midfield, and the student pilot's likely improper technique that resulted in a lack of sufficient climb performance and subsequent loss of control.
summary: A student pilot flying a light aircraft from a grass airstrip continued takeoff past midfield despite insufficient climb performance. The pilot's decision to continue and subsequent control inputs caused the airplane to lose energy and impact terrain near the departure end.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper PA-32R-300 experienced sudden engine power loss shortly after takeoff near Comanche, Texas, likely due to fuel system issues despite switching tanks. The pilot executed a forced landing in a field, but the aircraft struck a fence and sustained substantial damage to the wings and empennage.
summary: The pilot of a Piper PA-32R-300 experienced sudden engine power loss shortly after takeoff near Comanche, Texas, likely due to fuel system issues despite switching tanks. The pilot executed a forced landing in a field, but the aircraft struck a fence and sustained substantial damage to the wings and empennage.

synopsis: The flight instructor's delayed remedial action and the student pilot's failure to maintain helicopter control during hover.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot were practicing helicopter hovering when the aircraft rolled onto its left side after the left skid caught on a pavement crack. The operator reported no mechanical failures and subsequently implemented enhanced training protocols for hover instruction and rollover risk mitigation.

synopsis: The pilot's improper decision to continue with an unstabilized approach, which resulted in a hard landing, loss of directional control, and collision with a runway marker light and sign.
summary: The pilot executed an unstable approach, causing a hard landing and bounce that veered the aircraft off the runway into a light and sign, damaging the wing and puncturing the fuel tank. After aborting and declaring an emergency due to fuel fumes, the pilot landed safely, attributing the incident to forcing a landing instead of going around.

synopsis: A student pilot and flight instructor in a Cessna 172P suffered serious and minor injuries, respectively, when the aircraft crashed inverted near Pembroke Pines, Florida, during a short field takeoff. The accident occurred after the engine sounded abnormal and sputtered, causing a low-altitude descent and fuel leak, though no fuel contaminants were found.
summary: A student pilot and flight instructor in a Cessna 172P suffered serious and minor injuries, respectively, when the aircraft crashed inverted near Pembroke Pines, Florida, during a short field takeoff. The accident occurred after the engine sounded abnormal and sputtered, causing a low-altitude descent and fuel leak, though no fuel contaminants were found.

synopsis: The pilot of a Mustang II, N160MT, sustained minor injuries and the aircraft suffered substantial damage after a forced landing near Richmond, Texas. The accident occurred during a touch-and-go takeoff when the engine experienced a partial power loss while the pilot was using carburetor heat.
summary: The pilot of a Mustang II, N160MT, sustained minor injuries and the aircraft suffered substantial damage after a forced landing near Richmond, Texas. The accident occurred during a touch-and-go takeoff when the engine experienced a partial power loss while the pilot was using carburetor heat.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to properly latch the canopy before flight, which led to the canopy opening shortly after takeoff.
summary: The pilot of an experimental airplane reported that the canopy opened shortly after takeoff due to improper latching. Unable to close it, he landed straight ahead, overran the runway, and sustained substantial engine mount damage with no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control during the landing rollout and subsequent aborted landing.
summary: The pilot reported that after touchdown, the airplane swerved left, prompting an over-correction and a go-around. During the climb, the aircraft banked right, striking a runway sign and a grassy area, causing substantial damage to both right wings with no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: A commercial pilot flying a Robinson R66 helicopter under Part 135 struck trees and terrain near Dawsonville, Georgia, while en route to DeKalb-Peachtree Airport in rain and low clouds. The accident caused substantial damage to the aircraft and resulted in the deaths of the pilot and one passenger, with no pre-impact mechanical anomalies found.
summary: A commercial pilot flying a Robinson R66 helicopter under Part 135 struck trees and terrain near Dawsonville, Georgia, while en route to DeKalb-Peachtree Airport in rain and low clouds. The accident caused substantial damage to the aircraft and resulted in the deaths of the pilot and one passenger, with no pre-impact mechanical anomalies found.

synopsis: A pilot operating a Pipistrel Sinus 912, N1277P, was fatally injured when the aircraft struck a power transmission line and pole during a Part 91 personal flight near Columbus, Mississippi. The airplane was destroyed in a postcrash fire after departing Columbus-Lowndes County Airport and turning back toward the field.
summary: A pilot operating a Pipistrel Sinus 912, N1277P, was fatally injured when the aircraft struck a power transmission line and pole during a Part 91 personal flight near Columbus, Mississippi. The airplane was destroyed in a postcrash fire after departing Columbus-Lowndes County Airport and turning back toward the field.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna T210 experienced engine vibration, explosion noises, low oil pressure, and high oil temperature at 3,000 feet MSL during the first flight post-maintenance. Unable to return to the airport, he performed a forced landing on a road where the aircraft struck a pole, sustaining substantial damage to the wing, fuselage, and empennage.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna T210 experienced engine vibration, explosion noises, low oil pressure, and high oil temperature at 3,000 feet MSL during the first flight post-maintenance. Unable to return to the airport, he performed a forced landing on a road where the aircraft struck a pole, sustaining substantial damage to the wing, fuselage, and empennage.

synopsis: A pilot and passenger were seriously injured when their Part 91 Boeing E75, N181RF, crashed into a hay field near Dresden, Ohio. A witness reported hearing a loud pop and engine noise ceasing before impact, resulting in substantial damage to both right wings.
summary: A pilot and passenger were seriously injured when their Part 91 Boeing E75, N181RF, crashed into a hay field near Dresden, Ohio. A witness reported hearing a loud pop and engine noise ceasing before impact, resulting in substantial damage to both right wings.

synopsis: The pilot of a Grumman AA-1A experienced sudden shaking and total engine power loss during a Part 91 positioning flight near Amery, Wisconsin. After attempting an off-field landing, the main gear collapsed causing substantial wing damage, and a hole was later found in the engine crankcase.
summary: The pilot of a Grumman AA-1A experienced sudden shaking and total engine power loss during a Part 91 positioning flight near Amery, Wisconsin. After attempting an off-field landing, the main gear collapsed causing substantial wing damage, and a hole was later found in the engine crankcase.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed, which led to the airplane exceeding its critical angle of attack and experiencing an aerodynamic stall. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's decision to practice slow flight maneuvers at an altitude that precluded a recovery from the inadvertent stall after the turbulence encounter.
summary: A student pilot practicing slow flight encountered severe turbulence during a turn, causing an aerodynamic stall and spin. Although the pilot recovered from the spin, insufficient altitude prevented a return to level flight before the aircraft impacted trees, sustaining substantial damage with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain directional control of the airplane during the takeoff, which resulted in a runway excursion and collision with runway signs.
summary: A student pilot executing a solo takeoff retracted fully extended flaps during the roll, causing the aircraft to veer left, strike two runway signs, and sustain substantial elevator damage. The pilot reported no preimpact mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power on approach due to carburetor icing.
summary: During final approach, the pilot applied carburetor heat in icing conditions, causing total engine power loss and a forced landing in a cornfield. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the right wing and fuselage, with the pilot attributing the failure to carburetor icing.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a hard, bounced landing.
summary: A solo student pilot conducting soft-field landing practice experienced a bounce and porpoise, resulting in a hard landing. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the engine firewall and lower fuselage, with no preimpact mechanical malfunctions reported.

synopsis: A Cessna 182T pilot encountered ice and entered an uncontrolled spiral descent from 10,000 ft MSL near Newberry, Michigan, resulting in substantial wing damage. The pilot regained control at 1,400 ft MSL, climbed to 3,000 ft MSL, and landed safely at Luce County Airport with no injuries.
summary: A Cessna 182T pilot encountered ice and entered an uncontrolled spiral descent from 10,000 ft MSL near Newberry, Michigan, resulting in substantial wing damage. The pilot regained control at 1,400 ft MSL, climbed to 3,000 ft MSL, and landed safely at Luce County Airport with no injuries.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain aircraft control during landing in gusting wind conditions which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: The pilot reported that during landing in 23-knot winds gusting to 32 knots, the airplane ballooned, struck the ground hard, and porpoised on a second attempt due to a wind gust. No mechanical failures were reported, but the forward fuselage sustained substantial damage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to ensure the proper preflight assembly of the glider's wing attachment system, which resulted in substantial damage to the wing structure during flight.
summary: The pilot and three club members assembled a glider before a towed flight. In-flight structural damage occurred because the right main wing pin was not fully seated and secured during assembly, despite the left pin being correct.

synopsis: The pilot of an Air Tractor AT-602 operating under Part 137 agricultural rules reported total engine power loss at 300 feet AGL while climbing to a private airstrip. He executed a forced landing in a paddy field, but the aircraft nosed over and inverted, causing substantial empennage damage and minor pilot injuries.
summary: The pilot of an Air Tractor AT-602 operating under Part 137 agricultural rules reported total engine power loss at 300 feet AGL while climbing to a private airstrip. He executed a forced landing in a paddy field, but the aircraft nosed over and inverted, causing substantial empennage damage and minor pilot injuries.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate preflight inspection which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion.
summary: The pilot experienced engine power loss at 1,500 ft MSL due to fuel exhaustion after failing to visually verify fuel quantity. He executed an emergency landing on a highway, but the right wing struck a road sign, causing gear collapse and substantial damage.

synopsis: The pilot's improper approach, which resulted in a faster than normal touchdown and subsequent runway overrun.
summary: The pilot landed a general aviation airplane at a back-country airport with a suspected tailwind and high ground speed, failing to stop before the runway end. He attempted to avoid parked vehicles by pulling up but struck a car and signpost, causing substantial damage and injuries due to unfamiliarity with the environment and lack of ground speed verification.

synopsis: A pilot flying a Cirrus SF50 experienced an uncontained engine failure during climb to 13,000 ft MSL after an initial ITT warning. The pilot declared an emergency and executed a no-power landing at Athens-Ben Epps Airport following a loud bang and power loss.
summary: A pilot flying a Cirrus SF50 experienced an uncontained engine failure during climb to 13,000 ft MSL after an initial ITT warning. The pilot declared an emergency and executed a no-power landing at Athens-Ben Epps Airport following a loud bang and power loss.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to resume taxiing on a turf runway that was unable to adequately support the airplane's weight, which resulted in the nose landing gear sinking into the soft ground and the propeller striking the terrain.
summary: The pilot landed on a grass runway, but the right main gear stuck in soft terrain during a back-taxi turn. While attempting to taxi to drier ground using soft-field techniques, the nosewheel sank, causing the propeller to strike the ground and damage the firewall and fuselage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to ensure the loading hose had been disconnected before takeoff, which resulted in an interrupted takeoff and subsequent loss of control. Contributing to the accident was the ground loader's failure to disconnect the hose before communicating with the pilot.
summary: The helicopter pilot took off from a loading truck with the spray hose still attached, causing a loss of control during a hover while the ground crew disconnected it. The aircraft impacted adjacent terrain, sustaining substantial damage to the fuselage, cabin, and rotor systems, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's inadvertent excessive braking during the landing roll, which resulted in a nose over.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane nosed over and sustained substantial damage during a normal landing after the aircraft bounced. The investigation concluded the accident was likely caused by the pilot inadvertently applying excessive braking during the landing roll.

synopsis: During takeoff of an AutoGyro Cavalon gyroplane on a solo Part 91 flight, the pilot reported violent shaking and an uncontrollable left roll at 10 to 30 feet. The aircraft impacted terrain, rolled, and sustained substantial damage to the empennage, fuselage, and main rotors, though the pilot was uninjured.
summary: During takeoff of an AutoGyro Cavalon gyroplane on a solo Part 91 flight, the pilot reported violent shaking and an uncontrollable left roll at 10 to 30 feet. The aircraft impacted terrain, rolled, and sustained substantial damage to the empennage, fuselage, and main rotors, though the pilot was uninjured.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper J3C-65 experienced a total engine power loss at 200 feet after takeoff, forcing a landing in a farm field. The aircraft struck a greenhouse, causing partial landing gear collapse and substantial damage to the engine mount, though the pilot and passenger were uninjured.
summary: The pilot of a Piper J3C-65 experienced a total engine power loss at 200 feet after takeoff, forcing a landing in a farm field. The aircraft struck a greenhouse, causing partial landing gear collapse and substantial damage to the engine mount, though the pilot and passenger were uninjured.

synopsis: The pilot of an Air Tractor AT-602 conducting an agricultural flight experienced engine surges, rising temperatures, and exhaust flames before total power loss. The pilot executed a forced landing to a field, resulting in substantial damage to the aft fuselage while sustaining no injuries.
summary: The pilot of an Air Tractor AT-602 conducting an agricultural flight experienced engine surges, rising temperatures, and exhaust flames before total power loss. The pilot executed a forced landing to a field, resulting in substantial damage to the aft fuselage while sustaining no injuries.

synopsis: The flight instructor's inadequate preflight planning, which resulted in a rejected takeoff from a tailwind departure and subsequent runway excursion.
summary: A flight instructor aborted a soft-field takeoff on a 2,000-ft turf runway due to a tailwind preventing climb, causing a runway excursion. The aircraft struck a roadway with the propeller, sustaining substantial lower fuselage damage, with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cirrus SR22T experienced engine roughness and power loss at 21,000 ft MSL while returning to Casper. The engine seized at 500-600 ft AGL during the approach, forcing a landing short of the runway that resulted in substantial damage after impacting a perimeter fence.
summary: The pilot of a Cirrus SR22T experienced engine roughness and power loss at 21,000 ft MSL while returning to Casper. The engine seized at 500-600 ft AGL during the approach, forcing a landing short of the runway that resulted in substantial damage after impacting a perimeter fence.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: The pilot attempted a third landing when the aircraft contacted the runway hard with a high rate of descent and nose-high attitude. This caused immediate nose gear collapse and substantial fuselage damage before the airplane stopped on the runway.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to extend the landing gear prior to landing.
summary: The pilot landed an aircraft with the gear retracted during a straight-in approach after failing to use the checklist or make the "gear/flaps" callout. Although an audible warning horn sounded, the pilot did not recognize it, resulting in substantial lower fuselage damage with no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to abort the takeoff with insufficient runway remaining, which resulted in a runway excursion.
summary: During a post-maintenance test flight, the pilot aborted takeoff due to perceived sluggish performance, causing the aircraft to overrun the runway and strike a fence, damaging the left wing. Subsequent avionics data review confirmed the engine produced full power and acceleration was normal, with no mechanical failures or visibility issues identified.

synopsis: During a Part 91 instructional flight near Kissimmee Gateway Airport, a Cessna 150L suffered total engine power loss when the fuel shutoff valve stuck in the off position while switching tanks. The commercial and student pilots were seriously injured after the aircraft crashed in an open field following the fuel exhaustion.
summary: During a Part 91 instructional flight near Kissimmee Gateway Airport, a Cessna 150L suffered total engine power loss when the fuel shutoff valve stuck in the off position while switching tanks. The commercial and student pilots were seriously injured after the aircraft crashed in an open field following the fuel exhaustion.

synopsis: A private pilot flying an experimental Sonex N28YD suffered serious injuries when the engine unexpectedly stopped at 100 feet during takeoff from Jaffrey Airfield. The pilot attempted to land in a field but crashed, sustaining substantial damage to the left wing and fuselage.
summary: A private pilot flying an experimental Sonex N28YD suffered serious injuries when the engine unexpectedly stopped at 100 feet during takeoff from Jaffrey Airfield. The pilot attempted to land in a field but crashed, sustaining substantial damage to the left wing and fuselage.

synopsis: During airshow practice at 3,800 feet, the pilot of a North American SNJ-5C experienced a propeller separation caused by crankshaft torsional shear, which damaged the left wing. The pilot executed a safe emergency landing with no injuries to the pilot or passenger.
summary: During airshow practice at 3,800 feet, the pilot of a North American SNJ-5C experienced a propeller separation caused by crankshaft torsional shear, which damaged the left wing. The pilot executed a safe emergency landing with no injuries to the pilot or passenger.
