synopsis: A private pilot flying an Aero Commander N27007 under Part 91 experienced a loss of climb and airspeed 30 seconds after liftoff. The pilot attempted a forced landing at 300 to 500 feet, resulting in a hard touchdown and substantial damage to the fuselage, wings, and empennage.
summary: A private pilot flying an Aero Commander N27007 under Part 91 experienced a loss of climb and airspeed 30 seconds after liftoff. The pilot attempted a forced landing at 300 to 500 feet, resulting in a hard touchdown and substantial damage to the fuselage, wings, and empennage.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper PA-44-180T, N8390K, substantially damaged the aircraft during a Part 91 approach to St. George Regional Airport after the left engine lost power. The pilot attributed the power loss to fuel exhaustion following multiple aborted approaches and a headwind that extended flight time beyond calculated reserves.
summary: The pilot of a Piper PA-44-180T, N8390K, substantially damaged the aircraft during a Part 91 approach to St. George Regional Airport after the left engine lost power. The pilot attributed the power loss to fuel exhaustion following multiple aborted approaches and a headwind that extended flight time beyond calculated reserves.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to remain clear of a power line during an aerial application flight.
summary: During aerial application operations, a helicopter pilot misjudged clearance from power lines due to sun glare while turning, causing the right skid and boom to strike a wire. The helicopter subsequently impacted the ground, seriously injuring the pilot and sustaining substantial damage to the airframe with no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to extend the landing gear before landing.
summary: During a straight-in approach, the pilot forgot to extend the landing gear and landed with it retracted. The aircraft slid to a stop on the runway, sustaining substantial damage to the lower fuselage with no preaccident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The loss of engine power due to fuel starvation. Contributing to the accident was the separated wing fuel tank screen and sealant debris in the fuel tank.
summary: During an aerial application return, the pilot executed a forced landing after engine power loss caused by a missing fuel screen and sealant debris blocking the outlet. The aircraft struck trees, sustaining substantial damage to the right wing and fuselage.

synopsis: A Cessna P210N pilot and two passengers were seriously injured when the aircraft stalled and spun into a ditch during approach to runway 28 at Dona Ana County International Jetport. A witness observed the airplane at a high angle of attack before it impacted the ground without touching the runway.
summary: A Cessna P210N pilot and two passengers were seriously injured when the aircraft stalled and spun into a ditch during approach to runway 28 at Dona Ana County International Jetport. A witness observed the airplane at a high angle of attack before it impacted the ground without touching the runway.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airspeed during a go-around in shifting wind conditions, which resulted in an exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack and an aerodynamic stall.
summary: The pilot executed a go-around after a bounced landing at low altitude, low airspeed, and high gross weight. Shifting winds caused drift, and correcting this led to an aerodynamic stall and ground impact, resulting in substantial damage to the fuselage, wings, and empennage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane during an aborted landing attempt which resulted in an aerodynamic stall.
summary: During practice landings at a turf runway, the pilot aborted a second attempt after the aircraft turned right and bounced. The airplane subsequently stalled, dropped its left wing, and tumbled, causing substantial damage to the wing and fuselage due to exceeding the critical angle of attack.

synopsis: During a post-maintenance test flight of a Mooney M20J at Double Eagle II Airport, the pilot reported that the aircraft unexpectedly impacted the runway on short final approach despite normal engine and control indications. The airplane veered off onto grass, sustaining substantial damage to the wings and fuselage, and the pilot was seriously injured.
summary: During a post-maintenance test flight of a Mooney M20J at Double Eagle II Airport, the pilot reported that the aircraft unexpectedly impacted the runway on short final approach despite normal engine and control indications. The airplane veered off onto grass, sustaining substantial damage to the wings and fuselage, and the pilot was seriously injured.

synopsis: A flight instructor and student pilot substantially damaged a Cessna 172C during a Part 91 instructional takeoff near Cleburne, Texas, when the aircraft bounced and collapsed its nose gear. The instructor attributed the accident to insufficient airspeed caused by an incorrect nose-down elevator trim setting and a misplaced trim placard.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot substantially damaged a Cessna 172C during a Part 91 instructional takeoff near Cleburne, Texas, when the aircraft bounced and collapsed its nose gear. The instructor attributed the accident to insufficient airspeed caused by an incorrect nose-down elevator trim setting and a misplaced trim placard.

synopsis: A pilot operating a Cirrus SR20 under Part 91 was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed near Wheelers Mill, Ohio, shortly after takeoff. The plane entered a near-vertical descent and impacted a home, destroying both the aircraft and residence, with no mechanical anomalies found to explain the event.
summary: A pilot operating a Cirrus SR20 under Part 91 was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed near Wheelers Mill, Ohio, shortly after takeoff. The plane entered a near-vertical descent and impacted a home, destroying both the aircraft and residence, with no mechanical anomalies found to explain the event.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during takeoff roll, which resulted in a runway excursion and collision with an approach lighting system.
summary: The pilot reported a left main landing gear tire failure during takeoff roll, causing the airplane to pull left, depart the runway, and strike a VASI light. Post-accident examination confirmed the tire was flat and the left wing sustained substantial damage, with skid marks indicating the tire failed after the collision.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper PA-36-300 conducting a Part 137 mosquito abatement flight at dusk was fatally injured when the aircraft struck an unlit 50-foot beacon tower and terrain. The collision occurred at 40 feet AGL while the pilot flew toward the setting sun, resulting in substantial damage to the airplane.
summary: The pilot of a Piper PA-36-300 conducting a Part 137 mosquito abatement flight at dusk was fatally injured when the aircraft struck an unlit 50-foot beacon tower and terrain. The collision occurred at 40 feet AGL while the pilot flew toward the setting sun, resulting in substantial damage to the airplane.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna T206H conducting an aerial survey switched the fuel selector from "Both" to "Right" during cruise, causing engine power loss. Despite switching back to "Both," the pilot could not maintain altitude and executed a forced landing where the aircraft struck trees, sustaining substantial left wing damage.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna T206H conducting an aerial survey switched the fuel selector from "Both" to "Right" during cruise, causing engine power loss. Despite switching back to "Both," the pilot could not maintain altitude and executed a forced landing where the aircraft struck trees, sustaining substantial left wing damage.

synopsis: A Lancair 235 pilot was fatally injured when the aircraft was destroyed during takeoff on runway 02 near Hillsboro, Oregon. Witnesses reported the nosewheel bounced, brakes locked, and the plane exited the runway end in a nose-high attitude before rolling left, impacting terrain, and catching fire.
summary: A Lancair 235 pilot was fatally injured when the aircraft was destroyed during takeoff on runway 02 near Hillsboro, Oregon. Witnesses reported the nosewheel bounced, brakes locked, and the plane exited the runway end in a nose-high attitude before rolling left, impacting terrain, and catching fire.

synopsis: The student pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a hard landing, and the flight instructor's delayed remedial action.
summary: During a student training flight, the instructor attempted a go-around after a hard landing but lost directional control, causing the aircraft to exit the runway. The excursion resulted in gear separation and left wing impact, with the instructor reporting no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: A Pacific Aerospace 750XL conducting a skydiving flight departed Butler, Missouri, and entered a left turn during initial climb before impacting terrain nose-down. The pilot and 11 passengers died in the post-impact fire, with no pre-impact mechanical failures found in the engine or airframe.
summary: A Pacific Aerospace 750XL conducting a skydiving flight departed Butler, Missouri, and entered a left turn during initial climb before impacting terrain nose-down. The pilot and 11 passengers died in the post-impact fire, with no pre-impact mechanical failures found in the engine or airframe.

synopsis: The total loss of power to both engines due to fuel exhaustion. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's failure to verify the airplane's fuel quantity before departure.
summary: The pilot instructed line crew to top off fuel tanks without verifying levels, leading to dual engine power loss near the destination. The pilot executed a forced landing in a pasture, colliding with trees and causing substantial damage to the wings and empennage due to fuel exhaustion.

synopsis: An in-flight collision with a bird.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot experienced a bird strike at 1,200 ft MSL during training maneuvers. The bird collided with the right wing causing substantial damage, but the instructor took control and landed the aircraft uneventfully.

synopsis: During a Part 91 sightseeing hover at North Perry Airport, a Robinson R44 helicopter drifted left then sharply right, exceeding the critical roll angle and causing a dynamic rollover into a parked airplane. The pilot reported no mechanical failures, resulting in substantial damage to the aircraft and minor injuries to the pilot and three passengers.
summary: During a Part 91 sightseeing hover at North Perry Airport, a Robinson R44 helicopter drifted left then sharply right, exceeding the critical roll angle and causing a dynamic rollover into a parked airplane. The pilot reported no mechanical failures, resulting in substantial damage to the aircraft and minor injuries to the pilot and three passengers.

synopsis: The pilot's selection of an unsuitable landing area, which resulted in the airplane nosing over during the landing roll.
summary: The pilot nosed over an airplane during an off-airport landing on a dry lakebed when main gear wheels sank into unexpectedly soft soil. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the rudder, left wing, and strut, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper PA-28-235 experienced total engine power loss just after rotation at 60 knots and 60 feet during takeoff near Key West. Unable to restore power, the pilot landed straight ahead into mangrove trees, causing substantial damage to the aircraft while sustaining only minor passenger injuries.
summary: The pilot of a Piper PA-28-235 experienced total engine power loss just after rotation at 60 knots and 60 feet during takeoff near Key West. Unable to restore power, the pilot landed straight ahead into mangrove trees, causing substantial damage to the aircraft while sustaining only minor passenger injuries.

synopsis: The pin on the nose gear brace assembly that engages with the cam on the nose landing gear door actuator shaft was not seated inside the cam, which rendered the nose landing gear inoperative.
summary: The pilot experienced a nose gear failure during the traffic pattern entry, resulting in a gear-up landing and substantial belly damage. Postaccident examination revealed the nose gear brace pin was not seated in the cam, likely due to a rigging issue, despite the mechanic reporting the gear was within tolerance during the last annual inspection.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental Van's RV-3A was killed when the aircraft was destroyed during a formation break maneuver near Lakeland, Florida. The accident occurred when the right wing folded upward and separated from the fuselage, causing the airplane to roll inverted and enter a fatal dive.
summary: The pilot of an experimental Van's RV-3A was killed when the aircraft was destroyed during a formation break maneuver near Lakeland, Florida. The accident occurred when the right wing folded upward and separated from the fuselage, causing the airplane to roll inverted and enter a fatal dive.

synopsis: The pilot of an Air Tractor AT-502B conducting an agricultural flight near Forbes, Missouri, was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed nose-down into tree-covered terrain. No distress calls or mechanical issues were reported prior to the accident, and a detailed wreckage examination is pending.
summary: The pilot of an Air Tractor AT-502B conducting an agricultural flight near Forbes, Missouri, was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed nose-down into tree-covered terrain. No distress calls or mechanical issues were reported prior to the accident, and a detailed wreckage examination is pending.

synopsis: A NetJets Textron 680A crew encountered fuel pressure and electrical failures during approach to Laredo, leading to dual engine flameouts and an off-airport landing on a highway. The accident, which caused substantial damage and one fatality, was attributed to a fractured right engine fuel tube assembly and a failed starter generator with a bent shaft and broken cooling fan.
summary: A NetJets Textron 680A crew encountered fuel pressure and electrical failures during approach to Laredo, leading to dual engine flameouts and an off-airport landing on a highway. The accident, which caused substantial damage and one fatality, was attributed to a fractured right engine fuel tube assembly and a failed starter generator with a bent shaft and broken cooling fan.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airplane control during takeoff, which resulted in a runway excursion and collision with terrain.
summary: During takeoff, the pilot reported the aircraft suddenly turned left and departed the runway, striking a terrain wall with the right wingtip. The pilot attributed the accident to no mechanical malfunctions, as post-accident examinations found no flight control anomalies.

synopsis: The flight instructor's delayed remedial action during the student pilot's miscalculated landing flare which resulted in a hard landing and the nose landing gear collapsing.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot experienced a hard landing and bounce during a student-led final approach in the traffic pattern. The nose gear collapsed when the instructor attempted a go-around, causing substantial damage to the tunnel structure, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: A Cessna 177RG pilot and passenger were fatally injured when the aircraft was substantially damaged during takeoff from Basham Field. The accident occurred after the left wingtip struck a tree and an irrigation pipe, causing structural separation and loss of control before the airplane impacted a cornfield.
summary: A Cessna 177RG pilot and passenger were fatally injured when the aircraft was substantially damaged during takeoff from Basham Field. The accident occurred after the left wingtip struck a tree and an irrigation pipe, causing structural separation and loss of control before the airplane impacted a cornfield.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airspeed and encounter with a tailwind while landing on a rough runway, which resulted in a runway overrun and subsequent nose over.
summary: The pilot landed a single-engine airplane on a short, rough runway with a 17-knot tailwind and high groundspeed, causing an overrun and nose-over. The pilot attributed the accident to the strong tailwind and poor surface reducing braking effectiveness, while data confirmed excessive approach speed.

aircraft: Scoda Aeronautica Ltda SUPER PETREL XP
synopsis: A private pilot flying a Super Petrel XP seaplane struck a 7-inch wave at 45 knots during a water takeoff in Long Island Sound. The impact caused the aircraft to break apart and sink, resulting in substantial damage to the fuselage, though both occupants were rescued uninjured.
summary: A private pilot flying a Super Petrel XP seaplane struck a 7-inch wave at 45 knots during a water takeoff in Long Island Sound. The impact caused the aircraft to break apart and sink, resulting in substantial damage to the fuselage, though both occupants were rescued uninjured.

synopsis: A commercial pilot with a suspended certificate and expired medical flew an experimental Piper PA-20 from Yakutat to Cordova using automotive fuel. The aircraft impacted mountainous terrain in instrument meteorological conditions, destroying the airplane and fatally injuring the pilot.
summary: A commercial pilot with a suspended certificate and expired medical flew an experimental Piper PA-20 from Yakutat to Cordova using automotive fuel. The aircraft impacted mountainous terrain in instrument meteorological conditions, destroying the airplane and fatally injuring the pilot.

synopsis: The pilot and passenger of an experimental Comp Air CA6-WB were fatally injured when the aircraft separated into fuselage and wings during a Part 91 flight near Nicholasville, Kentucky. Witnesses reported a grinding noise and popping sound before the airplane entered an inverted, near-vertical descent and impacted terrain.
summary: The pilot and passenger of an experimental Comp Air CA6-WB were fatally injured when the aircraft separated into fuselage and wings during a Part 91 flight near Nicholasville, Kentucky. Witnesses reported a grinding noise and popping sound before the airplane entered an inverted, near-vertical descent and impacted terrain.

synopsis: Delta Air Lines flight 2351 (A319) and American Airlines flight 3161 (B737-800) were involved in a runway incursion at Boston Logan while DAL2351 was landing on runway 33L and AAL3161 was taking off from runway 27. DAL2351 executed a go-around after AAL3161 began its takeoff roll, resulting in a closest proximity of 670 feet with no injuries or damage.
summary: Delta Air Lines flight 2351 (A319) and American Airlines flight 3161 (B737-800) were involved in a runway incursion at Boston Logan while DAL2351 was landing on runway 33L and AAL3161 was taking off from runway 27. DAL2351 executed a go-around after AAL3161 began its takeoff roll, resulting in a closest proximity of 670 feet with no injuries or damage.

synopsis: A pilot and two passengers were killed when a Piper PA-24-250 crashed into a field near Geauga County Airport during a VFR approach. The aircraft entered a steep, nose-down descent after a sharp right turn, resulting in substantial damage with no pre-impact mechanical failure identified.
summary: A pilot and two passengers were killed when a Piper PA-24-250 crashed into a field near Geauga County Airport during a VFR approach. The aircraft entered a steep, nose-down descent after a sharp right turn, resulting in substantial damage with no pre-impact mechanical failure identified.

synopsis: A Piper PA-28-181 pilot and two passengers were fatally injured when the aircraft crashed into a wooded area near Bowie, Maryland, during a Part 91 night flight. The pilot declared an emergency and requested vectors to Freeway Airport but lost radar contact while maneuvering at low altitude, resulting in substantial damage with wing separation.
summary: A Piper PA-28-181 pilot and two passengers were fatally injured when the aircraft crashed into a wooded area near Bowie, Maryland, during a Part 91 night flight. The pilot declared an emergency and requested vectors to Freeway Airport but lost radar contact while maneuvering at low altitude, resulting in substantial damage with wing separation.

synopsis: During a Part 91 positioning flight, the pilot of an experimental Zodiac 601XL reported the main canopy latch failed and broke, causing the canopy to fly open and creating excessive drag. This forced a landing in a field where the aircraft nosed over, inverted, and sustained substantial damage, injuring the pilot.
summary: During a Part 91 positioning flight, the pilot of an experimental Zodiac 601XL reported the main canopy latch failed and broke, causing the canopy to fly open and creating excessive drag. This forced a landing in a field where the aircraft nosed over, inverted, and sustained substantial damage, injuring the pilot.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna 182S aborted a takeoff from Naples Airport after the aircraft felt sluggish and the stall warning horn activated upon liftoff. The airplane exited the damp runway, struck a concrete wall with its left wing, and sustained substantial damage, though all occupants were uninjured.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna 182S aborted a takeoff from Naples Airport after the aircraft felt sluggish and the stall warning horn activated upon liftoff. The airplane exited the damp runway, struck a concrete wall with its left wing, and sustained substantial damage, though all occupants were uninjured.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control during an off-airport landing.
summary: During an off-airport landing roll, a tailwheel-equipped airplane contacted ground dips, causing it to bounce, porpoise, and nose over when the propeller struck the ground. The aircraft came to rest inverted with substantial damage to the spar, fuselage, and rudder, with no preimpact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: During a glider tow flight near Whitewater, Wisconsin, a Bailey-Moyes Dragonfly tow plane pilot felt a cable anomaly at 30 feet and observed the hang glider pilot hanging from the base bar before falling to the ground. The hang glider pilot was fatally injured, while the tow plane pilot landed safely after releasing the glider, with no obvious defects found in the harness or carabiner.
summary: During a glider tow flight near Whitewater, Wisconsin, a Bailey-Moyes Dragonfly tow plane pilot felt a cable anomaly at 30 feet and observed the hang glider pilot hanging from the base bar before falling to the ground. The hang glider pilot was fatally injured, while the tow plane pilot landed safely after releasing the glider, with no obvious defects found in the harness or carabiner.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna 208B Part 135 flight reported a whining noise and propeller RPM surging en route from Coldfoot to Anaktuvuk Pass, leading to low power and a failed feathering attempt. The pilot executed a forced landing in a riverbed where the nose gear collapsed and the left wing struck the ground, causing substantial damage while the engine continued running after evacuation.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna 208B Part 135 flight reported a whining noise and propeller RPM surging en route from Coldfoot to Anaktuvuk Pass, leading to low power and a failed feathering attempt. The pilot executed a forced landing in a riverbed where the nose gear collapsed and the left wing struck the ground, causing substantial damage while the engine continued running after evacuation.

synopsis: During a Part 91 sightseeing flight, an Ultramagic SA N-300 balloon sustained substantial damage near Pahrump, Nevada, when increasing wind tilted the basket after touchdown. The pilot and two passengers were seriously injured, while seven others suffered minor injuries as the basket dragged, fractured, and partially inverted.
summary: During a Part 91 sightseeing flight, an Ultramagic SA N-300 balloon sustained substantial damage near Pahrump, Nevada, when increasing wind tilted the basket after touchdown. The pilot and two passengers were seriously injured, while seven others suffered minor injuries as the basket dragged, fractured, and partially inverted.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna TR182 operating under Part 91 reported that the left main landing gear suddenly collapsed while taxiing after landing on runway 16R at Van Nuys. This caused substantial damage to the left elevator, though the pilot was uninjured and the gear selector was found in the down position.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna TR182 operating under Part 91 reported that the left main landing gear suddenly collapsed while taxiing after landing on runway 16R at Van Nuys. This caused substantial damage to the left elevator, though the pilot was uninjured and the gear selector was found in the down position.

synopsis: During a Part 91 instructional flight, an Emigh Trojan A-2 suffered a propeller separation at 2,200 feet due to a fractured crankshaft flange. The flight instructor executed a forced landing in a vineyard, resulting in substantial damage to the aircraft, though both occupants were uninjured.

synopsis: A partial blockage of the pitot static system that precluded the airspeed indicator from displaying the correct airspeed which led to the faster landing speed and bounced landing.
summary: The pilot departed a private grass strip and landed with a faster-than-normal approach due to suspected low airspeed from a pitot obstruction. The aircraft bounced, broke the nose gear, nosed over, and inverted, causing substantial damage to the wing and stabilizer, though post-accident inspection found no confirmed blockage.

aircraft: Burkhart Grob Flugzeugbau G103 TWIN ASTIR
synopsis: The flight instructor's improper planning during the simulated aborted launch which resulted in a touchdown on unsuitable terrain.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot practicing an immediate landing after liftoff in a glider overshot the runway and landed on a downward sloping hill. The glider pivoted and sustained substantial rudder damage, with the instructor attributing the incident to insufficient remaining runway and inadequate terrain briefing.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental Lancair Legacy 2000, N84BZ, substantially damaged the aircraft during a go-around at Whiteman Airport after failing to verify landing gear extension. Ground contact with the flaps impinged aileron control, causing the airplane to strike a fence and come to rest in a parking lot.
summary: The pilot of an experimental Lancair Legacy 2000, N84BZ, substantially damaged the aircraft during a go-around at Whiteman Airport after failing to verify landing gear extension. synopsis: The pilot of a Cirrus SR22 experienced total engine failure at 7,000 feet due to metal fragments in the oil system. He attempted a forced landing at Kee Field but overshot the runway, striking a fence and guardrail, resulting in substantial damage to the aircraft.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to remove the maintenance spacer before takeoff, which resulted in restricted flight control movement and a loss of control.
summary: During takeoff, the pilot lost control when a plastic maintenance spacer left on the elevator shaft restricted control movement, causing a steep climb and terrain impact. The accident resulted in substantial fuselage damage, with no other pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to taxi the tailwheel-equipped airplane over uneven terrain while operating with limited forward visibility, which resulted in the left main landing gear entering a hole.
summary: The pilot landed a tailwheel-equipped airplane on grass between the runway and taxiway, where the tailwheel reduced forward visibility. Continuing over uneven terrain, the left main gear struck a hole, causing substantial lower fuselage damage due to the pilot's inability to detect the hazard.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing and subsequent go-around with a gusty right crosswind.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane veered left during a touch-and-go on Runway 12 due to a wind gust, causing a go-around failure where the left gear collapsed after exiting the runway. The aircraft sustained substantial wing damage, with the pilot reporting no pre-accident mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: A Cessna 402C Part 135 flight crew executed an ILS approach in low ceilings, but the pilot flying reduced power early and over-flared, causing the aircraft to float and land long on a wet runway. The pilot attempted an aggressive exit at the runway end, aborted, and subsequently overran, collapsing the right main gear and seriously injuring one passenger.

synopsis: An instrument-rated private pilot flying a Cessna 172S solo at night deviated from the planned Mountain Road VFR transition and continued northbound over mountainous terrain near Willard, Utah. The aircraft impacted terrain at approximately 9,000 feet MSL, destroying the airplane and fatally injuring the pilot.
summary: An instrument-rated private pilot flying a Cessna 172S solo at night deviated from the planned Mountain Road VFR transition and continued northbound over mountainous terrain near Willard, Utah. synopsis: The pilot and flight instructor's failure to maintain directional control while maneuvering on the runway, which resulted in a runway excursion. summary: During final approach in mountainous terrain, a pilot executed a go-around after floating down the runway but could not maintain terrain clearance. The pilot intentionally landed on a rocky hillside to avoid obstacles, resulting in the aircraft nosing over and resting inverted with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to ensure clearance while taxiing, which resulted in contact with another airplane that was performing an engine run-up. synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane veered right after a 3-point landing on runway 27, exiting the surface despite left rudder input. The aircraft pivoted 180° in grass, damaging the left aileron and elevator, with no pre-accident mechanical failures found.

aircraft: Diamond Aircraft Ind Inc DA 40 NG
synopsis: During a Part 91 instructional flight in a Diamond DA40 NG, a flight instructor and student pilot sustained injuries after a loud bang caused engine power to drop below 40% during climb following a go-around. synopsis: A private pilot and passenger were seriously injured when their experimental Flight Star II SC descended shortly after takeoff near Mulberry, Florida. The airplane struck soybeans, nosed over, and sustained substantial damage, resulting in serious injury to the pilot with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's excessive braking during the landing roll, which resulted in a nose over.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane nosed over on a turf runway after excessive braking caused the aircraft to veer left following an initial right excursion. The pilot attributed the loss of control to unfamiliarity with the aircraft's original mechanical drum brakes compared to modern hydraulic systems, resulting in substantial wing damage.

synopsis: The pilot's improper flare which resulted in a hard landing and their subsequent loss control of during a go-around. Contributing to the accident was the flight instructor's inadequate remedial action.

The aircraft subsequently struck an airport sign with the right wing, resulting in substantial damage.

summary: The pilot reported that during landing rollout, the aircraft veered left despite right rudder application, ground-looped after tailwheel contact, and departed the runway. The left wing and elevator struck terrain causing substantial damage, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: An inadvertent collision with a large wave during touchdown on a river, which resulted in a subsequent bounce and hard landing.
summary: The pilot of an amphibious airplane executed a go-around on the first approach due to choppy water but struck a large wave on the second approach due to flat light. This caused a hard landing that collapsed the left float strut and damaged the left elevator, with no preimpact mechanical malfunctions reported.

synopsis: The pilot's exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack during the initial climb, which led to an aerodynamic stall and a loss of airplane control at too low of an altitude to recover. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's lack of recent experience in the airplane.
summary: The pilot of an experimental air racing airplane stalled during initial climb after exceeding the critical angle of attack while attempting a familiarization flight. After reducing descent to communicate, the pilot executed a steep approach, overran the runway, and impacted trees, causing substantial damage to the engine mount, left wing, and fuselage.

summary: A student pilot flying a glider extended the downwind leg for a departing tow plane, resulting in a high, fast approach without dive brake use. The glider landed near the runway end, struck a person on the ground causing serious injury, and ground looped with substantial wing damage.

summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane ground looped left during landing on runway 05 due to a wind gust lifting the left wing. Despite control inputs, the right wing contacted the runway, collapsing the gear and causing substantial damage with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: A commercial pilot flying an Air Tractor AT-502B on an aerial application mission experienced left brake failure and gear collapse during landing rollout. summary: A commercial pilot flying an Air Tractor AT-502B on an aerial application mission experienced left brake failure and gear collapse during landing rollout. summary: The pilot of a Piper PA-18-150 conducting a Part 135 aerial survey near Mekoryuk, Alaska, experienced partial then total engine power loss at 200 feet AGL. summary: During landing in high density altitude, the pilot bounced, attempted a go-around, and ground-looped after failing to establish a positive climb. synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll.

synopsis: A pilot ferrying a Mooney M20 with a known No. 5 cylinder issue diverted to Tallahassee International Airport due to engine surging. summary: A pilot ferrying a Mooney M20 with a known No. 5 cylinder issue diverted to Tallahassee International Airport due to engine surging. The crew returned to Thessaloniki for an uneventful landing after the blade separation breached the cabin window and damaged the horizontal stabilizer.

summary: The pilot of a Glasair 1RG conducting a Part 91 flight test lost engine power at 2,000–3,000 feet due to an empty header tank despite the transfer pump being on. The pilot executed a forced landing to a road, struck a culvert while avoiding obstacles, and sustained minor injuries with substantial damage to the forward fuselage.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental Vans RV-12 reported a total engine power loss and G3X display failure shortly after departing Blake Field Airport. He executed a forced landing to a field, sustaining substantial damage to the horizontal stabilizer, while both occupants remained uninjured.
summary: The pilot of an experimental Vans RV-12 reported a total engine power loss and G3X display failure shortly after departing Blake Field Airport. He executed a forced landing to a field, sustaining substantial damage to the horizontal stabilizer, while both occupants remained uninjured.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from an antenna while maneuvering during a low-level aerial application flight.
summary: During a low-level aerial application pass, a pilot reported the aircraft struck an antenna inside a fenced area, causing engine failure and a forced landing. The impact resulted in substantial damage to the airframe and a post-impact fire, with the propeller hub found near the damaged antenna.

synopsis: During a Part 91 test flight of an experimental Montana Coyote, the pilot was fatally injured when the aircraft entered a descending spiral and crashed near Fredericksburg, Virginia. Post-accident examination revealed the left aileron torque tube separated from the fuselage bellcrank with no bending or witness marks.
summary: During a Part 91 test flight of an experimental Montana Coyote, the pilot was fatally injured when the aircraft entered a descending spiral and crashed near Fredericksburg, Virginia. Post-accident examination revealed the left aileron torque tube separated from the fuselage bellcrank with no bending or witness marks.

synopsis: Two pilots operating a Canadair CF-5D on a Part 91 instructional flight near Mojave, California, experienced dual engine fire warnings during the landing roll. The aircraft stopped on the runway and sustained substantial fuselage and empennage damage from a fire that started after white vapor was observed trailing from the left side.
summary: Two pilots operating a Canadair CF-5D on a Part 91 instructional flight near Mojave, California, experienced dual engine fire warnings during the landing roll. The aircraft stopped on the runway and sustained substantial fuselage and empennage damage from a fire that started after white vapor was observed trailing from the left side.

aircraft: Tag Aviation Pty Ltd Titanium Explorer
synopsis: A pilot flying a Tag Aviation Titanium Explorer gyrocopter, N665TE, died after the engine stopped and the aircraft crashed into trees near Larkspur, Colorado. The witness reported the engine was struggling before failure, and the rotor tachometer indicated 500 rpm at impact.
summary: A pilot flying a Tag Aviation Titanium Explorer gyrocopter, N665TE, died after the engine stopped and the aircraft crashed into trees near Larkspur, Colorado. The witness reported the engine was struggling before failure, and the rotor tachometer indicated 500 rpm at impact.

synopsis: The sole pilot of a Luscombe 8A was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed in a field 800 feet northwest of a private airstrip in Canton, Texas. The accident occurred during a personal flight after the pilot likely took off into a north wind, resulting in a steep, nose-down impact.
summary: The sole pilot of a Luscombe 8A was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed in a field 800 feet northwest of a private airstrip in Canton, Texas. The accident occurred during a personal flight after the pilot likely took off into a north wind, resulting in a steep, nose-down impact.

aircraft: Remos Acft Gmbh Flugzeugbau REMOS GX
synopsis: A student pilot and flight instructor in a Remos GX N126GX experienced a fractured rear elevator control rod during a go-around at Glendale Regional Airport. The resulting loss of pitch control caused the aircraft to impact terrain on final approach, sustaining substantial damage while both occupants remained uninjured.
summary: A student pilot and flight instructor in a Remos GX N126GX experienced a fractured rear elevator control rod during a go-around at Glendale Regional Airport. The resulting loss of pitch control caused the aircraft to impact terrain on final approach, sustaining substantial damage while both occupants remained uninjured.

synopsis: The first officer's excessive aft sidestick input following a bounced landing, and the line check pilot's delayed remedial action, which resulted in an increase in the airplane's pitch attitude and a subsequent tailstrike.
summary: During a Delta Air Lines Part 121 landing at LGA, a First Officer trainee caused a tailstrike by applying excessive aft sidestick input after a hard bounce. The incident resulted in substantial fuselage damage due to an increased pitch angle of 10.02°, though no injuries occurred.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to compensate for the gusty and variable wind conditions, which resulted in a loss of control and collision with trees during takeoff.
summary: An airline transport pilot attempting takeoff from a grass runway in variable wind and light rain encountered a sudden right crosswind shift at 30 feet. Despite leveling the wings, the aircraft rolled right and struck trees, causing substantial damage to the wings and fuselage with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during takeoff in gusty crosswind conditions.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane lost directional control during takeoff on runway 20 due to a gusty crosswind causing the aircraft to weathervane right. The airplane exited the runway, struck a ditch, and collapsed the left main gear, resulting in substantial damage to the fuselage and left wing.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll, in variable wind conditions.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane ground looped on runway 33 during landing roll after a side gust pushed the left gear off the surface. This caused the right gear to collapse and the right wing to strike the ground, resulting in substantial damage with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from a power line during a low-level aerial application flight.
summary: During aerial application operations, a helicopter pilot struck power lines while maneuvering around a tree, causing a loss of main rotor RPM and an autorotation into a cornfield. The subsequent landing resulted in substantial damage to the rotor system, engine mount, fuselage, and tailboom, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental Vans RV-4 was fatally injured when the aircraft was substantially damaged near Yuba City, California, during a personal flight. The airplane overshot runway 35 after a turn back, struck a perimeter fence, and spun 270° before coming to rest upright in a field.
summary: The pilot of an experimental Vans RV-4 was fatally injured when the aircraft was substantially damaged near Yuba City, California, during a personal flight. The airplane overshot runway 35 after a turn back, struck a perimeter fence, and spun 270° before coming to rest upright in a field.

synopsis: The pilot's inability to see and avoid a piece of loose wire in a field during an off-airport landing in a glider, which resulted in a ground loop. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's inability to maintain a safe position behind the tow airplane after taking off which required them to release from tow at too low of an altitude to return to the airport.
summary: A glider pilot released the tow rope at 300 ft AGL after losing position behind the tow airplane due to a wind gust. The pilot landed off-airport, where a wingtip caught hidden wire, causing a ground loop and fracturing the tail boom with no pre-impact mechanical anomalies.

synopsis: The pilot of a Dakota Cub Super 18 was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed into water near Plymouth, Massachusetts, during a personal flight. The accident resulted from engine failure caused by fuel starvation and water contamination in the fuel system.
summary: The pilot of a Dakota Cub Super 18 was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed into water near Plymouth, Massachusetts, during a personal flight. The accident resulted from engine failure caused by fuel starvation and water contamination in the fuel system.

synopsis: Degraded engine and propeller performance during hot and high-density altitude operations, which resulted in a high descent rate and subsequent hard landing.
summary: A remote pilot operating an experimental Leigh Aerosystems E100 UAS during a hover test at Bisbee Douglas International Airport experienced a hard landing due to degraded engine and propeller performance caused by high-density altitude. The aircraft sustained substantial damage with the right spar and wing separating from the fuselage, but no injuries occurred.

synopsis: An encounter with convectively induced turbulence during cruise flight in an area of forecast thunderstorm activity.
summary: SkyWest flight 3723 encountered severe convective turbulence at FL370 while en route to Atlanta, causing a flight attendant to sustain a serious head injury. The crew reported no radar or visual warnings before the encounter, which resulted in an altitude loss and a diversion to Jacksonville.

synopsis: The commercial pilot of an experimental Vans RV-8A experienced intermittent engine power loss after switching fuel tanks at 9,000 feet, leading to a forced landing on runway 11. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the wings, firewall, and engine mount, though the pilot remained uninjured.
summary: The commercial pilot of an experimental Vans RV-8A experienced intermittent engine power loss after switching fuel tanks at 9,000 feet, leading to a forced landing on runway 11. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the wings, firewall, and engine mount, though the pilot remained uninjured.

synopsis: The pilot's improper pitch control during landing, which resulted in a bounced landing, nose landing gear collapse, and nose over.
summary: During landing, the pilot reported the airplane porpoised, causing nose gear collapse, a runway excursion, and an inverted nosed-over stop. The pilot stated no preimpact mechanical malfunctions occurred, yet the fuselage, vertical stabilizer, and rudder sustained substantial damage.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate preflight and in-flight monitoring of the fuel quantity, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion.
summary: The pilot, distracted by personal matters and failing to visually verify fuel, experienced engine power loss after both tanks depleted during cruise at 9,500 ft. He attempted a forced landing on a logging road but struck trees, causing substantial damage to the right wing and fuselage.

synopsis: The pilot of a DeHavilland DHC-2, N791PW, reported that the right brake failed to respond during landing at a remote airstrip near Nondalton, Alaska. The aircraft ground looped and departed the runway, causing substantial damage to the right wing and elevator while the pilot remained uninjured.
summary: The pilot of a DeHavilland DHC-2, N791PW, reported that the right brake failed to respond during landing at a remote airstrip near Nondalton, Alaska. The aircraft ground looped and departed the runway, causing substantial damage to the right wing and elevator while the pilot remained uninjured.

synopsis: The pilot's exceedance of the airplane's performance capabilities in mountainous terrain, which resulted in a forced landing.
summary: The pilot departed an airplane at 11,000 ft density altitude and could not maintain altitude while climbing over mountainous terrain. He executed a forced landing in a grass field, resulting in substantial damage to the wings and empennage with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate lookout, which resulted in a collision with ground equipment during taxi.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane struck obscured ground equipment during a fast-taxi maneuver after landing on a private gravel airstrip. A gust of wind caused a long touchdown, leading to landing gear collapse and substantial left wing damage, with no preimpact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to perform a take-off in high-density-altitude, gusting-crosswind conditions, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall, hard landing and subsequent nose-over.
summary: The pilot reported that after fueling, a gusting crosswind caused an aerodynamic stall during takeoff at 10,700 ft density altitude. The aircraft dropped, struck an earth berm, and nosed over, resulting in substantial damage to the right wing, fuselage, and rudder.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate fuel planning and in-flight decision making, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion.
summary: The pilot of an amphibious float-equipped airplane experienced total engine power loss twice during a straight-in approach due to fuel exhaustion. He executed a forced landing in a field, striking a fence and sustaining substantial wing damage, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: A pilot flying a Robinson R44 during agricultural spraying encountered repeated low rotor rpm warnings caused by an unsecured governor control unit. The pilot executed an autorotation into a cornfield, resulting in substantial damage to the helicopter, though the pilot was not injured.
summary: A pilot flying a Robinson R44 during agricultural spraying encountered repeated low rotor rpm warnings caused by an unsecured governor control unit. The pilot executed an autorotation into a cornfield, resulting in substantial damage to the helicopter, though the pilot was not injured.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper PA-28-161 reported that the right main landing gear collapsed while taxiing to the run-up area at San Bernardino International Airport. This caused the right wing to impact the taxiway, resulting in substantial damage to the aircraft, though the pilot and passenger were uninjured.
summary: The pilot of a Piper PA-28-161 reported that the right main landing gear collapsed while taxiing to the run-up area at San Bernardino International Airport. This caused the right wing to impact the taxiway, resulting in substantial damage to the aircraft, though the pilot and passenger were uninjured.

synopsis: The failure of the pilot to verify the loading hose had been disconnected before taking off and the failure of the loader to disconnect the fuel hose from the helicopter.
summary: A helicopter pilot took off from a mobile loading platform after seeing a loader descend stairs, but the aircraft impacted terrain when a dry break coupler remained attached to the refueling hose. The accident caused substantial damage, and the pilot failed to visually verify hose disconnection or receive a thumbs-up signal.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll.
summary: The pilot reported that while giving rides, the airplane's right main gear contacted tall grass, causing a ground loop and runway exit. The left wing and elevator struck the ground, resulting in the aircraft nosing over inverted with substantial damage to the left wing, elevator, and empennage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to extend the landing gear before landing.
summary: During approach, a pilot's before-landing checklist was interrupted by ATC, causing him to forget to lower the landing gear. After ATC alerted him at 20 feet, the aircraft touched down with gear retracted, resulting in substantial damage to the left wing and aileron.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper PA-24-260 sustained serious injuries when the aircraft impacted trees near Baraboo, Wisconsin, during an instrument approach. The pilot reported the engine failed to produce climb power despite no audible sputtering, causing the accident in moderate haze from wildfires.
summary: The pilot of a Piper PA-24-260 sustained serious injuries when the aircraft impacted trees near Baraboo, Wisconsin, during an instrument approach. The pilot reported the engine failed to produce climb power despite no audible sputtering, causing the accident in moderate haze from wildfires.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane during takeoff, resulting in an aerodynamic stall and impact with water.
summary: The pilot of an amphibious airplane stalled during takeoff from glassy water after pulling the control stick hard to break surface tension. The resulting nose-high attitude caused the left float to impact the water, break loose, and strike the left wing, causing substantial damage and sinking.

synopsis: The pilot and passenger of an Enstrom F-28F helicopter experienced an engine fire during ground operations after the engine lost power and restarted with smoke and flames. Despite multiple attempts to shut down the engine using mixture, ignition, and manual fuel controls, the pilot and passenger evacuated as the helicopter burned.
summary: The pilot and passenger of an Enstrom F-28F helicopter experienced an engine fire during ground operations after the engine lost power and restarted with smoke and flames. Despite multiple attempts to shut down the engine using mixture, ignition, and manual fuel controls, the pilot and passenger evacuated as the helicopter burned.

synopsis: The pilot's distracted attention on approach to landing on their failure to attain a proper touchdown point and his inability to stop the landing roll on the grass runway.,
summary: The pilot, while on approach to a short-field grass runway, failed to adjust his aimpoint due to distraction. The aircraft overran the runway at 70 mph, sustaining substantial damage to the engine mount and fuselage after coming to rest in a drainage culvert.

synopsis: During a Part 91 instructional flight in a Piper PA-28-180, the flight instructor and student pilot suffered minor injuries when the engine lost power at 50 to 60 feet during a fourth takeoff. The subsequent forced landing resulted in substantial damage to the fuselage, wings, and empennage after the aircraft struck trees.
summary: During a Part 91 instructional flight in a Piper PA-28-180, the flight instructor and student pilot suffered minor injuries when the engine lost power at 50 to 60 feet during a fourth takeoff. The subsequent forced landing resulted in substantial damage to the fuselage, wings, and empennage after the aircraft struck trees.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare which resulted in a stall and a hard bounced landing.
summary: During his first solo glider flight on final approach, the pilot flared at 5-8 feet, causing the aircraft to pitch up, stall, and bounce three times. This resulted in substantial fuselage damage, with the pilot reporting no pre-accident malfunctions.

synopsis: The pilot's distraction during taxi, which resulted in a taxiway excursion.
summary: The pilot reported that while taxiing from the ramp to the runway, distraction by a helicopter caused the airplane to inadvertently enter a grassy area and impact a drainage pipe. This resulted in substantial fuselage damage, with no mechanical malfunctions reported prior to the accident.

synopsis: A flight instructor and student pilot in a Cessna 152 experienced total engine power loss at 1,500 to 2,000 feet agl during a Part 91 training flight. The subsequent forced landing resulted in substantial damage after the left wing struck a tree, with post-accident testing revealing a ruptured left fuel tank and rough engine operation.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot in a Cessna 152 experienced total engine power loss at 1,500 to 2,000 feet agl during a Part 91 training flight. The subsequent forced landing resulted in substantial damage after the left wing struck a tree, with post-accident testing revealing a ruptured left fuel tank and rough engine operation.

synopsis: The flight instructor's failure to maintain directional control during landing.
summary: During an instructional landing, the flight instructor overcorrected rudder inputs while realigning the aircraft, causing it to veer off the runway and strike a tetrahedron. The nose gear separated, resulting in substantial damage to the forward fuselage and wings, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: A commercial pilot flying a Piper J3C-65 near Richmond, Texas, struck a house roof while operating under Part 91, sustaining serious injuries and substantial aircraft damage. The pilot had no memory of the event, and post-accident examination showed no engine power indications on the propeller.
summary: A commercial pilot flying a Piper J3C-65 near Richmond, Texas, struck a house roof while operating under Part 91, sustaining serious injuries and substantial aircraft damage. The pilot had no memory of the event, and post-accident examination showed no engine power indications on the propeller.

synopsis: A pilot flying a De Havilland DHC-3 Otter on a Part 135 air taxi flight attempted to land on water near Sucia Island due to inclement weather. The left wingtip and pontoon struck the water at 4 feet altitude, causing the aircraft to impact rocks and sustain substantial damage, followed by a post-accident fire.
summary: A pilot flying a De Havilland DHC-3 Otter on a Part 135 air taxi flight attempted to land on water near Sucia Island due to inclement weather. The left wingtip and pontoon struck the water at 4 feet altitude, causing the aircraft to impact rocks and sustain substantial damage, followed by a post-accident fire.

synopsis: The private pilot of an experimental Zenith Zodiac 601HDS was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed into a lake near Sioux City, Iowa, during a VFR cross-country flight. The accident occurred in deteriorating weather conditions, with the pilot lacking an instrument rating and the aircraft sustaining structural separation upon impact.
summary: The private pilot of an experimental Zenith Zodiac 601HDS was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed into a lake near Sioux City, Iowa, during a VFR cross-country flight. The accident occurred in deteriorating weather conditions, with the pilot lacking an instrument rating and the aircraft sustaining structural separation upon impact.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental Czech Aircraft Works Mermaid Skeeter 2, N42SK, was seriously injured when the aircraft impacted Yale Lake during a low-altitude right banking turn. The airplane was substantially damaged and submerged while operating under Part 91 personal flight rules.
summary: The pilot of an experimental Czech Aircraft Works Mermaid Skeeter 2, N42SK, was seriously injured when the aircraft impacted Yale Lake during a low-altitude right banking turn. The airplane was substantially damaged and submerged while operating under Part 91 personal flight rules.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from power lines while conducting a low-altitude aerial application.
summary: During a low-altitude aerial herbicide application, a helicopter struck power lines and impacted terrain, sustaining substantial damage to the tailboom, main rotor, and fuselage. The pilot was seriously injured, and the operator reported no preaccident mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing with a right crosswind, which resulted in the airplane's impact with terrain.
summary: During landing, the pilot encountered a right crosswind causing left drift and attempted a go-around with opposite rudder and increased power. The left wing contacted the ground, resulting in terrain impact and substantial damage to the right wing, tail, and empennage with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The separation of the right main landing gear axle, which resulted in a loss of control during the landing roll.
summary: The pilot reported that after a smooth touchdown, the aircraft veered right uncontrollably, causing both main wheels to separate and the left wing to drag until stopping off the runway. Post-accident analysis suggests a right main gear axle fracture during touchdown caused the uncorrectable veer and subsequent gear separation.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a hard, bounced landing.
summary: The pilot reported a hard landing and two bounces during the flare, resulting in substantial lower fuselage damage. No pre-accident mechanical malfunctions were identified that would have prevented normal operation.

synopsis: A private pilot flying an experimental Kitfox III, N573TB, experienced a total engine power loss during approach to runway 14 at Ephraim Airport. The pilot executed a forced landing in a nearby field, resulting in substantial damage to both wings, though both occupants remained uninjured.
summary: A private pilot flying an experimental Kitfox III, N573TB, experienced a total engine power loss during approach to runway 14 at Ephraim Airport. The pilot executed a forced landing in a nearby field, resulting in substantial damage to both wings, though both occupants remained uninjured.

synopsis: The pilot of an Aero Commander Callair A-9B operating a Part 137 agricultural flight reported abrupt engine power loss at 50 feet AGL while spraying. This forced a landing into a soybean field, substantially damaging the ailerons, fuselage, empennage, and rudder, though the pilot was uninjured.
summary: The pilot of an Aero Commander Callair A-9B operating a Part 137 agricultural flight reported abrupt engine power loss at 50 feet AGL while spraying. This forced a landing into a soybean field, substantially damaging the ailerons, fuselage, empennage, and rudder, though the pilot was uninjured.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control during landing and the flight instructor's inadequate remedial action, which resulted in a ground loop.
summary: A student pilot and flight instructor were conducting a tailwheel endorsement training flight when the student ground looped during a three-point landing attempt. Excessive rudder inputs while correcting drift caused the ground loop, resulting in substantial damage to the right wing with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot and passenger of an American AA-1, N6132L, were seriously injured when the engine lost all power during descent from 3,000 to 1,500 feet near Martinsburg, West Virginia. The pilot attempted an emergency landing in a field, resulting in the right wing and engine separating from the fuselage and causing substantial damage.
summary: The pilot and passenger of an American AA-1, N6132L, were seriously injured when the engine lost all power during descent from 3,000 to 1,500 feet near Martinsburg, West Virginia. The pilot attempted an emergency landing in a field, resulting in the right wing and engine separating from the fuselage and causing substantial damage.

synopsis: Two pilots operating a Piper PA-24 for personal flight experienced a landing gear collapse shortly after touchdown at Medford Airport. Despite visual confirmation from air traffic control that the gear was down, the gear failed during the landing roll, causing substantial damage to the engine mount.
summary: Two pilots operating a Piper PA-24 for personal flight experienced a landing gear collapse shortly after touchdown at Medford Airport. Despite visual confirmation from air traffic control that the gear was down, the gear failed during the landing roll, causing substantial damage to the engine mount.

synopsis: The pilot of a Beech V35 experienced rough running and zero oil pressure shortly after takeoff, leading to total engine power loss and smoke. He performed a forced landing in a bean field, sustaining substantial damage to the right aileron due to an engine crankcase failure and oil loss.
summary: The pilot of a Beech V35 experienced rough running and zero oil pressure shortly after takeoff, leading to total engine power loss and smoke. He performed a forced landing in a bean field, sustaining substantial damage to the right aileron due to an engine crankcase failure and oil loss.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from a fuel farm fence while taxiing.
summary: The pilot reported that while taxiing near a fuel farm, the airplane's left wing struck a fence, causing substantial damage to the wing and fuselage. The pilot attributed the incident to insufficient obstacle clearance during the turn and noted no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: A Piper PA-22-150 carrying a pilot and two passengers crashed near Chitina, Alaska, while attempting to land at an uncharted airstrip. The aircraft impacted a riverbank in a left-wing-low attitude after witnesses heard the engine power increase, resulting in fatalities and a post-impact fire.
summary: A Piper PA-22-150 carrying a pilot and two passengers crashed near Chitina, Alaska, while attempting to land at an uncharted airstrip. The aircraft impacted a riverbank in a left-wing-low attitude after witnesses heard the engine power increase, resulting in fatalities and a post-impact fire.

synopsis: The pilot's inadvertent selection of the fuel selector valve to the OFF position resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel starvation and subsequent forced landing to a field.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane attempted manual gear extension during landing preparation but inadvertently moved the fuel selector to OFF instead of the hydraulic depressurization valve. This caused total engine power loss, forcing a field landing that resulted in substantial damage to the left wing and fuselage.

synopsis: A pilot operating a Piper PA-28-180 on a Part 91 personal flight was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed near Chandler, Arizona, shortly after departing runway 22R. Witnesses and video reported the engine sound ceased, followed by a sharp right turn and rapid descent into a commercial yard.
summary: A pilot operating a Piper PA-28-180 on a Part 91 personal flight was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed near Chandler, Arizona, shortly after departing runway 22R. Witnesses and video reported the engine sound ceased, followed by a sharp right turn and rapid descent into a commercial yard.

synopsis: During a maintenance ferry flight, a Delta Boeing 757-200 experienced a left engine fire at 12,000 feet while climbing from Atlanta. The crew successfully shut down the engine and discharged a fire bottle, returning for a safe landing; post-flight inspection revealed a tear in the outer diffuser case.
summary: During a maintenance ferry flight, a Delta Boeing 757-200 experienced a left engine fire at 12,000 feet while climbing from Atlanta. The crew successfully shut down the engine and discharged a fire bottle, returning for a safe landing; post-flight inspection revealed a tear in the outer diffuser case.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control during a turn, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall.
summary: During agricultural spray operations, a pilot stalled the aircraft while circling a parked vehicle. The plane entered a secondary stall during recovery, struck power lines and trees, and crashed into a residential yard, causing substantial damage with no reported mechanical failure.

synopsis: The flight instructor's failure to maintain clearance from obstacles during low altitude maneuvering, which resulted in a collision with a fence.
summary: A flight instructor and private pilot struck a barbed wire fence with the left wing during a low-altitude crosswind turn after a soft-field takeoff demonstration. The instructor landed, removed the wire, and returned home, though the wing sustained substantial damage with no mechanical failure reported.

synopsis: A Cessna 172G pilot conducting a Part 91 night flight was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed into an airport perimeter fence and adjacent road near Blackfoot, Idaho. The accident caused substantial damage to the airframe and propeller, with no witnesses or data available to determine the specific cause.
summary: A Cessna 172G pilot conducting a Part 91 night flight was fatally injured when the aircraft crashed into an airport perimeter fence and adjacent road near Blackfoot, Idaho. The accident caused substantial damage to the airframe and propeller, with no witnesses or data available to determine the specific cause.

synopsis: A commercial pilot was fatally injured when his Beech E18S crashed near Guymon, Oklahoma, shortly after departing runway 18. Witnesses observed the aircraft descending in a nose-low, left-wing-low attitude before impacting a field and burning, with no pre-impact mechanical failures found.
summary: A commercial pilot was fatally injured when his Beech E18S crashed near Guymon, Oklahoma, shortly after departing runway 18. Witnesses observed the aircraft descending in a nose-low, left-wing-low attitude before impacting a field and burning, with no pre-impact mechanical failures found.

synopsis: During a night instructional flight in a Cessna 172M, the engine lost power while descending to land, causing the flight instructor and private pilot to attempt a forced landing. A gust of wind from a canyon caused unexpected altitude loss, resulting in a hard landing where the aircraft nosed over, inverted, and sustained substantial damage.
summary: During a night instructional flight in a Cessna 172M, the engine lost power while descending to land, causing the flight instructor and private pilot to attempt a forced landing. A gust of wind from a canyon caused unexpected altitude loss, resulting in a hard landing where the aircraft nosed over, inverted, and sustained substantial damage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain the proper glidepath during the landing approach, which resulted in a touchdown prior to the runway threshold, impact of the main landing gear with the pavement edge.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane landed short of the runway threshold on final approach, striking a 12-inch pavement edge with the right main gear. This impact caused the aircraft to pitch nose down, overturn, and sustain substantial damage to the right wing lift strut, with no preaccident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to keep the tail rotor clear of an obstacle while attempting to land.
summary: During a right pedal turn for landing, the helicopter's tail rotor struck a fuel farm standpipe, causing instability. The pilot lowered the collective to land upright with no injuries, though the tail rotor blades and gearbox sustained substantial damage.

synopsis: During a Part 137 agricultural flight, the pilot of a Robinson R44 II helicopter reported airframe vibration and performed an autorotation after passing a tree line. The helicopter descended rapidly from about 20 feet, resulting in a hard landing and substantial damage to the airframe and tailboom.
summary: During a Part 137 agricultural flight, the pilot of a Robinson R44 II helicopter reported airframe vibration and performed an autorotation after passing a tree line. The helicopter descended rapidly from about 20 feet, resulting in a hard landing and substantial damage to the airframe and tailboom.

synopsis: A pilot and passenger were seriously injured when their Taylorcraft BC12-D suffered an engine failure shortly after departing Boyceville, Wisconsin. The engine sputtered and quit at 75 to 100 feet, causing the aircraft to impact a cornfield with substantial damage to the fuselage and wings.
summary: A pilot and passenger were seriously injured when their Taylorcraft BC12-D suffered an engine failure shortly after departing Boyceville, Wisconsin. The engine sputtered and quit at 75 to 100 feet, causing the aircraft to impact a cornfield with substantial damage to the fuselage and wings.

synopsis: The flight instructor and pilot receiving instruction's failure to verify that the landing gear was extended before landing, which resulted in a gear-up landing.
summary: A flight instructor and student landed an airplane with the gear retracted between the base turn and final approach, causing substantial fuselage damage. The accident resulted from a worn safety notch on the landing gear selector switch that allowed inadvertent movement to the UP position.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper PA-24-250 entered Class A airspace above 18,000 feet without clearance or an oxygen system. The aircraft impacted terrain after entering convective activity, destroying the airplane and killing the pilot.
summary: The pilot of a Piper PA-24-250 entered Class A airspace above 18,000 feet without clearance or an oxygen system. The aircraft impacted terrain after entering convective activity, destroying the airplane and killing the pilot.

synopsis: A pilot operating a Cirrus SR22T under Part 91 was fatally injured when the aircraft impacted terrain near Bend, Oregon. Preliminary data indicated the accident occurred after the left fuel tank sensor read zero gallons and the right tank read one gallon, resulting in a nose-down pitch and loss of control.
summary: A pilot operating a Cirrus SR22T under Part 91 was fatally injured when the aircraft impacted terrain near Bend, Oregon. Preliminary data indicated the accident occurred after the left fuel tank sensor read zero gallons and the right tank read one gallon, resulting in a nose-down pitch and loss of control.

synopsis: Marine One (VM1) and Envoy Air flight 3742 (ENY3742) experienced a loss of separation near DCA due to failed radio communications preventing the required 3-minute departure call. The aircraft passed within 0.82 miles laterally and 700 feet vertically, but both flights completed their missions without injury.
summary: Marine One (VM1) and Envoy Air flight 3742 (ENY3742) experienced a loss of separation near DCA due to failed radio communications preventing the required 3-minute departure call. The aircraft passed within 0.82 miles laterally and 700 feet vertically, but both flights completed their missions without injury.

synopsis: The in-flight opening of the engine cowling, which resulted in engine baffling separating from the airplane and impacting the right elevator.
summary: The pilot reported that seven minutes into flight, the right engine cowling opened and flapped, causing an emergency diversion and uneventful landing. Post-accident examination found separated engine baffling damaged the right elevator, though the cowling latch mechanism functioned normally.

synopsis: A private pilot and passenger were fatally injured when their Beech H35 crashed shortly after takeoff from Bogalusa, Louisiana, while operating under Part 91. The aircraft struck trees and caught fire, with the fuel selector found in the AUX position and no pre-accident engine abnormalities reported by witnesses.
summary: A private pilot and passenger were fatally injured when their Beech H35 crashed shortly after takeoff from Bogalusa, Louisiana, while operating under Part 91. The aircraft struck trees and caught fire, with the fuel selector found in the AUX position and no pre-accident engine abnormalities reported by witnesses.

synopsis: A flight instructor and student pilot in a Cessna 177B experienced total engine power loss at 1,500 ft AGL during S-turn practice. The instructor executed an emergency field landing where the aircraft struck vegetation and nosed over, causing substantial damage to the left wing and fuselage.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot in a Cessna 177B experienced total engine power loss at 1,500 ft AGL during S-turn practice. synopsis: The pilot's failure to ensure the canopy was properly locked before flight, which resulted in the canopy opening during takeoff.
summary: The pilot reported that during the takeoff roll of a local flight, the canopy opened and struck the right wing because he failed to push it up after locking. He aborted the takeoff and taxied back to the ramp with substantial canopy damage but no mechanical failures.

synopsis: A collision with a deer during landing.
summary: During final approach, the pilot aborted a landing after spotting a deer on the runway, but the aircraft struck the animal, causing a left yaw and substantial damage to the empennage and left flap. The pilot completed the landing on the remaining runway with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: Helicopter Transport Services pilots flying a Sikorsky CH-54A Skycrane on an aerial firefighting mission near Cove Fort, Utah, were fatally injured when the helicopter impacted rising terrain. The crash occurred during a right turn maneuver behind a knoll while the crew was verifying a water drop target.
summary: Helicopter Transport Services pilots flying a Sikorsky CH-54A Skycrane on an aerial firefighting mission near Cove Fort, Utah, were fatally injured when the helicopter impacted rising terrain. The crash occurred during a right turn maneuver behind a knoll while the crew was verifying a water drop target.

synopsis: An ATP Flight School Cessna 172S instructor and student were fatally injured when the aircraft crashed into Provo Bay shortly after takeoff from Runway 18. The accident occurred during an instrument training flight amid reported severe turbulence and observed dust formations, causing a rapid descent and impact with the water.
summary: An ATP Flight School Cessna 172S instructor and student were fatally injured when the aircraft crashed into Provo Bay shortly after takeoff from Runway 18. The accident occurred during an instrument training flight amid reported severe turbulence and observed dust formations, causing a rapid descent and impact with the water.
