synopsis: A private pilot flying an experimental Avid Mark IV was fatally injured when the aircraft impacted trees and terrain near Arp, Texas, during a low-altitude maneuver. The pilot entered a steep left bank and descending turn after takeoff, with no preimpact mechanical or flight control anomalies found.
summary: A private pilot flying an experimental Avid Mark IV was fatally injured when the aircraft impacted trees and terrain near Arp, Texas, during a low-altitude maneuver. The pilot entered a steep left bank and descending turn after takeoff, with no preimpact mechanical or flight control anomalies found.

synopsis: The pilot of a Mooney M20E experienced engine roughness and power loss shortly after departing Conway-Horry County Airport for an IFR flight. Unable to return to the airport, the aircraft struck trees and sustained substantial damage, though the pilot remained uninjured.
summary: The pilot of a Mooney M20E experienced engine roughness and power loss shortly after departing Conway-Horry County Airport for an IFR flight. Unable to return to the airport, the aircraft struck trees and sustained substantial damage, though the pilot remained uninjured.

synopsis: A pilot was fatally injured when a PZL-Bielsko B1-PW-5 glider, N105WS, was substantially damaged during an auto-tow launch near Briggs, Texas. After release at 1,000 ft, the glider yawed right, entered a descending spiral, and impacted terrain in a near-vertical attitude.
summary: A pilot was fatally injured when a PZL-Bielsko B1-PW-5 glider, N105WS, was substantially damaged during an auto-tow launch near Briggs, Texas. After release at 1,000 ft, the glider yawed right, entered a descending spiral, and impacted terrain in a near-vertical attitude.

synopsis: The fuel truck driver's distraction and inadequate visual lookout, which resulted in a collision with an airplane.
summary: After landing and exiting the runway, a pilot stopped past the hold short line for the after-landing checklist when a fuel truck struck the aircraft's empennage. The truck driver reported looking at his phone while crossing the runway, causing him to miss the airplane until it was too late to stop.

synopsis: A private pilot flying a Piper PA-32-260 from Martin County to Ocracoke Island experienced a total engine power loss at 3,000 feet. The pilot attempted a forced landing in a wooded area, but the left wing struck a tree, causing substantial damage to the aircraft and minor injuries to the occupants.
summary: A private pilot flying a Piper PA-32-260 from Martin County to Ocracoke Island experienced a total engine power loss at 3,000 feet. The pilot attempted a forced landing in a wooded area, but the left wing struck a tree, causing substantial damage to the aircraft and minor injuries to the occupants.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental Velocity 173 experienced total engine power loss at 7,500 feet, likely due to improper mixture control settings, and diverted to Zelmer Memorial Airpark. The aircraft departed the runway during landing and sustained substantial damage to the fuselage, right wing, and canard, though all occupants were uninjured.
summary: The pilot of an experimental Velocity 173 experienced total engine power loss at 7,500 feet, likely due to improper mixture control settings, and diverted to Zelmer Memorial Airpark. The aircraft departed the runway during landing and sustained substantial damage to the fuselage, right wing, and canard, though all occupants were uninjured.

synopsis: The pilot of a Van's RV-8, C-GFWR, ground looped right during landing rollout at Great Falls International Airport after applying power to correct a veer. The accident, occurring on the first flight since a tailwheel replacement, caused left main gear collapse and substantial damage to the wing and fuselage.
summary: The pilot of a Van's RV-8, C-GFWR, ground looped right during landing rollout at Great Falls International Airport after applying power to correct a veer. The accident, occurring on the first flight since a tailwheel replacement, caused left main gear collapse and substantial damage to the wing and fuselage.

synopsis: A flight instructor and student in a Cessna 180 were seriously injured when the aircraft crashed near La Center, Washington, during a Part 91 instructional flight. The instructor reported that the engine lost power, causing the airplane to come up short and impact the trees.
summary: A flight instructor and student in a Cessna 180 were seriously injured when the aircraft crashed near La Center, Washington, during a Part 91 instructional flight. The instructor reported that the engine lost power, causing the airplane to come up short and impact the trees.

synopsis: The pilot and passenger of an experimental Glasair Sportsman 2 Plus 2 were fatally injured when the aircraft impacted terrain near Pine, Arizona, during a Part 91 personal flight. The airplane descended into a canyon and struck a sloping draw after turning southwest above mountainous terrain, resulting in a post-impact fire that consumed most of the wreckage.
summary: The pilot and passenger of an experimental Glasair Sportsman 2 Plus 2 were fatally injured when the aircraft impacted terrain near Pine, Arizona, during a Part 91 personal flight. synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna 208B Part 135 air taxi experienced an uncommanded 45° left roll during the base leg after a loud pop caused by a loose flap bolt. This hardware failure allowed the aft bellcrank to move freely, damaging the left wing spar, though the pilot landed safely with no injuries.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna 208B Part 135 air taxi experienced an uncommanded 45° left roll during the base leg after a loud pop caused by a loose flap bolt. This hardware failure allowed the aft bellcrank to move freely, damaging the left wing spar, though the pilot landed safely with no injuries.

synopsis: Two pilots operating a Cessna 150M experienced low climb performance and subsequent engine power loss during initial climb from Lancaster Regional Airport. The resulting emergency landing caused substantial damage to the engine mount structure after the aircraft cleared obstacles but lacked altitude to return to the runway.
summary: Two pilots operating a Cessna 150M experienced low climb performance and subsequent engine power loss during initial climb from Lancaster Regional Airport. The resulting emergency landing caused substantial damage to the engine mount structure after the aircraft cleared obstacles but lacked altitude to return to the runway.

synopsis: An in-flight collision with a bird while on approach.
summary: The flight crew reported a large bird strike on the left wing leading edge while turning from base to final, causing substantial structural damage. The pilot landed safely on the intended runway and confirmed no pre-accident mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: An airline transport pilot and passenger were seriously injured when their experimental Staudacher ZZ 102 impacted terrain near Vicksburg, Michigan, shortly after climbing to 1,500 feet. Postaccident examination found an orange substance in the fuel line, though the specific cause of the descent remains under investigation.
summary: An airline transport pilot and passenger were seriously injured when their experimental Staudacher ZZ 102 impacted terrain near Vicksburg, Michigan, shortly after climbing to 1,500 feet. Postaccident examination found an orange substance in the fuel line, though the specific cause of the descent remains under investigation.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from a tree during a low-level aerial application flight.
summary: During an aerial application climb, a gust of wind pushed the airplane into a tree, striking the left wing. The pilot maintained control and landed safely, though the aircraft sustained substantial wing damage with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: China Airlines crew reported an Engine 3 fire warning at 5,500ft during climb, causing electrical failures and autopilot disengagement. A cracked fuel manifold tube caused an undercowl fire, leading to an overweight landing at Anchorage after fuel jettison failed.
summary: China Airlines crew reported an Engine 3 fire warning at 5,500ft during climb, causing electrical failures and autopilot disengagement. A cracked fuel manifold tube caused an undercowl fire, leading to an overweight landing at Anchorage after fuel jettison failed.

synopsis: The pilot of a Mooney M20G declared an engine power loss emergency while en route to San Antonio and executed a forced landing on a road. The left wingtip struck vegetation, pulling the aircraft off the road into trees and causing substantial damage to the left wing.
summary: The pilot of a Mooney M20G declared an engine power loss emergency while en route to San Antonio and executed a forced landing on a road. The left wingtip struck vegetation, pulling the aircraft off the road into trees and causing substantial damage to the left wing.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from trees during the landing approach.
summary: The pilot of a tandem seat biplane misjudged the descent rate during a short-field landing approach after being unable to see the aiming point past the front passenger. The left wing struck a tree, causing the aircraft to crash and burn, with no preaccident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from power lines while maneuvering at low-level altitude during an agricultural operation.
summary: A helicopter pilot conducting aerial pollination struck a power line with the tail rotor while turning for a pass after losing sight of the hazard. The subsequent precautionary landing resulted in ground contact and structural damage, with no pre-impact mechanical failures identified.

synopsis: The pilot of a Gulfstream G-IV operating a Part 135 flight forgot to install a secondary safety pin on the nose landing gear pip pin during preflight. This omission caused the nose gear to separate upon touchdown at St. Louis, resulting in a collapsed main gear and substantial damage, though all occupants were uninjured.
summary: The pilot of a Gulfstream G-IV operating a Part 135 flight forgot to install a secondary safety pin on the nose landing gear pip pin during preflight. This omission caused the nose gear to separate upon touchdown at St. Louis, resulting in a collapsed main gear and substantial damage, though all occupants were uninjured.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane during an aborted landing, which resulted in a nose over on the grass runway.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane lost control while attempting to abort a bounced three-point landing on a grass airstrip. The aircraft nosed over and landed inverted, sustaining substantial damage to the left wing and vertical stabilizer with no reported mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: The collision with a deer during touch-and-go landings.
summary: The pilot executed a go-around after seeing deer on runway 27, sustaining an undetected right main gear strike. Upon returning to land, the damaged gear caused the aircraft to veer right, strike a sign, collapse the left gear, and skid into grass with substantial fuselage damage.

synopsis: The pilot of a Taylorcraft DCO-65, N48446, was seriously injured when the aircraft stalled and impacted the ground near Copper City, Michigan, during takeoff from a grass airstrip. The accident occurred after the pilot turned to avoid trees while the airplane failed to climb and approached stall speed.
summary: The pilot of a Taylorcraft DCO-65, N48446, was seriously injured when the aircraft stalled and impacted the ground near Copper City, Michigan, during takeoff from a grass airstrip. The accident occurred after the pilot turned to avoid trees while the airplane failed to climb and approached stall speed.

synopsis: The pilot and passenger of a Robinson R44 Raven II sustained minor injuries when the helicopter was substantially damaged during a Part 91 personal flight near Anthony, Florida. Violent shaking and low rotor rpm warnings led to an autorotation, but the engine lost all power again upon climb initiation, forcing an emergency landing.
summary: The pilot and passenger of a Robinson R44 Raven II sustained minor injuries when the helicopter was substantially damaged during a Part 91 personal flight near Anthony, Florida. Violent shaking and low rotor rpm warnings led to an autorotation, but the engine lost all power again upon climb initiation, forcing an emergency landing.

synopsis: A private pilot flying an experimental Zenith 601 HDS lost all engine power during a left turn onto the downwind leg while practicing touch-and-go landings. The pilot made an emergency off-field landing in a tree clearing, resulting in substantial damage and serious injury after the aircraft nosed over and came to rest inverted.
summary: A private pilot flying an experimental Zenith 601 HDS lost all engine power during a left turn onto the downwind leg while practicing touch-and-go landings. The pilot made an emergency off-field landing in a tree clearing, resulting in substantial damage and serious injury after the aircraft nosed over and came to rest inverted.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to properly stow the motor in preparation for approach and landing that resulted in a loss of airspeed and an inadvertent aerodynamic stall and spin.
summary: The pilot of an electric motor glider selected the system enable switch to off instead of lowering the motor mast during descent, causing the propeller to windmill and induce a stall and spin. Unable to recover at low altitude, the pilot deployed the ballistic parachute, but the glider impacted terrain inverted with substantial right wing damage.

synopsis: The flight instructor's failure to maintain control of the helicopter during a hover, which resulted in the left skid contacting ground and a subsequent dynamic rollover.
summary: During a student helicopter training flight practicing off-airport landings, the aircraft drifted and rolled onto its left side while hovering. The flight instructor attributed the accident to inattention while clearing the tail rotor, noting no mechanical failures occurred.

synopsis: During a Part 91 flight test of an experimental Zenith Cruzer, the pilot and owner/builder experienced lateral rocking shortly after takeoff while verifying oil cooler adjustments. The aircraft impacted the runway left-wing down, collapsing the main gear and separating the nosewheel, causing minor injuries and substantial damage.
summary: During a Part 91 flight test of an experimental Zenith Cruzer, the pilot and owner/builder experienced lateral rocking shortly after takeoff while verifying oil cooler adjustments. The aircraft impacted the runway left-wing down, collapsing the main gear and separating the nosewheel, causing minor injuries and substantial damage.

synopsis: Two pilots flying an Aviat A-1B on an aerial photography mission experienced a partial left aileron detachment due to a fractured hinge bracket. The pilot executed an emergency field landing where the aircraft nosed over, sustaining substantial damage to the wings and empennage.
summary: Two pilots flying an Aviat A-1B on an aerial photography mission experienced a partial left aileron detachment due to a fractured hinge bracket. The pilot executed an emergency field landing where the aircraft nosed over, sustaining substantial damage to the wings and empennage.

synopsis: The pilot's descent below the glidepath and collision with trees during a missed approach.
summary: An instrument-rated pilot flying an RNAV approach in IMC experienced disorientation, deviated below the glidepath, and struck treetops during a missed approach climb. The pilot declared an emergency, received radar vectors to another airport, and landed safely despite substantial damage to the wings and horizontal stabilizer.

synopsis: A Pennsylvania State Police Bell 407 helicopter and a Cessna 150H collided near Carlisle Airport while the helicopter hovered off Runway 28 and the airplane approached on base leg. The helicopter crew could not see the airplane behind them, resulting in a fatal collision that destroyed the airplane and substantially damaged the helicopter.
summary: A Pennsylvania State Police Bell 407 helicopter and a Cessna 150H collided near Carlisle Airport while the helicopter hovered off Runway 28 and the airplane approached on base leg. The helicopter crew could not see the airplane behind them, resulting in a fatal collision that destroyed the airplane and substantially damaged the helicopter.

synopsis: A Para-Ski VX powered parachute, C-IFBY, crashed near Westport, South Dakota, killing one passenger and seriously injuring the pilot and another passenger. The pilot, holding only a remote pilot certificate, operated the non-compliant aircraft which impacted terrain and a fence shortly after departing a field.
summary: A Para-Ski VX powered parachute, C-IFBY, crashed near Westport, South Dakota, killing one passenger and seriously injuring the pilot and another passenger. The pilot, holding only a remote pilot certificate, operated the non-compliant aircraft which impacted terrain and a fence shortly after departing a field.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to extend the landing gear before landing.
summary: The pilot landed an aircraft with the landing gear retracted, causing the lower fuselage to grind against the runway and sustain substantial damage. The pilot attributed the accident to failing to confirm gear extension and lock on short final, reporting no preimpact mechanical failures.

synopsis: A pilot and passenger in a Diamond DA20-A1 experienced low oil pressure, smoke, and total engine power loss during a personal flight near Bristol, Maine. The pilot attempted a forced landing but the aircraft struck trees and water, causing substantial damage and the pilot's death due to an in-flight engine failure.
summary: A pilot and passenger in a Diamond DA20-A1 experienced low oil pressure, smoke, and total engine power loss during a personal flight near Bristol, Maine. The pilot attempted a forced landing but the aircraft struck trees and water, causing substantial damage and the pilot's death due to an in-flight engine failure.

synopsis: A Cessna 441 Part 135 air taxi with two pilots and six passengers crashed near Cape Newenham, Alaska, while executing a second RNAV Runway 15 approach in fog and low ceilings. The flight crew canceled their IFR clearance during a missed approach, then descended below the 1,320 ft minimum descent altitude in deteriorating weather, resulting in a fatal collision with terrain.
summary: A Cessna 441 Part 135 air taxi with two pilots and six passengers crashed near Cape Newenham, Alaska, while executing a second RNAV Runway 15 approach in fog and low ceilings. The flight crew canceled their IFR clearance during a missed approach, then descended below the 1,320 ft minimum descent altitude in deteriorating weather, resulting in a fatal collision with terrain.

synopsis: The glider's encounter with atmospheric conditions where lift was not sufficient to maintain flight.
summary: The glider pilot executed an off-airport landing at 1,000 ft AGL after thermal lift dissipated. The left wing struck a terrain undulation, causing the nose to impact and the empennage to separate, resulting in substantial damage with no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The flight instructor's failure to maintain airplane control during landing in gusting wind conditions.
summary: A flight instructor and student encountered unexpected windshear on short final during a thunderstorm return, causing a hard landing and runway excursion. A subsequent go-around attempt resulted in a wing strike and 360° spin, sustaining substantial damage with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to extend the airplane's landing gear before landing.
summary: The pilot of a retractable gear airplane landed with the gear retracted during a night currency flight, causing substantial fuselage damage. The pilot reported no preaccident mechanical malfunctions that would have prevented normal operation.

synopsis: A pilot operating a Schweizer G-164B on a Part 137 agricultural flight was seriously injured when the aircraft was destroyed near Orlene, Oregon. A witness reported hearing a loud bang and seeing black smoke before assisting the pilot in evacuating the burning airplane.
summary: A pilot operating a Schweizer G-164B on a Part 137 agricultural flight was seriously injured when the aircraft was destroyed near Orlene, Oregon. A witness reported hearing a loud bang and seeing black smoke before assisting the pilot in evacuating the burning airplane.

synopsis: The pilot's improper execution of rejected takeoff procedures, which resulted in loss of control and subsequent runway excursion.
summary: During takeoff from a 600 ft grass airstrip, a gyroplane pilot rejected the roll after hitting a bump but inadvertently applied throttle instead of the handbrake. The aircraft overran the runway into a pond, sustaining substantial damage to the empennage and a main rotor blade with no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The flight instructor's failure to maintain control of the helicopter during a low hover over a grass area, which resulted in left skid contact with the ground and a dynamic rollover to the left.
summary: A flight instructor and a non-pilot mechanic conducted a local helicopter check flight. During a hover, the mechanic over-controlled the cyclic, causing the helicopter to roll onto its left side and sustain substantial damage to the main rotor blades and tailboom.

synopsis: During a Part 91 instructional flight in a Cessna 172L, the throttle failed to advance during a stall recovery, forcing an idle-power landing on a dry lakebed. The aircraft nosed over into a marshy area during rollout, sustaining substantial wing damage, while the flight instructor and student remained uninjured.
summary: During a Part 91 instructional flight in a Cessna 172L, the throttle failed to advance during a stall recovery, forcing an idle-power landing on a dry lakebed. The aircraft nosed over into a marshy area during rollout, sustaining substantial wing damage, while the flight instructor and student remained uninjured.

synopsis: The misfuelling of the airplane by the refueler. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's failure to verify that the airplane had been properly fueled prior to departing on the accident flight.
summary: The pilot of a reciprocating multi-engine airplane experienced engine overheating and deterioration after being fueled with Jet-A instead of 100LL, leading to a forced landing in a cornfield. The accident resulted in substantial damage because the pilot failed to verify the fuel type or inspect the tanks before departure.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the final approach in variable and gusting wind conditions. Contributing to the accident were localized wind effects associated with mountainous terrain and with nearby convective activity.
summary: The pilot, on his first flight to a mountainous grass airstrip, lost control and struck trees after a gust displaced the aircraft left of centerline during final approach to runway 09. The accident was caused by rapidly changing wind conditions associated with nearby convective activity, resulting in substantial damage to the airplane.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll.
summary: The pilot reported that after landing, the aircraft drifted left and ground looped right despite rudder corrections, causing substantial fuselage damage. The pilot stated no pre-accident mechanical malfunctions occurred.

synopsis: A pilot and three passengers were fatally injured when their Piper PA-24-260, N9485P, was substantially damaged during a landing attempt at Seldovia Airport. Witnesses reported the aircraft approached fast, bounced abnormally, pitched up, and impacted a tree before descending into water while landing opposite the standard direction.
summary: A pilot and three passengers were fatally injured when their Piper PA-24-260, N9485P, was substantially damaged during a landing attempt at Seldovia Airport. Witnesses reported the aircraft approached fast, bounced abnormally, pitched up, and impacted a tree before descending into water while landing opposite the standard direction.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper PA-18A banner tow aircraft experienced a total loss of engine power and a loud pop while descending through 600 feet AGL near New Smyrna Beach. He performed a forced landing on water, resulting in the aircraft nosing over and sustaining substantial damage, though the pilot was uninjured.
summary: The pilot of a Piper PA-18A banner tow aircraft experienced a total loss of engine power and a loud pop while descending through 600 feet AGL near New Smyrna Beach. He performed a forced landing on water, resulting in the aircraft nosing over and sustaining substantial damage, though the pilot was uninjured.

synopsis: A Consolidated Aeronautics Lake LA-4-200, N6185V, carrying a pilot and passenger, crashed near Ithaca, New York, during a Part 91 personal flight, resulting in fatal injuries and substantial damage. The aircraft struck trees and the ground while descending on a westerly heading, though post-accident examination found the engine and fuel systems functional with no mechanical failure identified.
summary: A Consolidated Aeronautics Lake LA-4-200, N6185V, carrying a pilot and passenger, crashed near Ithaca, New York, during a Part 91 personal flight, resulting in fatal injuries and substantial damage. The aircraft struck trees and the ground while descending on a westerly heading, though post-accident examination found the engine and fuel systems functional with no mechanical failure identified.

synopsis: The pilot's excessive braking during the landing roll, which resulted in a nose over.
summary: A private pilot receiving tailwheel endorsement instruction nosed over the aircraft during landing due to excessive brake application. The airplane came to rest inverted with substantial damage to the fuselage, vertical stabilizer, and rudder, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: A pilot and flight instructor were fatally injured when their Mooney M20C, N2783W, collided with terrain near Hood River, Oregon, during a Part 91 instructional flight. Witnesses reported the aircraft entered a nose-down attitude while performing aerobatic or stall-practice maneuvers before impacting sloping terrain.
summary: A pilot and flight instructor were fatally injured when their Mooney M20C, N2783W, collided with terrain near Hood River, Oregon, during a Part 91 instructional flight. Witnesses reported the aircraft entered a nose-down attitude while performing aerobatic or stall-practice maneuvers before impacting sloping terrain.

synopsis: During takeoff of an IAI 1124A Westwind air ambulance at Harry Reid International Airport, the left main tire burst at 130 knots, causing the aircraft to veer left and exit the runway. The pilot's attempt to regain control resulted in landing gear collapse, a second tire blowout, and substantial fuselage damage, though all five occupants were uninjured.
summary: During takeoff of an IAI 1124A Westwind air ambulance at Harry Reid International Airport, the left main tire burst at 130 knots, causing the aircraft to veer left and exit the runway. The pilot's attempt to regain control resulted in landing gear collapse, a second tire blowout, and substantial fuselage damage, though all five occupants were uninjured.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper PA-22-150 experienced partial engine power loss and RPM drop shortly after a soft-field takeoff from J-22 Ranch Airport. Unable to gain airspeed, the pilot attempted an off-field landing but struck treetops, resulting in substantial damage to both wings.
summary: The pilot of a Piper PA-22-150 experienced partial engine power loss and RPM drop shortly after a soft-field takeoff from J-22 Ranch Airport. Unable to gain airspeed, the pilot attempted an off-field landing but struck treetops, resulting in substantial damage to both wings.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental Zenith CH701 suffered a total engine power loss while climbing through 300 feet AGL after takeoff tests at Byron Airport. The pilot landed in a grass area adjacent to the runway, where the aircraft struck a ditch, nosed over, and sustained substantial damage.
summary: The pilot of an experimental Zenith CH701 suffered a total engine power loss while climbing through 300 feet AGL after takeoff tests at Byron Airport. The pilot landed in a grass area adjacent to the runway, where the aircraft struck a ditch, nosed over, and sustained substantial damage.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control during the rejected takeoff, which resulted in a runway excursion. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's decision to abort the takeoff after the airplane had accelerated above its normal rotation speed. Also contributing to the accident was the flight school's non-standard engine break-in takeoff procedure.
summary: During a first engine break-in flight, the pilot aborted takeoff after realizing the throttle was not advanced, causing the aircraft to briefly lift off at 60 knots before departing the runway into a ditch. The pilot attributed the incident to failing to reach the operator's required 75-knot rotation speed, which exceeded the handbook's normal 55-knot value.

synopsis: During an ILS approach to Newark, a Hawker 400A crew encountered heavy rain and possible wind shear, causing a loss of airspeed and runway sight. The aircraft's right wing struck the runway surface during a go-around attempt, sustaining substantial damage before the pilots diverted to Morristown.
summary: During an ILS approach to Newark, a Hawker 400A crew encountered heavy rain and possible wind shear, causing a loss of airspeed and runway sight. The aircraft's right wing struck the runway surface during a go-around attempt, sustaining substantial damage before the pilots diverted to Morristown.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing.
summary: The pilot reported that during landing on runway 17 in a crosswind, the aircraft yawed left and ground looped despite control inputs. The airplane skidded off the runway, shearing the right landing gear and sustaining substantial right wing damage, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: Two pilots flying a Cessna 560XL on a Part 135 flight substantially damaged the aircraft after a high-speed visual approach to Porterville Municipal Airport. The airplane floated down the runway, overran the threshold, and exited into a field, resulting in minor injuries to the pilots but no injuries to the four passengers.
summary: Two pilots flying a Cessna 560XL on a Part 135 flight substantially damaged the aircraft after a high-speed visual approach to Porterville Municipal Airport. The airplane floated down the runway, overran the threshold, and exited into a field, resulting in minor injuries to the pilots but no injuries to the four passengers.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing in gusting wind conditions.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane reported that gusting winds, possibly from a dust devil, lifted the right wing during a three-point landing roll. Attempts to correct with aileron and rudder resulted in both wings striking the ground, causing the aircraft to nose down and sustain substantial damage.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna 150E experienced a total engine power loss during descent near Siler, Washington, after applying carburetor heat. Unable to restore power despite troubleshooting attempts, the pilot executed a forced landing in a riverbed, resulting in substantial fuselage damage but no injuries.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna 150E experienced a total engine power loss during descent near Siler, Washington, after applying carburetor heat. Unable to restore power despite troubleshooting attempts, the pilot executed a forced landing in a riverbed, resulting in substantial fuselage damage but no injuries.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to adequately manage the available fuel onboard the airplane, which resulted in a total loss of power due to fuel starvation and a forced landing on uneven terrain.
summary: The pilot of a cross-country flight experienced engine power loss near the destination and performed a forced landing on uneven terrain, collapsing the landing gear and damaging the right wing. The accident was likely caused by fuel starvation after the pilot failed to reposition the fuel selector from the empty left tank to the full right tank.

synopsis: A private pilot flying a Cessna 210K experienced a crankcase breach and broken connecting rod near No. 6 cylinder while climbing through 4,500 ft MSL, causing total power loss. Unable to locate an unlit airport at night, the pilot forced-landed on a road, striking utility poles and a guardrail, resulting in substantial damage but no injuries.
summary: A private pilot flying a Cessna 210K experienced a crankcase breach and broken connecting rod near No. 6 cylinder while climbing through 4,500 ft MSL, causing total power loss. The nose gear collapsed after contacting a grass dip, causing substantial damage to the firewall and right wing, with no preimpact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: A private pilot flying a Socata TB 9 Tampico sustained substantial left wing damage after the aircraft descended onto a closed runway section and impacted terrain during takeoff. The pilot reported no mechanical failures, attributing the accident to the aircraft exiting the reduced runway length due to construction.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna 414A reported left engine power loss during takeoff from runway 17 at Boerne Stage Airfield shortly after cylinder replacement. The pilot continued the takeoff but the aircraft struck a utility pole and terrain, resulting in a post-impact fire that destroyed the airplane while both occupants escaped uninjured.

synopsis: A pilot operating a Piper PA18-150 on a Part 91 flight was seriously injured when the aircraft impacted a field near Karinen, South Dakota. The accident likely resulted from reduced visibility due to fog and a low ceiling while the pilot conducted routine aerial observations.

synopsis: The pilot of a Fairchild 24H reported a stuck left rudder pedal during landing rollout near Indianapolis, causing the aircraft to drift right and depart the runway. Post-accident examination found a bent metal part contacting the rudder bellcrank, which caused the sticking and resulted in substantial damage after the plane hit a ditch.

synopsis: A pilot and passenger were fatally injured when their Diamond DA-40, N162GL, impacted rising mountainous terrain near Eldorado Springs, Colorado, during a Part 91 personal flight. The aircraft was destroyed after the final ADS-B data point at 7,375 ft msl, with the ELT activating shortly before the crash.

synopsis: The pilot of a Lancair IV-P-T, N5UC, experienced engine power loss at 3,325 feet MSL during initial climb from Ontario Municipal Airport. synopsis: Two airline transport pilots operating a Cessna 525 on a Part 91 positioning flight aborted takeoff due to heavy controls and inability to rotate. The aircraft departed the runway, breached the perimeter fence, and sustained substantial damage with partial post-accident fire.

synopsis: During a student landing roll at Phoenix Deer Valley Airport, a Cirrus SR20's nose gear collapsed upon nosewheel contact, substantially damaging the firewall. The aircraft lost radar and radio contact at 8,000 feet, and wreckage was found nose-down on forested terrain with throttle levers fully forward.

synopsis: During a post-maintenance test flight of a Mooney M20F, the pilot encountered a left rolling tendency and significant right aileron correction needs shortly after takeoff. Upon landing, the aircraft veered left, exited the runway, and struck a taxiway sign, causing substantial damage to the left wing.

synopsis: A private pilot flying a Piper PA-28-140 experienced total engine power loss at 700 feet AGL during a local Part 91 flight, likely due to fuel exhaustion from not switching tanks. The pilot forced-landed in a field, sustaining substantial left wing damage, while the aircraft lacked a current annual inspection.

synopsis: A pilot flying a Piper J3C-65 near Boonville, Indiana, struck a vehicle on South Baker Road while performing a low approach in ground effect. The collision occurred because tall weeds, shadows, and the car's dark color obscured the vehicle until it was too late to avoid impact, resulting in the passenger's death.

synopsis: The pilot of a Maule M-7-260, N3217V, lost directional control during landing at The Sea Ranch Airport (CA51) when the aircraft pulled right. The pilot attributed the runway excursion and substantial damage to a suspected re-engagement of the right parking brake.

synopsis: A student pilot operating a Hughes 269C helicopter during solo traffic pattern practice at Gastonia Municipal Airport experienced a loud bang and loss of rotor RPM below 100 feet. The accident, caused by a fractured clutch linear actuator shaft, resulted in a hard landing with substantial damage to the fuselage and tail rotor transmission.

synopsis: During a Part 91 personal flight, a Consolidated Aeronautics Lake LA-4-200 suffered substantial damage when an explosion occurred behind the occupants upon engine start. synopsis: During a Part 91 instructional flight in a Piper PA-28-160, the engine lost power at 2,500 feet while the student pilot descended toward the airport. The flight instructor executed a forced landing in a field, but the nose gear collapsed in soft ground, substantially damaging the aircraft.
